temperature.tooltip: Sampling randomness when num_beams == 1. 0.2–0.4 is focused, 0.7+ is creative.

top_p.tooltip: Nucleus sampling cutoff when num_beams == 1. Lower values keep only top tokens; 0.9–0.95 allows more variety.

num_beams.tooltip: Beam-search width. Values >1 disable temperature/top_p and trade speed for more stable answers.

repetition_penalty.tooltip: Values >1 (e.g., 1.1–1.3) penalize repeated phrases; 1.0 leaves logits untouched.

frame_count.tooltip: Number of frames extracted from video inputs before prompting Qwen-VL. More frames provide context but cost time.

video_frame_size.tooltip: Control the maximum resolution for video frames. 'auto' computes safe budget to prevent OOM/overflow while keeping small videos untouched.

model_name.tooltip: GGUF model entry defined in gguf_models.json.

prompt_text.tooltip: Prompt text to enhance. Leave blank to just emit the preset instruction.

english_output.tooltip: Force final output in English using translation prompt.

device.tooltip: Select device; auto prefers GPU when available.

model_name.tooltip: Pick the Qwen-VL checkpoint. First run downloads weights into models/LLM/Qwen-VL, so leave disk space.

quantization.tooltip: Precision vs VRAM. FP16 gives the best quality if memory allows; 8-bit suits 8–16 GB GPUs; 4-bit fits 6 GB or lower but is slower.

attention_mode.tooltip: auto tries flash-attn v2 when installed and falls back to SDPA. Only override when debugging attention backends.

use_torch_compile.tooltip: Enable torch.compile('reduce-overhead') on supported CUDA/Torch 2.1+ builds for extra throughput after the first compile.

device.tooltip: Choose where to run the model: auto, cpu, mps, or cuda:x for multi-GPU systems.

prompt_text.tooltip: Prompt text to enhance. Leave blank to just emit the preset instruction.

eta.tooltip: Controls the scale of the parallel guidance vector. Default CFG behavior at a setting of 1.

norm_threshold.tooltip: Normalize guidance vector to this value, normalization disable at a setting of 0.

momentum.tooltip: Controls a running average of guidance during diffusion, disabled at a setting of 0.

model.tooltip: The model to patch with AReA. FLUX, Z-Image (Lumina2), Krea-2 and Qwen-Image-2.1 share the same 16 px patch grid, so the same width/height serve any of them.

width.tooltip: Target image width. Must match the width of your empty latent — AReA builds its schedule from this geometry and validates it against the latent at every forward.

height.tooltip: Target image height. Must match the height of your empty latent.

model_type.tooltip: Specify the model architecture. 'auto' usually works. FLUX and Z-Image (Lumina2 / NextDiT) share a 16 px patch grid, so the same width/height serve either; Krea-2 (SingleStreamDiT) uses the same 16 px token grid (ASSUMED — its VAE downscale is unverified, so a 16x VAE would make its token 32 px) and needs no padding; Qwen-Image-2.1 (QwenImage21Transformer2DModel) uses the same 16 px token grid (MEASURED — its latent format downsamples 16x and 2.1 does not patchify) and pads nothing, and AReA switches its prefix K/V cache off on its own clone (the cached path is indistinguishable from the image segment, so with the cache on AReA would engage on no call at all); Nunchaku's fused kernels bypass the attention seam, so it is reported unchanged.

enable_area.tooltip: Enable or disable AReA. When disabled, the model is returned with nothing patched.

phase1_steps.tooltip: Number of leading denoising steps that run Phase I (coarse cross-scale attention), clamped to the total step count. 8 = the reference's FLUX constant (of 28). 0 = all Phase II (windowed attention from the first step). Only read when phase1_mode is 'steps'. Z-Image Turbo runs short (8-step) schedules: use 1-3 there (or sigma mode) — 8 of an 8-step run pools every step, which the distilled sampler cannot re-detail. On a SHORT schedule the effective coarse steps are capped at total_steps - 2 (two fine steps must remain, or the pooling footprint never heals): the forward-time log prints the knob, the cap and the effective count once per schedule, so a capped run is readable and the knob stays authoritative below the cap.

phase1_mode.tooltip: How the Phase I -> Phase II switch is expressed. 'auto' = resolved per backbone: 'sigma' on Z-Image and Qwen-Image-2.1 (the leading steps still at or above phase1_sigma run Phase I, so the switch follows the schedule) and 'steps' on FLUX and Krea-2. 'steps' = the leading phase1_steps steps run Phase I (the reference's mode). 'sigma' = the leading steps whose noise level is still at or above phase1_sigma run Phase I, so the switch follows the schedule rather than a fixed count (8 of 28 sits at a sigma of roughly 0.88 on a shift-3.0 flow). 'bootstrap' = the paper's Appendix F mode: no Phase I at all, windowed Phase II from the first step; the early steps must have composed the canvas in a separate native-resolution pass whose latent was upscaled and re-noised to phase1_sigma (see the README pattern).

phase1_sigma.tooltip: Noise level at which Phase I gives way to Phase II, when phase1_mode is 'sigma'. 0.89 = the paper's value for its first backbone; 0.86 was its Qwen-Image value, so treat this as per-schedule calibration rather than a universal constant.

pooling.tooltip: Phase I pooling: which token of each f x f image block the pooled key/value comes from. 'auto' = resolved per backbone: 'subsample' on FLUX, 'mean' on Z-Image and Krea-2, 'medoid' on Qwen-Image-2.1. 'subsample' = block centre. 'mean' = block average for values, and for keys the block-mean direction rescaled to the mean member norm (the centroid keeps every token contributing while the norm keeps the attention temperature at the un-pooled one). 'medoid' = the token closest to the block-mean key — on Qwen-Image-2.1 it keeps ONE real token's key AND value, so the pooled cell carries a single content instead of a synthetic key over a blended value. 'random' = a token drawn per (seed, step, block). Keys must be pooled BEFORE the position rotation, so all four keep the survivors in the query's frame.

halo.tooltip: Widest Halo ring a Phase II window may draw (in patches). Each side of each window draws its own fresh width in [0, halo] at every step; AReA narrows it only when the windowed step would otherwise cost more than a full-attention step.

bridge_ratio.tooltip: Rho of the bridge: each Phase II window also attends to R = round(rho * w)^2 of the canvas's most distinctive unrotated keys, spread over an 8x8 cell grid so no region is starved. 0 = no bridge.

bridge_floor_steps.tooltip: How many leading Phase II steps keep the paper's full bridge (R = round(rho*w)^2) and the full halo instead of the cost-capped ones. On short schedules (12 total steps or fewer) the cost cap starves the bridge exactly on the composition-critical steps, so those steps are exempted here; a 28-step FLUX run is never floored (long schedules ignore this knob). 0 = the cost cap on every step. The exemption costs about 1.0-1.4x full attention per floored step (measured 1.25x-1.41x on the 2048px Turbo schedule), and warns once naming the multiplier.

window_start.tooltip: Window side (patches) Phase II starts its ramp at, instead of the cost-optimal size — smaller gives the early windows more global context. Short schedules only: a long (28-step) schedule ignores this knob. 0 = the cost-optimal start, which is clamped into [w_min, grid]; the ramp still shrinks to w_min.

window_hold_steps.tooltip: Extra Phase II steps that hold the start window before the ramp shrinks it (a start-heavy ramp for short schedules). Short schedules only: a long (28-step) schedule ignores this knob.

seed.tooltip: Seed of every draw (tile placement, Halo widths and reaches, random pooling). Keyed by (seed, step), so the same seed and step always build the same windows and halos — and cond and uncond attend through identical graphs. No global RNG is read.

output_tooltips: The model patched with AReA.
AReA.name: AReA
AReA.description: AReA (arXiv 2610.17227). Replaces FLUX / Z-Image / Krea-2 / Qwen-Image-2.1 image self-attention with a time-dependent attention graph: coarse cross-scale attention on leading steps, DWT-guided windowed attention (Halo + bridge tokens) on the rest. Training-free; a no-op at or below 1024 px.

image.tooltip: BHWC image batch to align.

multiple.tooltip: Width and height come out divisible by this. 16 or 32 suits most diffusion models; latent-space nodes usually want at least 8.

mode.tooltip: How to reach the multiple. resize rescales to the NEAREST multiple (slight stretch, keeps every pixel's content). crop trims DOWN to the next multiple at the chosen anchor (no distortion, loses edges). pad adds edges UP to the next multiple with edge pixels or a colour (no distortion). A side smaller than one multiple always grows to exactly one.

crop_position.tooltip: Crop mode only: which part of the frame survives. center trims both edges evenly; top, bottom, left, or right pin that edge and trim the opposite one. Ignored by resize and pad.

pad_position.tooltip: Pad mode only: where the image sits on the grown canvas — the new pixels land on the opposite side. center splits them evenly.

pad_fill.tooltip: Pad mode only: what fills the new area. replicate stretches the edge pixels out; color uses pad_color as a solid.

pad_color.tooltip: Solid fill for pad_fill: color. Hex, R,G,B numbers, or a CSS color name.

AUSBOSS_NODES_AlignImage.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_AlignImage
AUSBOSS_NODES_AlignImage.description: Snaps an image's width and height to a clean multiple of a number you choose — 8, 16, 32, whatever the model wants. Qwen image models, VAEs, and many samplers behave best on cleanly divisible sizes. Resize rescales to the nearest multiple, crop trims down to one from the anchor you pick, pad grows up to one with edge pixels or a colour; the new size comes out as INTs for wiring into latent nodes.
output_tooltips: The aligned batch; both sides are multiples of the chosen number.
Aligned width in pixels.
Aligned height in pixels.

text.tooltip: What the note says. A blank line starts a new point. Put **double stars** around a word to stress it. An arrow emoji, or -> and <-, becomes an arrow.

AUSBOSS_NODES_Callout.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_Callout
AUSBOSS_NODES_Callout.description: A note for the canvas. Write a line or two and the text grows to fill the note, so it reads without zooming in. An arrow emoji in the text turns into a teal arrow that sits in the line. Double-click to edit. Nothing runs: the node has no inputs or outputs.

text.tooltip: What the note says. A blank line starts a new point. Put **double stars** around a word to stress it. An arrow emoji, or -> and <-, becomes an arrow.

AUSBOSS_NODES_CalloutTile.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_CalloutTile
AUSBOSS_NODES_CalloutTile.description: A compact title or colored link button for a workflow. Double-click to edit; use its menu to choose a title, YouTube or Discord tile. Saved tiles require a pack that supports tiles, so an older install can report the missing node. Nothing runs.

image.tooltip: BHWC image whose colors get corrected.

strength.tooltip: Blend between the original (0) and the fully matched image (1).

reference.tooltip: The image whose color statistics to copy — for an inpainted crop, feed the original image here. A single reference broadcasts across a batch. Required unless reference_mode is first_frame.

method.tooltip: How the colors move. lab: perceptual mean/std shift, the safe default. rgb: the same in raw channels. mkl: full covariance mapping, best when hues are rotated, not just shifted. histogram: exact per-channel distribution match, the strongest and least subtle.

mask.tooltip: Restricts the correction to the white area — both the statistics measured on the image and where the fix is applied; typical for recoloring just an inpainted region. Black pixels pass through bit-identical, so the mask itself never changes — wire your original mask onward. Without a mask the whole image is matched.

invert_mask.tooltip: Treat the mask's black area as the region to correct instead of the white area.

reference_mode.tooltip: Where the target statistics come from. reference uses the connected reference image. first_frame uses the batch's own first frame as the target for every frame, which reduces a video's colour drift; the reference input is ignored.

AUSBOSS_NODES_ColorMatch.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_ColorMatch
AUSBOSS_NODES_ColorMatch.description: Transfers the reference image's color statistics onto the input — fixes the color shift on inpainted or stitched regions. Four methods: lab and rgb move per-channel mean/std, mkl maps the full color covariance, histogram matches each channel's distribution exactly. An optional mask restricts both the measurement and the correction to its white area (invert_mask flips that), which is why the node takes a mask but outputs none: the mask only scopes the fix, and passes through your graph unchanged. Strength blends between the original and the fully matched result. For video, reference_mode: first_frame matches every frame to the batch's own first frame, which reduces colour drift between frames without a reference; it does not stabilise motion.
output_tooltips: The color-matched image; pixels outside the mask are untouched.

image_a.tooltip: Baseline batch. Its first frame is preview A, and the whole batch passes through the image_a output unchanged.

image_b.tooltip: Comparison batch. Its first frame is preview B, revealed by sliding across the panel or flipping the A/B toggle. The whole batch passes through the image_b output unchanged.

filename.tooltip: Optional. A name for the files that Erase saves, such as the source picture's file name. Its folder and extension are dropped. Not wired: the name typed on the node is used.

AUSBOSS_NODES_Compare.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_Compare
AUSBOSS_NODES_Compare.description: Shows A and B on one panel: slide across it to reveal B up to the pointer, or hold A or B with the switch under the picture. Erase rubs parts of one picture away with a brush so the other shows through, and saves that mix as a PNG, with a layered PSD and the mask if you want them. image_a and image_b pass through unchanged so the node can sit mid-graph.
output_tooltips: image_a passed through unchanged, so downstream nodes keep working while you compare.
The image_b batch, untouched: the picture you compared against, often the edited one.

image.tooltip: BHWC image or video frames to crop around the mask.

mask.tooltip: White marks the area to inpaint. A multi-frame mask is unioned into one crop window; an empty mask selects the whole image.

context_factor.tooltip: Grows the mask bounding box symmetrically by this factor so the inpainter sees surrounding context.

blend_pixels.tooltip: Feather width for pasting the result back: the paste mask is widened by this many pixels and blurred. It never touches the sampling mask (mask_blur softens that). 0 pastes hard.

output_multiple.tooltip: The crop's size is rounded up to a multiple of this. 32 suits most models; a smaller step can come back trimmed and look slightly bigger.

target_width.tooltip: Rescale the crop to this width for the sampler; 0 keeps the native crop width (or follows target_height at the crop's aspect ratio).

target_height.tooltip: Rescale the crop to this height for the sampler; 0 keeps the native crop height (or follows target_width at the crop's aspect ratio).

mask_grow.tooltip: Dilate the sampling mask by this many pixels (negative shrinks) so the inpainter repaints past the drawn edge. Reshapes what gets painted, unlike blend_pixels which only feathers the paste-back.

mask_blur.tooltip: Gaussian sigma softening the sampling mask's edge for models that honor soft masks. 0 keeps the hard edge.

invert_mask.tooltip: Inpaint the black area instead of the white area — everything outside the drawn region.

context_pixels.tooltip: Flat extra context in pixels added around the mask box after context_factor's growth.

target_megapixels.tooltip: Rescale the crop for the sampler so its area is about this many megapixels — 1.0 suits SDXL-class models, 0 keeps the native crop size. Explicit target_width/height overrides this.

rescale_algorithm.tooltip: Resize filter for the sampler round trip. bilinear is the safe default, bicubic keeps upscales a touch crisper, area suits heavy downscales, nearest never invents pixels.

extend_left.tooltip: Outpainting: grow the frame this many pixels leftward. The new band is added to the mask and becomes part of the stitched output.

extend_right.tooltip: Outpainting: grow the frame this many pixels rightward. The new band is added to the mask and becomes part of the stitched output.

extend_up.tooltip: Outpainting: grow the frame this many pixels upward. The new band is added to the mask and becomes part of the stitched output.

extend_down.tooltip: Outpainting: grow the frame this many pixels downward. The new band is added to the mask and becomes part of the stitched output.

keep_inside.tooltip: Keep the crop inside the picture. On: the context stops at the picture's edges, so the model sees only real picture. Off: the crop can run past the edges, filled with stretched copies of the edge pixels (the old behavior).

AUSBOSS_NODES_CropForInpaint.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_CropForInpaint
AUSBOSS_NODES_CropForInpaint.description: Cuts the masked region plus surrounding context out of an image so an inpainter works at native resolution, and emits a stitcher that Stitch Inpaint 🆎 uses to paste the result back seamlessly. The selection can be inverted, grown or shrunk, and edge-softened before cropping; context comes from a growth factor plus optional flat pixels, and stops at the picture's edges unless keep_inside is off. target_megapixels rescales the crop to a sampler-friendly area, and the extend inputs grow the frame itself for outpainting. By default the sampling mask stays hard-edged; feathering lives in a separate blend mask used only while pasting. An empty mask selects the full image and stitches back unchanged.
output_tooltips: Cropped BHWC region around the mask, sized for the sampler.
The sampling mask, cropped like the image: the input mask after invert, grow and blur. blend_pixels never feathers it.
Stitch data for Stitch Inpaint 🆎: canvas, rects, blend mask, scale.

model.tooltip: The edit model. Patch last, after any LoRAs.

vae.tooltip: The same VAE the workflow decodes with.

image.tooltip: The picture you are editing, at the size of the result. Use the same picture the edit model gets.

lock.tooltip: auto locks the untouched parts and steps aside when the whole picture changes. always locks even then. off does nothing.

tolerance.tooltip: How big a change must be to count as part of the edit. Raise it if the lock lets small unwanted changes through; lower it if it holds back part of your edit.

mask.tooltip: Optional. White marks where the edit may happen; everything else is locked. With a mask the node does not look for the change itself.

AUSBOSS_NODES_EditLock.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_EditLock
AUSBOSS_NODES_EditLock.description: Keeps every part of your picture that an edit did not change exactly where it was, with the colors it had. Edit models redraw the whole picture, so untouched parts often come back slightly zoomed, shifted or tinted. Put this between the model and the sampler and give it the picture you are editing. It needs no mask: it sees what the edit changes while the picture is made. When the edit changes the whole picture (a new style, new light, new weather) it steps aside. Add Edit Lock Restore 🆎 after the decode to get your own pixels back in the untouched parts.
output_tooltips: The model with the lock on. Plug it into the sampler.
What the lock kept. Plug it into Edit Lock Restore 🆎 after the decode.

image.tooltip: The edited picture, straight from the VAE decode.

feather.tooltip: How softly your original fades into the edit, in pixels. The fade stays outside the edit.

remove_tint.tooltip: Takes out the faint pink tint the edit model adds to the whole picture. Edits meant to recolor everything, like golden hour, are left alone.

AUSBOSS_NODES_EditLockRestore.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_EditLockRestore
AUSBOSS_NODES_EditLockRestore.description: Puts your picture's own pixels back in every part the edit did not change. Use it right after the VAE decode, with the edit_lock output of Edit Lock 🆎. The untouched parts then match your original pixel for pixel; only the edit is new. It also takes out the faint pink tint some edit models add to the whole picture, which matters most when the lock stepped aside (a new hair color, background or weather).
output_tooltips: The edit with your original pixels in the untouched parts.
White where the edit changed the picture.
How much of the picture was kept. Plug it into Show Text 🆎 to read it.

frames.tooltip: The video frames to make larger.

model.tooltip: The FlashVSR model file, from ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models.

scale.tooltip: How many times larger each side gets. 1 keeps the size and only sharpens.

color_match.tooltip: Keeps each frame's colours the same as your video. Leave it on.

vae.tooltip: Optional. Connect the Wan 2.1 VAE for a slower, finer finish. Left empty, the fast decoder inside the model file is used.

AUSBOSS_NODES_FlashVSRUpscale.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_FlashVSRUpscale
AUSBOSS_NODES_FlashVSRUpscale.description: Makes a video larger and sharper with the FlashVSR model. Pick the model file, set how much larger, and run. It reads the clip a few frames at a time, so a long clip needs no more graphics memory than a short one, and every frame comes back. Connect the Wan 2.1 VAE for a slower, finer finish.
output_tooltips: The larger, sharper frames: as many as went in.

AUSBOSS_NODES_Float.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_Float
AUSBOSS_NODES_Float.description: A single FLOAT value on its own wire. Share one strength, scale or CFG across several nodes and change it in one place.
output_tooltips: The float, unchanged.

frames.tooltip: Video frames as a BHWC IMAGE batch.

source_fps.tooltip: Frame rate of the incoming batch; wire Load Video's fps output to match the source.

target_fps.tooltip: Frame rate to resample to. Matching the source fps passes the frames through unchanged.

method.tooltip: blend crossfades neighboring frames: instant, no downloads, soft on fast motion. Optical flow warps both neighbors along RAFT motion vectors for sharper in-betweens. It only uses an already-cached checkpoint and never downloads one.

scene_cut_threshold.tooltip: Mean absolute frame difference above this counts as a hard cut, and the new frame holds the last frame before the cut instead of morphing across it. 0 disables cut detection.

batch_size.tooltip: In-between frames computed per batch: higher is faster but uses more VRAM.

AUSBOSS_NODES_FrameInterpolate.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_FrameInterpolate
AUSBOSS_NODES_FrameInterpolate.description: Resamples a frame batch from a source fps to a target fps, so 24 to 30 works as naturally as doubling. New in-between frames come from a fast crossfade blend or cached RAFT optical flow; frames that land exactly on a source frame are copied untouched. Hard scene cuts hold the last frame instead of morphing across the cut.
output_tooltips: The resampled BHWC frame batch at the target rate.
The actual output fps; wire this into Save Video so rounding to a whole frame count never drifts the timing.

value.tooltip: Any wire. Memory is freed when this node runs, then the value continues unchanged.

AUSBOSS_NODES_FreeMemory.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_FreeMemory
AUSBOSS_NODES_FreeMemory.description: Passes any wire through unchanged and, on the way, unloads comfy's cached models and empties the CUDA cache — put it between a heavy stage and the next so the second starts with free VRAM instead of an out-of-memory error. Every release step is best-effort: if an API is missing or moves, that step is skipped and the wire still flows. Like any node it only runs when its input changes, so it never breaks caching downstream.
output_tooltips: The input, passed through unchanged.

script.tooltip: What happens, one line for each moment. A blank line cuts to a new place. @1 is Picture 1. Start a line with 3s: to put it on that second.

seconds.tooltip: How long the clip is. Plan on about one moment a second at most.

clip.tooltip: Optional: a small text model such as Qwen3-VL 8B. It adds moments after a one-line idea and matches the sound to the place. In a swap it writes what the new person looks like, from their picture.

picture_1.tooltip: Your first picture. Type @1 to name it in a line.

picture_2.tooltip: Optional: a second picture, with its own job. Type @2 to name it.

picture_3.tooltip: Optional: a third picture, with its own job. Type @3 to name it.

picture_4.tooltip: Optional: a fourth picture, with its own job. Type @4 to name it.

video.tooltip: Optional: the frames of a video. Pick what it is for under Video does.

video_sound.tooltip: Optional: the video's own sound. Only keep going uses it.

voice.tooltip: A clip of the voice to use, about 10 seconds.

song.tooltip: The music to use. Each moment moves onto its beat.

camera.tooltip: How the camera moves the whole way through. As typed leaves it to your words; with a video wired it shows as from the video and keeps the video's own camera.

look.tooltip: From the picture keeps your photo's look. The others redraw it in that style.

song_start.tooltip: The second of the song to start from, so the clip gets the good part.

cut_on_beat.tooltip: Moves each moment onto the nearest beat of the song. Pick off to keep your own seconds.

language.tooltip: The language of the words in quotes.

job_1.tooltip: What this picture is for. Person goes wherever your lines say. Place is where it happens. Outfit and thing work best with nobody in the picture. Style gives only the look. Start on it and end on it fix the first or last moment.

job_2.tooltip: What this picture is for. Person goes wherever your lines say. Place is where it happens. Outfit and thing work best with nobody in the picture. Style gives only the look. Start on it and end on it fix the first or last moment.

job_3.tooltip: What this picture is for. Person goes wherever your lines say. Place is where it happens. Outfit and thing work best with nobody in the picture. Style gives only the look. Start on it and end on it fix the first or last moment.

job_4.tooltip: What this picture is for. Person goes wherever your lines say. Place is where it happens. Outfit and thing work best with nobody in the picture. Style gives only the look. Start on it and end on it fix the first or last moment.

video_job.tooltip: What the video is for: copy its moves, swap the person in it, keep it going, give it a new voice, or change something in it and keep the person (a hat, a shirt). Copy its moves, swap, new voice and change something ignore Seconds and keep the video's length.

sound.tooltip: What you hear the whole way through, like rain on a window. Leave it empty for none.

music.tooltip: The music, like a slow lo-fi beat. A clip with music comes out louder. Empty means no music.

clip_sound.tooltip: Turn on when a swap keeps the video's own sound. Each line is timed from that sound, and words from anyone else are left out so only the new person's mouth moves.

full_prompt.tooltip: Your own edit of the finished prompt, from the Full prompt tab. When it holds text, H3 gets exactly this text instead of the prompt the node writes. Empty means the node's own prompt.

AUSBOSS_NODES_H3PromptWriter.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_H3PromptWriter
AUSBOSS_NODES_H3PromptWriter.description: Type what happens, one line for each moment, and leave a blank line to cut to a new place. Connect up to four pictures, give each one a job such as person, place or outfit, and name them @1 and @2 in your lines. Connect a video to copy its moves or carry it on. Add a voice or a song and it writes the lines H3 needs. H3's own six parts go through as they are. Connect a small text model and it fills in a one-line idea.
output_tooltips: The finished prompt. Wire it into H3's prompt.
Your pictures in the order the prompt counts them. Wire it into H3's first ref_image.
The next picture. Wire it into H3's second ref_image. Empty when there is no such picture.
The next picture. Wire it into H3's third ref_image. Empty when there is no such picture.
The next picture. Wire it into H3's fourth ref_image. Empty when there is no such picture.
The video, or only its end to keep going from. Wire it into H3's first ref_video.
The video's sound, when it should reach H3. Wire it into H3's first ref_video_audio.
The voice, 15 seconds at most. Wire it into H3's first ref_audio.
The song, cut to the clip. Wire it into H3's next ref_audio. Empty when a voice is connected too.
With a voice and a song, the song to mix under the finished clip's sound. Wire it into Audio Merge.
The clip's length in frames. Wire it into H3's length.
The width of your video, or else of your first picture. Wire it into H3's width.
The height of your video, or else of your first picture. Wire it into H3's height.
On when the finished clip should keep your video's own sound: with clip_sound on, or always for change something.

image.tooltip: Choose or upload an image from ComfyUI's input folder.

rotation_degrees.tooltip: Clockwise rotation applied before crop and padding.

crop_aspect_ratio.tooltip: Locks crop handles to a ratio; free allows any rectangle.

crop_x.tooltip: Left edge of the crop in pixels, measured on the rotated image.

crop_y.tooltip: Top edge of the crop in pixels, measured on the rotated image.

pad_left.tooltip: Fill-color pixels added on the left; padding lands in the output mask.

pad_top.tooltip: Fill-color pixels added on top; padding lands in the output mask.

pad_right.tooltip: Fill-color pixels added on the right; padding lands in the output mask.

pad_bottom.tooltip: Fill-color pixels added on the bottom; padding lands in the output mask.

feather.tooltip: Feathers the mask into kept pixels; the image keeps a hard edge against the fill.

canvas_multiple.tooltip: Makes the width and height divide evenly by this number: padding grows by a few pixels, and a side with no padding is trimmed by a few instead. Some models need sizes divisible by 8, 16 or 32; 1 = off.

fill_color.tooltip: Color for rotation voids and padding; accepts #RGB/#RRGGBB hex, R, G, B (0-255 or 0..1 floats), one grayscale number, or a CSS color name. Unparseable values fall back to mid-gray.

resize_to_megapixels.tooltip: Resize the output to the megapixel budget below, aspect preserved.

megapixels.tooltip: Output pixel budget in megapixels (x 1024x1024, matching the core Scale Image to Total Pixels node).

resize_method.tooltip: Sampling filter for the resize; lanczos is the sharp default.

resolution_steps.tooltip: Rounds each resized dimension to a multiple of this - 8 or 64 keeps VAE-friendly sizes.

stitch_blend.tooltip: Ramp of the stitcher's paste, in pixels, into the kept picture: where generated pixels fade over the source. Separate from feather, which shapes the mask itself.

stitch_grow.tooltip: Moves the paste boundary before the ramp: positive lets the generation replace a strip of the source next to the seam, negative keeps more of the source.

painted_area.tooltip: What the parts you painted in the MaskEditor are handed on as (see-through parts of a PNG count too). Fill: flat fill, so the model never sees what was there. Keep picture: your picture stays under the paint and only the mask marks it. Pick keep picture when a later step needs what was there, like a denoise under 1.

AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageCropRotatePad.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageCropRotatePad
AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageCropRotatePad.description: Loads an image and applies one visual rotate, crop, and pad transform. The mask marks what to paint: new padding, the corners a turn leaves empty, and see-through parts of the picture (less than 90% solid), which are filled like the padding unless painted_area keeps the picture there. Optionally resizes the result to a megapixel budget (core Scale Image to Total Pixels semantics: aspect preserved, dimensions rounded to resolution_steps).
output_tooltips: The transformed image batch in BHWC format.
White where the model paints: padding, the corners a turn leaves empty, and see-through parts of your picture.
Full-canvas stitcher: restores kept source pixels over an outpaint result; wire to Stitch Inpaint.
Your picture before rotation, crop, padding or resize. See-through parts show as white, or as your picture when painted_area keeps it.
Output width after the transform and any resize.
Output height after the transform and any resize.

The image with see-through parts shown on white instead of the fill. Wire it to the node that writes your prompt, so a cutout gets a real backdrop. The same as image when your picture has no see-through parts, or painted_area keeps the picture.

source.tooltip: Which of ComfyUI's folders to look in: input (pictures you put there) or output (pictures you made).

folder.tooltip: The folder inside it. Empty is the input or output folder itself. Browse lists the folders there.

subfolders.tooltip: Also take the pictures in the folders inside this one.

sort.tooltip: The order of the pictures: by name, or by when the file was last changed.

pictures.tooltip: The picked pictures. Tick them on the node. Empty means every picture in the folder.

run.tooltip: All in one run: one press of Run does every picked picture. One per run: each run loads one picture and steps on, so a picture that fails only skips itself.

position.tooltip: With one per run: which of the picked pictures the next run loads, counted from 1.

after_run.tooltip: With one per run: next moves Picture on by one each time a run is queued, so queuing several runs walks the folder. Stay keeps loading the same picture. Random jumps to any of the picked ones.

at_the_end.tooltip: With one per run, after the last picture: stop the run with a message, or go back to the first and keep going.

AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageFolder.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageFolder
AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageFolder.description: Pick a folder, tick the pictures you want, and run the workflow on each of them. All in one run does every picked picture with one press of Run. One per run loads one picture each run and steps to the next by itself, so one that fails only skips itself. It gives each picture's mask, its file name for saving the result under the same name, its number and how many there are. Folders are the ones inside ComfyUI's input or output folder.
output_tooltips: Each picked picture, one at a time. What comes after runs once for each.
White where the picture is see-through. A picture with no see-through part gives the same empty mask core Load Image does.
The picture's file name without its ending. Wire it to Save Image's filename and the result keeps the name.
The picture's number among the picked ones, counted from 1.
How many pictures are picked.

image.tooltip: BHWC image batch to resize.

target_mode.tooltip: What sets the output size: width+height reads the two size widgets; longest_edge and shortest_edge scale until that edge hits edge_length; megapixels scales to a pixel budget; scale_factor multiplies the source. Each mode reads only its own widget(s).

width.tooltip: Target width for width+height mode. 0 keeps the source width, or follows height to preserve the aspect when only height is set.

height.tooltip: Target height for width+height mode. 0 keeps the source height, or follows width to preserve the aspect when only width is set.

edge_length.tooltip: Target length for the longest_edge and shortest_edge modes; the chosen edge lands exactly here and the other keeps the aspect. 0 keeps the source size.

megapixels.tooltip: Pixel budget for megapixels mode: the image scales (aspect preserved) until width x height is about this many million pixels. 0 keeps the source size.

scale_factor.tooltip: Multiplier for scale_factor mode: 0.5 halves both dimensions, 2.0 doubles them. 0 keeps the source size.

keep_proportion.tooltip: When the width+height box differs from the source aspect: stretch distorts to the exact target; fit shrinks the target box to the source aspect (output may be smaller than requested, no bars); cover_crop fills the target and center-crops the overflow; pad fits inside and fills the rest with fill_color, marking the bars in the mask output. The other target modes derive the box from the source itself, so they never crop, distort visibly, or invent pixels regardless of this setting.

fill_color.tooltip: Bar color for pad mode; accepts #RGB/#RRGGBB hex, R, G, B (0-255 or 0..1 floats), one grayscale number, or a CSS color name. Other modes ignore it.

divisible_by.tooltip: Snaps each output dimension to the nearest multiple of this (never below one step) - set 16 for WAN, 8 for most latent spaces. 1 leaves sizes exactly as computed. The snap is always resolved by a sub-half-step resize, never by inventing pixels.

interpolation.tooltip: Resampling filter: lanczos is the sharpest all-rounder, bicubic and bilinear are softer, nearest keeps hard pixels (pixel art, masks), area is best for strong downscales.

mask.tooltip: Optional BHW mask carried through the exact same resize, crop, and pad geometry as the image.

AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageResize.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageResize
AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageResize.description: Resizes an image (and an optional mask, identically) to a target width+height, longest or shortest edge, megapixel budget, or scale factor. keep_proportion decides what happens when the aspect changes: stretch, fit inside, cover and center-crop, or pad with a fill color - pad marks the new bars as 1.0 in the mask output. divisible_by snaps the result to a clean multiple (16 for WAN), and 0 in a size widget keeps the source dimension.
output_tooltips: The resized image batch in BHWC format.
The input mask through the identical transform; in pad mode the new bars are 1.0 (a ready outpaint mask). All zeros when no mask is wired.
Output width in pixels.
Output height in pixels.

image.tooltip: BHWC image batch to measure.

AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageSize.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageSize
AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageSize.description: Reads an image's dimensions as INTs: width, height, the longest and shortest edges, and the batch's image count. Wire them into resize, latent, or conditioning nodes instead of retyping numbers that drift out of date. After a run the node shows each number beside its output.
output_tooltips: Width in pixels.
Height in pixels.
The larger of width and height.
The smaller of width and height.
Number of images in the batch - the frame count for video frames.

image.tooltip: The picture to work on. A batch is worked on picture by picture.

job.tooltip: What to do with the picture. split sheet at gaps: cut a row of pictures apart at the gaps between them.

pieces.tooltip: How many pictures sit side by side on the sheet. 4 for a four-view character sheet.

AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageToolbox.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageToolbox
AUSBOSS_NODES_ImageToolbox.description: Small picture jobs in one node: pick the job from the list. split sheet at gaps cuts a row of pictures, such as a character sheet's views, into separate pictures. Each cut goes to the gap between two pictures, not to an equal share of the width, so no piece gets part of its neighbour. The pieces come out as one batch, all the same size, padded with the sheet's backdrop colour.
output_tooltips: The result. For split sheet at gaps: the pieces from left to right, one batch, all the same size.

AUSBOSS_NODES_Integer.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_Integer
AUSBOSS_NODES_Integer.description: A single INT value on its own wire. Set steps, sizes or counts in one place and feed every node that needs the same number.
output_tooltips: The integer, unchanged.

clip.tooltip: The Krea 2 text encoder.

prompt.tooltip: Describe the whole finished canvas, not just the new area — the model is generating all of it and matching the reference where it must.

negative_prompt.tooltip: Ignored at CFG 1.0, which is where turbo runs — an empty negative is the normal case there.

vae.tooltip: Needed to turn the reference images into latents. Without it the references are skipped.

reference.tooltip: The image the result follows: Load Image + Pad 🆎's padded image for AnyPaint, or its unpadded `reference` output for Registered Outpaint. Any image works; it is fitted to a multiple of 16 first.

extra_image.tooltip: A second reference, e.g. a style or character plate.

vlm_reference.tooltip: Also show the references to the vision tower, so the text encoder describes them. On for AnyPaint with the padded canvas as the reference; off for Registered Outpaint with the unpadded source, where the description tends to pull the result toward a paraphrase of the source.

mask.tooltip: The area to paint, from the node that padded the picture. Wire it for AnyPaint: the model then sees that area in your picture's own colour instead of gray, so a dark picture no longer comes back with a gray frame.

AUSBOSS_NODES_Krea2Encode.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_Krea2Encode
AUSBOSS_NODES_Krea2Encode.description: Encodes a Krea 2 prompt pair and attaches reference latents in one node. Wire a VAE and a reference image and the reference is encoded and appended to the positive conditioning; leave them unwired and this is a plain two-prompt encoder. The negative comes out of the same node so a turbo graph at CFG 1.0 still has something to plug in without a second text encode sitting there doing nothing. For an outpaint, wire the mask too, so the new area reaches the model in the picture's own colour instead of gray.
output_tooltips: Prompt conditioning with the reference latents attached.
Negative prompt conditioning.

model.tooltip: A Krea 2 model. Patch last, after any LoRAs.

stitcher.tooltip: From Load Image + Pad 🆎 or a Crop + Rotate + Pad 🆎 node — supplies the rectangle the source occupies on the canvas. A stitcher without one places the reference over the full frame.

kv_cache.tooltip: Compute the reference's keys and values once per run instead of every step. The reference does not change while sampling, so this is free speed; turn it off only to rule the cache out when debugging.

placement.tooltip: Where the reference tokens are registered. 'source rectangle' pins the unpadded source to the rectangle the stitcher reports - the Registered Outpaint LoRA's contract, one padded axis per pass. 'whole canvas' spreads the reference over the full frame - for the AnyPaint LoRA, where the reference IS the padded canvas and the sampler's noise mask keeps the known pixels, so every side can be padded at once.

AUSBOSS_NODES_Krea2OutpaintModelPatch.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_Krea2OutpaintModelPatch
AUSBOSS_NODES_Krea2OutpaintModelPatch.description: Teaches Krea 2 where a reference image belongs on the canvas. Reference latents normally arrive with no position, so the model treats them as a loose style hint; this registers them into the target grid at the rectangle the stitcher reports, which is what makes an outpaint continue the source instead of reinventing it. Place it after any LoRA loader and before the sampler.
output_tooltips: The model with reference tokens registered into the canvas grid.

image.tooltip: BHWC images or video frames to inpaint.

mask.tooltip: White areas are replaced. One mask may be broadcast across the full image batch.

model.tooltip: The LaMa model from ComfyUI/models/lama. Only known copies of big-lama.pt open; any other file stops the run.

preview.tooltip: Show this node's result on its face. Off skips writing the preview file to ComfyUI's temp folder.

AUSBOSS_NODES_LaMaInpaint.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_LaMaInpaint
AUSBOSS_NODES_LaMaInpaint.description: Removes masked content with a TorchScript LaMa model while preserving unmasked pixels. Models are read from ComfyUI/models/lama and are never downloaded by the node.
output_tooltips: Inpainted BHWC image batch with the original dimensions and unmasked pixels preserved.

background.tooltip: A picture to draw the boxes on (optional). It shows under the boxes, and its size becomes the canvas size.

bboxes.tooltip: Boxes to start from (optional): bounding boxes, prompt elements, or either as JSON text. When the wire brings new boxes they fill the canvas; changes you make on the canvas then stay until the boxes on the wire change.

width.tooltip: Canvas width in pixels: the width of the picture you make. Wire it from Latent Size to keep the two the same.

height.tooltip: Canvas height in pixels: the height of the picture you make. Wire it from Latent Size to keep the two the same.

layout.tooltip: The boxes, drawn on the node and saved here as text: where each box is (as parts of the canvas), how far it is turned, its type, its words and its colors.

AUSBOSS_NODES_LayoutBoxes.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_LayoutBoxes
AUSBOSS_NODES_LayoutBoxes.description: Draw boxes on a canvas and say what goes in each one: a thing, or words to write in the picture. Wire elements to MOSS-Image Layout Prompt. Drag on the canvas to draw a box; drag a box to move it, its corners to size it, and the round handle above it to turn it. Works in the classic look and in Nodes 2.0, and gives what ComfyUI's own Create Bounding Boxes gives, so it can take that node's place. A picture on background shows under the boxes and sets the canvas size. The mask output is white inside every box: use it to change only those places of a picture, such as the words on a sign. h3_prompt says the boxes in words for MiniMax H3 Image: describe each person as "the man from <Picture 2>, sitting on the couch".
output_tooltips: A picture of the boxes with their numbers and words, to check the layout. Wire it to Preview Image.
The boxes in pixels of the canvas (x, y, width, height), for nodes that take bounding boxes. A turned box gives the straight box around it.
The boxes as prompt elements: type, place, words and colors. Wire it to MOSS-Image Layout Prompt. A turned text box says its slant in its description.
The boxes as a mask: white inside every box, turned boxes as they are turned. Use it to change only those places of a picture, such as the words on a sign.

The boxes as a prompt for MiniMax H3 Image: where each thing goes, in words. Describe each person by their picture and what they do, such as "the man from <Picture 2>, sitting on the couch". The background is <Picture 1>.

audio.tooltip: A sound file in ComfyUI's input folder. Use Upload to add one.

start_seconds.tooltip: Where the sound starts. Drag the wave's left handle or type a Start.

end_seconds.tooltip: Where the sound stops. 0 plays to the end. The face sets a Duration instead.

max_seconds.tooltip: How long the sound is: the Duration box. 0 runs to the end of the file.

AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadAudio.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadAudio
AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadAudio.description: Loads a sound file and hands on only the part you pick. The node shows the sound as a wave, so you can see where the loud parts are. Drag the two handles to set where it starts and stops, and press play to hear just that part. Type a Duration to get a sound of an exact length, such as the length of the video you are making.
output_tooltips: The part of the sound you picked, ready for any node that takes audio.
How long that sound is, in seconds.

image.tooltip: The picture to load. Pick one from ComfyUI's input folder or upload a new one.

size.tooltip: How the picture is resized. off keeps it as it is. megapixels, longest side and scale keep its shape. fit inside shrinks or grows it to sit in a box. crop to fill covers the box and cuts off what sticks out. crop cuts a piece out without resizing. crop to ratio cuts the largest piece of a shape.

megapixels.tooltip: For megapixels: the picture's total size. 1.0 is about 1024 x 1024.

longest_side.tooltip: For longest side: the length of the longer edge, in pixels. The other edge follows.

scale.tooltip: For scale: 0.5 is half the size, 2 is double.

width.tooltip: For fit inside, crop to fill and crop: the box's width in pixels.

height.tooltip: For fit inside, crop to fill and crop: the box's height in pixels.

multiple.tooltip: Rounds the new width and height to a multiple of this. Most models want 8 or 16. 1 leaves the numbers as they are. Not used while size is off.

method.tooltip: How pixels are resampled. lanczos is the sharpest for photos; nearest keeps pixel art crisp.

enlarge.tooltip: On: a small picture is made bigger to reach the size you asked for. Off: a picture is only ever made smaller, and a small one comes out at its own size.

crop_from.tooltip: For the three crop choices: the part of the picture that is kept. top keeps the top and cuts from the bottom.

ratio.tooltip: For crop to ratio: the shape to cut, width to height. width : height uses the numbers in the width and height boxes.

AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadImage.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadImage
AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadImage.description: Loads a picture and sets its size in the same node. Pick a file, upload one, or step through the input folder with the arrows. Size can stay off, or bring the picture to a megapixel count, a longest side, a scale, a box it must fit inside, or a box it fills by cropping. It can also cut a piece or a shape out of the picture without resizing, keeping the side you choose. The node shows the picture going in and coming out, with both sizes, before you run.
output_tooltips: The picture, at its new size.
White where the picture is see-through, black where it is solid. All black for a picture with no transparency. Same size as the picture.
Width of the picture that comes out, in pixels.
Height of the picture that comes out, in pixels.
The file's name without its folder or its ending, ready for a save node's prefix.
Width of the file before any resize.
Height of the file before any resize.

image.tooltip: Choose or upload an image from ComfyUI's input folder.

pad_left.tooltip: Pixels added to the left edge (drag the canvas edge on the node).

pad_top.tooltip: Pixels added to the top edge (drag the canvas edge on the node).

pad_right.tooltip: Pixels added to the right edge (drag the canvas edge on the node).

pad_bottom.tooltip: Pixels added to the bottom edge (drag the canvas edge on the node).

mode.tooltip: color = solid fill_color; edge = each side takes the average color of the nearest image edge; edge pixel = the outermost rows and columns smear outward; pillarbox blur = the image itself, stretched to cover the canvas, blurred and dimmed behind the sharp original; mirror = the picture flipped outward at every edge, so the padding looks like more of the scene (the best margin before an edit you realign with Realign to Source).

fill_color.tooltip: Padding color for the color mode; accepts #RGB/#RRGGBB hex, R, G, B (0-255 or 0..1 floats), one grayscale number, or a CSS color name. Other modes ignore it.

backdrop_blur.tooltip: Pillarbox blur only: one knob for how strongly the backdrop is blurred and dimmed; 0 keeps it sharp and full brightness.

feather.tooltip: Ramps the mask inward across the image edge on each padded side so the sampler blends the seam; 0 keeps the seam hard.

canvas_multiple.tooltip: Rounds the final canvas to this multiple. The extra pixels join a side you padded; if you padded neither left nor right (or neither top nor bottom), none are added there: the source is scaled to fit when a megapixel target is set, otherwise trimmed by those few pixels, evenly from both edges.

target_megapixels.tooltip: 0 = off. Rescales the SOURCE so the padded canvas lands on this many megapixels (then re-rounds to canvas_multiple) — resizing before padding keeps the mask seam crisp.

source_image.tooltip: Optional. Wire an image here to pad it instead of the file chosen above; the wire wins. The canvas on the node shows the last image it padded, and the same padding applies to every image that arrives.

AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadImagePad.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadImagePad
AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadImagePad.description: Loads an image and pads it into an outpaint canvas in one node. Drag any edge of the canvas drawn on the node to set the per-side padding visually; the mask covers exactly the new padding, optionally feathered inward across the seam. The canvas rounds to a clean multiple without adding a strip to an edge you did not pad, and a megapixel target rescales the source first so the mask seam stays crisp.
output_tooltips: The padded image; the original pixels are untouched (resized only when a megapixel target is set; without one, Multiple may trim a few pixels off a pair of edges you did not pad).
White over the new padding, feathered inward per the feather widget — feed it straight to an inpainter as the outpaint mask.
Final canvas width after multiple/megapixel rounding.
Final canvas height after multiple/megapixel rounding.

Hand to Stitch Inpaint 🆎 with the sampled result to keep only the new padding and restore the original pixels bit-identically. Also carries where the source sits on the canvas, which Krea 2 Outpaint Model Patch 🆎 reads to place the reference and Realign to Source 🆎 reads to cut your picture back out of an edit made on this canvas.

The source alone, no padding, fitted to a small multiple of 16 — the reference image for Krea 2 Encode 🆎 and other reference conditioning. It is a quick resize, made on every run whether wired or not.

video.tooltip: Video in ComfyUI's input folder; use the upload button to add one.

start_seconds.tooltip: Skip everything before this time. It is the Start box under the player.

end_seconds.tooltip: Stop at this time; 0 plays to the end. The face sets a Duration instead.

custom_width.tooltip: 0 keeps the source width; set one side only to preserve aspect.

custom_height.tooltip: 0 keeps the source height; set one side only to preserve aspect.

every_nth.tooltip: Keep one frame in this many — 2 halves the frame count. The fps output divides to match, so the clip still plays at real speed downstream.

max_frames.tooltip: Stop after this many kept frames: the Duration box. 0 loads the whole window. Caps memory on long clips — the decode ends early instead of loading and discarding.

single_frame.tooltip: Load only the frame at the start time as a one-image batch. The timing card becomes a frame picker (the FRAME button toggles this), and end_seconds, every_nth, and max_frames are ignored.

AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadVideo.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadVideo
AUSBOSS_NODES_LoadVideo.description: Loads a video as a BHWC frame batch plus its audio, trimmed to an optional window set with Start, Duration and Ends at under the player, with frame count, fps, size, and duration outputs ready for downstream wiring, plus a lazy core VIDEO output for nodes that consume whole videos. every_nth thins the batch and max_frames caps it, so long clips load without filling memory. single_frame flips the loader into a frame picker that returns just the frame at the start time as a one-image batch.
output_tooltips: Trimmed BHWC frame batch.
Audio for the same trim window; silent when the video has no audio track.
Number of frames returned.
Frames per second of the returned batch: the source rate divided by every_nth.
Frame width after any custom sizing.
Frame height after any custom sizing.
Duration in seconds of the returned frames.

Core VIDEO for the same trim window at the source size; frames decode only when a consumer asks for them. None on ComfyUI cores without the comfy_api VIDEO type (present on every version this pack supports).

model.tooltip: The diffusion model the LoRA stack patches.

loras.tooltip: Serialized LoRA stack managed by the node's row editor; edit the rows, not this value.

clip.tooltip: Optional CLIP to patch; without it, CLIP strengths are ignored.

trigger_separator.tooltip: Joins the enabled rows' trigger words into the triggers output. Set from the node's gear menu; hidden on the canvas.

on_missing.tooltip: What happens when an enabled row's file cannot be found. error (the default) fails validation before sampling and names the file, so an unattended or scripted run never renders without a LoRA it asked for; skip warns once in the console and applies the rest of the stack. Set from the node's gear menu (Stop on missing LoRA); hidden on the canvas.

AUSBOSS_NODES_LoraLoader.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_LoraLoader
AUSBOSS_NODES_LoraLoader.description: Applies a stack of LoRAs to a model and CLIP from one compact node. Each row has an enable toggle, a searchable LoRA picker, drag-to-scrub model/CLIP strengths, and a center-zero strength bar behind its name; trigger words from all enabled rows are joined into one string output. The bar's ▤ button saves and applies named templates of the whole stack, and a gear-menu action absorbs every LoRA loader wired into the model chain - upstream and downstream - into this stack and bypasses the originals. Moved LoRA files resolve by name at run time; a genuinely missing one fails validation before anything is sampled and the error names the file - turn the gear menu's Stop on missing LoRA switch off to warn and skip it instead.
output_tooltips: The model with every enabled LoRA applied in row order.
The CLIP with every enabled LoRA applied in row order.
Enabled rows' trigger words, deduplicated and joined with trigger_separator (set in the gear menu). A row skipped for a missing file adds none.

image.tooltip: The picture to search.

model.tooltip: SAM 3: MODEL from a Load Checkpoint that loads the SAM 3 file.

clip.tooltip: SAM 3's text reader: CLIP from the same Load Checkpoint.

name.tooltip: What to find, in a few plain words: "the dog", "the red jacket". Several things: put a comma between them.

several.tooltip: When more than one thing matches: mask all of them, or only the biggest.

grow.tooltip: Pixels to grow the mask past the thing's edge. 0 keeps the exact outline.

soften.tooltip: Soften the mask's edge by this many pixels. 0 keeps a hard edge.

if_nothing.tooltip: When nothing matches the name. Stop the run: the workflow stops here with a message, and nothing after this node runs. Empty mask: the run goes on with a mask of nothing.

preview.tooltip: Show what was found on this node. Off skips writing the preview file to ComfyUI's temp folder.

threshold.tooltip: How sure SAM 3 must be that something matches the name. Lower it when a small thing is missed. Raise it when it picks up something that is not the thing.

fill_holes.tooltip: Fill gaps that lie fully inside the mask, like the spots SAM 3 leaves in hair or cloth. On gives a solid shape.

free_vram.tooltip: Takes SAM 3 out of the graphics card's memory right after the search. Turn it on in a workflow that loads a big model after this node; off keeps the next search a little faster.

AUSBOSS_NODES_MaskByName.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_MaskByName
AUSBOSS_NODES_MaskByName.description: Type what to find in a picture, like "the dog" or "the jacket", and get its mask. Nothing to paint. The node shows what it found, tinted on the picture. When it finds nothing it stops the run with a plain message, so nothing after it runs on an empty mask (or it can pass an empty mask on: a setting). Find runs only this node, to check the mask first. It uses ComfyUI's own SAM 3: wire model and clip from a Load Checkpoint that loads the SAM 3 file. It also returns the thing cut out on a see-through background.
output_tooltips: White where the thing is. One mask per picture.
The picture with everything but the thing see-through (RGBA).
How many things matched the name in the first picture.

image.tooltip: The picture to pick from.

model.tooltip: SAM 3: MODEL from a Load Checkpoint that loads the SAM 3 file.

clip.tooltip: SAM 3's text reader: CLIP from the same Load Checkpoint.

touches.tooltip: What you picked on the node's picture. The node writes this itself when you click or paint; Clear on the node empties it.

grow.tooltip: Grow the picked area by this many pixels. Below zero shrinks it. 0 keeps the exact outline.

soften.tooltip: Soften the mask's edge by this many pixels. 0 keeps a hard edge.

smooth.tooltip: Round off a ragged outline by this many pixels. 0 leaves the outline as found.

fill_holes.tooltip: Closes pinholes inside the picked area. Larger openings stay open, like a mug's handle. Off keeps every hole you pick.

if_nothing.tooltip: When nothing is picked. Stop the run: the workflow stops here with a message, and nothing after this node runs. Empty mask: the run goes on with a mask of nothing.

free_vram.tooltip: Takes SAM 3 out of the graphics card's memory when the workflow has run this node. Turn it on in a workflow that loads a big model after this node.

invert.tooltip: Turns the mask round: white everywhere except what you picked. With nothing picked the mask stays empty.

ask.tooltip: Used by the node's own picture for a single run. Leave it empty: it is never saved with the workflow.

fine_edges.tooltip: Hair and fur, strand by strand: where what you picked ends at the outline of the picture's main subject, that outline is taken from ComfyUI's background-removal model. The cut-out also loses the colour of the old background. Off keeps the edge as found. The ? page says where to get the model file.

new_picture.tooltip: When a different picture comes in. Keep picks uses your clicks and paint on it, in the same places (scaled if the size changed). Start over drops them, and the run stops until you pick again.

AUSBOSS_NODES_MaskByTouch.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_MaskByTouch
AUSBOSS_NODES_MaskByTouch.description: Click a thing on the picture, or paint over it, and get its mask. No name to type and no MaskEditor. Moving over the picture lights up what a click would take. A painted stroke takes the thing under it, or exactly the paint. What is lit is what the mask will be. When nothing is picked it stops the run with a plain message, so nothing after it runs on an empty mask (or it can pass an empty mask on: a setting). It uses ComfyUI's own SAM 3: wire model and clip from a Load Checkpoint that loads the SAM 3 file. It also returns the picked area cut out on a see-through background, and the names of what you picked as text.
output_tooltips: White where the picked area is. One mask per picture.
The picture with everything but the picked area see-through (RGBA).
The names of the things you picked, in the order you picked them, like: jacket, hat. Empty when nothing you picked has a name.

expression.tooltip: Arithmetic over a, b and c: numbers, + - * / // % **, parentheses, and min/max/abs/round/floor/ceil/sqrt.

a.tooltip: The value of a in the expression - wire a FLOAT or an INT; unwired reads as 0.

b.tooltip: The value of b in the expression - wire a FLOAT or an INT; unwired reads as 0.

c.tooltip: The value of c in the expression - wire a FLOAT or an INT; unwired reads as 0.

AUSBOSS_NODES_MathExpression.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_MathExpression
AUSBOSS_NODES_MathExpression.description: Evaluates one arithmetic expression over the inputs a, b and c and returns it as both FLOAT and INT — width and height math, strength ramps, frame counts. Allowed: numbers, a/b/c, + - * / // % ** and parentheses, and min, max, abs, round, floor, ceil, sqrt. The expression is parsed, never eval()'d, so a shared workflow cannot smuggle code through this node.
output_tooltips: The result as a float.
The result rounded to the nearest whole number (halves round away from zero).

a.tooltip: The first batch; its frames come first in the result.

b.tooltip: The second batch, appended after a's frames.

on_mismatch.tooltip: When the sizes differ: resize b's frames to a's size, resize a's to b's, or stop with an error.

AUSBOSS_NODES_MergeBatches.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_MergeBatches
AUSBOSS_NODES_MergeBatches.description: Joins two IMAGE batches into one, a's frames first — reassemble a split batch, or append a comparison strip to a run. When the two resolutions differ, on_mismatch picks which side is resized (bilinear) or refuses with both sizes named; channel counts must already match.
output_tooltips: One batch: a's frames followed by b's.

text.tooltip: Your prompt. Put choices in curly brackets, split by |, such as {tank top|sweater|shirt}. One is picked from each set.

seed.tooltip: Wire in the seed your sampler uses. A new seed picks new choices; the same seed picks the same ones again.

AUSBOSS_NODES_PromptVariations.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_PromptVariations
AUSBOSS_NODES_PromptVariations.description: A prompt box that changes on every run. Write choices in curly brackets, such as a {red|blue|green} {sweater|jacket}, and the node picks one from each set. The seed decides the picks: the same seed gives the same prompt again, and a new seed on each run gives a new mix. Text without brackets comes out exactly as typed.
output_tooltips: The prompt with one choice picked from each set.

source.tooltip: The original picture you edited, at the size the edit model saw it. The result comes out at this size.

fit.tooltip: zoom + shift fixes the usual Qwen drift. affine also fixes a slight tilt.

empty_fill.tooltip: If the edit slid past the edge, a thin strip ends up with nothing in it. edge stretches the nearest pixels into it, source fills it from the original, gray fills it flat gray for inpainting.

max_zoom.tooltip: The biggest zoom it will undo, in percent. Anything bigger is treated as a change you meant and left alone.

stitcher.tooltip: Optional. Plug in the stitcher from Load Image + Pad 🆎 if you padded the picture before editing. You get your picture back without the padding, with no empty edges.

AUSBOSS_NODES_RealignToSource.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_RealignToSource
AUSBOSS_NODES_RealignToSource.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Lines an edited picture back up with the original. Qwen Image 2.1 often draws an edit slightly zoomed in or shifted, especially style changes like watercolor or anime, so the edit no longer sits on top of the original. This node measures how far it moved and moves it back. Best result: pad the picture with Load Image + Pad before editing and plug its stitcher in here, so the edit has room to move and you get real picture all the way to the edges.
output_tooltips: The edit, lined up with the original and at its size.
White where the lined-up edit has nothing (a strip that slid off the edge). All black when there is none.
How far the edit had moved and what was done. Plug it into Show Text 🆎 to read it.

mask.tooltip: BHW mask; white is the selected area.

expand.tooltip: Pixels to grow (+) or shrink (-) the mask.

blur.tooltip: Gaussian feather strength in pixels; 0 keeps hard edges.

fill_holes.tooltip: Fill fully enclosed gaps inside the mask before feathering.

smooth.tooltip: Melts staircase jaggies by this many pixels while keeping a hard edge; 0 is off. Runs before the feather blur.

black_point.tooltip: Mask values at or below this become fully black; clears faint gray haze outside the subject. Applied last.

white_point.tooltip: Mask values at or above this become fully white; solidifies the mask core. Applied last.

edge_refine.tooltip: Snap the mask edge to the guide_image. 'guided filter' is fast edge-aware filtering (needs opencv-contrib-python); 'matting' solves closed-form alpha matting around the edge (needs pymatting). Both require the guide_image input.

preview.tooltip: Show this node's result on its face. Off skips writing the preview file to ComfyUI's temp folder.

guide_image.tooltip: RGB frames the mask belongs to; required when edge_refine is 'guided filter' or 'matting'.

max_hole_size.tooltip: The biggest hole fill holes fills, in percent of the picture. 2 fills the gaps a quick brush leaves but keeps a person or pet you left unpainted; 0 fills every hole.

AUSBOSS_NODES_RefineMask.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_RefineMask
AUSBOSS_NODES_RefineMask.description: Cleans up a mask in one fixed-order pass: expand (grow/shrink by whole pixels), fill enclosed holes (all, or only those up to max_hole_size), smooth (melts staircase jaggies without feathering), feather with a gaussian blur, edge-refine against the optional guide_image (guided filter or alpha matting), then remap levels with black_point/white_point to clear gray haze. Returns the refined mask and its inverse.
output_tooltips: The refined BHW mask.
The refined mask inverted, for operations that target the background.

width.tooltip: Output width in pixels. Set from the panel; typed values are never re-snapped.

height.tooltip: Output height in pixels. Set from the panel; typed values are never re-snapped.

latent.tooltip: Latent family for the LATENT output. 16ch: SD3, Flux 1, Krea 2, Qwen Image, Z-Image. 4ch: SD 1.5 and SDXL. 128ch: Flux 2 (Klein). Set from the panel's gear.

batch_size.tooltip: How many latents to make. Set from the panel's gear.

workflow_sizes.tooltip: Workflow resolutions set in the gear menu. Strict mode checks wired dimensions too.

AUSBOSS_NODES_Resolution.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_Resolution
AUSBOSS_NODES_Resolution.description: Canvas size picker: ratio chips pick the shape, a live stage lets you drag the rectangle's edges and corner, and a size ladder offers on-grid rungs for the current ratio — snapped to VAE-friendly multiples with a ratio lock that stays exact AND on-grid. Outputs the width and height as INTs plus an empty LATENT of that size, so it feeds the sampler directly; the latent family (16ch for SD3 / Flux / Krea 2 / Qwen / Z-Image, 4ch for SD1.5 / SDXL, 128ch for Flux 2 Klein) and the batch size live behind the panel's gear.
output_tooltips: The picked width in pixels.
The picked height in pixels.
An empty latent of this size in the chosen family — wire it straight into the sampler in place of an Empty*LatentImage node.

AUSBOSS_NODES_RunTimer.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_RunTimer
AUSBOSS_NODES_RunTimer.description: A stopwatch for the whole run. It starts when a queued prompt begins executing, ticks on the node while it runs, and holds the total when it finishes. Right-click it for the few runs before, so a settings change can be judged against the last one. The times are saved with the workflow, so a shared graph carries its author's run time as a reference. No inputs, no outputs; it listens to the queue rather than sitting on a wire.

images.tooltip: BHWC batch; every frame in it is saved.

filename_prefix.tooltip: The local filename, with optional subfolders: the name tags (date, time, size, counter, batch) are appended to it. Ignored while filename is linked or exact_name is set.

format.tooltip: png saves everywhere and preserves alpha. webp lossless is usually smaller than png, alpha kept. jxl lossless is the most compact; it needs the optional pillow-jxl-plugin in ComfyUI's python and few browsers preview it.

save_metadata.tooltip: On embeds the prompt and workflow (PNG text chunks; EXIF in webp and jxl), so the file drags back into ComfyUI. Off writes a clean file with no workflow inside - for sharing or datasets.

exact_name.tooltip: Save under exactly this filename - no tags. An image extension on the value is replaced by the chosen format's own. Subfolders are allowed; a batch appends _001, _002... Empty composes the name from filename_prefix instead. A linked filename input takes precedence.

on_existing.tooltip: What a save that lands on an existing file does: overwrite replaces it, skip leaves it, error stops the run. Only reachable with the counter off, an exact name, or a linked filename - the counter never collides.

output_dir.tooltip: Subfolder of ComfyUI's output folder to save into, such as sets/portraits; created if missing. Empty saves to the output folder itself. Save Image never writes outside the output folder.

caption.tooltip: When not empty, writes this text as a UTF-8 .txt sidecar with the same basename as each saved image. The caption_text input takes precedence.

filename.tooltip: Exact filename from upstream (a Load Image name, a caption tool's id). Its image extension is replaced by the chosen format's; no tags are added; a batch appends _001, _002... A linked but empty value stops the run rather than saving under a made-up name.

caption_text.tooltip: Caption from upstream: saved as a .txt in the same folder with the same name as the image (portrait.png -> portrait.txt). Empty writes no sidecar.

name_counter.tooltip: Append the next free five-digit number. On is collision-safe; off reuses the same path and replaces an existing file.

name_date.tooltip: Append the local save date as YYYY-MM-DD.

name_time.tooltip: Append the local save time as HH-mm-ss.

name_size.tooltip: Append the image dimensions as WIDTHxHEIGHT, such as 1024x1024.

name_batch.tooltip: For an image batch, append b001, b002... so each image's position in this run is visible. A single image is unchanged.

preview.tooltip: Show the saved image on the node. Display only: the file is saved either way, and still listed in the queue.

step_preview.tooltip: Show the picture here while it is being made, one step at a time, with a Stop button. Display only: what is saved does not change. A run with this on asks ComfyUI for the step pictures, unless you chose a preview method in ComfyUI's settings.

autosave.tooltip: On: every run saves its pictures. Off: the pictures only show on the node, and its Save button keeps the ones you want.

AUSBOSS_NODES_SaveImage.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_SaveImage
AUSBOSS_NODES_SaveImage.description: Saves an IMAGE batch as PNG, lossless WebP or lossless JPEG XL, with the workflow embedded or deliberately left out. The name is either composed here - a prefix plus the tags you switch on (date, time, size, a collision-safe counter, a batch number) - or supplied exactly by the filename input, so an edit or caption pass keeps the source file's name. A non-empty caption writes a .txt sidecar with the same basename, the dataset-captioning pair.
output_tooltips: Absolute path of the first file this run saved (empty when every file was skipped), for downstream nodes that want the file itself.
The input batch, unchanged - save first, keep wiring.

fps.tooltip: Playback frame rate; wire Load Video's fps output to match the source. A connected video input brings its own rate and overrides this widget. Fractional rates like 23.976 and 29.97 can be typed in.

filename_prefix.tooltip: Saved under the output folder; subfolders are created automatically.

crf.tooltip: Encode quality: lower is better and larger. 19 is visually lossless for h264; h265 and vp9 read the same scale (vp9 tolerates a few points higher).

frames.tooltip: BHWC frame batch to encode. Not needed when a video is connected.

audio.tooltip: Optional track muxed into the file, e.g. Load Video's audio output.

video.tooltip: Optional core VIDEO. When connected, its frames and audio supersede the frames and audio inputs, and its own frame rate wins over the fps widget; a differing widget rate is logged once to the console. ComfyUI core decodes the whole file into memory before this node sees a frame: that phase reports no progress and does not stop on Cancel, which takes effect once the encode starts. Wiring frames instead keeps the whole run interruptible.

format.tooltip: Container and codec. mp4 h264 plays everywhere; mp4 h265 halves the size at the same quality where supported; the nvenc pair encodes on an NVIDIA GPU instead of the CPU (much faster, slightly larger); webm vp9 and webm av1 suit the web and mux Opus; mov prores is a ProRes HQ editing master; mkv ffv1 is bit-exact lossless and very large. gif and webp are silent, loop forever, and hold every frame in memory - keep those to short clips.

pingpong.tooltip: Play the clip forward then backward so it loops seamlessly. Roughly doubles the frame count and the encode time; the first and last frames are not repeated at the turnaround.

save_metadata.tooltip: Embed the prompt and workflow in the file, so an mp4 dragged back onto the canvas restores its graph. Turn off to share a file without your prompts and node graph inside it. gif and webp never carry metadata.

step_preview.tooltip: Show the clip here while it is being made: after each step, a few of its frames play in a loop, with a Stop button. Display only: what is saved does not change. A run with this on asks ComfyUI for the step pictures, unless you chose a preview method in ComfyUI's settings.

AUSBOSS_NODES_SaveVideo.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_SaveVideo
AUSBOSS_NODES_SaveVideo.description: Saves a frame batch as mp4 (h264/h265, CPU or NVENC), webm (vp9/av1), ProRes mov, lossless ffv1 mkv, gif or webp - with optional muxed audio and the workflow embedded, so the file drags back into ComfyUI. pingpong bounces the clip for a seamless loop. Wire fps straight from Load Video 🆎 to keep the source timing, or connect a core VIDEO to encode that whole video instead.
output_tooltips: Absolute path of the file this run saved, for downstream nodes that want the file itself.

seed.tooltip: The seed sent down the wire. The control beneath it decides what happens after each queue: fixed keeps it, randomize picks a new one.

AUSBOSS_NODES_Seed.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_Seed
AUSBOSS_NODES_Seed.description: A seed on its own INT wire, so several samplers share one number and a shared workflow can pin the exact seed that made its example. Random, Fixed and Step work like a sampler's control after generate. Because Random replaces the value the moment a run is queued, the node reports the seed it actually ran with: the line under the box shows it, Use last run puts it back in the box and pins it, and the history menu keeps the last few so a good result is never lost to the next click.
output_tooltips: The seed, unchanged — wire it to every sampler that should share it.

images.tooltip: The BHWC IMAGE batch to thin out.

nth.tooltip: Keep one frame in every nth: 2 keeps every other frame.

offset.tooltip: Frames to skip before the first kept frame.

fps.tooltip: Optional: the batch's frame rate, such as Load Video's fps. The fps output divides it by nth.

AUSBOSS_NODES_SelectEveryNth.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_SelectEveryNth
AUSBOSS_NODES_SelectEveryNth.description: Keeps every nth frame of an IMAGE batch — halve a video's frame count before an expensive stage, or thin a sweep down to samples. offset skips that many frames before the first kept one, so nth 2 / offset 0 keeps frames 1, 3, 5 and offset 1 keeps 2, 4, 6. Wire the batch's fps in and the fps output divides it by nth, so the thinned clip keeps its duration.
output_tooltips: The kept frames, in their original order.
The wired fps divided by nth, so the kept frames still span the same time; 0 when no fps is wired.

frames.tooltip: Video frames or any other BHWC IMAGE batch.

frame_number.tooltip: One-based frame number: 1 selects the first frame. Negative counts from the end: -1 is the last frame, -2 the one before it. 0 is invalid.

preview.tooltip: Show the selected frame on the node. Off skips writing the preview file to ComfyUI's temp folder.

AUSBOSS_NODES_SelectFrame.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_SelectFrame
AUSBOSS_NODES_SelectFrame.description: Selects one frame from an IMAGE batch with a one-based frame number. Negative numbers count from the end: -1 is the last frame, -2 the one before it; 0 is invalid. The selected frame is returned unchanged as a one-image batch.
output_tooltips: The selected frame as a one-image BHWC batch.

text.tooltip: What to show. Text, a number, or any other wire.

AUSBOSS_NODES_ShowText.name: AUSBOSS_NODES_ShowText
AUSBOSS_NODES_ShowText.description: Shows what arrives on a wire, on the node itself: a prompt, an LLM reply, a file name, a number. Text passes through unchanged, so the node can sit in the middle of a wire. A number or any other value comes out as the text that is shown. The text can be selected and copied.
output_tooltips: The text that is shown. Text that came in passes through unchanged.
