mode.tooltip: attention logits (recommended): modifies attention logits (log(gain) * attention_strength) and scales V for gain < 1.0, bypassing DiT RMSNorm for strong control. embedding magnitude: scales raw input embeddings before DiT (often absorbed by RMSNorm).

inspect_only.tooltip: On: populate the token panel and stop before sampling (no GPU render). Switch off and queue again to generate.

weights_json.tooltip: JSON weight map managed by the token panel. Automatically resets if the upstream prompt changes.

original_prompt.tooltip: Exact clean prompt sent to the upstream text encoder. Used with CLIP to map token positions without re-encoding.

weighted_phrases.tooltip: Synced with the panel. Supports (phrase:weight) from -2.0 to 3.0 (>1 boost, 0.05..0.99 suppress logits+V, 0 zero V, <0 invert V) and [a|b:bias] blending. Does not re-run Qwen3-VL unless [a|b] blending is used.

attention_strength.tooltip: Global sensitivity multiplier on attention logit biases (attention_strength * log(gain)). Does not affect tokens at 1.0.

report_format.tooltip: report output format: json (raw indices), compact (changes only, ideal for video overlay labels), or annotated prompt (full text with (word:weight)).

start_percent.tooltip: Start of the sampling range where token attention weights apply (0.0 = first step). Keep 0.0..1.0 for full generation.

end_percent.tooltip: End of the sampling range where token attention weights apply (1.0 = last step).

BFSH3TokenWeightEditor.name: BFSH3TokenWeightEditor
BFSH3TokenWeightEditor.display_name: BFS H3 Token / Word Weight Editor (Experimental)
BFSH3TokenWeightEditor.description: Post-encoder per-token/phrase weight editor for MiniMax H3 (T2V, I2V/FL2VA, Ref2V, Image, and TARA). Works without re-running Qwen3-VL: upstream encodes the clean prompt once, and this node maps token positions via CPU tokenizer and applies weights in DiT attention (or Flash Partitions with TARA). Weights (-2.0..3.0): >1.0 boosts attention logits; 0.05..0.99 lowers logits and scales V; 0.0 zeros V (neutralizes); <0.0 inverts V (pushes away). Panel tips: click a token, Ctrl/Cmd-click to multi-select, double-click to select all occurrences of a word. Visual tokens are never modified.

guide_video.tooltip: Source video (scene/body/motion kept). Output size = this.

head_image.tooltip: Reference head/face image (identity). Crop to head only.

length.tooltip: Frame count (snapped to 4k+1). Trained at 73.

amplify_reference.tooltip: ON: head reference goes on positive only, so the sampler's CFG amplifies the identity (guide stays on both as a stable canvas). Use CFG ~3-5, no LightX2V (CFG 1.0 = no amplification). OFF: reference on both (legacy, weaker).

guider.tooltip: Provides CFG/STG settings; its conds are replaced per chunk.

guide_video.tooltip: Source clip: body, motion, camera, scene. Output geometry follows it.

identity_image.tooltip: Reference image for the LoRA that wants one — a head crop for a head swap, a subject for identity transfer. Leave it unconnected for any IC-LoRA that works from the guide alone (an instruction edit, a sharpener, a restyler): the slot is simply not packed and the guide is the only reference.

latent.tooltip: Empty latent from EmptyLTXVLatentVideo, sized to the CROP when cropping is on. Strongly recommended: LTX-2.5 latents are AV (video+audio) and this node cannot fabricate that structure -- without it a plain video latent is built and the model may ignore the guide entirely.

subject_mask.tooltip: Per-frame mask of the region to edit (head, with margin). Drives the crop box and, with inpaint_with_mask on, restricts denoising to it. Leave unconnected for a plain swap.

crop_mode.tooltip: Sample inside a box around the subject instead of the whole frame -- the fix for faces that are too small to carry identity. combined: one static box for the clip. tracked: a constant-size box that stays still until the subject would leave it. zoomed: the box follows the subject's size too, planned over the whole clip.

crop_scale.tooltip: Box size as a multiple of the subject. 1.5 leaves a third as margin. Keep neck and shoulders in: a face-tight crop is a framing the LoRA never saw in training.

uncrop_feather.tooltip: Blend width when pasting the crop back, in pixels. Sides sitting on the image edge are never feathered -- there is nothing outside to blend into.

paste_back.tooltip: Composite the crop into the original frames before returning. Turn OFF for a second pass: images/latent then stay in the crop's own space, so you can upscale and refine the crop -- where the face actually has pixels -- and composite at the end with the Head Swap Paste Back node, feeding it the crop_bboxes output.

paste_confine_to_mask.tooltip: Composite only inside the mask, so anything the model changed outside it never reaches the frame. With a crop this confines the paste to the mask instead of the whole box; WITHOUT a crop it is what keeps the untouched pixels the source's own — otherwise the whole frame is the VAE's round trip of it, softer everywhere the edit never went. Off pastes the full frame or box.

inpaint_with_mask.tooltip: Send the mask to the sampler as a denoise mask, so only the masked region changes and everything else stays the guide's own pixels. Native ComfyUI inpainting -- the LoRA never sees the mask and the original face stays visible to the model.

mask_grow.tooltip: Dilate the mask before use, in pixels. The new head can be bigger than the old one.

mask_blur.tooltip: Soften the mask edge, in pixels, to avoid a hard seam.

mask_hard_for_inpaint.tooltip: Binarise the mask before it becomes the denoise mask. Blur belongs to the paste-back, where a soft edge hides the seam; in the DENOISE mask a soft edge means partial denoising, which blends the original latent -- and the original identity -- back in exactly at the edge of the head. Off passes the soft mask through to the sampler as well.

latent_mask_dilate.tooltip: Grow the mask by whole LATENT cells after the reduction. One cell is 32 px, so this is much coarser than mask_grow -- and it is what guarantees the head sits inside editable blocks instead of clipping at a cell boundary. Check the latent_mask output to see the effect.

latent_mask_dilate_frames.tooltip: Same, along time: grow by whole latent frames (one covers 8 video frames).

mask_strength.tooltip: How completely the masked region is replaced. 1.0 = fully regenerated. Below that the original latent is blended back, which keeps the original geometry and expression in pixels -- and drags the original identity back with them, so the result becomes an average of both faces. Expression does NOT need this: it reaches the model through the aligned guide, which carries the whole source performance regardless of the mask.

decode.tooltip: How to turn the sampled latent into frames. full: one shot, fine at the size the sampler ran at. tiled: for a big latent (a second pass after a 2x upscaler), where a full decode thrashes VRAM and looks like a hang. none: skip decoding and return the latent only -- use your own VAE Decode (Tiled) downstream. With none there is nothing to paste back, so images comes out empty.

decode_temporal_size.tooltip: Frames decoded at once in tiled mode.

temporal_tile_size.tooltip: Frames per chunk. 0 samples the whole clip in one pass. Use the length the LoRA trained at (73 for the LTX head-swap recipe) for clips longer than that.

auto_config.tooltip: Measure the subject in the mask and set crop mode, crop scale, mask grow and blur, paste feather and latent dilation from its size -- ignoring those widgets. Needs subject_mask. Every amount below is in pixels, which only means something relative to how big the head is in frame: the same 8 px is generous on a distant head and invisible on a close one, and that mismatch is what leaves a seam. The debug output prints what it chose.

identity_headroom.tooltip: auto_config only. How much bigger the reference head may be than the head in the guide. The mask is the OLD head, so a wider face or more hair lands outside it and gets clipped -- the seam. The reference's PROPORTIONS are measured from identity_image against the mask; its absolute size cannot be, because a cropped head carries no scale. Raise it for big hair or a visibly larger head; 1.0 assumes the two heads match.

BFSHeadSwapMaskedSampler.name: BFSHeadSwapMaskedSampler
BFSHeadSwapMaskedSampler.description: Sampler for guide-driven IC-LoRAs, with an optional stable crop around the subject, native mask inpainting and temporal chunking. Connect only what you need: a guide alone runs the LoRA over the whole clip; add an identity image for a LoRA that takes one; add a mask to restrict the edit; add a crop mode to sample the subject full-frame when it is too small to carry detail. auto_config measures the subject in the mask and derives every pixel amount from its size.
output_tooltips: Final frames, with the crop pasted back when cropping is on.
The mask painted over the ORIGINAL frames, plus the crop box outline. The quickest way to see whether the mask is where you think it is, at the scale you think it is, on the frames it belongs to.
Exactly what the model was fed as the guide: cropped and resized. If this does not look like the region you meant to edit, nothing downstream will.
The mask after grow/blur (and cropping), in the crop's pixel space.

The mask as the sampler actually sees it: reduced to the latent grid with max and upsampled back for viewing. One frame per latent frame -- this is the real resolution of the edit, and where a too-thin mask disappears.
Sampled latent. With cropping on this is the CROP's latent, which is what you want to upscale and refine in a second pass.
The crop boxes, one per frame. Feed to Head Swap Paste Back after a second pass.
What the node decided: crop mode and box, mask ops, tiling.

crop_bboxes.tooltip: Connect the sampler's crop_bboxes output -- one box per frame. This is a socket, not something to fill in: typing a single box by hand would paste every frame into the same fixed rectangle.

confine_mask.tooltip: Confines the paste to the mask instead of the whole box, in the crop's space.

BFSHeadSwapPasteBack.name: BFSHeadSwapPasteBack
BFSHeadSwapPasteBack.description: Composites processed crops back into the original frames, with edge-aware feathering and optional mask confinement. The other half of the sampler's paste_back: off, for refining a crop before it goes home.

guide_video.tooltip: The guide frames the track was made on (same frames as the Planner's guide).

masks.tooltip: The person to replace: one mask per guide frame, or one per keyframe (Segment Picker batch_masks on the Planner's source_frames).

keyframe_spec.tooltip: BFS Keyframe Planner keyframe_spec: which frames are keyframes.

mark_color.tooltip: Tint of the person in marked_frames (hex).

mark_opacity.tooltip: How strongly the person is tinted (0.3 = the Colored Mark default).

grow_pixels.tooltip: Grow (positive) or shrink (negative) each mask before tinting, e.g. to cover hair.

threshold.tooltip: Mask values above this count as the person.

BFSKeyframeMarks.name: BFSKeyframeMarks
BFSKeyframeMarks.description: BFS Keyframe Marks: the tracked person's mask at every keyframe, and the keyframe frames marked for an image edit.
output_tooltips: The keyframe frames with the person tinted, one per keyframe (in keyframe_spec order).
The person's mask at each keyframe.
The untouched keyframe frames.
JSON: per keyframe its frame, time, mask area and whether the mask is empty.

guide_video.tooltip: The guide frames (e.g. BFS H3 Prepare Native Video).

plan.tooltip: Set by the panel: keyframe frames, edited frames and pictures.

picture_1.tooltip: Reference picture 1; overrides the one dropped in the panel.

picture_2.tooltip: Reference picture 2; overrides the one dropped in the panel.

picture_3.tooltip: Reference picture 3; overrides the one dropped in the panel.

picture_4.tooltip: Reference picture 4; overrides the one dropped in the panel.

BFSKeyframePlanner.name: BFSKeyframePlanner
BFSKeyframePlanner.description: BFS Keyframe Planner: pick keyframe times on the guide video, drop in edited frames and reference pictures.
output_tooltips: The guide, unchanged.
The original guide frames at the keyframe times (one per keyframe), e.g. to edit them.
The edited frame of every keyframe, at the guide size; a keyframe without one gives its source frame.
JSON: frames, times (s), fps and which keyframes have an edited frame.
Reference picture 1 (None when not set).
Reference picture 2 (None when not set).
Reference picture 3 (None when not set).
Reference picture 4 (None when not set).

label.tooltip: Only a name, to tell slots apart in the loop's list.

rules.tooltip: JSON list of rules. The panel writes this for you.

BFSLoraSurgery.name: BFSLoraSurgery
BFSLoraSurgery.description: Scale or drop a LoRA's module groups (attention, MLP, per block range) and apply it live. Finds which layers carry a defect without retraining.

rules.tooltip: Same JSON the surgery panel writes.

filename.tooltip: Leave empty to name it after the rules.

BFSLoraSurgerySave.name: BFSLoraSurgerySave
BFSLoraSurgerySave.description: Apply the same surgery rules and write the result to models/loras.

image.tooltip: Single image or video frames already resampled to 24 fps.

audio.tooltip: Optional aligned guide soundtrack; never routed to the text encoder.

lora_name.tooltip: Validate metadata only. Load the same LoRA using your normal LoRA loader.

BFSMiniMaxH3DownscaledGuide.name: BFSMiniMaxH3DownscaledGuide
BFSMiniMaxH3DownscaledGuide.description: Aligned lower-resolution VAE guides for H3 LoRAs trained with target_grid_stride_v1. Connect both returned MODEL and CONDITIONING to the sampler.

frames.tooltip: 1 for a true still image, or exactly 17*n+5 video frames.

BFSMiniMaxH3IdentityReference.name: BFSMiniMaxH3IdentityReference
BFSMiniMaxH3IdentityReference.description: Caption-only image identity reference. Match source_id to the training control channel. Requires an upscale checkpoint trained with the same reference role and RoPE options.

motion_video_index.tooltip: Native <Video N> supplying motion. Picture numbering is independent.

attention_backend.tooltip: Flash partitions is the default. An official Model Attention Backend Kitchen selection is detected automatically. Kitchen uses an optional one-pass temporal extension when installed, otherwise frame-wise compatibility. Flex is the original implementation.

structure_guidance.tooltip: Experimental structure CFG (SolarRenderer): output + (w-1)*(output - output without <Video N>). 1 = off; ~1.5 follows the motion video more. Costs one extra model pass per step where active.

structure_sigma_min.tooltip: Structure guidance only at noise levels >= this (structure is laid down at high noise); lower-noise steps skip the extra pass.

BFSMiniMaxH3NativeTemporal.name: BFSMiniMaxH3NativeTemporal
BFSMiniMaxH3NativeTemporal.display_name: BFS MiniMax H3 TARA - Native Temporal Alignment (Experimental)
BFSMiniMaxH3NativeTemporal.description: Experimental native_temporal_v1 inference for the matching motion-transfer LoRA. Keep the motion video in MiniMax H3 Reference to Video positive conditioning; route this MODEL to the guider. No Add Guide or VSA. Guide/output must share a 24fps temporal grid. Does not encode video or load the LoRA. Defaults match training.

reference_strength.tooltip: Multiplier of unnormalized attention weights to this Picture inside the mask. 1 = neutral. Not a quality percentage.

other_reference_strength.tooltip: Multiplier for other Pictures inside the same mask. Keep 1 initially; try 0.75 to reduce identity mixing. Includes environment/continuity pictures too.

target_mask.tooltip: One static mask or one mask per prepared shot frame at 24fps. White = affected. Must track the target subject; this node performs no tracking.

BFSMiniMaxH3ReferenceBinding.name: BFSMiniMaxH3ReferenceBinding
BFSMiniMaxH3ReferenceBinding.description: Experimental reference-attention control. Connect AFTER TARA and send this MODEL to the guider. Uses exact Flash Partitions instead of Kitchen/Sol kernels while active. No mask = global target influence. Masks refer to output/guide positions, not the reference image. Does not change prompt bindings or guarantee identity.

length.tooltip: Frame count at 24 fps, (124 = ~5s, trained range is ~124-362)

ref_image_size.tooltip: Reference image sizing. 'match' scales each ref (down only, keeping aspect) to the generation's pixel area; 'max' uses the reference pipeline's 2048px short edge for best identity fidelity. Reference tokens ride through every sampling step, so 'max' can be several times slower.

clip_video_fps.tooltip: Guide 0 sampling rate for Qwen only. Default/native presentation is 2 fps; try 4 or 8 fps. Higher values increase context and encoding cost, not output fps. Never duplicates frames above the source rate. Actual reference videos stay native 2 fps.

guide_video_0.tooltip: The motion guide / current shot, as native 24-fps frames. Qwen sees it at clip_video_fps as <Video 1>; no native guide video reference latents are added. Connect the same frames to Add Guide for motion. Other ref_videos start at <Video 2>.

vae.tooltip: Video VAE. Without it reference images/videos only condition the text encoder.

audio_vae.tooltip: Audio VAE. Without it reference audio only conditions the text encoder.

ref_image.tooltip: Reference image, in <Picture N> order

ref_videos.tooltip: Actual native video references, separate from guide_video_0. With a guide connected, these are <Video 2>, <Video 3>, etc. They enter both CLIP and native reference latents, as in the original node. Up to 3 reference videos.

ref_video.tooltip: Actual native video references, separate from guide_video_0. With a guide connected, these are <Video 2>, <Video 3>, etc. They enter both CLIP and native reference latents, as in the original node. Up to 3 reference videos.

ref_video_audio.tooltip: Soundtrack of the same-numbered reference video

BFSMiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideoGuideContext.name: BFSMiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideoGuideContext
BFSMiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideoGuideContext.display_name: MiniMax H3 Reference to Video — Guide 0 CLIP Context (BFS)
BFSMiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideoGuideContext.description: guide_video_0 enters Qwen/CLIP only as <Video 1>, without native guide video reference latents. Pictures and other reference videos retain native semantics. Use Add Guide separately for aligned motion. The target latent starts empty.

rules.tooltip: JSON: [{"pattern":"*final_layer*video_out.weight","scale":0.9}]. Glob or regex:true. Optional rows:[start,exclusive_stop].

BFSModelSurgery.name: BFSModelSurgery
BFSModelSurgery.description: Inspect and scale arbitrary model weights or row ranges. Rules run in order and overlapping scales multiply. Uses native reversible patches without copying the model. Run once to populate the layer panel. Does not scale CLIP or VAE.

fit_mode.tooltip: crop: zoom+center-crop to fill each panel completely (matches training data, may cut off edges). fit: scale each reference down to fit entirely inside its panel with no cropping (preserves every pixel, aspect ratio never distorted -- one uniform scale factor for both axes -- leftover space padded with background). cover: row-justified like fit, but fills the WHOLE 1536x1024 canvas on both axes (no background bars) by cropping the minimum shared amount needed.

BFSMultiRefSheetBuilder.name: BFSMultiRefSheetBuilder
BFSMultiRefSheetBuilder.description: Combines 1-5 plugged-in reference images into the fixed 1536x1024 composite sheet the multi-ref LoRA was trained on. Leave slots empty for fewer refs; an empty slot is simply skipped, not padded with blank content.

megapixels.tooltip: Editable target area in megapixels. 4 is only the default; width and height follow the original aspect ratio.

scale_method.tooltip: Editable interpolation method used by native Resize Image/Mask.

BFSOptionalReferenceImage.name: BFSOptionalReferenceImage
BFSOptionalReferenceImage.description: Load a character reference and resize it proportionally using the native Resize Image/Mask implementation. An unused [none] slot returns no image and skips resizing.

sam3_model.tooltip: SAM 3.1: MODEL of a Load Checkpoint node with sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors.

sam3_clip.tooltip: SAM 3.1: CLIP of the same Load Checkpoint node; turns the concepts and Find texts into SAM prompts.

concepts.tooltip: What the automatic pass looks for, comma separated (one SAM 3 text prompt each), e.g. person, animal, car, chair. Empty = no automatic pass, only what you add.

threshold.tooltip: SAM 3 detection score threshold: lower finds more (and more false hits).

max_per_concept.tooltip: Most objects one concept or text prompt can return.

min_area.tooltip: Automatic objects smaller than this share of the image are dropped.

mark_color.tooltip: Tint of the selection in the marked output (hex).

mark_opacity.tooltip: How strongly the marked output tints the selection (0.3 = the Colored Mark default).

selection.tooltip: Set by the canvas: the selected objects and the ones added by text or points.

BFSSegmentPicker.name: BFSSegmentPicker
BFSSegmentPicker.description: BFS Segment Picker: segment an image into objects with SAM 3.1, pick them with the mouse, get their masks. Click objects on the canvas to select them; add missed ones by text, points or the brush.
output_tooltips: Union of the selected objects, minus the selected remove / eraser ones (one mask).
One mask per selected object (remove ones already cut out), in selection order.
The image with the selection tinted (mark_color, mark_opacity).
Every object found, numbered; the selection stronger.
JSON: size, selected ids and every object's id, label, score, box (relative x, y, w, h) and area.

images.tooltip: The source clip (or one frame).

subject.tooltip: What SAM 3 covers with static (e.g. person, man, dog).

BFSSettingPicture.name: BFSSettingPicture
BFSSettingPicture.display_name: BFS Setting Picture (place, person in static)
BFSSettingPicture.description: TSC's setting picture for a duet: one frame of the clip with the person covered in TV static. Give it to BFS H3 Duet's `setting` input: the generated half then takes the place, light and framing from it instead of from the character picture.

guide_mode.tooltip: aligned guide: the shot's frames sit on the generated frames (MiniMax H3 Add Guide), frame by frame. native reference video: the shot enters as <Video 1> like the reference video input. both: the two together. aligned guide + CLIP video context: Qwen sees the shot at clip_video_fps, while its latents enter only as an aligned guide. Native temporal alignment: experimental mode matching native_temporal_v1 training; requires MODEL routing, 24 fps and no Add Guide/VSA.

first_frame.tooltip: Anchor the shot's own first frame as an extra aligned image guide. Leave this at none when replacing the source location: its first frame also anchors the original background.

with_audio.tooltip: Attach the shot's soundtrack to the guide / reference video (needs audio_vae).

model.tooltip: Optional: passed through, or patched in native temporal mode. Route MODEL output to the guider (workflows that routed the model through this node keep working).

vlm.tooltip: Optional VLM (CLIPLoader with a Qwen3-VL text encoder). Fills {details} when the planner left it (no 📝 Describe refs, no VLM on the planner).

setting_ref.tooltip: This references the ORIGINAL source setting; leave it off when replacing that location. TSC's trick: one more reference picture, the shot's middle frame with the person covered in TV static, so the model sees the place in full detail (the panel / guide is often small). It is the last <Picture n>; a sentence about it is added to subject_definitions (or write {setting} where you want its tag). Mask: setting_mask, else the shot's SAM 3 mask (crop or not), else SAM 3 'person' on that frame. 'source size' uses the video's own resolution (up to 2048 short edge): sharper, slower.

setting_mask.tooltip: Optional mask of the person to cover in the setting picture.

inpaint.tooltip: per shot (planner): each shot's mode in the Shot Planner decides (Full frame / Mask only / Crop / Crop + mask). only the mask: every shot. off: never. Regenerate ONLY the person. The latent starts from the shot's own frames and the shot's SAM 3 mask (grown by the mask's expand + one latent cell) becomes H3's generation mask; everything else stays exactly as it was. With 'Crop to mask' on the shot it works inside the crop (more pixels for the person, BFS Shot Join pastes it back); without crop it works on the whole frame (no crop / uncrop at all). Needs a mask (text or points) on the shot. Crop + H3 generation mask: credit to Neko (Nekodificador) and AbleJones, whose workflow and nodes this follows. On ComfyUI builds without native H3 generation masks, add a per-row mask patch to the model (e.g. ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-PerRowMasking).

mask_guide: instead of the full guide (masked region only)

mask_guide.tooltip: Experimental, 'Mask only' shots (mask, no crop): the shot with ONLY the masked region visible (the rest grey), so the model looks at the subject's pose and outline on its own while the mask limits where it generates. '+ extra guide': a second aligned guide latent next to the normal one (the model sees both). 'instead of the full guide': replaces the normal guide. '+ reference video': enters as a native reference video (<Video n>, after the shot's own if guide_mode uses it). The LoRAs were trained with one full guide, so test against off; it can also pull the old subject's look.

source_blur.tooltip: Blur the source person in what the model SEES of the source (aligned guide, native reference video): '<region> (<what stays sharp>)'. Region: face / head + hands / person (every person the segmenter finds) or masked area (the shot's own mask, the person being replaced, with its expand). keep mouth: lips, teeth and tongue stay sharp; keep lips + tongue: the teeth are blurred too; mouth too: nothing stays sharp. The model still reads the pose and motion but has no face to copy, so the identity comes from the reference. The kept area of 'Mask only' and the output are never blurred. JalenBrunson's swap trick.

source_blur_strength.tooltip: How coarse the source blur is (1 = no detail left).

source_blur_segmenter.tooltip: What finds the face / head / hands / person and the mouth for source_blur. SAM 3.1: text prompts (already used by the planner). Sapiens2: body-part classes in one pass, finer lips and teeth (downloads facebook/sapiens2-seg-0.4b, 1.6 GB, to models/sapiens2 the first time). The 'keep lips + tongue' modes always use Sapiens2 for the lips.

source_blur_effect.tooltip: blur: no detail left. invert colours: keeps the shapes and the expression but not the skin tone or the colours.

mask_guide_look.tooltip: What the mask guide shows of the subject. grey blurred: its volume, light and head direction without colours or a face (default). colour: as it is (can make the model copy the old subject). silhouette: only its flat shape. edges: only its outlines. pose (people): the skeleton of the people in the mask (OpenPose colours), from a YOLO pose model in models/ultralytics (e.g. pose/yolov8m-pose.pt; uses ultralytics). The less it shows, the less the model can copy the old subject; the more, the better it follows the pose.

mask_ref_size.tooltip: mask_guide '+ reference video' only: size of that reference video (fraction of the generation size). The native reference channel keeps a smaller video as it is, so 1/2 costs ~1/4 of the tokens; it only has to show the pose and outline.

clip_video_fps.tooltip: Only for aligned guide + CLIP video context. Qwen sampling rate for this shot; try 2, 4 or 8 fps. Higher values cost more context/encoding time, not output fps. Console confirms sent frames, video vision tokens and completed encoding.

native_guide_scale.tooltip: Native temporal mode only: spatial scale of the motion video before encoding; output size, frame count and identity references stay unchanged. Try 0.5 to reduce guide tokens/VRAM.

native_temporal_backend.tooltip: Native temporal mode only. Flash partitions preserves the temporal attention policy without compilation; Flex is the original implementation.

normals.tooltip: Optional MoGe normals of the shot's frames (BFS Shot Unpack's frames -> Run MoGe Inference -> Render MoGe Geometry, normal_directx). Only for shots whose Colored Mark style is 'normal map'.

BFSShotH3Conditioning.name: BFSShotH3Conditioning
BFSShotH3Conditioning.description: Build MiniMax H3 conditioning for one shot with the native nodes: Reference to Video (prompt, references, length) plus the shot as an aligned guide and/or reference video. CLIP video context lets Qwen see the shot without native shot reference latents.

guide_mode.tooltip: aligned guide: preserve the shot frame by frame with MiniMax H3 Add Guide. native reference video: provide it as <Video 1> context. both: use both paths. aligned guide + CLIP video context: Qwen sees the shot at clip_video_fps without native shot reference latents; motion still uses Add Guide. Native temporal alignment: experimental native video mode for its matching LoRA; MODEL input and output must be connected, no Add Guide or VSA.

with_audio.tooltip: Condition on the shot soundtrack too. This can improve lip sync when audio_vae is connected.

vlm.tooltip: Optional Qwen3-VL encoder. Fills missing reference details in the planner prompt.

inpaint.tooltip: Use each shot's Planner mask mode, force mask-only generation, or disable it.

source_blur.tooltip: Blur the source subject in the guide so the model is less likely to copy its identity: '<region> (<what stays sharp>)'; masked area = the shot's own mask.

source_blur_segmenter.tooltip: What finds the face / head / hands / person and the mouth for source_blur. SAM 3.1: text prompts (already used by the planner). Sapiens2: body-part classes in one pass, finer lips and teeth (downloads facebook/sapiens2-seg-0.4b, 1.6 GB, to models/sapiens2 the first time). The 'keep lips + tongue' modes always use Sapiens2 for the lips.

source_blur_effect.tooltip: blur: no detail left. invert colours: keeps the shapes and the expression but not the skin tone or the colours.

clip_video_fps.tooltip: Only for aligned guide + CLIP video context. Qwen sampling rate for this shot; try 2, 4 or 8 fps. Higher values cost more context/encoding time, not output fps. Console confirms sent frames, video vision tokens and completed encoding.

model.tooltip: Required for native temporal mode. Route MODEL output to the guider.

native_guide_scale.tooltip: Native temporal mode only: spatial scale of the motion video before encoding; output size, frame count and identity references stay unchanged. Try 0.5 to reduce guide tokens/VRAM.

native_temporal_backend.tooltip: Native temporal mode only. Flash partitions preserves the temporal attention policy without compilation; Flex is the original implementation.

normals.tooltip: Optional MoGe normals of the shot's frames (BFS Shot Unpack's frames -> Run MoGe Inference -> Render MoGe Geometry, normal_directx). Only for shots whose Colored Mark style is 'normal map'.

BFSShotH3ConditioningSimple.name: BFSShotH3ConditioningSimple
BFSShotH3ConditioningSimple.description: Build the usual MiniMax H3 shot conditioning with references, prompt and an aligned guide and/or native reference video. Use the Advanced node for the mask guide, setting picture and first frame.

mode: duet (pin the shot, no LoRA needed)

mode.default: duet (pin the shot, no LoRA needed)
mode.tooltip: duet: the shot's own clip is pinned beside the video and copied in sync. guide: the shot sits on the generated frames as a latent guide (use with a body-swap LoRA). duet + guide: both.

task.tooltip: Writes the prompt when the shot has none (no per-shot or global prompt in the Planner).

instruction.tooltip: What changes, in a few seen words (see BFS H3 Duet).

position.tooltip: Side of the video the strip is added to (TSC's duet pins the source clip on the left).

size.tooltip: Strip size as a fraction of the video's height (top/bottom) or width (left/right), snapped to 32 px.

fit.tooltip: contain keeps the whole clip (smaller, with grey around) so nothing is cropped

gap.tooltip: Gray separator between panel and video, in 32 px patches (held like the panel).

panel_noise.tooltip: 0 pins the panel exactly. 0.05-0.15 lets the model loosen it a little when the result copies too much of it (TSC's SOURCE NOISE).

source_blur.tooltip: Blur the source person in what the model sees (the panel / the guide): '<region> (<what stays sharp>)'. keep mouth: lips, teeth and tongue stay sharp; keep lips + tongue: the teeth are blurred too; mouth too: nothing stays sharp. masked area: the shot's own mask (elsewhere: the whole person). It reads the pose and motion but has no face to copy. The output is never blurred.

source_blur_segmenter.tooltip: What finds the face / head / hands / person and the mouth for source_blur. SAM 3.1: text prompts. Sapiens2: body-part classes in one pass, finer lips and teeth (downloads facebook/sapiens2-seg-0.4b, 1.6 GB, to models/sapiens2 the first time). 'keep lips + tongue' always uses Sapiens2 for the lips.

source_blur_effect.tooltip: blur: no detail left. invert colours: keeps the shapes and the expression but not the skin tone or colours.

vlm.tooltip: Optional VLM (Qwen3-VL CLIPLoader): fills {details} in the shot's prompt from its references when the planner left it.

BFSShotH3Duet.name: BFSShotH3Duet
BFSShotH3Duet.display_name: BFS Shot H3 Duet (render one shot)
BFSShotH3Duet.description:
Renders one shot with MiniMax H3 (duet, aligned guide, or both) and returns its frames for BFS Shot Join. Runs once per shot of the Planner's list. The prompt comes from the Planner (per shot or global), or from the task when there is none.

Duet modes: How to write a duet prompt (TSC, newer strategy): H3 has no idea what is pinned and what is noised, it reads one description of one video. Describe the finished split screen as plain footage: never write 'kept footage', 'kept exactly', 'generated', 'preserved', 'in sync with', 'seamlessly'. The pinned clip gets no tag and no retention line: name its region by where it is plus what is seen there, in one clause ('the top quarter shows a man dancing in a small bedroom'; {panel_region} / {video_region} give the region names for the current layout, {layout} the whole split-screen sentence). Write the other region as its own scene in a real place with concrete details. Spell out the motion beat by beat, with times for the big moments (cuts, strikes, jumps, a line), on the video's clock. The soundscape is the sounds of the new scene. Cuts: '[Shot 2] At MM:SS.mmm, both halves cut together to ...'.

Credits: the initial idea for this H3 node came from TSC's latent-pin duet (the source pinned beside the video with a noise mask). BFS had already used the same principle on LTX (a green side panel holding the reference) and implemented the virtual sidecar approach (reference tokens placed beside the frame in RoPE). New here: the shifted RoPE layout (the video keeps its own grid and the panel sits past its edge, with an optional gap), dynamic references, task prompts and the shot-loop node.

images.tooltip: Decoded frames of every shot (the list from VAE Decode). Not requested when every shot is already stored: nothing is generated again.

shots.tooltip: The shots list from BFS Shot Planner.

crossfade.tooltip: Frames to blend across boundaries that are not camera cuts, using the overlap each shot generated past its end. 0 = hard joins everywhere.

audio.tooltip: Soundtrack to return with the video (e.g. the planner's audio output).

timeline.tooltip: The planner's timeline. With it, shots that did not run are filled with the original video (or dropped, per the planner's setting) and the soundtrack follows.

comparison.tooltip: Also output a side-by-side video: original shot | references | result, with the shot's info on top and its prompt below.

label.tooltip: Extra text for the comparison's top bar, e.g. the model, LoRA, steps and seed.

comparison_height.tooltip: Height of each column in the comparison (0 = full size). Smaller is much lighter for long videos.

edge_hardness.tooltip: Cropped / Frame + paste shots: harden the soft edge of the paste (0 = as feathered, 1 = hard cut). Raise it when a faint ghost of the original person shows around the new one. From NKD Inpaint Stitch.

match_colors.tooltip: Cropped / Frame + paste shots: correct the colour / brightness drift of the generated patch (Reinhard in LAB, statistics over the whole shot, so no flicker). 0.5-1 typical. From NKD Inpaint Stitch.

match_region.tooltip: Where the colour statistics are measured. 'around the subject (swap)': a ring of background around the mask, so a new person keeps their own colours and only the scene's light drift is fixed. 'inside the subject': inside the mask (retouching the same person/content).

seamless_edges.tooltip: Cropped / Frame + paste shots: Poisson blend (OpenCV seamlessClone) for stubborn seams. Slower; can shift colours near the edge. From NKD Inpaint Stitch.

paste_new_outline.tooltip: 'Frame + paste' shots: also paste where the NEW subject is (SAM 3 on the result near the original one, with the shot's 'new subject' text from the planner, default 'person'), so a bigger silhouette (hair, body) is not cut. Off = only the original mask (+ expand).

comparison_mask.tooltip: In the comparison, shots with a crop or a generation mask (Mask only / Crop + mask) show the selected mask over the original column; Colored Mark uses its selected colors, other masks use red. Crop boxes are yellow.

keep_colors.tooltip: Shot by shot / queue loop with continuity: shots that continue from the previous one can drift in colour over a long take. On: the new subject's colours (chroma) of every continuing shot are matched to the first shot of the take before it is stored (the background and the lightness are not touched; a camera cut or a shot without continuity starts a new take). Off by default: the match is one shift for the whole shot, so with continuity 'head' (whose first frames already continue the previous shot) it shows as a colour jump at every seam. Turn it on only for a long take whose colours visibly drift.

keep_colors_strength.tooltip: How much of that correction is applied (1 = fully to the first shot).

save_to.tooltip: images: output the video as IMAGE (connect Create Video / Save Video); the whole video is held in memory. mp4 file: the join writes the video (and the comparison) straight to MP4 files in the output folder, one shot at a time, so memory stays at about one shot: use it for long videos. The images and comparison outputs still carry the video, read back from the files at a size that fits the free RAM (the files keep the full size), the node shows the files, and video_path gives the path. In mp4 file mode, bypass downstream VHS Video Combine / Create Video / Save Video nodes: they only encode the completed video again and can exhaust RAM.

filename_prefix.tooltip: mp4 file: the file name in the output folder (a counter is added).

mp4_crf.tooltip: mp4 file: H.264 quality (lower = better and bigger; 0 = lossless, 17 = visually lossless, 23 = ffmpeg's default).

BFSShotJoin.name: BFSShotJoin
BFSShotJoin.description: Concatenate the generated shots in order, trim each to its length and cross-fade soft joins. When save_to is 'mp4 file', this node is the final encoder; downstream video save nodes are redundant.
output_tooltips: The joined video.
Its soundtrack.
Its frame rate.
original | references | result, side by side (needs 'comparison').
The MP4 written in 'mp4 file' mode (empty otherwise).
The original frames under each output frame, same length and timing as 'images', at comparison_height (needs 'comparison'): connect it with 'images' to BFS Video Compare.

seed.tooltip: The seed (the base seed when a shot is connected).

shot_seed.tooltip: Only with a shot connected: the seed of each shot (same / counting up / unrelated but repeatable).

shared_base.tooltip: 0 = off (plain noise). The coarse pattern of the noise comes from base_seed instead of the shot's seed: every shot, any length or size, agrees on it; the fine detail stays per shot. 1 = fully shared. Try 0.5 - 1.

static_share.tooltip: 0 = off. A part of the noise that is identical in every frame (temporally correlated noise). Try 0.1 - 0.3; too much freezes the motion.

guide_structure.tooltip: 0 = off. Needs guide_frames + vae. Outside the mask the guide's latent is mixed into the noise, so the background starts closer to the guide (without a mask: everywhere, which also pulls toward the original person). Try 0.05 - 0.2.

distribution.tooltip: gaussian = what the model was trained on. laplacian / student-t: more extreme values (stronger, sparser kicks). uniform: none. All at unit variance. Like AdvancedNoise's types, but for H3's video + audio latent (the audio noise always stays gaussian).

spectrum_tilt.tooltip: 0 = off (white noise). > 0: more energy in the large blobs (fractal / pink noise, AdvancedNoise's 'fractal' alpha): the coarse layout, where the swap is decided, gets a harder push. < 0: more fine grain. Try 0.2 - 0.6; large values burn colours.

pyramid.tooltip: 0 = off. Adds coarser layers of noise (each half the size, weight = this value per level): another way to put more energy in the large scales. Try 0.3 - 0.6.

ref_tint.tooltip: 0 = off. Needs ref_image + vae. Inside the mask (everywhere without one) the noise leans toward the reference's average latent, i.e. its colours. Try 0.05 - 0.15.

shot.tooltip: From BFS Shot Planner / Unpack: per-shot seeds, and the shared base is read at the shot's position on the timeline.

base_seed.tooltip: Seed of the shared coarse pattern and of static_share. -1 = the seed above. Put here the seed of a result that worked to keep its coarse noise while the detail changes with the seed.

overrides.tooltip: Seeds for single shots: 'shot:seed, shot:seed' (shots count from 1).

base_grid.tooltip: Blocks of the coarse pattern along the short side (the long side in proportion). Fewer = only the broadest layout is shared.

time_block.tooltip: Latent frames per block of the coarse pattern.

vae.tooltip: The video VAE, for guide_structure and ref_tint.

ref_image.tooltip: The reference picture (ref_tint).

mask.tooltip: The person, one mask per frame (white = the person): guide_structure stays outside it, ref_tint inside it.

BFSShotNoise.name: BFSShotNoise
BFSShotNoise.description: Optional structured starting noise. With every amount at 0 it is exactly RandomNoise. shared_base: the coarse noise pattern is the same for every shot / size / length (from base_seed), the detail per shot. static_share: a part identical in all frames. guide_structure: the guide's latent mixed in outside the mask. ref_tint: lean toward the reference's colours inside the mask. Experimental: the model was trained on plain noise, so use small amounts and compare with 0.
output_tooltips: For SamplerCustomAdvanced.
The seed this shot used.

plan.tooltip: The panel writes this. JSON with the video, split settings, boundaries and the per-shot reference and prompt.

prompt.tooltip: Default prompt for shots without their own (overrides the panel's global prompt).

mask.tooltip: Optional mask of the WHOLE video (white = the subject), e.g. rotoscoped in another tool and loaded with Load Video (+ Convert Image to Mask). Replaces SAM 3 for every shot without its own mask video / text / points. One mask per source frame; a different count is spread over the video.

vlm.tooltip: Optional vision-language model (CLIPLoader with qwen3vl_4b / qwen3vl_8b). It looks at every shot and suggests what to segment, a description of the shot (fills {shot} in the prompt). Settings in the panel's VLM card.

point_model.tooltip: Optional MolmoPoint-8B (Auto Download & Load MolmoPoint-8B). When connected, a selection written as text ('the man on the left', 'the red car') is pointed by MolmoPoint and SAM 3 tracks from those points, instead of SAM 3 reading the text. The panel's previews use it after one run.

BFSShotPlanner.name: BFSShotPlanner
BFSShotPlanner.description: Split a long video into model-sized shots (at camera cuts, fixed length, or by hand), give every shot its own reference image and prompt, and run the rest of the graph once per shot. Join the decoded shots with BFS Shot Join.
output_tooltips: One item per shot. Every node that receives this list runs once per shot; connect it to BFS Shot Unpack or BFS Shot H3 Conditioning, sample, decode, then BFS Shot Join.
Number of shots that will run.
Timeline frame rate.
Generation width.
Generation height.
The whole soundtrack, trimmed to the planned duration.
Human-readable plan.
Every shot in order, including the ones that do not run (disabled or filtered out). Connect it to BFS Shot Join so skipped shots are filled with the original video (or dropped).
Every reference picture the shots use, without repeats, <Picture 1> first (a grey image when there is none).
How many different reference pictures the shots use.
Run tab > Second pass: on or off. Use it to switch the upscale branch (latent upscale + second sampler).
Second pass width (the generation width upscaled as set in the Run tab, on the latent grid).
Second pass height.

guide_frames.tooltip: Replacement guide frames. Resized to the shot's generation size; padded or trimmed to its length.

refs.tooltip: Replacement reference pictures: BFS Shot Unpack's refs list after any processing (e.g. background removed), one image per picture, in order.

prompt.tooltip: Replacement prompt.

BFSShotRepack.name: BFSShotRepack
BFSShotRepack.description: Rebuild a shot after editing its pieces (Unpack -> any processing -> Repack). Inputs left unconnected keep the shot's original values; timing, cuts and audio are unchanged.

seed.tooltip: The base seed (shot 1 always uses it).

mode.tooltip: same for every shot: every shot starts from the same noise (as when one seed widget feeds the sampler). increment per shot: seed, seed+1, seed+2 ... random per shot: an unrelated seed for each shot, derived from the base seed, so the run is still repeatable.

overrides.tooltip: Seeds for single shots, 'shot:seed' pairs separated by commas (shots count from 1), e.g. '3:12345, 5:777'. To keep a shot that came out well and re-roll the others.

BFSShotSeed.name: BFSShotSeed
BFSShotSeed.description: One seed per shot from a single base seed: the same for every shot, counting up, or random per shot, with optional per-shot overrides. Connect the shot from BFS Shot Planner / Unpack and feed the seed to the sampler.
output_tooltips: This shot's seed: connect it to the sampler / noise node.
'shot N: seed' for notes and the comparison bar.

BFSShotUnpack.name: BFSShotUnpack
BFSShotUnpack.description: Split one shot into its guide frames, reference pictures, prompt and length.
output_tooltips: The shot's guide frames, already at a length the model accepts.

This shot's reference pictures, <Picture 1> first, as a list: the next node runs once per picture (e.g. a background remover), and BFS Shot Repack's refs input puts them back in this shot. A grey placeholder when the shot has none.
How many reference pictures the shot has.
This shot's prompt.
Frames to generate (the grid-valid length).
First guide frame of the shot.
Soundtrack of the shot (silence if the video has none).
Generation width.
Generation height.
Shot index (0-based).
The same shot, unchanged: connect it to BFS Shot Repack after editing the pieces.
The previous shot's result frame this shot continues from (Continuity in the planner; queue loop), or a grey image.
The shot's SAM 3 mask over the guide frames (in the crop when the shot is cropped), or all ones.

sigmas.tooltip: The schedule that goes to the sampler (after the scheduler and the shift).

compare.tooltip: Another schedule drawn behind it, e.g. the same steps with another shift.

BFSSigmasPreview.name: BFSSigmasPreview
BFSSigmasPreview.description: Shows a sigma schedule: the noise level at the start of each step and how many steps fall on layout / identity (high noise), shapes and detail (low noise). With H3's video shift of 12 most steps sit at the top; lowering the shift moves steps toward detail. Changes nothing: sigmas pass through.
output_tooltips: The same sigmas, untouched.
The chart: connect a Preview Image.
The values and the step count per zone.

guide_video.tooltip: The guide frames (the same the Planner gets).

mask.tooltip: The person on the anchor frame (BFS Segment Picker mask).

anchor_frame.tooltip: Guide frame the mask was made on; -1 = the first keyframe of keyframe_spec.

BFSTrackFromFrame.name: BFSTrackFromFrame
output_tooltips: One mask per guide frame.
The anchor frame used.

guide.tooltip: The original video (e.g. BFS Shot Join's 'guide' output).

target.tooltip: The result to compare with it (e.g. BFS Shot Join's 'images').

fps.tooltip: Frame rate of both videos (connect BFS Shot Join's 'fps').

audio.tooltip: Soundtrack for the player (e.g. BFS Shot Join's 'audio').

gain.tooltip: How strongly differences light up in the map: a mean RGB difference of 1/gain (128/255 at 2) is already white. Raise it to see small changes.

size.tooltip: Which video's size the other is scaled to before comparing. The Join's guide is at comparison_height, so 'guide' is lighter.

preview_height.tooltip: Height of the player's videos (0 = the compared size). Only the preview: the difference is measured before it.

reference.tooltip: Optional reference pictures (e.g. the people swapped in), shown in a strip below the videos, numbered as <Picture n>, and in what ⬇ save / ● rec download. Takes the refs list of BFS Shot Planner / Unpack (pictures of any size) or a batch; up to 12.

free_memory_after.tooltip: After the workflow finishes, release cached node outputs and unloaded model weights from RAM. The next run reloads models.

BFSVideoCompare.name: BFSVideoCompare
BFSVideoCompare.description: Play two videos in one player (wipe, overlay or side by side; choose which is on top) and see where they differ, pixel by pixel.
output_tooltips: The difference map, one frame per compared frame (black = equal, white = very different).
Frame count, sizes, mean difference, PSNR and the most / least different frames.
Mean absolute RGB difference over all frames, 0-255.

image.tooltip: The frames: the Keyframe Planner's source_frames or a short clip (at most 32).

sam3_model.tooltip: SAM 3.1: MODEL of a Load Checkpoint node with sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors.

sam3_clip.tooltip: SAM 3.1: CLIP of the same Load Checkpoint node; turns the concepts and Find texts into SAM prompts.

concepts.tooltip: What the automatic pass looks for, comma separated (one SAM 3 text prompt each), e.g. person, animal, car, chair. Empty = no automatic pass, only what you add.

threshold.tooltip: SAM 3 detection score threshold: lower finds more (and more false hits).

max_per_concept.tooltip: Most objects one concept or text prompt can return.

min_area.tooltip: Automatic objects smaller than this share of the image are dropped.

mark_color.tooltip: Tint of the selection in the marked output (hex).

mark_opacity.tooltip: Opacity of the subject mark in both outputs: the marked preview and the H3 hybrid guide. Use 1 for a clearly visible normal map; lower values blend the original frame into both outputs.

selection.tooltip: Set by the panel: the selection on each frame.

track.tooltip: Frames without a selection take the nearest selected frame's mask, tracked with SAM 3.

normals.tooltip: Optional: MoGe normals of the same frames (Run MoGe Inference -> Render MoGe Geometry, a normal mode). With it the node also returns the normal-map hybrid guide.

normals_convention.tooltip: The Render MoGe Geometry output mode the normals come from.

hybrid_base.tooltip: Optional: the hybrid output of another Video Segment Picker, to add this subject on top (one picker per subject).

pose_keypoint.tooltip: Optional: DWPose Estimator keypoints of the same frames (body + hands + face), for mark_style 'openpose + face'.

molmo_clip.tooltip: Optional: Molmo2 as H3 encoder. It sees the whole video, finds the picked person again after camera cuts and helps recover missed masks. In the default Molmo2 (classic) mode it describes the selected person, tracks that description through the video, and uses its points to guide SAM 3.1.

point_model.tooltip: MolmoPoint-8B point tracker. Use with propagation_method 'MolmoPoint-8B'; its native point tokens guide SAM 3 without changing the H3 text encoder.

mark_style.tooltip: How each subject is drawn in the hybrid output, always in its color: the normal map, the DWPose skeleton with the face, or texture-free alternatives that need no MoGe (flat, blur, pixelate, gray detail, edges). 'normal map inside mask' hides source texture only inside the person: everything outside is protected automatically. It feathers the boundary and also keeps objects selected with the padlock or protect_mask unchanged inside the person mask. 'translucent overlay' colors the exact mask with mark_opacity. 'colored outline' draws only a thin border inside the mask, preserving frame detail and held objects. 'colored hatching + contour' draws lines and a matching inner contour, preserving the original texture and lighting between lines. These modes need no normals.

hybrid_grow.tooltip: Margin around the subject in the hybrid guide, relative to its size (normal map: 0.04-0.12; openpose: 0.08-0.18 around the person's convex hull).

strip_frames.tooltip: How many frames the panel shows to pick on (SAM segments each one): fewer is faster.

free_after: unload all models from the GPU
unload all models + release Molmo2 RAM
unload all models + clear the picker caches

free_after.default: unload all models from the GPU
free_after.tooltip: After the node: free the GPU for the next nodes (H3). 'all models' also unloads H3 / the text encoder left from the last generation. 'release Molmo2 RAM' drops its CPU weights too, so the next Molmo2 run reloads them. Clearing the caches also frees RAM, but the next run segments and tracks again. Before MoGe / DWPose / Molmo2 run (only on Propagate) every model is unloaded anyway, so a second run does not run out of memory.

pose_region.tooltip: openpose mark: the gray region around each subject. The outline (hybrid_grow ~0.02-0.05) hides the least background and usually looks best; the convex hull (with hybrid_grow margin) hides the original body shape (the new one stays free); the outline follows the person (less background hidden, but the original silhouette shows).

pose_gray_opacity.tooltip: openpose mark: how opaque the gray region is (1.0 = fully hidden). Lower lets the background show through, but also the original person (clothes, body), which the result may then copy.

max_subjects.tooltip: Limit active subjects: 'auto' automatically detects connected picture inputs in downstream H3 conditioning (ignoring extra subjects like green if only 2 pictures are connected), or force 1, 2, or 3.

propagate_scope.tooltip: Fill only empty masks keeps every existing non-empty frame unchanged and fills only frames whose mask is empty. Only this frame replaces one mask; from active frame onward recalculates from the open frame and preserves earlier results; all frames recomputes the clip.

propagation_method.tooltip: MolmoPoint-8B uses native point tokens to track and re-anchor the selected person; Molmo2 (classic) uses text coordinates. Both use SAM 3 for per-frame masks.

molmo_descriptions.tooltip: Optional tracking description for subject 1. Leave blank to let Molmo2 describe the person you selected automatically. This only overrides the text query; the selected mask remains the visual anchor.

protect_mask.tooltip: Optional external mask of objects to keep unchanged in 'normal map inside mask'. You can instead select protected objects with the padlock in this node. One mask or one per guide frame.

edge_feather.tooltip: 'normal map inside mask': soften the mark inward from the person and protected-object edges. Fraction of the shorter frame side.

hatch_width.tooltip: Hatching line and contour thickness multiplier. 1 matches the training format.

hatch_spacing.tooltip: Hatching line spacing multiplier. 1 matches the training format.

clean_masks.tooltip: Clean the subject masks on every frame (the picked frames before tracking too): any piece smaller than this, in % of the subject's area, joins what surrounds it. Stray specks of one color on another subject (e.g. where hands and arms cross) go to that subject, holes inside a mask are filled, and a subject's main body is never removed. 0 = off; 0.5-2 is usually enough. Too high can swallow a small real part, like a fingertip of the other person.

BFSVideoSegmentPicker.name: BFSVideoSegmentPicker
BFSVideoSegmentPicker.description: BFS Video Segment Picker (SAM 3): pick who to replace in a video or in a set of keyframes.
output_tooltips: One mask per frame: the person to replace.
Every frame with the person tinted (mark_color, mark_opacity).
The strip frames with all objects found, numbered.
JSON per frame: picked by hand, tracked from frame N, or empty.
The H3 guide with each subject drawn in its color using mark_style and mark_opacity; 'normal map inside mask' keeps pixels outside the person and protect_mask unchanged.

result.tooltip: What one iteration produces; everything upstream of it can be looped.

loop.tooltip: Set by the panel: injected nodes and per-iteration widgets.

items.tooltip: The batch to iterate over: item i is injected on iteration i.

items_b.tooltip: A second batch, same length (e.g. the marked frames next to the plain ones).

item_masks.tooltip: One mask per item, injected where the panel says (source 'item_masks').

count.tooltip: Iterations when there are no items (params only); 0 = as many as the longest value list.

BFSWorkflowLoop.name: BFSWorkflowLoop
BFSWorkflowLoop.description:
BFS Workflow Loop: run any part of any workflow once per item, injecting the item (and per-iteration parameters)
into nodes you pick, and collect the results in order.
output_tooltips: The result of every iteration, in order, as one batch (resized to the first one's size).
Iterations run.

result.tooltip: The image or decoded video to compare; the sweep runs everything upstream of it.

frames_per_cell.tooltip: For videos: how many frames (evenly spread) each cell shows.

save_videos.tooltip: Save every multi-frame result as an mp4 in output/bfs_sweep/, named by its values.

sweep.tooltip: Set by the panel: the swept widgets and their values.

BFSXYSweep.name: BFSXYSweep
BFSXYSweep.description: BFS XY Sweep: run any workflow over a grid of widget values and get one labeled grid back.
output_tooltips: The labeled grid.
Every result (the cells' frames), resized to one size.
JSON: the values of every cell, in order.

question.default: What does the background consist of?

BackgroundScaler.name: BackgroundScaler
BackgroundScaler.description: Sets the masked area color in grayscale range.

samples.tooltip: Rays per texel. More = smoother, slower. Raise if grainy.

max_distance.tooltip: Ray length, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Smaller = tighter, more local occlusion.

strength.tooltip: Scales the occlusion. >1 darkens, <1 lightens.

bias.tooltip: Ray origin lift off the surface, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Raise if even surfaces show dark blotches/holes.

BakeAmbientOcclusion.name: BakeAmbientOcclusion
BakeAmbientOcclusion.description: Bakes an ambient-occlusion map from a high-poly mesh into a low-poly's UV layout (white = open, dark = crevices). Feed the UV-unwrapped low_poly and the high_poly it was decimated from. Outputs a grayscale image for Apply Texture To Mesh's occlusion input (packed into the ORM map / occlusionTexture).

cage_distance.tooltip: Surface search band, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Raise for wrong/missing patches under heavy decimation; lower if it grabs across gaps.

ignore_backfaces.tooltip: Skip high-poly surfaces facing away from the texel, so crevices/enclosed spaces don't grab the opposite wall. Disable only if the high-poly winding is inconsistent.

BakeNormalMapFromMesh.name: BakeNormalMapFromMesh
BakeNormalMapFromMesh.description: Bakes a tangent-space normal map (glTF/OpenGL +Y) from a high-poly mesh into a low-poly's UV layout, capturing detail lost during decimation. Feed the UV-unwrapped low_poly and the high_poly it was decimated from. Outputs an image for Apply Texture To Mesh's normal_map input.

mesh.tooltip: The UV-unwrapped mesh that was rendered.

images.tooltip: One image per camera, in camera order (Batch Images). Any resolution with the render's aspect ratio; higher gives a sharper bake.

resolution.tooltip: Square texture resolution. 0 = the mesh's current texture size (2048 if it has none); otherwise the current texture is resampled to it.

blend_exponent.tooltip: Views are weighted by cos(view angle)^exponent. Higher favours the most head-on view (sharper, harder seams); lower averages more views (softer).

fill_unseen.tooltip: Texels no view sees take colour grown from the seen surface instead of the mesh's own texture or vertex colours. For views that replace the whole texture.

camera_info.tooltip: The cameras the images were rendered with, as connected to Render Mesh. Join rigs with Batch Cameras. None: Render Mesh's auto-framed front view.

mask.tooltip: Edited areas per view; only masked pixels are projected. A single mask applies to every view.

output_tooltips: Per texel, how head-on the best view saw it, 0 = unseen. Render it as the texture from another rig to see what those views still need to cover.
BakeTextureFromViews.name: BakeTextureFromViews
BakeTextureFromViews.description: Projects images back onto the mesh's UV layout: render with Render Mesh, edit or regenerate the images, then bake them with the same mesh and cameras. Texels no view covers keep the mesh's own texture (or vertex colours). Outputs the base_color for Apply Texture to Mesh and a confidence mask of how well the views saw each texel. Renders made with a viewer model transform do not line up.

reference_mesh.tooltip: Optional dense pre-decimation mesh; back-projects each texel onto its true surface before sampling, removing faceted baking on coarse meshes.

BakeTextureFromVoxel.name: BakeTextureFromVoxel
BakeTextureFromVoxel.description: Bakes PBR textures onto the mesh's existing UV layout (trilinear-sample the sparse voxel volume). Does NOT unwrap — connect a UV unwrap node upstream. Outputs base_color + metallic/roughness grayscale IMAGEs (black if no PBR); feed them to ApplyTextureToMesh (SAME mesh) for SaveGLB.

mid_level.tooltip: Brightness at the exact center of the video.

end_level.tooltip: Brightness at the very last frame.
