model.tooltip: LTX2 model. Chain after any anchor/clamp nodes — those operate INSIDE the model's forward; this guider orchestrates three forwards from outside.

sigmas.tooltip: Sigma schedule. Same SIGMAS that drive your sampler. Per-step parameter lists must align with this length.

cfg_per_step.tooltip: Comma-separated CFG values per sampling step. Length must match number of sigmas (typically steps + 1, since last sigma is 0.0). For distilled CFG=1, set all to 1.0.

stg_scale_per_step.tooltip: Comma-separated STG scale values per step. 0.0 disables STG for that step (skips the perturbed forward). Typical: 2.0 early, ramping to 1.0 for the bulk of sampling.

stg_rescale_per_step.tooltip: Per-step STD-rescaling factor (0.0 = no rescale; 1.0 = full rescale to match positive prediction's standard deviation). Typically 1.0 throughout.

cfg_mode.tooltip:
How CFG values are determined per step.
  per_step_list: parse cfg_per_step (default, full manual control).
  sigma_curve: linear interpolation in sigma-space between cfg_min and cfg_max — cfg_per_step is IGNORED.

cfg_min.tooltip: CFG value when sigma reaches 0 (end of sampling). Only used when cfg_mode=sigma_curve. 1.0 = no CFG at the end.

cfg_max.tooltip: CFG value when sigma is at schedule max (start of sampling). Only used when cfg_mode=sigma_curve. The curve interpolates linearly in sigma between cfg_max (start) and cfg_min (end). Note: linear in sigma, NOT in step index — LTX2 sigma schedules concentrate non-uniformly, so the curve is intentionally steeper at the start.

stg_mode.tooltip:
How STG scale values are determined.
  per_step_list: parse stg_scale_per_step.
  sigma_curve: linear interpolation between stg_min and stg_max — stg_scale_per_step is IGNORED.

stg_min.tooltip: STG scale at sigma=0. Only used when stg_mode=sigma_curve. 0.0 = no STG at end.

stg_max.tooltip: STG scale at schedule's max sigma. Only used when stg_mode=sigma_curve.

stg_rescale_mode.tooltip: How STG rescale values are determined.

stg_rescale_min.tooltip: STG rescale at sigma=0. Only used when stg_rescale_mode=sigma_curve.

stg_rescale_max.tooltip: STG rescale at schedule's max sigma.

block_indices.tooltip: Comma-separated indices of transformer blocks where self-attention will be V-shortcut (perturbed) during the STG pass. Default '14, 19' matches upstream Lightricks — two mid-depth blocks produce a modest, well-calibrated perturbation. Adding more blocks dramatically strengthens STG; you would need to reduce stg_scale proportionally. Set '9999' (any out-of-range index) to functionally disable STG perturbation while keeping the per-step CFG schedule active.

skip_steps_sigma_threshold.tooltip: Sigmas above this threshold get a zero noise prediction (CFG zero-init). 1.0 default = no skipping (sigmas typically max at 1.0). Lower to skip very-noisy early steps.

LTX2STGGuider.name: LTX2STGGuider
LTX2STGGuider.description: STG (Spatio-Temporal Guidance) guider for LTX2. Perturbs self-attention on selected transformer blocks during a third forward pass per step, combining the result via pred = pos + (cfg-1)*(pos-neg) + stg_scale*(pos-perturbed). Each of cfg, stg_scale, stg_rescale can use either a per-step list (full control) or a sigma_curve mode (linear interpolation between min/max bounds — set once and adapts to any sigma schedule).

nag_alpha.tooltip: Mixing coefficient in that controls the balance between the normalized guided representation and the original positive representation.

nag_tau.tooltip: Clipping threshold that controls how much the guided attention can deviate from the positive attention.

inplace.tooltip: If true, modifies tensors in place to save memory. Leads to different numerical results which may change the output slightly.

model.tooltip: LTX2 model to patch. Chain order is flexible — does not conflict with anchor nodes (attn1) or SemanticClamp (also attn2 but different sentinel).

clip.tooltip: CLIP / text encoder that produced your positive conditioning. Required to encode the action vocabulary for correspondence search.

positive.tooltip: Positive prompt conditioning. The node analyzes this and fingerprint-matches at runtime so only the cond pass is amplified.

amplification_strength.tooltip: How aggressively to boost matched action tokens. 0 = no-op. 0.3 (default) = gentle upward scaling. 0.5-0.7 = stronger. 1.0 = maximum (matched tokens scaled by 1 + scale_ceiling, default +30%).

action_vocabulary_text.default: moving, walking, running, turning, lifting, reaching, pushing, pulling, gesturing, waving, pointing, leaning, tilting, raising, lowering, bending, stepping forward, walking toward, turning around, looking around, glancing, pivoting, rotating, jumping, dancing, swaying, rocking, extending, retracting, opening, closing, action, motion, movement, gesture
action_vocabulary_text.tooltip: Comma-separated action / motion vocabulary. Encoded via CLIP, used as the correspondence target. Default covers common verbs and phrases. Customize if your domain has specific motion vocabulary (sports, dance, etc.).

scale_ceiling.tooltip: Maximum K/V scale factor delta. At amplification_strength=1.0 and weight=1.0, K/V are scaled by (1 + scale_ceiling). Default 0.30 = max +30%. Higher values produce stronger redistribution but risk the same noise pattern as the deprecated TextAmplifier.

auto_threshold.tooltip: Auto-calibrate correspondence threshold to encoder's score distribution. p95 targets top ~5% of most action-like tokens. p98 = top 2%. Encoder-agnostic selection.

similarity_threshold.tooltip: Literal threshold when auto_threshold=disabled. Otherwise overridden by percentile.

similarity_sharpness.tooltip: Sigmoid steepness. 16 (default) = near-binary partition. Lower = softer transition.

amplification_floor.tooltip: Hard floor on per-token weights. Below this, weights become 0 (no boost). Eliminates sigmoid soft-tail leak. 0.3 default cuts off weak matches.

top_k.tooltip: Number of top similarity values averaged per positive token. Higher = requires more confirming matches in vocabulary.

bypass.tooltip: If True, model passes through unchanged. Also restores any prior amplifier patches.

LTXActionAmplifier.name: LTXActionAmplifier
LTXActionAmplifier.description: Selectively amplify action / motion text tokens in the positive prompt at attn2. Boosts K/V magnitude for matched verb tokens, leaving descriptive tokens unchanged. Symmetric inverse of LikenessSemanticClamp; replaces deprecated TextAmplifier's blanket-scaling approach.

output_path.tooltip: Bucket/file this pool accumulates into. Use a distinct path per condition (agree/conflict/dmd_on/dmd_off).

target_filter.tooltip: Regex; a module is captured if its dotted path matches. Note 'attn1' also matches 'audio_attn1' — use exclude_filter to drop the audio stream.

exclude_filter.tooltip: Regex; modules whose path matches are skipped even if target_filter matched. E.g. 'audio_' for video-only, or 'to_gate_logits' to drop gates.

reset.tooltip: Clear this path's accumulator before this pass. Set True on the FIRST prompt of a pool only.

LTXActivationCalibrator.name: LTXActivationCalibrator
LTXActivationCalibrator.description: Accumulates per-layer input E[x^2] during sampling into a named bucket. Pair with LTXCalibratorFlush downstream of the sampler to write the mask.

clear_after_flush.tooltip: Drop the in-memory bucket after writing. Leave False while accumulating a pool.

LTXCalibratorFlush.name: LTXCalibratorFlush
LTXCalibratorFlush.description: Writes a bucket's running-mean E[x^2] mask to a safetensors file. Run after the sampler.

mask.tooltip: Plain white/binary mask (e.g. from SAM2), one or more frames. Any non-black pixel counts as 'inside' the mask, regardless of exact shade.

color.tooltip: Preset color to recolor the mask to (matches scail2v2's per-person palette: blue=person 0, red=person 1, x-sorted left-to-right). Pick 'custom' to use the custom_r/g/b inputs instead.

style.tooltip: silhouette: recolor, keep the full shape -- use for the GUIDE mask slot (mask_video). flat_marker: recolor AND collapse to a small dot at the mask's centroid -- use for the IDENTITY mask slot (identity_mask_image); a shaped mask there re-injects a competing pose signal (the ref's own held pose).

marker_radius_frac.tooltip: flat_marker only: dot radius as a fraction of min(H, W). Matches the training-side default (flatten_ref_masks.py).

background_black.tooltip: On: output background is black (matches guide_mask's white-bg-colored-shape convention actually being colored-on-black internally once VAE-encoded -- for identity_mask specifically, training used a black bg). Off: keep the mask's original background color where nothing was recolored (rare; only if your source mask isn't black/white).

LTXColorMask.name: LTXColorMask
LTXColorMask.description: Recolors a plain white/binary SAM2-style mask into scail2v2's trained convention. 'silhouette' for the guide mask slot, 'flat_marker' (small color dot, no shape) for the identity mask slot -- see each input's tooltip for why the two differ.

guide_strength.tooltip: Auto-populated from the timeline editor (comma-separated guide strengths for image segments).

audio_vae.tooltip: Optional. Connect an Audio VAE to generate audio latents.

LTXDirector.description: Same as Prompt Relay Encode, but local prompts and segment lengths are edited visually as draggable blocks on a timeline. The duration_frames input only sets the timeline scale (pixel space) — actual frame count is still read from the latent.

LTXE_CropBack.name: LTXE_CropBack
LTXE_CropBack.description: Removes the padding an LTXE plan added: the extra frames at the end and the border, so the frames come back at the source size (or the delivered frame). Works after a 2x upscale too. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU, not yet benchmarked on real LTX weights.

images.tooltip: The SDR source frames (display values 0-1).

strength.tooltip: 1 = the full cleanup; lower blends back towards the source.

radius.tooltip: Smoothing radius in pixels. Wide banding steps need a larger radius; no pixel moves more than half a code whatever the radius.

shadow_sensitivity.tooltip: Extra smoothing in the shadows, where banding shows most.

tolerance.tooltip: How far a pixel may move, as a fraction of half a code (below 1 so rounding cannot flip a code).

bit_depth.tooltip: From LTXE HDR Source Audit bit_depth. Not connected: the node checks whether the values sit on the 8-bit grid.

LTXE_HDR8bitCleanup.name: LTXE_HDR8bitCleanup
LTXE_HDR8bitCleanup.description: Removes 8-bit banding before HDR reconstruction: fills in the values between code steps while every pixel stays within half a code of the source, so re-quantising gives back exactly the source codes (checked on every run and shown in the report). Only 8-bit sources are changed; 10-bit, float and unknown sources pass through untouched. Feed the guide path; keep the original for the masks. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

frames.tooltip: Frames in the source clip (ignored when images is connected).

fps.tooltip: Source frame rate (23.976 / 29.97 / 59.94 are read as the NTSC fractions).

width.tooltip: Working width in pixels (ignored when images is connected).

height.tooltip: Working height in pixels (ignored when images is connected).

segment_frames.tooltip: Frames per window, 8k+1 (97 is the official SDR-to-HDR graphs' window).

overlap.tooltip: Frames shared by neighbouring windows; the seam sits in the middle. Not yet tuned on real runs.

first_frame_number.tooltip: Number of the first source frame (e.g. 1001), kept for the delivered frames.

images.tooltip: Optional: frames, width and height are read from these.

LTXE_HDRChunkPlanner.name: LTXE_HDRChunkPlanner
LTXE_HDRChunkPlanner.description: Plans the temporal windows for SDR -> HDR: 8k+1-frame windows that overlap, a seam in the middle of each overlap, delivered ranges that cover the clip exactly once, padding of the last window (discarded later), conditioning at min(source, 30) fps while the output keeps the source rate, and token / memory estimates. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

images.tooltip: The decoded window (VAE Decode output: ACEScct codes, 0-1), every generated frame.

plan.tooltip: From LTXE HDR Chunk Planner (the same plan the window was cut with).

index.tooltip: The window index (the same as on LTXE HDR Take Segment).

output_folder.tooltip: Folder inside ComfyUI's output folder; layers go in sub-folders (hdr/, metadata/).

input_transfer.tooltip: acescct = the LTX-2.5 HDR VAE decode. acescg = frames that are already scene-linear ACEScg.

output_space.tooltip: acescg = scene-linear ACEScg (AP1), for comp and grade. acescct = the log codes.

source_report_json.tooltip: Optional: LTXE HDR Source Audit report_json, copied into the sidecar.

LTXE_HDRDelivery.name: LTXE_HDRDelivery
LTXE_HDRDelivery.description: Writes one decoded window as scene-linear EXR frames named after the source frames (<shot>_hdr_1001.exr ...): only the frames the plan delivers (seam context and padding dropped), converted from the ACEScct decode to ACEScg without clamping, half float + ZIP by default, plus a JSON sidecar in metadata/. Files go into ComfyUI's output folder. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

images.tooltip: SDR source frames (display values 0-1), the same window and size as the generated frames.

hard_clip.tooltip: A channel at or above this value counts as clipped.

near_white.tooltip: Luma where the near-white map starts rising (it reaches 1 at the clip level).

channel_policy.tooltip: any = one clipped channel is enough; all = every channel; luma = the luma value.

expand_px.tooltip: Grow the clip mask by this many pixels.

feather_px.tooltip: Soften the clip-mask edge by this many pixels.

temporal_frames.tooltip: Average the mask over this many frames (1 = off).

user_mask.tooltip: Optional mask to add, subtract or replace.

user_mode.tooltip: How the user mask is applied.

LTXE_HDRHighlightAnalyzer.name: LTXE_HDRHighlightAnalyzer
LTXE_HDRHighlightAnalyzer.description: Finds clipped highlights in the SDR source: a pixel is clipped only when a channel sits at the code ceiling, so a bright but unclipped area stays out of the clip mask. A separate soft near-white map covers the area just below. Feed it the source resized like the guide and cut with the same plan window. The masks never go into the model; they are used after generation. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

images.tooltip: Source frames at their own size (convert first, resize after).

input_space.tooltip: srgb_gamma: ordinary display-encoded video. srgb: scene-linear Rec.709 / sRGB. acescg: linear AP1. acescct: already ACEScct (passed through).

LTXE_HDRInputColor.name: LTXE_HDRInputColor
LTXE_HDRInputColor.description: Maps the source into ACEScct, the working space of the LTX-2.5 SDR-to-HDR IC-LoRA, before any resize. srgb_gamma (ordinary video) and srgb (scene-linear Rec.709) use ComfyUI core's Convert Image Color Space, the node the official graph uses; acescg uses this pack's ACEScct curve (core has no ACEScg input); acescct passes through. The untouched source is passed on for later source-preserving compositing. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

source.tooltip: The source window as the model saw it (LTXE HDR Take Segment window, ACEScct).

synth_mask.tooltip: From LTXE HDR Synth Mask (same window, same size).

generated_transfer.tooltip: Encoding of the generated input; the output uses the same.

synth_mix.tooltip: Scales the mask (1 = full generated contribution inside it).

color_match.tooltip: per_channel_gain = scale the generated image to the source exposure, measured outside the mask.

shadow_mask.tooltip: Optional: also take the generated image here (shadow recovery).

custom_mask.tooltip: Optional: also take the generated image here.

LTXE_HDRPreservationComposite.name: LTXE_HDRPreservationComposite
LTXE_HDRPreservationComposite.description: Keeps the approved source outside the synth mask and takes the generated HDR inside it, in linear ACEScg. Where the mask is 0 the result is exactly the source in that space. An optional per-channel gain matches the generated image to the source (the source is never changed). The output keeps the generated input's encoding, so LTXE HDR Delivery can write it. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

shot_name.tooltip: The shot name used on LTXE HDR Delivery.

output_folder.tooltip: The output folder used on LTXE HDR Delivery.

sample_every.tooltip: Read every n-th frame for the pixel checks (numbering is always checked for every frame).

jump_stops.tooltip: An exposure jump between two frames above this is flagged.

flicker_stops.tooltip: Mean frame-to-frame change above this is a warning.

preview_exposure.tooltip: Exposure of the contact sheet only, in stops (never changes the delivered frames).

LTXE_HDRQC.name: LTXE_HDRQC
LTXE_HDRQC.description: Checks a delivered shot before it goes out, from the output folder alone: every frame present once (missing windows and frames listed), readable and free of NaN / Inf, EXR header (precision, compression, ACEScg primaries, fps), exposure jumps between frames (seams), flicker, and how much of each frame was reconstructed above 1.0. It recommends accept, review or hold; it never re-renders anything by itself. The contact sheet is a tonemapped preview only. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

images.tooltip: This window, every generated frame (e.g. the composite's final).

shot_name.tooltip: The same shot name as on LTXE HDR Delivery.

output_folder.tooltip: The same output folder as on LTXE HDR Delivery.

mode.tooltip: luma = one exposure gain; per_channel = one per colour channel; local = a smooth gain map.

seam_width.tooltip: Frames over which the correction fades out after the seam.

protect_above.tooltip: Linear ACEScg values above this (reconstructed highlights) are not used to measure.

max_stops.tooltip: A difference larger than this is reported, not corrected (it is not a seam).

LTXE_HDRSeamExposureMatch.name: LTXE_HDRSeamExposureMatch
LTXE_HDRSeamExposureMatch.description: Matches this window's exposure to the window before it at the seam. The frames this window generates before its first delivered frame were already written by the previous window (EXR in the same output folder); the difference on them is corrected at the seam and faded out over seam_width frames, so the rest of the window is untouched. Run the windows in order; window 0 and a missing previous window pass through (the report says why). Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

source.tooltip: The source window as the model saw it (ACEScct).

display.tooltip: The SDR source window (display values), to find the crushed areas.

enabled.tooltip: Off = the source passes through unchanged.

black_threshold.tooltip: Display luma at or below this counts as crushed.

strength.tooltip: How much of the recovered detail is used.

transition_px.tooltip: Soft edge of the crushed areas, in pixels.

local_radius.tooltip: How far around a crushed area the local exposure is measured, in pixels.

LTXE_HDRShadowRecovery.name: LTXE_HDRShadowRecovery
LTXE_HDRShadowRecovery.description: Optional (off by default): where the SDR source is crushed to black, uses the generated shadow detail brought to the source's local exposure (measured from the just-above-black source pixels around it). Outside the crushed areas the result is exactly the source; inside it never goes below the source. Feed its output to the Source-Preservation Composite as the source. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

images.tooltip: The SDR frames, as loaded (display-referred 0-1).

fps.tooltip: The source frame rate (0 = not known).

scan_every.tooltip: Look at every n-th frame (1 = all; duplicates are only checked at 1).

clip_level.tooltip: A channel at or above this value counts as clipped.

crush_level.tooltip: Luma at or below this value counts as crushed to black.

metadata_json.tooltip: Optional container facts as JSON, e.g. {"primaries": "bt709", "transfer": "bt709", "range": "tv", "pix_fmt": "yuv420p"}. Reported as given.

LTXE_HDRSourceAudit.name: LTXE_HDRSourceAudit
LTXE_HDRSourceAudit.description: Checks an SDR clip before any model is loaded: size, frame rate, bit depth (estimated from the values), clipped highlights, near-white areas, crushed shadows, duplicate frames, likely cuts, softness, an upscale hint, and whether the input is already HDR (then use the Native HDR workflow). Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

include_near_white.tooltip: Also use the soft near-white map.

near_white_weight.tooltip: How much of the near-white map is used.

grow_px.tooltip: Expand (positive) or contract (negative) the mask, in pixels.

temporal_frames.tooltip: Average the mask over this many frames (1 = off).

user_mode.tooltip: How the user mask is applied.

preview_images.tooltip: Optional: the source frames, for the red preview.

LTXE_HDRSynthMask.name: LTXE_HDRSynthMask
LTXE_HDRSynthMask.description: Decides where the generated HDR is used in the final image: the clip mask, optionally the near-white map, grown, feathered and smoothed over time, plus your own mask. The model still sees the whole frame; this mask is only used by the Source-Preservation Composite. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

images.tooltip: The whole source clip (the same frames the plan was made for).

LTXE_HDRTakeSegment.name: LTXE_HDRTakeSegment
LTXE_HDRTakeSegment.description: Cuts one planned window out of the source frames, padded to its 8k+1 length with copies of the last frame, and says which of its frames are delivered (the rest is seam context or padding). Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU; the HDR model run itself is the official LTX-2.5 graph and has not been benchmarked by this pack.

images.tooltip: Source frames.

target.tooltip: Delivered frame size. The sampled canvas is that size rounded up to a multiple of 32 (DCP 2K 1920x1080 is sampled at 1920x1088, DCP 4K 4096x2160 at 4096x2176).

custom_width.tooltip: Delivered width when target is 'custom'.

custom_height.tooltip: Delivered height when target is 'custom'.

fit.tooltip: pad: place the source as it is (refuses a source larger than the target). fit-inside: scale down or up keeping the aspect ratio, then pad. crop-to-fill: scale to cover, crop the overflow.

pad_mode.tooltip: How the added border is filled: reflect (mirror the edge), replicate (repeat the edge pixels) or constant (pad_value). Padding happens in pixels, before encoding.

placement.tooltip: center: split the border evenly (the odd pixel goes right or bottom). top-left: keep the source at (0, 0).

tile_width.tooltip: Tile width in pixels for the plan summary and LTXE Tiled Model (0 = no tiling).

tile_height.tooltip: Tile height in pixels (0 = no tiling).

mask.tooltip: Optional mask; padded with the same transform (edge replicated).

vae.tooltip: Optional: read the scale factors from this VAE instead of assuming the LTX geometry (32 px per cell, 8 frames per latent frame).

LTXE_ResolutionPlan.name: LTXE_ResolutionPlan
LTXE_ResolutionPlan.description: Plans an LTX canvas for a size and length: aligned width, height and 8k+1 frame count, the padding to remove afterwards, the tile grid and token counts. For text-to-video. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU, not yet benchmarked on real LTX weights.

stop_on_problem.tooltip: On: stop the run when the schedule is unusable. Off: report only.

LTXE_SigmaCheck.name: LTXE_SigmaCheck
LTXE_SigmaCheck.description: Passes a sigma schedule through and stops the run with a plain-English message when it is NaN, rising, flat or saturated, the failures ComfyUI's LTX schedulers show on large latents. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU, not yet benchmarked on real LTX weights.

model.tooltip: An LTX model (LTX-Video 0.9.x or LTX-2 / 2.3 / 2.5).

tile_width.tooltip: Tile width in pixels. Match the model's or the LoRA's trained window.

min_overlap.tooltip: Minimum overlap between tiles in pixels; 0 = half a tile (the LTX-2 default). Capped at half a tile.

weight.tooltip: trapezoid: flat inside, linear ramps over the overlaps (default). gaussian: experimental.

on_out_of_memory.tooltip: shrink tiles: when a tile runs out of GPU memory, free memory, halve the larger tile side and retry (down to 128 px); the smaller size is kept for the rest of the run. stop: fail at once. A tile as large as the frame means 'tile only if needed'.

LTXE_TiledModel.name: LTXE_TiledModel
LTXE_TiledModel.description: Makes every model call run tile by tile and blends the tiles' predictions with trapezoid weights, while your sampler, noise and schedule stay as they are. Any sampler works, including ancestral and multi-step ones. Audio in an LTX-2 audio-video latent is shared by all tiles; IC-LoRA guides (full size) are cut with the tile. Not supported: ControlNet, downscaled guides. Experimental: implemented and tested on CPU, not yet benchmarked on real LTX weights.

padding.tooltip: Padding around detected face bbox as fraction (0.15 = 15% expansion). Captures hair/neck context for stronger identity preservation.

fallback_bbox.tooltip: Bbox to use if face detection fails or no face is found. Format: 'x1,y1,x2,y2' normalized 0-1. Empty = empty output on fail.

LTXFaceDetector.name: LTXFaceDetector
LTXFaceDetector.description: Detect face in image, emit normalized bbox string. Wire output to LikenessGuide's face_bbox_within_reference, LikenessAnchor's override_face_bbox / frame_0_bbox, or face_anchor's face_bbox_norm. Decouples detection from per-node logic so multiple nodes can share the same bbox.

identity_strength.tooltip: Scales reference latent magnitude. 1.0 = Best-Face-ID default.

face_padding.tooltip: Face bbox expansion — captures hair/neck context.

auto_face_crop.tooltip: When a face is detected, auto-crop the reference image around the face at zoom_factor extent and match target aspect ratio. Dramatically improves identity transfer for wide/full-body references by giving the VAE much more face detail to encode. Turn off if reference is already tightly cropped.

crop_zoom_factor.tooltip: How much context around the face to include. 2.0 = crop is 2x the face bbox (shoulders + hair). 1.5 = very tight (face + hair only). 3.0 = wide (upper body). Ignored if auto_face_crop off.

spatial_gating.tooltip: Constrain identity influence to face region. mask_soft = cosine falloff (recommended). mask_hard = binary. off = uniform (raw Best-Face-ID).

placement_mode.tooltip: i2v_safe / t2v_overlap = pure overlap layout (Best-Face-ID's 'what we use' default). Reference reuses target's coord grid, disambiguated by clean/noisy state and sequence position. prefix = additive offset (legacy).

source_id.tooltip: RoPE source tag applied via v2 phase rotation. Best-Face-ID LoRA expects 2.0. source_id=0 disables rotation (falls back to overlap-only v1 behavior).

phase_scale.tooltip: Phase rotation magnitude multiplier. Best-Face-ID LoRA expects 1.0. Lower values reduce reference/target separation strength.

LTXFaceIdentityReinforcer.name: LTXFaceIdentityReinforcer
LTXFaceIdentityReinforcer.description: Unified LTX-Best-Face-ID identity reinforcer. Combines reference latent injection, RoPE source-phase tagging, face detection, and spatial mask gating in a single node. Makes Best-Face-ID work correctly alongside i2v frame 0 conditioning by placing reference tokens at a distinct RoPE position while preserving the source_id=2 tag the LoRA was trained against. Replaces LikenessAnchor for identity workflows.

prompt.default: ref_t2v: a person in a room, medium shot.

reference_face_front.tooltip: REQUIRED — frontal face (source_id 2). Also drives the ArcFace projector.

phase_scale.tooltip: Global RoPE phase scale (training used 1.0). Applied to every view's source_id.

id_strength.tooltip: Multiplies the ArcFace projector tokens (frontal face only).

reference_back_head.tooltip: OPTIONAL — back of the head / nape, hair from behind (source_id 3). Leave empty to skip.

reference_body_front.tooltip: OPTIONAL — full-body front, build/proportions (source_id 4). Leave empty to skip.

reference_side_profile.tooltip: OPTIONAL — side / profile of the face (source_id 5). Leave empty to skip.

reference_temporal_offset_latents.tooltip: Temporal RoPE offset for appearance/reference tokens only, in VAE latent-time steps. 0 keeps the standard frame-0 placement used by existing LoRAs. -1 places the reference one latent step before frame 0 (normally -8 pixel frames), which can be tested to reduce overlap frame-0 reference leakage. Guide, mask, and target positions are never changed.

LTXIdentityMultiAngle.name: LTXIdentityMultiAngle
LTXIdentityMultiAngle.description: Multi-angle identity transfer: frontal face (required) + optional back/body/side reference views, each injected as its own overlap+source_phase segment (source_id 2/3/4/5), matching the multi-view training. Load the multi-view LoRA on MODEL first.

reference_image.tooltip: Reference to copy into the generation -- any subject (object, animal, character, person...), not just a face. Accepts a BATCH of N images (use an Image Batch node to combine several) for checkpoints trained on multiple STACKED references (layout='strata') -- each image in the batch becomes its own reference block with source_id = source_id + its index (0-based: 1st image keeps 'source_id' as-is, 2nd gets source_id+1, ...). For the exact historical frame-0 placement, set the reference temporal offset to 0.

source_id.tooltip: source_phase segment id (training used 2). 0 = no phase.

ref_resize_mode.tooltip: match_target: resize ref to the OUTPUT video's pixel size via a CENTER-CROP then resize (old single-face-crop recipes — ref resolution never mattered, but this silently discards whatever isn't in the middle of the ref for mismatched aspect ratios, e.g. a landscape character sheet used for a portrait output loses the side panels/face closeup). match_target_letterbox: same target pixel size, but fits the WHOLE ref inside it preserving aspect ratio (no crop, pads with white) -- use this for a landscape composite sheet + portrait (or any mismatched-aspect) output so no panel/face-detail gets cut off. native_resolution: encode the ref at ITS OWN size (rounded to the nearest 32px), independent of the video size — REQUIRED for checkpoints trained on a fixed ref resolution bucket that differs from the video's own bucket (e.g. the composite face+3views ref, trained at 2048x1024 regardless of output video size) -- but for aspect-mismatched outputs (e.g. portrait video) this can bias the model toward the ref's own (landscape) composition, causing an off-center/cropped-looking result; try match_target_letterbox first if you hit that.

debug_log.tooltip: Print per-step [LTXIdOverlap] shape logs to the console (for debugging).

crop_anchor.tooltip: New in v1.10.13, optional -- old workflows without this input keep the previous always-center-crop behavior. Only used by match_target (the crop-then-resize mode). Which part of the reference survives the crop when its aspect ratio doesn't match the output -- e.g. if your sheet's face closeup is in the top row, set 'top' instead of the default center crop so it doesn't get cut off. No effect on match_target_letterbox or native_resolution (neither ever crops).

layout.tooltip: The base positional layout used by the checkpoint. 'overlap' starts from the target's own RoPE coordinate range and then applies the independent reference temporal offset; use offset 0 for the exact historical overlap grid. 'st_drc' shifts the WHOLE reference block past the target's coordinate extent on every axis (non-overlapping region). 'strata' shifts ONLY the temporal axis to a slot past the target's own length -- one slot per image in the reference_image batch (1st image -> slot 0, 2nd -> slot 1, ...), leaving H/W overlapping the target; this is the 'stacked references' convention (ltx_trainer TASS strata layout). Only use whichever layout the loaded checkpoint was actually trained with -- using the wrong one is not a quality hit, it's a coordinate convention the model never learned, so identity transfer likely won't work at all.

reference_guidance_scale.tooltip: ST-DRC-style reference-CFG (arxiv 2606.02441). 1.0 = off (identical to before this input existed). >1.0 adds a THIRD forward pass per step with the reference tokens dropped, and amplifies the reference's own contribution: denoised += (scale-1)*(with_ref - without_ref) -- the same way CFG amplifies the text prompt's. Costs one extra (cheaper, ref-token-free) forward pass per step when enabled. Start around 2-4; same units/convention as CFG scale on the sampler.

reference_temporal_offset_latents.tooltip: Temporal RoPE offset for appearance/reference tokens only, in VAE latent-time steps. 0 keeps the standard frame-0 placement used by existing LoRAs. -1 places the reference one latent step before frame 0 (normally -8 pixel frames), which can be tested to reduce overlap frame-0 reference leakage. Guide, mask, and target positions are never changed.

LTXIdentityOverlapConditioning.name: LTXIdentityOverlapConditioning
LTXIdentityOverlapConditioning.description: Overlap/st_drc/strata + source_phase reference conditioning via a model patch, with an experimental reference-only temporal offset to reduce frame-0 composition leakage. Reference is separate tokens (NOT I2V), any subject -- not just a face. Accepts a BATCH of images for checkpoints trained on stacked references (layout='strata'). Load LoRA on MODEL first. ref_preview/crop_overlay outputs show exactly what gets encoded and, for match_target, what part of the reference survives the crop (green box) vs gets discarded.

LTXKeyframer.name: LTXKeyframer
LTXKeyframer.description: Replaces video latent frames with the encoded input images. Number of widgets is dynamically configured.

model.tooltip: LTX2 model to patch with per-block attention hooks. The returned model has the same behavior plus identity anchoring during sampling.

sigmas.tooltip: Connect from your sigma scheduler (e.g. BasicScheduler, LTX's STG scheduler). Required for predictable cache timing — without it the node falls back to manual_calls mode which is less reliable.

strength.tooltip: Magnitude of pull toward cached anchor state. 0.05-0.15 typical. 0.10 is default. Higher values can over-damp motion or flatten frame-to-frame variation.

cache_at_step.tooltip: Sampling step at which to lock the anchor (snapshot the model's representation as the stable target). Mid-sampling values (3-9 on 13-step schedules) work best — peak conditioning alignment moment before fine refinement begins.

similarity_threshold.tooltip: Minimum centered-cosine similarity for a token to receive pull. Lower = broader effect (more tokens pulled). 0.50 is balanced; raise to 0.60-0.70 to limit pull to most similar tokens only.

decay_with_distance.tooltip: Per-frame strength decay from frame 0 (anchor frame) to last frame. 0 = uniform across all frames. 0.3-0.5 lets later frames drift more freely while keeping early frames anchored.

bypass.tooltip: If True, the node passes the model through unchanged. Useful for A/B comparison without rewiring.

advanced_mode.tooltip: Toggle to expose research/diagnostic parameters: cache_mode, forwards_per_step, cache_warmup, anchor_frame, depth_curve, block_index_filter, debug.

cache_mode.tooltip: How cache timing is determined. schedule (default, requires sigmas wired): cache fires at the sigma corresponding to cache_at_step. live_extraction: no cache, regenerate target every call (softer effect). manual_calls: cache fires after cache_warmup block calls (fallback when sigmas not wired).

forwards_per_step.tooltip: How many model forward passes occur per sampling step. 1 for distilled CFG=1 (typical). 2 for standard CFG > 1 (cond + uncond). 3+ for CFG+STG. Affects cache timing math when in schedule mode. Variable-CFG schedules use a single approximate value.

cache_warmup.tooltip: Number of block calls before cache fires (when cache_mode=manual_calls). 144 ≈ 3 sampling steps × 48 blocks at CFG=1. Used as fallback when sigmas isn't connected.

anchor_frame.tooltip: Which frame's features to use as anchor source. 0 = first frame (the conditioning frame in i2v workflows — recommended). Set higher to anchor to a different frame.

depth_curve.tooltip: Per-block strength scaling across the 48 transformer blocks. flat = uniform (recommended default). ramp_up = stronger late blocks (handles refinement). ramp_down = stronger early blocks (handles semantics). late_focus = quadratic late emphasis. middle = strongest in middle blocks.

block_index_filter.tooltip: Limit hooks to specific blocks, e.g. '10-30' or '5,7,15-20'. Empty = all 48 blocks. Useful for ablation studies; rarely needed in normal use.

debug.tooltip: Verbose per-block diagnostic output during sampling. Shows cache state, similarity stats, and per-block timing. Helpful first time tuning a workflow.

LTXLatentAnchor.name: LTXLatentAnchor
LTXLatentAnchor.description: Whole-scene latent anchor for LTX2.x. Stabilises prompt + image conditioning and physical sensibility across long sampling. Connect SIGMAS for predictable cache timing. Toggle advanced_mode to access research parameters.

model.tooltip: LTX2 model to patch with per-block attention hooks. The returned model adds identity / scene anchoring with optional reference-image spatial energy weighting.

reference_image.tooltip: Optional reference image for spatial energy weighting. High-energy regions of this image (edges, faces, details) get stronger anchor pull; low-energy regions (sky, flat areas) get less. Wire alongside vae. For best results, use the i2v conditioning image or a composition reference.

vae.tooltip: VAE required when reference_image is wired (encodes the image into latent space for energy computation). Wire the LTX2 VAE.

energy_latent.tooltip: Alternative to reference_image+vae: provide a pre-encoded LATENT for energy weighting. Useful when you already have an encoded latent and want to skip re-encoding.

sigmas.tooltip: Connect from your sigma scheduler. Required for predictable cache timing (cache_mode=schedule). Without it the node falls back to manual_calls mode which is less reliable.

strength.tooltip: Magnitude of pull toward cached anchor state. 0.05-0.20 typical. 0.10 is default. Higher values can over-damp motion; lower values barely register.

cache_at_step.tooltip: Sampling step at which to lock the anchor (snapshot the model's representation as stable target). Mid-sampling values (3-9 on 13-step schedules) work best — peak conditioning alignment before refinement.

similarity_threshold.tooltip: Minimum centered-cosine similarity for a token to receive pull. Lower = broader effect. 0.50 is balanced; raise to 0.60-0.70 to narrow pull to most-similar tokens only.

decay_with_distance.tooltip: Per-frame strength decay from frame 0 to last frame. 0 = uniform. 0.3-0.5 lets later frames drift more while keeping early frames anchored.

energy_threshold.tooltip: Energy gating cutoff (when reference_image / energy_latent is wired). 0 = uniform energy (no spatial weighting, like plain LatentAnchor). 0.30 = broad: above-30%-percentile regions get pull. 0.50 = above-median only. 0.80 = top 20% energy regions only.

bypass.tooltip: If True, model passes through unchanged. Useful for A/B comparison without rewiring.

debug.tooltip: Verbose per-block diagnostic output during sampling. Shows cache state, similarity stats, energy gating, and per-block timing.

advanced_mode.tooltip: Toggle to expose research/diagnostic parameters: cache_mode, forwards_per_step, cache_warmup, anchor_frame, depth_curve, block_index_filter.

cache_mode.tooltip: How cache timing is determined. schedule (default, requires sigmas wired): cache fires at the sigma corresponding to cache_at_step. live_extraction: no cache, regenerate target every call (softer effect). manual_calls: cache fires after cache_warmup block calls (fallback when sigmas not wired).

forwards_per_step.tooltip: How many model forward passes occur per sampling step. 1 for distilled CFG=1. 2 for standard CFG > 1. 3+ for CFG+STG. Affects cache timing math when in schedule mode.

cache_warmup.tooltip: Number of block calls before cache fires (when cache_mode=manual_calls). 144 ≈ 3 sampling steps × 48 blocks at CFG=1.

anchor_frame.tooltip: Which frame's features to use as anchor source. 0 = first frame (conditioning frame in i2v — recommended).

depth_curve.tooltip: Per-block strength scaling. flat = uniform (recommended). ramp_up = stronger late blocks. ramp_down = stronger early. late_focus = quadratic late emphasis. middle = strongest in middle blocks.

block_index_filter.tooltip: Limit hooks to specific blocks, e.g. '10-30' or '5,7,15-20'. Empty = all 48 blocks. Useful for ablation studies.

LTXLatentAnchorAware.name: LTXLatentAnchorAware
LTXLatentAnchorAware.description: Latent anchor with optional spatial energy modulation from external reference. Reference image (or LATENT input) provides spatial weighting; matching itself uses running latent (correct feature space).

strength.tooltip: Magnitude of pull toward reference features. 0.08-0.18 typical with directional pull. Higher values (0.30-0.60) usable for stronger identity lock. Variance-collapse side effects at very high values are possible but practical ceiling unconfirmed — test with clean state (no prior runs' hooks leaked) before drawing conclusions.

reference_info.tooltip: Optional: wire from LikenessGuide if using Guide+Anchor combined approach. Leave disconnected to use frame_0 of the latent as the reference (recommended for i2v workflows where frame_0 is already the conditioning).

reference_source.tooltip: auto: use guide if reference_info wired, else use latent_frame_0. guide: requires reference_info from LikenessGuide. Reads the appended reference frame. latent_frame_0: read the first frame of the latent as the reference. Avoids the end-keyframe interpolation issue; ideal for i2v workflows where frame_0 is the conditioned start image.

frame_0_bbox.tooltip: When reference_source=latent_frame_0: bbox within frame_0 to use as identity source. Format: 'x1,y1,x2,y2' normalized 0-1. Empty = whole frame_0 used as reference.

similarity_threshold.tooltip: Minimum centered-cosine similarity for a generated token to receive pull. Lower = broader effect (more tokens pulled).

decay_with_distance.tooltip: Per-frame strength decay from frame 0 to frame F_orig-1. 0 = uniform across all frames.

depth_curve.tooltip: Per-block strength scaling. flat = uniform (recommended). ramp_down = stronger early, lighter late (good for avoiding over-sharpening). late_focus = stronger late blocks (CAUTION: can over-sharpen by pulling still-image detail into video refinement steps).

block_index_filter.tooltip: Limit to specific blocks, e.g. '0-36' to skip the final 12 blocks where over-sharpening tends to manifest. Empty = all blocks.

similarity_sharpness.tooltip: Sigmoid steepness for similarity gating. Higher = more binary in/out. Lower values (4-6) soften the transition.

override_face_bbox.tooltip: Override face_bbox_within_reference set in LikenessGuide. Format: 'x1,y1,x2,y2' normalized 0-1. Empty = use guide's bbox.

skip_when_sigma_above.tooltip: Disable anchor when sigma > this value (high-noise early steps). 0 = always active.

pull_mode.tooltip: directional (recommended): rotate token features toward reference identity direction WITHOUT changing magnitude. Preserves color/saturation. additive (legacy): pull toward reference features including magnitude. Identity + tonal pull; can cause desaturation/fade with strong settings.

late_block_falloff.tooltip: Additional per-block strength falloff in the last 12 blocks (37-47), which handle fine detail. 0 = no falloff. 0.5 = late blocks at half strength. 1.0 = late blocks disabled. Use 0.3-0.6 to reduce over-sharpening or texture-flattening from late-block pull.

LTXLikenessAnchor.name: LTXLikenessAnchor
LTXLikenessAnchor.description: Per-block attention pull toward reference features for identity preservation. Two modes: (1) wire reference_info from LikenessGuide to use Guide's appended reference frame. (2) leave reference_info unconnected and the node uses frame_0 of the latent as reference — ideal for i2v workflows where frame_0 is the conditioning start image. v1.2 uses directional pull mode (preserves color).

LTXLikenessCrop.name: LTXLikenessCrop
LTXLikenessCrop.description: Crop likeness reference frames off latent before VAE decode. Inverts LTXLikenessGuide's emit_latent=extended mode. Use only if Guide is emitting an extended latent. With Guide in passthrough mode (default), this node is unnecessary — wire the latent directly to VAE Decode.

strength.tooltip: How strongly the reference frames are preserved via noise_mask. 1.0 = fully preserved (clean reference throughout sampling). With placement_mode=silent_reference (default), strength=1 is safe and recommended — no looping.

placement_mode.tooltip: silent_reference (recommended): place reference in latent and preserve via noise_mask, but DO NOT register it as a keyframe in conditioning. The model still attends to it naturally for identity, without interpolation pressure that causes end-frame looping. keyframe: use LTXVAddGuide's full keyframe registration (original v1.1 behavior). May cause composition loop back to first frame.

face_detect.tooltip: auto: detect face via MediaPipe/OpenCV. manual: use face_bbox_within_reference. none: whole reference treated as identity (matches v1.0 behavior).

reference_mask_mode.tooltip: How to mask the reference latent. whole_frame = unchanged (model attends to entire reference, may cause looping). bbox_only = zero outside bbox in latent. bbox_softfade (recommended) = Gaussian fade outside bbox.

face_padding.tooltip: Padding around detected face bbox as fraction (0.15 = 15% expansion). Captures hair/neck context for stronger identity.

crf.tooltip: CRF for reference image preprocessing. Higher = softer reference, less rigid pull.

blur_radius.tooltip: Blur radius for reference image. Higher = softer reference.

attention_strength.tooltip: Metadata for downstream attention hooks (LTXLikenessAnchor). Doesn't affect this node's own output, only what downstream anchors read.

face_bbox_within_reference.tooltip: Manual bbox 'x1,y1,x2,y2' normalized 0-1. Used when face_detect=manual, or as fallback when auto detection fails. Empty + auto failed = whole frame.

emit_latent.tooltip: passthrough (recommended): the latent output is the unmodified input latent. Guide's value comes from its conditioning modifications (which feed into Guider) and the reference_info metadata it emits (which feeds into LikenessAnchor). Wire the input latent directly to your sampler. extended: emits the extended latent with the reference frame appended. Requires LikenessCrop downstream to remove the extension before VAE decode. Note: may cause end-keyframe interpolation pressure even in silent_reference mode (the spatial pattern itself can trigger learned keyframe behavior).

LTXLikenessGuide.name: LTXLikenessGuide
LTXLikenessGuide.description: Attach likeness reference image to conditioning for identity preservation. Emits modified positive/negative conditioning (for Guider) and reference_info metadata (for LikenessAnchor). By default the latent output is a passthrough of the input — no extension, no crop needed. The Guide's value comes from its conditioning-level interaction with the model and its bbox metadata, not from latent modification.

model.tooltip: LTX2 model to patch with semantic-aware attn2 forward replacements. Chain after LikenessAnchor.

clip.tooltip: CLIP / text encoder used by your prompt conditioning (typically Gemma-3-12B for LTX2). Required to encode the face-modifier keywords for correspondence search.

positive.tooltip: The positive prompt conditioning. The node fingerprints this and matches at runtime so only the positive (cond) pass is modified, not the negative (uncond) pass.

suppression_strength.tooltip: How much to suppress attention from face-bbox video tokens to face-modifier text tokens. 0 = no-op. 0.5 = halve their influence (recommended). 1.0 = fully block their influence (may cause rigidity).

reference_info.tooltip: Wire from LikenessGuide for the bbox and spatial dims. If not wired, falls back to override_face_bbox.

face_modifier_text.default: smiling, frowning, laughing, open mouth, closed mouth, eyes closed, eyes open wide, happy, sad, angry, surprised, expression
face_modifier_text.tooltip: Comma-separated keywords describing the expression / facial-modifier vocabulary to suppress. The node encodes this via your CLIP and uses correspondence search to identify matching tokens in your positive prompt. The default covers common expression vocabulary — usually no need to customize.

similarity_threshold.tooltip: Minimum top-K-mean cosine similarity for a positive-prompt token to be considered face-modifier-like. Only used when auto_threshold=disabled. Different encoders produce different absolute similarity values — prefer auto_threshold for portability.

auto_threshold.tooltip: Auto-calibrate similarity threshold to the encoder's score distribution. p95 = suppress top ~5% of most-modifier-like tokens. p98 = top 2%. p99 = top 1%. disabled = use similarity_threshold literal value. Recommended: p95 for balanced effect, p98 for narrower.

similarity_sharpness.tooltip: Sigmoid steepness around the threshold. Higher = more binary (sharp) partition between suppressed and not. 16 (default) makes the gate effectively binary within ~0.05 of threshold. Lower values (8) create soft tails that leak suppression to most tokens.

suppression_floor.tooltip: Hard floor on final suppression weights. Tokens with weight below this become 0 (unsuppressed). Eliminates sigmoid's soft tail leak. 0.3 default cuts off all weak matches; 0.5 only keeps strong matches; 0.0 disables (full sigmoid tail).

top_k.tooltip: Number of top similarity values to average for each positive token's match score. Higher K requires more confirming matches in modifier vocabulary, reducing false positives. K=1 = max (most permissive). K=3-5 (default 3) = robust.

soft_edge_frac.tooltip: Soft falloff fraction at bbox edges. 0.15 default for smooth transition. Lower = more focused, higher = more diffuse.

override_face_bbox.tooltip: Manual bbox 'x1,y1,x2,y2' normalized 0-1. Used when reference_info not wired.

bypass.tooltip: If True, model passes through unchanged.

LTXLikenessSemanticClamp.name: LTXLikenessSemanticClamp
LTXLikenessSemanticClamp.description: Semantic-aware text-token suppression on attn2 for face bbox region. Identifies face-modifier tokens in the prompt via embedding-space correspondence to a modifier vocabulary, then selectively suppresses ONLY those tokens' attention to the face region. Replaces deprecated LikenessClamp's blanket magnitude scaling approach.

num_loras.tooltip: How many LoRA slots to actually use. Only the first N slots (1-12) are applied; the rest are ignored entirely regardless of their values. Bump this up as you add more LoRAs to your stack.

lora_1.tooltip: LoRA file for slot 1. Set to 'None' to disable this slot.

strength_1.tooltip: Overall LoRA strength multiplier. Combined with audio_weight and video_weight per layer.

audio_weight_1.tooltip: Audio-block scale. Multiplied by strength to produce final scale for audio layers: audio_attn, audio_ff, audio_adaln, audio_embeddings_connector, and both A↔V cross-attention pairs. Set to 0 to disable audio-side adjustments from this LoRA.

video_weight_1.tooltip: Video-block scale. Multiplied by strength to produce final scale for video layers: main DiT transformer_blocks (attn1/attn2/ff), video_embeddings_connector, and video adaLN modulation. Set to 0 to disable video-side adjustments from this LoRA.

LTXLoraStackAV.name: LTXLoraStackAV
LTXLoraStackAV.description: Stack up to 12 LoRAs onto an LTX2 model with separate audio and video block-group scaling per LoRA. Replaces a chain of LoRA Loader Advanced nodes. Per-layer effective strength is: strength × (audio_weight if layer is audio else video_weight). Audio classification: keys containing 'audio' substring (catches audio_attn, audio_ff, audio_adaln, both cross-attention directions, and the audio embeddings connector). Set num_loras to control how many slots are actually used — slots beyond that count are ignored regardless of their values.

LTXModelInspector.name: LTXModelInspector
LTXModelInspector.description: Inspect diffusion model: top-level / name-filter / focus_path / trace hooks.

reference_1.tooltip: Reference image for slot 1 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 1>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots are numbered in order, so wiring 1 and 3 gives them source ids 1 and 2.

reference_2.tooltip: Reference image for slot 2 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 2>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots are numbered in order, so wiring 1 and 3 gives them source ids 1 and 2.

reference_3.tooltip: Reference image for slot 3 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 3>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots are numbered in order, so wiring 1 and 3 gives them source ids 1 and 2.

reference_4.tooltip: Reference image for slot 4 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 4>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots are numbered in order, so wiring 1 and 3 gives them source ids 1 and 2.

reference_5.tooltip: Reference image for slot 5 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 5>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots are numbered in order, so wiring 1 and 3 gives them source ids 1 and 2.

reference_6.tooltip: Reference image for slot 6 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 6>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots are numbered in order, so wiring 1 and 3 gives them source ids 1 and 2.

references.tooltip: Output of LTX Reference Images. Use this OR the individual reference_N slots below — the list wins if both are connected.

slot_embedding_lora.tooltip: The LoRA file to read the trained slot embedding from. Point this at the SAME LoRA you load for sampling. ComfyUI's LoRA loader applies only LoRA weights and drops the slot embedding, so without this the references are untagged and the checkpoint is sampled without a signal it was trained on. 'none' = phase separation only (older checkpoints).

start_source_id.tooltip: Source id of the first connected reference; the rest count up. The target is always 0. Start at 1 unless the checkpoint was trained otherwise.

slot_strength.tooltip: Scales the learned slot tag. The tag and the adapter were trained together at strength 1.0, so raising the LoRA on the loader without raising this leaves them out of proportion — the adapter shouts while the tag that tells the references apart stays quiet. Match this to the LoRA strength you set on the loader (an undertrained LoRA often wants 1.2-1.5, and the tag wants the same).

layout.tooltip: Where the references sit in the RoPE grid. Must match training.

ref_resize_mode.tooltip: Letterbox is the safe default for subject references: it keeps the whole image, where match_target centre-crops and can cut a subject in half when the aspect ratios differ.

LTXMultiReferenceSlots.name: LTXMultiReferenceSlots
LTXMultiReferenceSlots.description: Attaches up to six reference images as separate reference blocks, each with its own source id and, when the LoRA carries one, its trained slot embedding. Pair with LTX Reference Tags so the prompt names the slots the way training did.

guide_video.tooltip: Motion/structure driving video frames (IMAGE batch, e.g. from GetVideoComponents). Leave unconnected to skip the guide slot. Gets auto-masked black in the replacement region (see auto_mask_guide) unless disabled.

guide_source_id.tooltip: v13 recipe default: 0 (no RoPE phase tag at all -- must stay source_phase=false so the guide's positions line up with the target frame-by-frame). Non-zero only for older/experimental checkpoints.

guide_downscale_factor.tooltip: Encode at target_size/N instead of full res (cheaper VRAM). Must match whatever the checkpoint was trained with -- 1 for the no-downscale recipes, 2 for the earlier downscaled-guide recipes. Wrong value = positions the model never learned, not just a quality hit.

mask_video.tooltip: Per-frame replacement-region mask, same frame count/alignment as guide_video -- v13 expects a plain WHITE-on-black binary silhouette (person white, background black). Do NOT use a colored mask (see Color Mask node) -- confirmed to leak hue into the generated clothing during training. Also drives auto_mask_guide's black-out of guide_video. Leave unconnected to skip.

mask_source_id.tooltip: v13 recipe default: 0 (same non-tagged group as guide -- both need exact positional correspondence with the target). Non-zero only for older/experimental checkpoints.

mask_downscale_factor.tooltip: Same as guide_downscale_factor -- match the checkpoint's training recipe.

auto_mask_guide.tooltip: v13 requirement: paints guide_video BLACK wherever mask_video is white, before encoding -- an inpainting hole, so the model can't just copy guide's own person into the replacement region and must pull identity from identity_image instead (matches how the training data was built). Turn off only if guide_video is already pre-masked upstream.

mask_white_thresh.tooltip: auto_mask_guide only -- mask_video pixels with mean brightness >= this (0-1 scale) count as foreground (person) and get blacked out in guide.

identity_image.tooltip: Appearance reference (face/character), no positional correspondence with the target needed -- this is what fills auto_mask_guide's hole. Leave unconnected to skip.

identity_source_id.tooltip: v13 recipe default: 2. Nonzero = tagged with its own RoPE phase (matches source_phase=true, since identity has no positional correspondence with the target).

identity_downscale_factor.tooltip: Same as guide_downscale_factor -- match the checkpoint's training recipe.

identity_mask_image.tooltip: scail2-style color-pointer marker for the identity slot (small flat color dot/blob, NOT a body silhouette -- a body-shaped mask here would re-inject a competing pose signal, exactly the bug the flat-marker design fixes on the training side). Same source_id/phase as identity_image by default (they're trained as one group) -- override identity_mask_source_id if your checkpoint used a different grouping. Leave unconnected to skip.

identity_mask_source_id.tooltip: -1 = inherit identity_source_id/identity_phase_scale (matches training, where ref+ref_mask share one group). Set >=0 to give it its own separate phase.

identity_mask_downscale_factor.tooltip: -1 = inherit identity_downscale_factor. Same meaning otherwise as guide_downscale_factor -- match the checkpoint's training recipe.

crop_anchor.tooltip: Shared by all slots using ref_resize_mode=match_target with a mismatched aspect ratio -- which part of the source survives the crop.

reference_guidance_scale.tooltip: ST-DRC-style reference-CFG applied to the WHOLE combined reference set (all active slots together). 1.0 = off.

identity_temporal_offset_latents.tooltip: Temporal RoPE offset for appearance/reference tokens only, in VAE latent-time steps. 0 keeps the standard frame-0 placement used by existing LoRAs. -1 places the reference one latent step before frame 0 (normally -8 pixel frames), which can be tested to reduce overlap frame-0 reference leakage. Guide, mask, and target positions are never changed.

LTXMultipleControls.name: LTXMultipleControls
LTXMultipleControls.description: Guide + mask + identity + identity_mask reference conditioning in ONE node call, so all active slots' RoPE reference specs actually combine (chaining LTXIdentityOverlapConditioning nodes does NOT -- each call overwrites the previous one's specs). Every slot is optional and its own source_id/phase_scale/layout/ref_resize_mode -- nothing is hardcoded, only defaulted to match scail2v2_r128_v13 (guide=0, mask=0, both no-phase; identity=2, phased). guide_video is auto-masked black in the replacement region (auto_mask_guide) to match how v13 was trained -- this is the fix that made identity transfer actually work. identity_mask is unused by v13 (leave unconnected); kept for older checkpoints.

preamble.tooltip: Describes the WHOLE sequence -- setting, colour palette, lighting, overall camera grammar, mood. This is the paragraph that precedes 'Shot 1:' in the training captions. Leave empty to emit only the shot blocks.

image_1.tooltip: Reference keyframe for shot 1 (strata slot 0, source_id 2). Leave unconnected to end the sequence -- the slot is padded with the trained mid-gray blank.

shot_modifier_1.tooltip: Combines WITH the shot size (e.g. 'Over-the-shoulder' + 'Close-up' -> 'Over-the-shoulder close-up'). Not a size on its own.

action_1.tooltip: What happens in shot 1 -- subject, wardrobe, action, framing details. One or two sentences; the encoder caps the whole prompt at 1024 tokens.

image_2.tooltip: Reference keyframe for shot 2 (strata slot 1, source_id 3). Leave unconnected to end the sequence -- the slot is padded with the trained mid-gray blank.

shot_modifier_2.tooltip: Combines WITH the shot size (e.g. 'Over-the-shoulder' + 'Close-up' -> 'Over-the-shoulder close-up'). Not a size on its own.

action_2.tooltip: What happens in shot 2 -- subject, wardrobe, action, framing details. One or two sentences; the encoder caps the whole prompt at 1024 tokens.

image_3.tooltip: Reference keyframe for shot 3 (strata slot 2, source_id 4). Leave unconnected to end the sequence -- the slot is padded with the trained mid-gray blank.

shot_modifier_3.tooltip: Combines WITH the shot size (e.g. 'Over-the-shoulder' + 'Close-up' -> 'Over-the-shoulder close-up'). Not a size on its own.

action_3.tooltip: What happens in shot 3 -- subject, wardrobe, action, framing details. One or two sentences; the encoder caps the whole prompt at 1024 tokens.

image_4.tooltip: Reference keyframe for shot 4 (strata slot 3, source_id 5). Leave unconnected to end the sequence -- the slot is padded with the trained mid-gray blank.

shot_modifier_4.tooltip: Combines WITH the shot size (e.g. 'Over-the-shoulder' + 'Close-up' -> 'Over-the-shoulder close-up'). Not a size on its own.

action_4.tooltip: What happens in shot 4 -- subject, wardrobe, action, framing details. One or two sentences; the encoder caps the whole prompt at 1024 tokens.

LTXMultishotPrompt.name: LTXMultishotPrompt
LTXMultishotPrompt.description: Builds a ShotPlan-format multishot prompt plus the ordered, gray-padded reference batch for the multishot strata LoRA. Feed `references` into LTX Identity Transfer with layout='strata', source_id=2, phase_scale=1.0, and `prompt` into your LTX text encode.

LTXReferenceBypass.name: LTXReferenceBypass
LTXReferenceBypass.description: Clears any attached reference_latent from MODEL so downstream samplers run without memory injection. Useful between passes — e.g., apply Reference Conditioning for the primary generation pass, then route through Bypass before an upscale tiled sampler where memory isn't needed (and where the first-frame attention to memory tokens can introduce minor distortion).

target_latent.tooltip: Optional. Wire the same LATENT that goes into your sampler. The image will be resized in pixel space to match this latent's spatial dimensions before VAE encoding, guaranteeing memory and target have matching patches-per-frame. Without this, you'll get a tensor mismatch error if your image and target latent don't match exactly.

strength.tooltip: Scales the reference latent magnitude. 1.0 = native VAE output. <1.0 reduces influence; >1.0 boosts (may distort). Set to 0.0 to bypass completely and clear any prior reference state.

position_mode.tooltip: How reference tokens are positioned in the attention sequence. 'reference' (default): tokens overlap target's first frame temporally — uniform identity influence across all generated frames. 'prefix_continuous': tokens placed before target temporally — equivalent to standard i2v prior-context conditioning.

verbose.tooltip: Print detailed per-call info to the console. Useful for debugging. Disable for normal use.

LTXReferenceConditioning.name: LTXReferenceConditioning
LTXReferenceConditioning.description: Encodes an image through the LTX2 video VAE and attaches the resulting latent to the MODEL as a reference for prefix injection during sampling. Requires LTX Reference Enable upstream. Works on any LTX2.3 checkpoint (vanilla, Echo, merged variants). Complementary to standard i2v latent conditioning and existing latent_anchor/likeness_anchor approaches — these are different intervention points and can be combined.

zero_ref_timesteps.tooltip: Mark reference tokens as sigma=0 (clean reference). Default OFF based on empirical testing — most LTX2.3 checkpoints (including Echo's released T2V) produce better output when reference tokens share target's noise sigma. Enable only if a checkpoint was trained for clean-reference memory.

verbose.tooltip: Enable detailed per-call logging. Useful for debugging the first time you wire up this node. Disable for normal use to keep the console clean.

LTXReferenceEnable.name: LTXReferenceEnable
LTXReferenceEnable.description: Patches LTX2.3-AV models to accept a reference latent that gets prepended to the video token sequence inside the transformer. Works as a complementary identity-injection mechanism — most useful combined with standard i2v frame_0 latent conditioning. Pair with LTX Reference Conditioning to attach an image. The patches activate only when a reference latent is provided; safe passthrough otherwise.

image_1.tooltip: Reference for slot 1 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 1>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots renumber in order, so wiring 1 and 3 makes them <Image 1> and <Image 2>.

image_2.tooltip: Reference for slot 2 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 2>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots renumber in order, so wiring 1 and 3 makes them <Image 1> and <Image 2>.

image_3.tooltip: Reference for slot 3 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 3>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots renumber in order, so wiring 1 and 3 makes them <Image 1> and <Image 2>.

image_4.tooltip: Reference for slot 4 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 4>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots renumber in order, so wiring 1 and 3 makes them <Image 1> and <Image 2>.

image_5.tooltip: Reference for slot 5 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 5>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots renumber in order, so wiring 1 and 3 makes them <Image 1> and <Image 2>.

image_6.tooltip: Reference for slot 6 — the subject your prompt calls <Image 6>. Leave unconnected to skip; connected slots renumber in order, so wiring 1 and 3 makes them <Image 1> and <Image 2>.

LTXReferenceImages.name: LTXReferenceImages
LTXReferenceImages.description: Collects up to six reference images, in slot order, for LTX Multi Reference Slots. Images of different sizes are fine — each keeps its own.

LTXReferenceProbe.name: LTXReferenceProbe
LTXReferenceProbe.description: Inspects a MODEL after LTX Reference Enable + Conditioning to verify wiring. Reports patch status, reference latent presence and shape, position mode. Use before the sampler to catch config issues without running a generation.

images.tooltip: Multi-frame IMAGE input (a video frame sequence). Use a Load Video, image batch, or upstream frame producer.

target_latent.tooltip: Optional. Wire the same LATENT going to your sampler. Frames will be resized in pixel space to match this latent's spatial dims before VAE encoding.

start_frame.tooltip: Which frame in the input sequence to start the reference window at. Frames before this are discarded.

num_frames.tooltip: How many frames from start_frame to use as reference. Default 9 (1 + 8k matches LTX2 temporal compression — gives ~2 latent frames). 17, 25 also valid for more temporal context at higher cost.

strength.tooltip: Scales the reference latent magnitude. 0.0 bypasses and clears state.

position_mode.tooltip: 'reference': memory positions overlap target's first frames. 'prefix_continuous': memory positions precede target temporally.

verbose.tooltip: Print detailed per-call info to the console.

LTXReferenceSequenceConditioning.name: LTXReferenceSequenceConditioning
LTXReferenceSequenceConditioning.description: Multi-frame variant of LTX Reference Conditioning. Takes a frame-sequence IMAGE input and uses a chosen N-frame window as reference. Multi-frame reference can capture motion and temporal style that single-image reference can't.

subject_1.tooltip: What reference image 1 is, as a short noun phrase — 'the woman', 'the red sports car'. Becomes '<Image 1> is <this>.'. Leave empty to skip.

subject_2.tooltip: What reference image 2 is, as a short noun phrase — 'the woman', 'the red sports car'. Becomes '<Image 2> is <this>.'. Leave empty to skip.

subject_5.tooltip: What reference image 5 is, as a short noun phrase — 'the woman', 'the red sports car'. Becomes '<Image 5> is <this>.'. Leave empty to skip.

subject_6.tooltip: What reference image 6 is, as a short noun phrase — 'the woman', 'the red sports car'. Becomes '<Image 6> is <this>.'. Leave empty to skip.

scene.tooltip: The scene description, appended after the declarations. Refer back to the subjects by tag here ("<Image 1> hands <Image 2> a cup") — a tag that only ever appears in the declaration has to carry both jobs at once, which is a harder association for the model to use.

LTXReferenceTags.name: LTXReferenceTags
LTXReferenceTags.description: Assembles '<Image 1> is the woman. <Image 2> is the man. <scene>'. Order matters: tag N must describe the image wired into reference_N on the slots node, and must match the convention the checkpoint was trained with. Describe the subjects DISTINCTLY — two references both called 'the woman' carry no information about which is which.

LTXSequencer.name: LTXSequencer
LTXSequencer.description: Add multiple guide images at specified frame indices or seconds with strengths. Number of widgets is dynamically configured.

LTXTextAttentionAmplifier.name: LTXTextAttentionAmplifier
LTXTextAttentionAmplifier.description: Amplifies LTX2 text cross-attention (attn2) per block to compensate for conditioning dilution at upscaled token counts. Use during upscale-pass sampling to recover prompt adherence and color stability.

noise.tooltip: Noise generator from RandomNoise or similar. Wire from your existing noise source.

guider.tooltip: CFG/STG guider wrapping the model. Wire from BasicGuider, CFGGuider, or LTX's STG guider.

sampler.tooltip: Sampling algorithm. euler_ancestral_cfg_pp recommended for LTX2 distilled CFG=1 setups.

sigmas.tooltip: Noise schedule. Typical upscale-pass schedule starts moderate (e.g. 0.85) with 3 active steps.

latent_image.tooltip: Input latent. For upscale-pass refinement, this is typically the output of an upsampler.

bypass_tiling.tooltip: If True, route directly to standard single-pass sampling (video+audio together via wrapper). Equivalent to having no tiling at all. Useful for A/B comparison, small inputs that don't need tiling, or debugging whether issues are tile-related or sampling-related.

tile_axis.tooltip: Which spatial axis to tile along. 'auto' picks the longer axis (best for typical portrait/landscape aspects). Override to force tiling along H (vertical splits) or W (horizontal splits).

n_tiles.tooltip: Number of tiles along the chosen axis. Default 2 (split in halves) suits most aspect ratios. n_tiles=1 effectively disables tiling. Raise to 3-4 for very large outputs (4K+) along one axis.

tile_overlap.tooltip: Overlap between adjacent tiles in latent tokens. Default 8 reliably hides seams. Reduce only if memory is constrained; smaller overlaps risk visible seams.

max_size_for_no_tile.tooltip: Auto-skip tiling if the chosen-axis latent size is at or below this. 24 ≈ 768 pixels at 32x VAE compression, well within model's comfort zone. Inputs at or below this skip tiling and run a single normal sampling pass.

audio_pass.tooltip: How to handle audio when input is video+audio wrapper. 'passthrough' (default): preserve original audio unchanged. 'tile_carrying': audio rides along with one chosen tile's sampling for proper video-audio cross-attention (lipsync). No extra sampling steps.

audio_carrier_tile.tooltip: Which tile carries the audio when audio_pass=tile_carrying. 'first': top tile (ideal for vertical talking-face content where speaker is in upper half). 'middle': center tile (best for large outputs where subject is centered). 'last': bottom tile.

debug.tooltip: Verbose per-tile diagnostic output. Helpful first time using the node to verify it's operating as expected.

LTXTiledSampler.name: LTXTiledSampler
LTXTiledSampler.description: Spatially-tiled drop-in for SamplerCustomAdvanced for LTX2 upscale-pass light refinement. Each tile runs full sampling at training-distribution token count, then cosine-blends. Use only for light denoise. Audio passthrough by default; tile_carrying runs audio sampling alongside one chosen tile (no extra steps). Set bypass_tiling=True to act as a transparent passthrough to standard single-pass sampling (video+audio together), useful for debugging or when no tiling is desired.

positive.tooltip: Positive conditioning the keyframes are attached to.

negative.tooltip: Negative conditioning the keyframes are attached to.

vae.tooltip: Only used to read the latent scale factors.

latent.tooltip: Plain 5D video latent to generate keyframes alongside. Add them before Concat AV Latent.

interval_frames.tooltip: Pixel-frame stride for auto placement. Default 24 is about one keyframe per second at 24 fps. Occupied pixels are skipped. Ignored when frame_indices is set.

keyframes.tooltip: Optional content to initialize the new keyframes with. Connect keyframes from an earlier Separate (same spatial size), or a plain video latent to copy the nearest frame at each new slot (e.g. after temporal upscale). These are still denoised, not pinned as guides. Recorded indices on a keyframes latent are ignored unless frame_indices is set. Only has an effect when sampling starts below sigma 1.

frame_indices.tooltip: Optional pixel-frame indices. Leave empty to place from interval_frames on the current canvas. When set, this list is the placement (connected keyframes are matched in order). The last frame is allowed; frame 0 is not (it is already a standalone token).

output_tooltips: Positive conditioning with generated-keyframe attention attached.
Negative conditioning with generated-keyframe attention attached.
Video latent with generated keyframes appended on T.
LTXVAddGeneratedKeyframes.name: LTXVAddGeneratedKeyframes
LTXVAddGeneratedKeyframes.description: Append detailing keyframes to a video latent. Each keyframe is one latent frame of tokens whose RoPE position spans a single pixel frame; they are denoised with the video and are not part of the decoded output. Placement is one slot every interval_frames pixels, skipping I2V frames, existing guides, and detailing keyframes already on the cond. Connected keyframes are content only and are re-placed on this canvas unless frame_indices is set. Pull them back out with LTXV Separate Generated Keyframes. Requires a checkpoint trained for generated keyframes (one carrying keyframes_abs_pos_embedding).

image.tooltip: Image or video to condition the latent video on. Must be 8*n + 1 frames. If the video is not 8*n + 1 frames, it will be cropped to the nearest 8*n + 1 frames.

frame_idx.tooltip: Frame index to start the conditioning at. For single-frame images or videos with 1-8 frames, any frame_idx value is acceptable. For videos with 9+ frames, frame_idx must be divisible by 8, otherwise it will be rounded down to the nearest multiple of 8. Negative values are counted from the end of the video.

attention_mask.tooltip: Optional pixel-space spatial mask. Controls per-region conditioning influence via self-attention, multiplied by strength.

iclora_parameters.tooltip: Optional IC-LoRA parameters from a Get IC-LoRA Parameters node. Used for adjusting guide processing as required by certain IC-LoRAs (eg. those with a reference_downscale_factor > 1). When chained, each LTXVAddGuide uses only the parameters connected to it.

negative.tooltip: Negative conditioning to which guide keyframe info will be added

latent.tooltip: Video latent, guides are added to the end of this latent

num_guides.tooltip: Select how many guide images to use
