LTXVAddGuideMulti.name: LTXVAddGuideMulti
LTXVAddGuideMulti.description: Add multiple guide images at specified frame indices with strengths, uses DynamicCombo which requires ComfyUI 0.8.1 and frontend 1.33.4 or later.

images.tooltip: Batch of images - non-black images will be used as guides

strength.tooltip: Strength for all guides.

LTXVAddGuidesFromBatch.name: LTXVAddGuidesFromBatch
LTXVAddGuidesFromBatch.description: Adds multiple guide images from a batch to the latent at corresponding frame indices. Non-black images in the batch are used as guides.

latent.tooltip: Target video latent the guide is pinned onto.

guiding_latent.tooltip: Guide latent. Its spatial size must divide the target's by the same whole number on both axes; equal size pins it as-is, half size is treated as an x2 IC-LoRA reference.

latent_idx.tooltip: Latent frame index to start the guide at, counted in latent frames rather than pixel frames. Negative values place the guide on frames before the start of the latent, not counted back from its end.

strength.tooltip: Capped at 1.0. A dilated guide marks its padding positions with a negative denoise mask so the model drops them; above 1.0 the kept positions would go negative too and the whole guide would be dropped. Amplify beyond 1.0 with attention_mask instead.

attention_mask.tooltip: Optional pixel-space spatial mask. Controls per-region conditioning influence via self-attention, multiplied by strength.

LTXVAddLatentGuide.name: LTXVAddLatentGuide
LTXVAddLatentGuide.description: Pins an already-encoded latent as a guide, for when the guide comes out of an earlier stage rather than an image. Same effect as LTXV Add Guide without the VAE decode/encode round trip. A guide that is spatially smaller than the target (an IC-LoRA or detailing reference) is dilated onto a sparse grid, and its RoPE end positions are expanded by the same ratio so it covers the target canvas instead of addressing only the top-left corner of it.

samples.tooltip: The latent to be decoded.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model used for decoding the latent.

audio.tooltip: The audio to be encoded.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model to use for encoding.

video_start_time.tooltip: Start time in seconds for the video mask.

video_end_time.tooltip: End time in seconds for the video mask.

audio_start_time.tooltip: Start time in seconds for the audio mask.

audio_end_time.tooltip: End time in seconds for the audio mask.

max_length.tooltip: 'truncate': cut latent to end_time length. 'pad': extend latent to end_time. 'partial': mask range within existing latent.

existing_mask_mode.tooltip: How to combine with existing noise masks if present. 'add' will take the max of existing and new mask, 'overwrite' will replace with new mask. 'subtract' will set the masked region to 0 instead of 1, effectively unmasking it.

LTXVAudioVideoMask.name: LTXVAudioVideoMask
LTXVAudioVideoMask.description: Creates noise masks for video and audio latents based on specified time ranges. New content is generated within these masked regions

chunks.tooltip: Number of chunks to split the feedforward activations into to reduce peak VRAM usage.

dim_threshold.tooltip: Dimension threshold above which to apply chunking.

LTXVChunkFeedForward.name: LTXVChunkFeedForward
LTXVChunkFeedForward.description: EXPERIMENTAL AND MAY CHANGE THE MODEL OUTPUT!! Chunks feedforward activations to reduce peak VRAM usage.

LTXVConcatAVLatent.name: LTXVConcatAVLatent
LTXVConcatAVLatent.description: Merge a video latent and an audio latent into a joint AV latent (any AV model, e.g. LTXV or MiniMax H3).

model.tooltip: The model to apply context windows to during sampling.

context_length.tooltip: The length of the context window in real frames. Must be 8*n + 1.

context_overlap.tooltip: The overlap of the context window in real frames.

context_schedule.tooltip: Step-dependent scheduling algorithm for context windows.

context_stride.tooltip: The stride of the context window; only applicable to uniform schedules.

closed_loop.tooltip: Whether to close the context window loop; only applicable to looped schedules.

fuse_method.tooltip: The method to use to fuse the context windows.

freenoise.tooltip: Whether to apply FreeNoise noise shuffling, improves window blending.

retain_first_frame.tooltip: Retain the first latent frame in every context window (may help retain initial reference).

split_conds_to_windows.tooltip: Whether to split multiple conditionings (created by ConditionCombine) to each window based on region index.

output_tooltips: The model with context windows applied during sampling.
LTXVContextWindows.name: LTXVContextWindows
LTXVContextWindows.description: Set context windows for LTXV-like models.

LTXVDualCFGGuider.name: LTXVDualCFGGuider
LTXVDualCFGGuider.description: Separate CFG scales for the video and audio modalities of a packed LTXV-AV latent.

LTXVDurationPredictor.name: LTXVDurationPredictor
LTXVDurationPredictor.description: Predicts the natural shot duration for a prompt using the LTX 2.4 duration head (loaded with ModelPatchLoader), and snaps it to the VAE's 8k+1 frame grid.

guider.tooltip: Provides CFG/STG sampling settings. Its conds are overridden per chunk.

temporal_tile_size.tooltip: Temporal tile size in pixel frames.

lora_name.tooltip: Edit Anything LoRA. Used to load role_embedding + ref_adaln_proj weights. Leave on (none) if passing editanything_module instead.

editanything_module.tooltip: Alternative to lora_name: sidecar module from LTXV Edit Anything Module Loader.

ref_image.tooltip: Reference image (appearance anchor). Required for IC-LoRA ref tokens / AdaLN.

guide_frames.tooltip: Guide video frames (structure/motion). VAE-encoded internally, then sliced per chunk.

enable_ic_lora.tooltip: Append ref + guide_slice as IC-LoRA clean tokens per chunk.

enable_role_embedding.tooltip: Sum role_embedding bias onto IC-LoRA ref tokens. Must match training config `use_visual_ref_role_embedding`. stage2_ref_visual_adaln_crossattn was trained with this DISABLED.

reapply_per_chunk.tooltip: If True: append ref + (sliced) guide tokens on every chunk. If False: only on chunk 0; later chunks inherit no IC-LoRA append.

enable_visual_crossattn.tooltip: Auto-detect ref_visual_proj + ref_attn LoRA keys in the checkpoint and enable the visual cross-attention path (stage2_ref_visual_adaln_crossattn).

ref_context_scale.tooltip: Scale for ref_attn output added to each block. Training default for video_to_video_ref_visual_adaln is 0.01 (very conservative).

ref_token_scale.tooltip: Scale applied to projected visual memory tokens before cross-attn. stage2_ref_visual_adaln_crossattn was trained with 0.25.

ref_start_block.tooltip: First transformer block that consumes visual ref tokens (training default 12).

ref_end_block.tooltip: Last transformer block that consumes visual ref tokens (training default 35).

ref_init_from.tooltip: How to initialize ref_attn before applying its LoRA. CRITICAL: must match the training config `init_ref_attn_from`. stage2_ref_visual_adaln_crossattn was trained with 'attn2'.

ref_init_seed.tooltip: Seed for random ref_attn init when ref_init_from='none'. Ignored otherwise.

ref_attn_lora_strength.tooltip: Strength multiplier for the ref_attn LoRA deltas.

ref_temporal_offset_latents.tooltip: Temporal RoPE offset for appearance/reference tokens only, in VAE latent-time steps. 0 keeps the standard frame-0 placement used by existing LoRAs. -1 places the reference one latent step before frame 0 (normally -8 pixel frames), which can be tested to reduce overlap frame-0 reference leakage. Guide, mask, and target positions are never changed.

batch_size.tooltip: The number of latent audio samples in the batch.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model to get configuration from.

latent.tooltip: Only used to get the latent count
Video or audio latent to freeze. Audio is 4D; video is 5D.

LTXVFreezeLatent.name: LTXVFreezeLatent
LTXVFreezeLatent.description: Set noise_mask to 0 so this latent is kept clean during sampling. Works on video or audio. Typical uses: freeze audio before Concat AV so it only provides cross-attention, or freeze any latent that should not be denoised.

latent.tooltip: The target video latent to add the guides to, e.g. the temporally upscaled one.

keyframes.tooltip: The keyframes output of LTXV Separate Generated Keyframes, which carries the pixel frame index each keyframe was generated at.

strength.tooltip: Guide strength. 1.0 is a hard pin; lower values relax it.

override_frame_indices.tooltip: Optional — pin at these pixel frames instead of the recorded (or auto-scaled) positions. Provide one index per keyframe. Leave empty to reuse recorded positions, or to scale them when the target canvas is a different length (e.g. after temporal x2).

LTXVGeneratedKeyframesToGuides.name: LTXVGeneratedKeyframesToGuides
LTXVGeneratedKeyframesToGuides.description: Pin generated keyframes from an earlier stage as frozen image guides on a later canvas. They are decoded as standalone frames, resized if needed, and written with noise_mask=0 so they are not denoised again. After a temporal upscale, recorded indices are scaled from the canvas they were generated on onto this one (same moments). Use override_frame_indices to set positions explicitly. To keep generating (and denoising) keyframes at new positions, use Add Generated Keyframes instead.

LTXVImgToVideoInplaceKJ.name: LTXVImgToVideoInplaceKJ
LTXVImgToVideoInplaceKJ.description: Replaces video latent frames with the encoded input images, uses DynamicCombo which requires ComfyUI 0.8.1 and frontend 1.33.4 or later.

compare_noise_mask.tooltip: If True, also reports diff stats restricted to the noisy region of latent_a (where noise_mask > 0).

LTXVLatentUpsamplerTiled.name: LTXVLatentUpsamplerTiled
LTXVLatentUpsamplerTiled.description: Tiled drop-in replacement for LTXVLatentUpsampler. Solves color shifts and distortion at extreme aspect ratios by processing the upscale in spatial tiles with cosine-windowed overlap blending. Output is virtually identical to non-tiled in safe-aspect cases, free of upscale-model instability in extreme cases.

LTXVModalityGuidance.name: LTXVModalityGuidance
LTXVModalityGuidance.description: Cross-modal (audio-video) guidance for LTXV-AV. Runs one extra forward pass per step with the a2v/v2a cross-attention severed, then pushes the result toward the coupled prediction - strengthening audio-visual sync (e.g. lip-sync). Reference default modality_scale is 3.0. Stacks with the dual-CFG guider and STG. Set to 1.0 to disable (no extra pass).

img_compression.tooltip: Amount of compression to apply on image.

reference_audio.tooltip: Reference audio clip whose speaker identity to transfer. ~5 seconds recommended (training duration). Shorter or longer clips may degrade voice identity transfer.

audio_vae.tooltip: LTXV Audio VAE for encoding.

identity_guidance_scale.tooltip: Strength of identity guidance. Runs an extra forward pass without reference each step to amplify speaker identity. Set to 0 to disable (no extra pass).

start_percent.tooltip: Start of the sigma range where identity guidance is active.

end_percent.tooltip: End of the sigma range where identity guidance is active.

LTXVReferenceAudio.name: LTXVReferenceAudio
LTXVReferenceAudio.description: Set reference audio for ID-LoRA speaker identity transfer. Encodes a reference audio clip into the conditioning and optionally patches the model with identity guidance (extra forward pass without reference, amplifying the speaker identity effect).

stretch.tooltip: Stretch the sigmas to be in the range [terminal, 1].

terminal.tooltip: The terminal value of the sigmas after stretching.

LTXVSeparateAVLatent.name: LTXVSeparateAVLatent
LTXVSeparateAVLatent.description: Split a joint AV latent into its video and audio latents (any AV model, e.g. LTXV or MiniMax H3).

keyframes_to_batch.tooltip: Return the keyframes as a batch of single-frame latents. Leave off to get them as one multi-frame latent, which is what the latent upsampler and a later Add Generated Keyframes expect.

output_tooltips: Positive conditioning with generated-keyframe metadata removed.
Negative conditioning with generated-keyframe metadata removed.
Video latent with the generated keyframes stripped.

The peeled keyframes, labeled with generated_keyframe_indices and generated_keyframe_num_frames. Feed these to a later Add Generated Keyframes to initialize new slots, or to Generated Keyframes To Guides to pin them as frozen image guides (indices are remapped if the canvas length changed).
LTXVSeparateGeneratedKeyframes.name: LTXVSeparateGeneratedKeyframes
LTXVSeparateGeneratedKeyframes.description: Split the generated keyframes added by LTXV Add Generated Keyframes back out of a sampled latent, and remove them from the conditioning. Separate them before spatially upscaling the video latent. Do not run LTXV Crop Guides first — it treats generated keyframes as disposable guides and drops them.

blocks.tooltip: Comma-separated transformer block indices to perturb.

LTXVSpatioTemporalGuidance.name: LTXVSpatioTemporalGuidance
LTXVSpatioTemporalGuidance.description: Runs one extra pass per step with the self-attention of the selected blocks degraded to a value-passthrough, then guides away from it - improving spatial detail and motion coherence.

image.tooltip: Image batch to grade.

lut_path.tooltip: Filesystem path to an Adobe .cube LUT (1D or 3D).

strength.tooltip: Blend factor between the original (0) and graded (1) image.

LUTApplyMEC.name: LUTApplyMEC
LUTApplyMEC.description: Apply a .cube LUT (Adobe format, 1D or 3D) with optional strength blend.
output_tooltips: LUT-graded image (alpha kept).
JSON metadata describing LUT dim, size, and strength.

width.tooltip: Width of the output image

height.tooltip: Height of the output image

Latent Lerp (mtb).name: Latent Lerp (mtb)
Latent Lerp (mtb).description: Linear interpolation (blend) between two latent vectors

start_percent.tooltip: Start applying the operation at this fraction of the model's denoising schedule. 0 is the beginning.

end_percent.tooltip: Stop applying the operation at this fraction of the model's denoising schedule. 1 is the end.

self_correction.tooltip: Performs a final low-denoise polishing pass to fix small artifacts.

cfg_mode.tooltip: Constant: fixed CFG. Linear: straight transition to CFG Finish. Ease Down: fast move toward CFG Pivot, then gentle settle to CFG Finish.

cfg_finish.tooltip: Target CFG value at the final step. Only used when CFG Mode is not Constant.

cfg_pivot.tooltip: CFG value the curve moves toward quickly before settling to CFG Finish. Only used in Ease Down mode. When CFG > CFG Finish, the curve drops fast toward this value. When CFG < CFG Finish, it rises fast toward it.

LatentCrossFadeAutoConcat.name: LatentCrossFadeAutoConcat
LatentCrossFadeAutoConcat.description: Auto spatial match + temporal concat with optional cross-fade.

steps.tooltip: Number of steps to apply TTM inpainting for.

mask.tooltip: Latent mask where white (1.0) is the area to inpaint and black (0.0) is the area to keep unchanged.

LatentMotionRetime.name: LatentMotionRetime
LatentMotionRetime.description: Attenuate motion amplitude to correct 24->30fps pacing on an upsampled latent.

LatentMotionSharpener.name: LatentMotionSharpener
LatentMotionSharpener.description: Adaptive sharpening proportional to inter-frame motion magnitude.

edit_model_flux2klein.tooltip: Enable ReferenceLatent-style conditioning for edit models

strength.tooltip: 0 leaves the latent unchanged; 1 matches the resized reference latent.

LatentOperationBlend.name: LatentOperationBlend
LatentOperationBlend.description: Blend the entire latent toward the reference latent, resizing the reference with nearest-neighbor interpolation when needed.

maintain_aspect_ratio.tooltip: If Enabled: Crops edges slightly to fit grid without stretching.

crop_x.tooltip: Crop, as a fraction of the frame (x, y, width, height; 0, 0, 1, 1 = no crop). Set it with the Crop tool in the player; custom_width / custom_height then resize the cropped frame.

crop_y.tooltip: Crop, as a fraction of the frame (x, y, width, height; 0, 0, 1, 1 = no crop). Set it with the Crop tool in the player; custom_width / custom_height then resize the cropped frame.

crop_h.tooltip: Crop, as a fraction of the frame (x, y, width, height; 0, 0, 1, 1 = no crop). Set it with the Crop tool in the player; custom_width / custom_height then resize the cropped frame.

decoder.tooltip: auto: the fast path only where it is faster with the same colour - measured, that is the exact reader on the tested machine. fast: ffmpeg decodes 8-bit 4:2:0 video (the same frames; on an NVIDIA GPU the colour conversion runs there, mean 0.5/255 from the exact reader). exact: the frame-accurate PyAV reader (10-bit, HDR, alpha, ProRes and image sequences always use it).

seconds_cap.tooltip: Load at most this many seconds after skip_first_frames (0 = no limit), at the force_rate rate when set. Works with frame_load_cap: the smaller one wins, and a format preset then snaps the count.

resolution.tooltip: Output size by its LONGEST side, keeping the aspect: 2160p is 3840, 1080p is 1920. custom uses custom_width / custom_height (0 = keep the source size or follow the aspect). source ignores them. proxy 1/2, 1/4, 1/8: the source (after the crop) at that fraction of its size, read straight at that size for a fast, light look-dev pass; video_info and info record the full size.

divisible_by.tooltip: Round both output dimensions to a multiple of this. A format preset or a VAE may raise it.

audio_when_missing.tooltip: When the file has no audio: silence outputs a silent track as long as the loaded frames (what the loader always did, so downstream nodes keep working); none outputs nothing.

handles.tooltip: Handles = extra frames for a video model to settle on, added here and trimmed off again by Save Video (C2C) (it reads them from video_info). fit: pad the clip UP to the model's frame grid (handle_target = frames you want out, 0 = this clip's length). add: put handle_frames on, rounded onto the grid. Repeated edge frames, never black; the audio moves with them.

handle_frames.tooltip: add: frames to put on (side both: on EACH end). With a grid, 0 = just enough to land on it.

handle_target.tooltip: fit: how many frames you want out after the trim. 0 = this clip's own length.

handle_side.tooltip: Which end gets the handles. head is where a video model settles; both splits them.

handle_grid.tooltip: The model's frame grid: 'from format' uses the format preset above (MiniMax H3 17n+5, Wan 4n+1, LTXV 8n+1 ...), so there is one grid, not two; or pick one here.

handle_custom_step.tooltip: custom grid: step (frames = step * n + plus).

colorspace_in.tooltip: The colour space this file was rendered in. auto: read it from the file (a .colorspace / .c2c.json sidecar, the EXR colorInteropID or chromaticities, the DPX or movie colour tags). An EXR with none is the OCIO config's scene_linear role (Nuke's working space); an untagged movie or image is display. Pick a space to override. off: no colour management (what the loader always did).

working_space.tooltip: What the frames are converted to for the models. sRGB display: a Rec.709 / sRGB source stays as it is; anything else goes through the config's view (tone-mapped: ACES 2.0 SDR in the built-in config, what Nuke's viewer shows). Save Video (C2C) reverses exactly this. preserve source: no conversion.

name_prefix.tooltip: Save Video (C2C) on 'auto (from Load)' names its file name_prefix + this clip's name + name_suffix, e.g. proj_ + shot010 + _comp; with the version folder the name carries the folder's version. Empty = nothing added. Typing a name on Save wins.

name_suffix.tooltip: Save Video (C2C) on 'auto (from Load)' names its file name_prefix + this clip's name + name_suffix, e.g. proj_ + shot010 + _comp; with the version folder the name carries the folder's version. Empty = nothing added. Typing a name on Save wins.

extra_handles.tooltip: More handles on top of fit / add, in whole steps of the model's frame grid (MiniMax H3 17, Wan 4, LTX 8 ...), so the clip stays on the grid; on handle_side (both splits them). The details line shows k x step = frames and the total. Save Video (C2C) trims them with the rest.

location.tooltip: Where the source is. input folder: pick or upload it in 'video'. server path: type any path in 'path' (a clip, an image, a folder or a pattern like shot.####.exr) - what Load Video Path (C2C) did.

path.tooltip: server path mode: a clip, an image, an EXR, a folder of images, or a sequence pattern (shot.####.exr, shot.%04d.exr, shot.$F4.exr, shot.[1001-1100].exr). One frame of a sequence finds the whole sequence.

source_mode.tooltip: auto: a movie is a movie; a numbered image finds its sequence; a lone image is one frame. Force it when that guess is wrong: single image / single EXR loads exactly one file even when it has siblings (frame_range picks which frame of a sequence).

sequence_fps.tooltip: Rate of an image sequence or still. 0 = the file's own rate (EXR FramesPerSecond, DPX frame rate), else 24. A still is one frame at this rate - never a longer clip.

frame_range.tooltip: Source frame NUMBERS (Nuke style): 1001-1100, 1001-1100x2 (every 2nd), or one frame like 1050. Empty = all. For a movie, frame numbers count from 0.

reverse.tooltip: Play the selected frames last to first (the audio too).

frame_offset.tooltip: Shifts the frame numbers frame_map reports for the output (where frame 0 lands on your timeline). The pixels do not move.

missing_frames.tooltip: A frame inside the sequence's range with no file. error (default) stops and names them; black, hold previous and nearest fill the gap and say so in info; skip (as before) drops it - every later frame then plays early.

edge_policy.tooltip: frame_range beyond the first / last frame: hold repeats the edge frame, black adds black frames, loop wraps, bounce plays back and forth, error stops.

exr_layer.tooltip: The EXR layer the IMAGE shows: auto (the beauty / rgba), or a layer name from info - diffuse, depth, N, P, crypto00 ... Data layers (depth, normals, position, motion) load as raw values, never colour-converted. exr_passes carries every layer.

MMH3FunControlnetParams.name: MMH3FunControlnetParams
MMH3FunControlnetParams.description: Bundle Fun ControlNet settings for the 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale' node. Provide the ControlNet-Union checkpoint, a VAE (required to encode the control video into the model's latent space), the control video at its ORIGINAL low resolution, and the target upscale size. The main node crops and upscales the control video per chunk/tile automatically, so each tile is guided toward its own region of the source video. 'control_upscale_mode' controls how the low-res control frames are upscaled in batches to trade peak memory against up-front work.

'step': count of sampling steps from the start, expressed as a half-open [start_step, end_step) range. start_step 0 means the guidance applies from the very first step and end_step is exclusive, so end_step 1 means it applies for the first step only and later steps re-generate the seams freely.

start_percent.tooltip: [percent mode] Denoising fraction at which the inpaint guidance starts applying (0.0 = the start of denoising). Ignored in step mode.

end_percent.tooltip: [percent mode] Denoising fraction at which the inpaint guidance stops applying (1.0 = the end of denoising). Ignored in step mode.

start_step.tooltip: [step mode] Sampling step at which the inpaint guidance starts applying (0 = the very first step). Ignored in percent mode.

end_step.tooltip: [step mode] Exclusive upper step bound: the guidance applies for steps from start_step up to but NOT including end_step. So start 0 / end 1 gates only the first step, and end 2 gates the first two steps; later steps re-generate the seams freely. Clamped to the piece's total step count. Ignored in percent mode.

output_tooltips: Spatial seam inpaint settings consumed by 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale'.
MMH3SpatialInpaintParams.name: MMH3SpatialInpaintParams
MMH3SpatialInpaintParams.description: Bundle Fun ControlNet inpaint settings for the 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale' node's spatial split. On every non-first tile the overlap strips are pinned to the already-sampled neighbour content directly in latent space: the accumulated latent's kept strips feed the controlnet's masked_latent channel and the spatial fade mask doubles as the visibility channel, so no pixel decode/re-encode round-trip is needed. Eliminates the visible seam between tiles. Requires the spatial split to be active; stackable with the Fun ControlNet params.

upscale_width.tooltip: [rows_cols mode] Overall upscaled frame WIDTH in PIXELS that gets split into grid_cols equal-size tile columns. Must be a multiple of 32 and must match the width set in 'MMH3 Latent Upscale Params'. Ignored in specific_size mode.

upscale_height.tooltip: [rows_cols mode] Overall upscaled frame HEIGHT in PIXELS that gets split into grid_rows equal-size tile rows. Must be a multiple of 32 and must match the height set in 'MMH3 Latent Upscale Params'. Ignored in specific_size mode.

tile_size_mode.tooltip: How the tile size is determined. 'specific_size' (default): use tile_width/tile_height below. 'rows_cols': split the frame given by upscale_width/upscale_height into grid_rows x grid_cols EQUAL-SIZE tiles (edge tiles included) - the per-axis overlap is auto-solved so every tile ends up exactly the same size; errors out if the solved tiles would be smaller than min_tile_size.

tile_width.tooltip: [specific_size mode] Tile width in PIXELS at the (upscaled) chunk resolution. Must be a multiple of 32.

tile_height.tooltip: [specific_size mode] Tile height in PIXELS at the (upscaled) chunk resolution. Must be a multiple of 32.

grid_rows.tooltip: [rows_cols mode] Number of tile ROWS along the height axis (1-9).

grid_cols.tooltip: [rows_cols mode] Number of tile COLUMNS along the width axis (1-9).

spatial_w_overlap.tooltip: Horizontal overlap in PIXELS between neighbouring tiles. Must be a multiple of 32 and smaller than the tile width. In rows_cols mode this is the DESIRED overlap; the node auto-solves the actual value (multiple of 16px, the H3 latent token) so all tiles stay equal. If the solved tile size would not be a multiple of 32 (the model's 2x2 latent patch grid, which eliminates seams), the overlap is automatically increased by 32px and the tiles re-solved at the next valid 32px grid alignment.

spatial_h_overlap.tooltip: Vertical overlap in PIXELS between neighbouring tiles. Must be a multiple of 32 and smaller than the tile height. In rows_cols mode this is the DESIRED overlap; the node auto-solves the actual value (multiple of 16px, the H3 latent token) so all tiles stay equal. If the solved tile size would not be a multiple of 32 (the model's 2x2 latent patch grid, which eliminates seams), the overlap is automatically increased by 32px and the tiles re-solved at the next valid 32px grid alignment.

fade_width.tooltip: Width in PIXELS of the FADE segment (mask 0->1) at the interior edge of the overlap band. The overlap band splits into a FROZEN segment (seam side, mask=0, keeps the neighbour's content) + this FADE segment (interior side). fade_width sets the fade length; the frozen segment takes the rest (overlap - fade). Default 32. Set to 0 to freeze the entire overlap strip. Clamped to the solved overlap in rows_cols mode.

fade_height.tooltip: Height in PIXELS of the FADE segment (mask 0->1) at the interior edge of the overlap band. The overlap band splits into a FROZEN segment (seam side, mask=0, keeps the neighbour's content) + this FADE segment (interior side). fade_height sets the fade length; the frozen segment takes the rest (overlap - fade). Default 32. Set to 0 to freeze the entire overlap strip. Clamped to the solved overlap in rows_cols mode.

min_tile_size.tooltip: Minimum PIXEL size of edge tiles. If a leftover edge tile would be smaller, the last tile is pulled back until it reaches at least this size; the seam overlap then grows and is blended over its full width. 256 (default) keeps small leftover tiles as-is. Must not exceed the tile size. In rows_cols mode an error is raised if the solved tile size falls below this.

overlap_mode.tooltip: Who wins each shared overlap band when stitching. 'earlier' (default): the already-stitched content wins. 'later': the re-sampled tile wins. Does NOT affect the noise mask.

overlap_blend.tooltip: How the overlap band transitions when stitching: linear cross-fade (default), smoothstep (eased), overwrite (whole band from the overlap_mode side), midpoint (hard switch at the band's middle).

masked_area_noise.tooltip: How much noise is allowed into the masked (frozen/fade) overlap band during sampling. 0 (default): current behaviour, the masked area gets no noise injection and stays fixed. 1.0: the mask has no effect and every tile is sampled freely. Small values like 0.01 let a little noise through to probe how much the scene moves under the mask.

brightness_match.tooltip: Per-frame, per-channel median brightness match: after sampling, shift each tile's brightness baseline to the source region at the same (tile, frame). Reduces tile-to-tile and frame-to-frame luminance drift. Experimental - may be removed.

dynamic_fade.tooltip: Temporal fade schedule over each tile's sampling. 'off' (default): the FADE segment keeps its fixed width for the whole tile (current behaviour). 'narrowing': the fade width starts at fade_width/fade_height and shrinks linearly to dynamic_fade_min by the end of the tile. 'widening': it starts at dynamic_fade_min and grows linearly to fade_width/fade_height. Only takes effect when the tile is sampled in more than one step; if a per-axis fade is not larger than dynamic_fade_min it behaves like 'off'.

dynamic_fade_min.tooltip: Minimum width (PIXELS) the FADE segment can reach when dynamic_fade is 'narrowing' or 'widening'. Only effective when a per-axis fade is larger than this; otherwise the fade stays at its static width. Default 32.

output_tooltips: Spatial split settings consumed by 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale'.
Resolved tile width in PIXELS: the validated input in specific_size mode, or the equal-tile solution computed from upscale_width/grid_cols in rows_cols mode.
Resolved tile height in PIXELS: the validated input in specific_size mode, or the equal-tile solution computed from upscale_height/grid_rows in rows_cols mode.
MMH3SpatialSplitParams.name: MMH3SpatialSplitParams
MMH3SpatialSplitParams.description: Bundle the spatial tile settings for the 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale' node: tile size, per-axis overlap and fade, and seam stitching rules (inner loop). Two tile sizing modes: enter explicit pixel sizes, or enter a row/column count and let the node solve an equal-size tile grid (all tiles identical, edge tiles included) - the resolved tile size is exposed as tile_width/tile_height outputs.

seam_denoise.tooltip: 缝邻域降噪上限: <1 时高降噪下缝附近以中等降噪续写邻居内容, 防止快运动物体在缝处被切断; 建议 0.5~0.8; 1.0=关。

MMH3SpatialSplitParamsV10.name: MMH3SpatialSplitParamsV10
MMH3SpatialSplitParamsV10.description: 简化空间分块: 百分比重叠/渐变 + 缝邻域降噪上限。

MMH3SplitUpscale.name: MMH3SplitUpscale
MMH3SplitUpscale.description: 预防(冻结预填+三重锚) + 校正(颜色匹配+钉源) + 抗分叉(seam_denoise) + probe 门控 polish。

chunk_length.tooltip: Target pixel frames per chunk (at 24 fps). MUST be a multiple of 17 (one keyframe grid step). 136 = ~5.7s, 153 = ~6.4s.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: Pixel frames of overlap between consecutive chunks. MUST be a multiple of 17; recommended 17. Must be smaller than chunk_length.

anchor_strength.tooltip: How much of the previous chunk's re-sampled boundary the frozen frame-0 anchor keeps: 1.0 = exact content, 0.999 = model default, 0.0 = no anchoring.

output_tooltips: Temporal split settings consumed by 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale'.
MMH3TemporalSplitParams.name: MMH3TemporalSplitParams
MMH3TemporalSplitParams.description: Bundle the temporal split settings for the 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale' node: how the input latent is cut into overlapping time chunks (outer loop) and how seams are anchored.

MMH3TemporalSplitParamsV10.name: MMH3TemporalSplitParamsV10
MMH3TemporalSplitParamsV10.description: H3 原生网格时间分块 (5+17m 帧) + 三重锚。

model.tooltip: The MiniMax H3 diffusion model to patch.

method.tooltip: Overlap blending weight per tile: gaussian (Mixture of Diffusers, default - tiles dominate their center) or uniform (MultiDiffusion - plain averaging in overlaps).

tile_width.tooltip: Tile width in PIXELS, snapped to a multiple of 32 (the H3 2x2 latent patch grid).

tile_height.tooltip: Tile height in PIXELS, snapped to a multiple of 32 (the H3 2x2 latent patch grid).

tile_overlap.tooltip: Overlap between neighbouring tiles in PIXELS, snapped to a multiple of 32. Keep at least ~25% of the tile size or the tiles decouple into unrelated content. 0 gives hard tile edges.

output_tooltips: The patched model; feed it into 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale' (spatial_split_param unconnected) or any H3 sampler.
MMH3TiledDiffusion.name: MMH3TiledDiffusion
MMH3TiledDiffusion.description: Experimental per-step spatial Tiled Diffusion for MiniMax H3 (MultiDiffusion / Mixture of Diffusers style, ported from shiimizu/ComfyUI-TiledDiffusion). Patches the model so every denoising step slices the latent into spatial tiles, runs the DiT per tile, and blends the predictions with uniform or gaussian weights - all tiles share the same sigmas and noise field, so no overlap masks are needed. Tiles carry global frame positions so their predictions stay consistent with the full frame. Connect between the H3 model and 'MMH3 Ultimate Upscale' and leave that node's spatial_split_param unconnected. Use a tile_overlap of at least ~25% of the tile size, or the tiles decouple. Does not support fun controlnet, inpaint or denoise masks, and does not save VRAM/time (H3 runs batch 1); it is an experiment in seam quality.

model.tooltip: The diffusion model used to re-sample every chunk/tile (guider is built internally).

conditioning.tooltip: Conditioning used to generate this latent. Per chunk it is re-anchored in time; per tile its keyframes are spatially cropped; the frame-0 keyframe is pinned to the previous chunk's re-sampled frame.

latent.tooltip: Denoised MiniMax H3 AV latent to enhance.

noise.tooltip: Noise source; one noise tensor is generated per piece.

sigmas.tooltip: Sigma schedule used for every chunk/tile.

cfg.tooltip: CFG scale used when 'negative' is connected.

negative.tooltip: Negative conditioning. When connected, a CFGGuider is used with the 'cfg' value; otherwise a basic guider (positive only).

latent_upscale_param.tooltip: Output of 'MMH3 Latent Upscale with Model Params' (H3 3D upscaler) OR 'MMH3 Latent Upscale Params' (model-free interpolation). Leave unconnected to skip upscaling.

temporal_split_param.tooltip: Output of 'MMH3 Temporal Split Params'. Leave unconnected to process the latent as a single chunk.

spatial_split_param.tooltip: Output of 'MMH3 Spatial Split Params'. Leave unconnected to sample each chunk whole (no tiling).

fun_control_param.tooltip: Output of 'MMH3 Fun Controlnet Params'. When connected, every chunk/tile is sampled with a Fun ControlNet that guides the re-generation toward the provided control video (auto-cropped to each chunk's time range and tile's spatial window, and upscaled from low-res per the selected mode). Leave unconnected to disable.

inpaint_param.tooltip: Output of 'MMH3 Spatial Inpaint Params'. When connected with a spatial split, every non-first tile's overlap strips are pinned to the already-sampled neighbour content (VAE-decoded source + spatial fade mask), removing visible tile seams. Leave unconnected to disable.

output_tooltips: Upscaled, re-sampled, stitched MiniMax H3 AV latent.
DEBUG ONLY. Per-chunk metadata: frame start/count, video/audio token ranges, upscale applied.
DEBUG ONLY. Per-chunk spatial grid metadata: offsets, tile extents, overlaps, stitching mode.
MMH3UltimateUpscale.name: MMH3UltimateUpscale
MMH3UltimateUpscale.description: Re-sample an already-denoised MiniMax H3 AV latent through the full auto pipeline in one node: temporal split (outer loop) -> latent upscale (per chunk) -> spatial split (inner loop) -> per-tile sampling with preview -> spatial stitch -> temporal stitch. Each chunk/tile is sampled with a fresh guider built from the per-piece conditioning (re-anchored and cropped keyframes), keeping peak VRAM to one tile. 'latent_upscale_param', 'temporal_split_param' and 'spatial_split_param' are optional - leave any unconnected to skip that stage (no upscale / single chunk / full-chunk sampling).

positive.tooltip: Positive conditioning from CLIP encode

lora_name.tooltip: LoRA file to load and analyze

strength.tooltip: Overall LoRA strength (ignored when using schedule)

preset.tooltip: Quick preset selection. Individual toggles below override when changed.

lora_path_opt.tooltip: Optional: Override LoRA selection with a path

schedule_preset.tooltip: Select a preset schedule (populates the text field below for editing)

strength_schedule.tooltip: Strength schedule: 0:.2,.5:.8,1:1.0 (step:strength pairs). Edit freely after selecting preset.

save_refined_lora.tooltip: Enable to save the refined LoRA to disk

save_filename.tooltip: Filename for saved LoRA (timestamp auto-appended). Leave empty for auto-name.

block_weights_string.tooltip: Input/Output block profile string. Positional text syncs with the UI. String input overrides UI values.

strength.tooltip: Scales the maps' contribution to the image tokens. 0.0 is the same as no maps, 1.0 is the trained strength.

start_percent.tooltip: Sampling percent at which the control starts.

end_percent.tooltip: Sampling percent at which the control ends. Ending early keeps the layout and depth while the rest of the steps loosen the shapes.

color_map.tooltip: One flat color per region, at the output size. The colors are only region IDs.

depth_map.tooltip: Depth map at the output size, near is white.

MOSSImageControl.name: MOSSImageControl
MOSSImageControl.description: Adds the color region and depth maps for a MOSS-Image color/depth control adapter loaded with a LoRA loader.

prompt.tooltip: Description of the whole image.

element.tooltip: Prompt elements from the node Create Bounding Boxes. The description is the box's caption, text boxes also render their text.

width.tooltip: Width of the generated image; the boxes are placed in its pixels.

height.tooltip: Height of the generated image; the boxes are placed in its pixels.

character_boxes.tooltip: Numbers of the object boxes to label as characters instead of objects, as tagged in the Create Bounding Boxes preview, e.g. "1, 3".

MOSSImageLayoutPrompt.name: MOSSImageLayoutPrompt
MOSSImageLayoutPrompt.description: Builds a MOSS-Image layout prompt from the prompt and the boxes from Create Bounding Boxes.

block_weights_string.tooltip: 42 layer values, optionally followed by other_weights. Connected strings override sliders. Named example: %default=0, layer14-27=1, other=0.2

timing.tooltip: auto: read the audio latent rate and layout from the connected audio VAE. manual: enter them directly.

latents_per_second.tooltip: Audio latent frames per second. 40 for MiniMax H3, 25 for LTX.

layout.tooltip: Where time runs in the audio latent. time last for MiniMax H3 and audio-only models, time then bins for LTX spectrogram latents.

vae.tooltip: The audio VAE used to encode this latent. Required when timing is auto.

MVEx_AudioMaskDebug.name: MVEx_AudioMaskDebug
MVEx_AudioMaskDebug.description: Report which audio time ranges the latent's noise mask keeps (0.0) and generates (1.0). Accepts a joint AV latent or an audio latent alone; route the string to a Preview Any node.

latent.tooltip: Joint AV latent or audio latent to mask.

timing.tooltip: auto: read the audio latent rate and layout from the connected audio VAE. manual: enter them directly.

latents_per_second.tooltip: Audio latent frames per second. 40 for MiniMax H3, 25 for LTX.

layout.tooltip: Where time runs in the audio latent. time last for MiniMax H3 and audio-only models, time then bins for LTX spectrogram latents.

start_time.tooltip: Start of the regenerated audio range in seconds. Ignored when time_ranges or mask is used.

end_time.tooltip: End of the regenerated audio range in seconds. Ignored when time_ranges or mask is used.

existing_mask.tooltip: keep: merge the new ranges into the audio mask already on the latent, so copies of this node chain. replace: discard the existing audio mask first. The video side of a joint mask is kept either way.

vae.tooltip: The audio VAE used to encode this latent (for a joint AV latent, the audio VAE, not the video one). Required when timing is auto.

mask.tooltip: Mask over the audio timeline: time runs along the width axis, stretched to the audio duration. White = regenerate, black = keep.

time_ranges.tooltip: Comma-separated seconds forming in,out pairs (e.g. 0,1.5,3,4.25). Takes priority over mask and start/end when set.

output_tooltips: The latent with the audio noise mask attached.
MVEx_AudioMaskToLatent.name: MVEx_AudioMaskToLatent
MVEx_AudioMaskToLatent.description: Regenerate the selected audio time ranges and keep the rest. Ranges come from time_ranges when set, else from the mask when connected, else from start_time/end_time. Accepts a joint AV latent or an audio latent alone. On a joint latent without an existing noise mask the video is fully preserved; apply Set Latent Noise Mask before this node to control the video side.

softness.tooltip: Width of the soft threshold band in mask-value units. 0 is the stock hard threshold; larger values keep wider soft edges on each per-step mask (spatial width scales with the input mask's blur). 1 disables the schedule entirely and blends by the mask as-is.

strength.tooltip: Blend between the thresholded per-step mask (1) and the raw input mask (0), as in the stock node.

MVEx_DifferentialDiffusionSoft.name: MVEx_DifferentialDiffusionSoft
MVEx_DifferentialDiffusionSoft.description: Differential Diffusion whose per-step masks keep a soft edge proportional to the blur in the original mask, instead of the stock hard binary threshold. softness 0 reproduces the stock node; softness 1 degenerates to plain static mask blending.

width.tooltip: Mask width in pixels.

height.tooltip: Mask height in pixels.

frames.tooltip: Frames in the batch.

ranges.tooltip: Frames to mask, comma-separated. Ranges are Python slices written start:stop, with the stop frame excluded, so 0:24 masks frames 0 to 23. Leave a side out to run to the start or the end (5:, :3), or write 5:end for the same thing. Negative numbers count back from the end, so -1 is the last frame and 5:-1 stops one short of it. A bare number masks a single frame, an optional third field steps (0::2 is every other frame), frame numbers start at 0, and an empty list gives an empty mask.

output_tooltips: One mask per frame.
MVEx_FrameRangeMask.name: MVEx_FrameRangeMask
MVEx_FrameRangeMask.description: Builds a batch of solid masks at the given resolution, fully masked (1) on the listed frames and empty (0) on all the others. Ranges follow Python slice syntax, so 0:24 is frames 0 to 23.

mask.tooltip: Latent-resolution masks, one per latent frame.

compression.tooltip: auto: read the compression geometry from the connected VAE, including the exact frame cycle and 2x2 token grid of chunked models like MiniMax H3. manual: enter it directly.

spatial.tooltip: Pixels per latent pixel on each axis.

token_spatial.tooltip: Latent pixels per model token on each axis; the strongest value in each token block paints the whole block, matching how the model reads the mask. 2 for MiniMax H3, 1 for models that read the mask per latent pixel.

head_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in the model's leading frame group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX. 0 when the model has no leading group.

head_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by the leading group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

chunk_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in each repeating group after the leading group. 4 for Wan and Hunyuan, 8 for LTX. 1 disables temporal expansion (image models).

chunk_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by each repeating group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

frames_per_latent.tooltip: Exact pixel frames covered by each latent frame, comma-separated, repeating from the first frame. Overrides the grid above when set. 1,4,4,4,4 with spatial 16 for MiniMax H3. For frame counts off the model's grid, use auto.

frames.tooltip: Pixel frame count to paint. 0 uses the count the compression grid implies for the incoming latent frames. Set it explicitly to match a source video that is off the model's frame grid.

vae.tooltip: The VAE whose latents this mask matches. Required when compression is auto.

output_tooltips: Pixel-space masks, one per frame.
MVEx_LatentMaskToMask.name: MVEx_LatentMaskToMask
MVEx_LatentMaskToMask.description: Expands a latent-resolution mask back to pixel resolution for visualization or testing. Each latent frame paints every pixel frame in its group and each token block paints as one value, so detail collapsed by the latent reduction stays collapsed.

masks.tooltip: Mask batch to clean, one mask per frame.

threshold.tooltip: Mask values above this count as subject when finding blobs.

method.tooltip: shrink_grow: shrinks the mask so thin specks vanish, then restores the surviving blobs' exact shapes. components: drops blobs that are both small and short-lived.

shrink.tooltip: Shrink distance in pixels. Blobs thinner than about twice this are removed.

min_frames.tooltip: Surviving blobs must also persist at least this many frames. 1 disables the temporal check.

min_pixels.tooltip: Blobs whose largest single-frame area is below this many pixels are removed.

min_frames.tooltip: Small blobs must persist at least this many frames to survive.

edge_grow.tooltip: Grow kept regions by this many pixels so the subject's soft edges are preserved.

output_tooltips: Cleaned masks, same size and soft values as the input.
MVEx_MaskCleanup.name: MVEx_MaskCleanup
MVEx_MaskCleanup.description: Removes specks and brief flickering blobs from a video mask batch while keeping the real subject, including its soft edges.

masks.tooltip: Pixel-space masks, one per frame.

compression.tooltip: auto: read the compression geometry from the connected VAE, including the exact frame cycle and 2x2 token grid of chunked models like MiniMax H3. manual: enter it directly.

spatial.tooltip: Pixels per latent pixel on each axis.

token_spatial.tooltip: Latent pixels per model token on each axis; the mask is unified over each token block. 2 for MiniMax H3, 1 for models that read the mask per latent pixel.

head_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in the model's leading frame group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX. 0 when the model has no leading group.

head_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by the leading group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

chunk_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in each repeating group after the leading group. 4 for Wan and Hunyuan, 8 for LTX. 1 disables temporal reduction (image models).

chunk_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by each repeating group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

frames_per_latent.tooltip: Exact pixel frames covered by each latent frame, comma-separated, repeating from the first frame. Overrides the grid above when set. 1,4,4,4,4 with spatial 16 for MiniMax H3. For frame counts off the model's grid, use auto.

spatial_method.tooltip: How a block of pixels reduces to one latent pixel. max marks the cell if any pixel is masked, min only if all are.

temporal_method.tooltip: How a group of frames reduces to one latent frame. max marks the frame if any grouped frame is masked.

grow_spatial.tooltip: Grow (+) or shrink (-) the mask this many pixels before reduction.

grow_temporal.tooltip: Grow (+) or shrink (-) the mask this many frames before reduction.

grow_temp_mode.tooltip: Directionality of grow_temporal: both: earlier and later frames. forward: later frames only. backward: earlier frames only. chunks: whole encoder chunks instead of frames, so the mask only changes at chunk boundaries. (requires a chunked encoder like H3 VAE).

vae.tooltip: The VAE used to encode the latents this mask will be applied to. Required when compression is auto.

output_tooltips: Latent-resolution mask for Set Latent Noise Mask.
MVEx_MaskToLatentSpace.name: MVEx_MaskToLatentSpace
MVEx_MaskToLatentSpace.description: Reduces a pixel-space mask batch to latent resolution using the VAE's spatial and temporal compression, aligned to causal video VAE frame grouping and to the model's token grid (2x2 latent pixels for MiniMax H3). Feed the result to Set Latent Noise Mask.

masks.tooltip: Subject masks, one per frame. Clean them first (Mask Cleanup) if the segmentation is noisy.

mode.tooltip: In order of increasing complexity. combined: one static crop with padding around the subject's whole travel. tracked: a constant-size crop that stays still until the subject would leave it, then moves as little as possible. zoomed: the crop also follows the subject's size, planned over the whole clip, every crop resampled to a fixed output resolution.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's combined extent across all frames: 1.5 leaves a third of the crop as margin around the whole travel. 1.0 hugs the travel exactly. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Crop shape as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78), reached by growing the smaller dimension. 0 sizes width and height from the mask's whole travel.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's size: 1.5 keeps the subject at two thirds of the crop with the rest as padding, at any resolution. 1.0 crops tight, leaving no padding for the padding setting to keep; 4.0 surrounds the subject with three times its own size. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

padding.tooltip: How firmly the crop_scale padding is kept. guaranteed: never less than promised on any frame, whatever it costs in size or movement; only the image edge can break it, and mask noise counts as subject, so clean the masks first. firm: at least 70% is always kept, the rest yields briefly during fast motion. flexible: padding yields first whenever keeping it would cost stillness or tightness.

prefer.tooltip: What pays for keeping the padding when the subject moves. stillness: the crop runs larger so it can move less. tightness: the crop stays as small as the padding allows and moves as much as needed instead.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Crop shape as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78). 0 lets the planner choose the shape that best balances padding, stillness, and size for this clip.

seamless_loop.tooltip: Plan the crop path so the last frame wraps seamlessly into the first. Only for clips that genuinely repeat.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's size: 1.5 keeps the subject at two thirds of the crop with the rest as padding, so the subject holds a constant share of the output at any resolution. 1.0 crops tight, leaving no padding for the padding setting to keep; 4.0 surrounds the subject with three times its own size. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

padding.tooltip: How firmly the crop_scale padding is kept. guaranteed: never less than promised on any frame, whatever it costs in size, movement, or rescaling; only the image edge can break it, and mask noise counts as subject, so clean the masks first. firm: at least 70% is always kept, the rest yields briefly during fast motion. flexible: padding yields first whenever keeping it would cost stillness or tightness.

prefer.tooltip: What pays for keeping the padding when the subject moves. stillness: the crop moves and rescales as little as possible, running larger instead. tightness: the crop and the output resolution stay as small as the padding allows, moving and rescaling as much as needed instead.

pad_surplus_tol.tooltip: Extra padding (a crop bigger than needed) lasting shorter than this many frames is kept rather than trimmed, riding out occlusions and dips at a steady size. At 1 the crop follows every size change tightly; very high holds one constant size for the whole clip.

zoom_step.tooltip: Whether crop size changes smoothly or snaps to discrete zoom levels this ratio apart. At 1.0 size changes continuously; at 2.0 every zoom level doubles the previous one.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Shape of every crop and of the output resolution, as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78). 0 lets the planner choose the shape that best balances padding, stillness, and rescaling for this clip. Output size is automatic: the largest crop stays at 1:1 pixel scale.

seamless_loop.tooltip: Plan crop position and size so the last frame wraps seamlessly into the first. Only for clips that genuinely repeat.

divisible_by.tooltip: Crop width and height are rounded up to a multiple of this. Match the model's resolution requirement.

upscale_megapixels.tooltip: Upscale the cropped images/masks to this many megapixels, on the divisible_by grid. Set to 0.0 to disable. (Use a negative value to allow scaling down as well as up.)

resize_method.tooltip: Resampling filter used when a crop is resized (masks are unaffected). auto uses bicubic to enlarge and lanczos to shrink.

MVEx_SubjectCrop.name: MVEx_SubjectCrop
MVEx_SubjectCrop.description: Crops a region around the masked subject from every frame, sized so the whole batch stacks into one tensor. Position, size, and shape are chosen together over the whole clip, so the crop holds still through mask jitter and follows only sustained motion.

masks.tooltip: Subject masks, one per frame.

mode.tooltip: tracked: one constant-size crop, pixel-exact slices, its shape part of the plan. zoomed: position and size planned jointly, the shape swept as a candidate set, crops resampled to one resolution.

crop_scale.tooltip: How much padding the crop promises around the subject, as a multiple of its size. At 1.0 the crop is tight with no padding; at 4.0 the subject sits in three times its own size of padding. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

min_padding_allowed.tooltip: The padding you always get, as a fraction of the promise. At 0 padding may be sacrificed entirely (flexible); at 1 the full promise can only be broken by the image edge (guaranteed); 0.7 is firm.

min_padding_allowed_window.tooltip: How long motion must last (about half this many frames) before the minimum protects it. At 1 every raw frame is protected, mask noise included; at 256 brief excursions may dip below the minimum.

pad_deficit_tol.tooltip: Padding dips shorter than this many frames are ignored instead of chased, keeping the crop calm. At 1 every dip is corrected immediately; at 999 lost padding is never restored.

pad_surplus_tol.tooltip: Extra padding (a crop bigger than needed) lasting shorter than this many frames is kept rather than trimmed, riding out occlusions and dips at a steady size. At 1 the crop follows every size change tightly; at 999 it holds one constant size for the whole clip.

movement_cost.tooltip: How much the crop resists moving: the yardstick the other costs trade against. Near 0 it glues itself to the subject; at 16 it approaches one static box around the subject's whole travel.

center_pull.tooltip: How strongly the subject is kept centered when the plan has a choice. At 0 the crop parks wherever is cheapest, which can look arbitrary; at 0.5 it recenters constantly at the price of extra movement.

end_tightening.tooltip: Fraction of the normal shrink pressure that still applies inside the end window (end_tightening_window). At 0 the crop holds its size through the ends; at 1 the ends tighten to the subject like mid-clip and the window only steadies position.

end_tightening_window.tooltip: How many frames at each end the crop is held settled, so the clip starts and ends on a steady crop. At 0 the crop may drift and rescale right through the first and last frame; at 256 a long stretch at each end is held, shrinking only as much as end_tightening allows.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Fixes the crop shape as width divided by height (1.78 is 16:9). At 0 the planner chooses the shape that best balances padding, stillness, and size for this clip.

left.tooltip: Extend mask leftward by this many pixels.

right.tooltip: Extend mask rightward by this many pixels.

down.tooltip: Extend mask downward by this many pixels.

up.tooltip: Extend mask upward by this many pixels.

image.tooltip: Input image(s) — (B,H,W,C) float32 [0,1].

mask.tooltip: Mask to diagnose — (B,H,W) float32 [0,1]. Can be from any segmentation method.

ring_width.tooltip: Width in pixels of the boundary ring used for contrast/color analysis.

blur_threshold.tooltip: Laplacian variance threshold below which the image is considered blurry.

brightness_threshold.tooltip: Mean brightness threshold below which the scene is considered dark.

area_jump_threshold.tooltip: Timeline: a frame whose mask area changes by more than this fraction of the previous frame's area is flagged 'area_jump' (0.25 = 25 %).

preview_fix.tooltip: Corrective-action preview (non-destructive): apply one mask operation and return the result as corrected_mask with before/after mask metrics in fix_report. auto picks from the findings (holes -> fill_holes, fragments -> remove_specks, jagged -> smooth_edges, whole frame -> invert). none: corrected_mask is the analysed mask.

fix_radius_px.tooltip: Radius in pixels for dilate / erode / close_gaps / smooth_edges.

Heatmap mask highlighting regions most likely to be problematic.
Overall severity score in [0, 100] (higher means more issues).
Suggested masking method or refinement to try next.

Per-frame metrics and problem flags (dark, blurry, low boundary contrast, colour confusion, busy background, empty / whole-frame mask, area and centroid jumps) plus the list of problem frames, as JSON.
The mask after the preview_fix operation (the analysed mask unchanged when preview_fix is none).
Which fix was applied and why, with the mask metrics before and after, as JSON.
