image.tooltip: Source image or video frames (B,H,W,C).

segmenter.tooltip: Coarse-mask backend. Entries tagged [missing-deps] need an optional pip install to activate. sam3 / sam3.1 run on ComfyUI's own SAM 3 (ComfyUI 0.39+; C2C_SAM_CORE=0 turns that off). NON-COMMERCIAL weights: rmbg (briaai RMBG-1.4 / 2.0, Bria licences); locate_anything (NVIDIA License, academic / non-profit research only - auto / auto_best also use it for text prompts when it is installed; info.text_grounding says when).

matter.tooltip: Optional alpha refinement. 'none' returns the segmenter mask as alpha. vitmatte is Apache-2.0; matanyone (MatAnyone / MatAnyone2 weights) is S-Lab License 1.0 (NON-COMMERCIAL).

model.tooltip: Specific weight file to use. Tag prefix selects the backend folder; '(auto)' lets each backend pick.

matter_model.tooltip: Weight file for the matter backend.

precision.tooltip: Number format for the model backends that honour it (ViTMatte, RVM, BGMattingV2, salient, LocateAnything). fp16 = fastest, least memory; bf16 = safer on newer cards; fp32 = slowest, exact.

attention.tooltip: Currently no effect: stored for the backends, but none of them reads it yet.

offload.tooltip: Currently no effect: stored for the backends, but none of them reads it yet.

trimap_dilate.tooltip: Trimap: pixels the mask edge is grown outward to mark 'unknown' (the band the matter solves). Larger = catches more hair, slower.

trimap_erode.tooltip: Trimap: pixels the mask edge is shrunk inward; what is left is sure foreground.

edge_radius.tooltip: Edge band width in pixels the matter refines around the coarse mask (the advanced trimap uses it as its base radius).

edge_mode.tooltip: Final alpha edge. 'soft' = as the matter produced it. 'feather' = blur the existing edge. 'hard' = binary cut at edge_threshold, no partial alpha (what a holdout or garbage matte wants). 'hard+feather' = cut hard then feather — the edge width becomes yours rather than the model's, which is how you match edges across shots keyed by different backends.

edge_threshold.tooltip: Cut point for the hard modes. Lower keeps more of the soft fringe as solid; higher eats into it.

edge_feather.tooltip: Feather radius in pixels, read as ~2 sigma of a true Gaussian. 0 with a feather mode selected does nothing.

individual_objects.tooltip: If supported by the backend, return one mask per detected object.

tracking_direction.tooltip: Video: which way the tracker runs from the prompted frame. bidirectional covers frames before and after it.

frame_annotation.tooltip: Frame index (in clip) where prompts are anchored.

object_id.tooltip: Video: the tracker's id for the prompted object (change it only to keep ids stable across runs).

memory_size.tooltip: Video: how many past frames the tracker / video matter remembers. More = steadier through occlusion, more memory.

start_frame.tooltip: Video: first frame to process (0 = from the start).

auto_download.tooltip: Allow Download: fetch a missing weight from Hugging Face / torch.hub into its models/ subfolder. Off: installed copies are used wherever they are (this pack, other packs, the HF cache); without one the model-free method runs and the info output says so.

seed.tooltip: Seed for the backends that sample (text grounding); same seed + inputs = same result.

tta_flip.tooltip: Test-time augmentation: run segmenter on the H-flipped image and average. Slower but cleaner.

multiscale.tooltip: Run the segmenter at 0.75x / 1.0x / 1.25x and fuse. Helps small / thin subjects.

post_refine.tooltip: Final alpha refinement. 'guided' = guided filter (fast, torch-only). 'crf' = DenseCRF (requires pydensecrf, sharpest edges).

refine_radius.tooltip: Spatial radius for guided / CRF refinement.

despill.tooltip: Colour decontamination on the named backing. 'auto' estimates the colour from image corners.

despill_strength.tooltip: How aggressively to subtract the spill (0 = off).

preserve_skin.tooltip: Keep warm pixels (R>G>B) untouched during despill.

lightwrap_strength.tooltip: Light-wrap intensity. 0 = off; ~0.3-0.6 = natural blend over the new BG.

edge_band_radius.tooltip: Width of the soft edge band when splitting edge/inside/outside masks.

premultiply.tooltip: Premultiply preview by alpha. Disable for straight-alpha outputs.

enable_luma_key.tooltip: Run a luminance keyer on the source image BEFORE segmentation and use it as a hint / external_mask.

luma_mode.tooltip: Luma key: which brightness range keys in. highlights 0.7-1, midtones 0.3-0.7, shadows 0-0.3, custom = luma_low..luma_high, auto picks from the image.

luma_low.tooltip: Luma key, custom mode: bottom of the brightness ramp (BT.709 luma).

luma_high.tooltip: Luma key, custom mode: top of the brightness ramp.

luma_gamma.tooltip: Luma key: gamma on the key. Above 1 thins it, below 1 fattens it.

luma_falloff.tooltip: Luma key: ramp shape. 0 = hard cut, 1 = smoothstep, above 1 = more gradual.

luma_invert.tooltip: Luma key: swap keyed and unkeyed areas.

luma_mix.tooltip: How to combine the luma-key mask with the segmenter result. 'hint_only' = use as external_mask hint; 'intersect/union/replace' = combine with the final alpha.

enable_advanced_trimap.tooltip: Use the edge-aware trimap generator (asymmetric inner/outer scaling, image-edge snapping, smoothing) instead of the simple dilate/erode trimap.

trimap_inner_scale.tooltip: Advanced trimap: inward width of the unknown band, as a multiple of edge_radius.

trimap_outer_scale.tooltip: Advanced trimap: outward width of the unknown band, as a multiple of edge_radius (wider outside catches loose hair).

trimap_smooth.tooltip: Advanced trimap: blur (sigma, pixels) on the band transitions; sure foreground / background stay hard. 0 = off.

trimap_threshold.tooltip: Advanced trimap: mask value above which a pixel counts as foreground before the band is built.

auto_quality.tooltip: AUTOMATIC robustness for hard images. Detects motion blur, low light, low contrast, speckle noise and low bg/fg colour separation, then applies just-enough pre-processing (CLAHE, unsharp, NL-means, chroma stretch) BEFORE the segmenter, and a light guided-filter+edge-snap polish on the alpha. No knobs.

auto_disambiguate.tooltip: When BOTH positive and negative points are supplied, score SAM's 3 candidate masks by (pos-coverage − neg-coverage − size-penalty) instead of raw score. This is what makes `pos=face, neg=neck` return just the face, not the whole person.

quality_mode.tooltip: Strength of auto_quality pre/post processing. fast = mild, balanced = default, max_fidelity = NL-means denoise + larger guided filter.

enable_diagnose.tooltip: Run automatic mask-failure diagnostics (severity score + suggested method).

diag_ring_width.tooltip: Diagnostics: width in pixels of the ring around the mask edge where contrast and colour confusion are measured.

diag_blur_threshold.tooltip: Diagnostics: sharpness score (Laplacian variance x 1000) below which a frame is reported as blurry.

diag_brightness_threshold.tooltip: Diagnostics: mean brightness below which a frame is reported as too dark.

robust_propagation.tooltip: Confidence-aware re-anchor loop for video. After SAM2 propagation, every frame's mask is scored vs the last good mask (IoU × size-ratio). When confidence drops below the threshold, the chosen re-anchor strategy fires (flow warp / DINOv2 region search / convex blend). Robust against motion blur + lighting drift. Single-image inputs skip this stage.

robust_confidence_threshold.tooltip: Below this confidence the re-anchor fires.

robust_reanchor_method.tooltip: flow=Farneback optical-flow warp of last good mask. dino=DINOv2 patch-feature region search + SAM2 re-prompt. blend=convex mix of current+warped. none=accept drifted output (debug).

robust_blend_alpha.tooltip: Blend weight for current SAM2 mask when method=blend.

positive_coords.tooltip: JSON list of positive points [[x,y],...], e.g. the Image Mask Editor (C2C) positive_coords output.

negative_coords.tooltip: JSON list of negative points [[x,y],...], e.g. the Image Mask Editor (C2C) negative_coords output.

normal_bbox.tooltip: Generic bbox if you don't care about polarity.

text_prompt.tooltip: Open-vocabulary text prompt (SAM3 / GroundingDINO / VideoMaMa). Wire from any STRING source.

external_mask.tooltip: Optional mask used as a hint or overridden when input_mode='auto' falls through.

external_trimap.tooltip: Optional pre-computed trimap that bypasses internal trimap generation.

holdout_mask.tooltip: Garbage / holdout matte. Pixels where this is >0 are FORCED to alpha=0 (used to chop out boom mics, rigs, etc).

core_mask.tooltip: Core / inside matte. Pixels where this is >0 are FORCED to alpha=1 (used to lock down opaque interiors).

pipeline.tooltip: onyx = SAM3.1 video session + tiled ViTMatte. cascade (legacy) = previous multi-backend auto_best path.

scene_prompts.tooltip: Optional ONYX scene JSON (version 1). When empty, legacy prompt sockets map to object 1.

matte_tile.tooltip: ViTMatte tile size in pixels for both the ONYX and cascade pipelines.

temporal_stabilise.tooltip: 3-tap temporal median on alpha inside the unknown trimap band (ONYX path).

matte_overlap.tooltip: Overlap between ViTMatte tiles in pixels. Larger overlaps reduce seams but run more tiles.

matte_tile_batch.tooltip: How many tiles to run per GPU forward pass. Lower this if you hit out-of-memory errors. On the CPU tiles always run one at a time (faster there, and a third of the memory).

backend.tooltip: Which pipeline makes the matte. 'segment + matte' = this node's segmenter and matter (pipeline, segmenter, matter). 'SAM + ViTMatte' = a SAM model from a SAM Model Loader, then ViTMatte or a guided filter on the edges. 'SeC + MatAnyone2' = SeC / SAM segmentation, then MatAnyone2 (video) or ViTMatte. 'remove background' = RMBG-2.0 or BiRefNet, no prompt. Each control's tooltip names the backend that reads it.

sam_model.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: the model from a SAM Model Loader.

points_json.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte and SeC + MatAnyone2: point prompts: [{"x":100,"y":200,"label":1}, ...] (label 1 = keep, 0 = remove). The click editor writes this.

bbox_json.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte and SeC + MatAnyone2: box prompt [x1,y1,x2,y2]. Empty = points only. A wired pos_bbox wins.

sam_iterations.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: SAM passes; each pass uses the previous mask to place better prompts. 2-3 is ideal.

sam_refine_method.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: edge refinement. auto = ViTMatte, else multi-scale guided filter, else guided filter. vitmatte = neural matting. guided_filter = fast. multi_scale_guided = three scales (best without a model). color_aware = LAB colour edges. laplacian_blend = frequency blend.

sam_edge_radius.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: pixels around the edge that are refined (larger = softer transitions).

sam_detail_preservation.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: fine detail (hair, fur, lace) to keep. 0 = smooth, 1 = all.

sam_edge_contrast.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: edge contrast for hard lighting. Above 1 sharpens the boundary.

sam_multimask_output.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: SAM returns three candidate masks (off = its single best).

sam_mask_index.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: which of SAM's three candidates to keep (with multimask output on).

sam_score_threshold.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: skip SAM candidates below this confidence (0 = use mask_index).

sam_trimap_dilate.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: outer trimap radius (0 = edge radius x 1.5).

sam_trimap_erode.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: inner trimap radius (0 = edge radius x 1.0).

sam_batch_mode.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte: process every frame of the batch. Off = the first frame only (every output then has one frame).

sec_model.tooltip: SeC + MatAnyone2: segmentation model. SeC = video with text prompts; SAM 2 / 3 = point or box prompts.

sec_text_prompt.tooltip: SeC + MatAnyone2: what to track, e.g. 'cat' or 'person in red'. A wired text_prompt wins. Empty = point / box prompts.

sec_matting_backend.tooltip: SeC + MatAnyone2: alpha matting. auto = MatAnyone2 for video (more than one frame), ViTMatte small for an image. MatAnyone2 keeps the matte steady over time; ViTMatte has the best edge per frame.

sec_edge_radius.tooltip: SeC + MatAnyone2: edge refinement radius in pixels.

sec_n_warmup.tooltip: SeC + MatAnyone2: MatAnyone2 warm-up passes on the first frame (more = steadier start).

sec_edge_refine_method.tooltip: SeC + MatAnyone2: optional edge refinement after matting. none = the matting output as it is.

bg_model.tooltip: remove background: rmbg_2.0 = general purpose, fast. birefnet_general = detailed edges. birefnet_portrait = people.

bg_threshold.tooltip: remove background: above 0 the mask is cut hard at this value (0 = keep the soft mask).

bg_invert.tooltip: remove background: invert the mask (keep the background instead).

bg_mask_blur.tooltip: remove background: Gaussian blur on the mask edge, in pixels (0 = none).

fill_holes_enabled.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte and SeC + MatAnyone2: fill holes inside the mask.

min_region_size.tooltip: SAM + ViTMatte and SeC + MatAnyone2: remove separate regions smaller than this many pixels (0 = keep all).

keep_model_loaded.tooltip: SeC + MatAnyone2 and remove background: keep the models in memory between runs (off = free them after each run).

split_masks.tooltip: Make the edge / inside / outside masks (and, for the three other backends, a trimap from the final alpha). Off leaves those outputs empty, which saves three to four full-size masks per frame on long clips.

background_plate.tooltip: matter = bgmattingv2 only: the same shot WITHOUT the subject (a clean plate). One frame serves every frame; a plate batch as long as the clip is used frame by frame; a different size is resized to the image. Not connected: a plate is synthesised from the coarse mask, which is much less accurate.

picks.tooltip: The selection made in the viewer on this node (JSON: frame, subject, excluded objects, added / cut parts). When set it replaces the prompt inputs of the chosen backend. Empty = the prompt inputs as wired.

MaskOpsMEC.name: MaskOpsMEC
MaskOpsMEC.description: Production-grade segmentation + matting + AUTO-QUALITY + diagnostics in one node. Multi-backend (SAM 2.1 / SAM 3 / SAM 3.1 / BiRefNet / RMBG-2.0 / InSPyReNet + ViTMatte / RVM / MatAnyone). Optional Nuke-style luma-key pre-stage, edge-aware trimap, and AUTO-QUALITY pipeline that detects motion blur, low light, low contrast, speckle noise and similar bg/fg, then applies just-enough pre-processing before the segmenter and a light guided-filter polish on the alpha — no knobs to tune. When you supply pos+neg points (e.g. pos on face, neg on neck) it picks the SAM candidate that excludes the neg points, so you get the face only, not the whole person. For manual 11-stage refinement (hole-fill, joint bilateral, DenseCRF, etc.) chain MaskRefineMEC downstream. The `backend` input also runs SAM + ViTMatte, SeC + MatAnyone2 or background removal (RMBG-2.0 / BiRefNet) - the former separate nodes - through the same outputs.
output_tooltips: Coarse mask from the segmenter (B,H,W).
Refined alpha after matter + refinement (production output).
image * alpha premultiplied preview.
Trimap (0/0.5/1) used by the matter.
Tight bbox around the alpha as [x0,y0,x1,y1].
Same bbox as JSON {'x','y','w','h'}.
Overall production-quality score in [0,1] (boundary + coherence + size + smoothness).
JSON: backends, modes, per-frame quality breakdown, refine stages run, settings used.
Image with backing-colour spill suppressed (when `despill_strength`>0).
RGBA light-wrap layer to ADD over the new background.
Soft edge band where matting actually matters.
Solid-fg interior mask (safe to colour-grade).
Solid-bg exterior mask (safe to defocus / replace).
Luminance keyer output (empty if `enable_luma_key` is off).
Diagnostic problem-region heatmap from the failure explainer.
Severity score [0,1] from the failure explainer.
Suggested next masking method (string) from the failure explainer.
Per-object alpha mattes stacked object-major as (O*B,H,W).
The image times the final alpha (premultiplied), despilled when despill is on.

MaskOrImageToWeight.name: MaskOrImageToWeight
MaskOrImageToWeight.description:
Gets the mean values from mask or image batch  
and returns that as the selected output type.

images.tooltip: Video frames or a single still (B,H,W,3).

prompt.tooltip: What to cut out, e.g. 'dog', 'car', 'mouth'. Needs sam_model (+ a GroundingDINO model) wired. Ignored when source_mask is wired.

grounding_model.tooltip: GroundingDINO model for text->box grounding (same list as SAM Mask Generator).

track_mode.tooltip: How the placement follows the video. static: same place every frame. landmark_lock: follows the wired `landmarks` (face or body points nearest the quad). object_track: follows the image content inside the quad (feature tracking, no model; frames with too little detail hold and `info` says so). auto: landmark_lock when landmarks are wired, else static.

anchor_frame.tooltip: The frame the quad was placed on (and segmented from, when using prompt without ref_image).

placement_json.tooltip: Editor-owned: {"corners":[[x,y]x4 TL,TR,BR,BL], "feather":px} in anchor-frame pixel coords. Empty = centered 60%-size quad.

feather_px.tooltip: Edge feather (Gaussian, px) applied to the placed alpha. placement_json's feather wins when present.

source_mask.tooltip: BYO alpha (e.g. SAM Mask Generator / matting output). Skips prompt segmentation entirely.

source_image.tooltip: RGB that source_mask cuts out of (for the placed_rgb output). When absent, the mask is placed without pixels.

ref_image.tooltip: Segment the prompt from THIS image instead of the video's anchor frame (e.g. a photo of the dog you want).

sam_model.tooltip: From SAM Model Loader — needed only for prompt-based segmentation.

allow_download.tooltip: Download the grounding model for a text prompt if it is not installed. Off: an installed copy is used wherever it is.

landmarks.tooltip: Per-frame landmarks (OpenPose JSON) for track_mode landmark_lock / auto, e.g. from Face Landmarks (Facepoints) or a DWPose estimator. One entry per frame, pixel coordinates.

mesh_keyframes_json.tooltip: Animated mesh warp. Empty = the placement quad, exactly as before. JSON {"rows":R,"cols":C,"interp":"linear"|"smooth","keys":[{"frame":f,"points":[[x,y],...]}]}: R and C 1-16 (default 1), each key (R+1)*(C+1) points ROW-MAJOR from the top-left in frame pixels - a 1x1 mesh is TL,TR,BL,BR (placement_json is TL,TR,BR,BL). Frames before the first key hold it, after the last hold it, between keys each point is interpolated (smooth = ease in/out). The source cut-out is split into the same grid and each cell is warped onto its mesh cell. Replaces the quad for warping; with landmark_lock / object_track the quad still drives tracking and each frame's mesh is moved by that frame's tracking transform.

occlusion_mask.tooltip: Things in FRONT of the placement: the placed alpha is multiplied by (1 - this mask). Resized (bilinear) to the frames when needed; one frame applies to all, a shorter batch holds its last frame.

depth_map.tooltip: Depth image (channel mean used, 0..1). Pixels nearer than placement_depth occlude the placement. Same resize / batch rules as occlusion_mask; combined with it by maximum.

placement_depth.tooltip: Depth of the placed object on the depth_map's 0..1 'nearness' scale: pixels with nearness above this are in front of it and hide it.

depth_near_is_white.tooltip: On: white (1) in depth_map is near (Depth Anything / MiDaS style). Off: white is far (nearness = 1 - depth).

depth_softness.tooltip: Width of the depth edge: occluder = clamp((nearness - placement_depth) / softness + 0.5, 0, 1). 0 = hard step (nearness > placement_depth).

MaskPlacementMEC.name: MaskPlacementMEC
MaskPlacementMEC.description: Universal mask placement: source an alpha (wire a mask, or give a text prompt + SAM model and it segments the object for you), place it with a draggable 4-corner perspective quad, and propagate across the video. track_mode landmark_lock follows wired landmarks (POSE_KEYPOINT, e.g. Face Landmarks (Facepoints) or DWPose) frame by frame; object_track follows the image content inside the quad (feature tracking, no model). How-to: docs/mask-placement.md.
output_tooltips: Per-frame placed alpha (B,H,W float 0..1). Feed to inpaint/composite.
Per-frame RGB of the placed source pixels over black (use with `masks` to composite).
Frames with the placement tinted + quad drawn — visual verification.
JSON: source mode, quad, per-frame status, and which tracking actually ran.
The occluder applied to `masks` (B,H,W 0..1): max of occlusion_mask and the depth_map test; all zeros when neither is wired. `masks` = placed alpha x (1 - occluder); placed_rgb is not changed.

MaskPreview.name: MaskPreview
MaskPreview.description: Preview the masks without saving them to the ComfyUI output directory.

MaskPreview+.name: MaskPreview+
MaskPreview+.description: Saves the input images to your ComfyUI output directory.

show_bbox.tooltip: Draw bounding box of mask region

MaskPreviewOverlay.name: MaskPreviewOverlay
MaskPreviewOverlay.description: Deprecated — kept so old workflows load. Closest current node: MaskOpsMEC preview output.

image.tooltip: RGB guide. Required for all edge-aware stages.

mask.tooltip: Mask to refine (soft or hard).

preset.tooltip: Picks sensible numeric defaults for every enabled stage. Override with `advanced_overrides_json` if needed.

auto_edge_lock.tooltip: Pin the mask to real image edges to stop bleeding into the background. Force-enables guided_filter + edge_snap with parameters tuned by `subject_class`. Recommended for any face / garment / product / hair workflow.

subject_class.tooltip:
Tunes auto_edge_lock for the dominant subject:
  general     — balanced edge protection
  face        — tight 2-3 px band, high snap, no morph dilate
  hair        — thin-recover ON, soft band, low snap
  garment     — medium band, medium snap, close holes
  object      — medium band, high snap, fill holes
  hard_surface— thin band, max snap, threshold > 0.5

enable_hole_fill.tooltip: Stage 1: fill holes inside the mask (eyes, mouths, textures the segmenter punched through).

morph_op.tooltip: Stage 2: morphology with a round brush. open removes specks, close fills slivers, dilate / erode grow / shrink.

enable_thin_recover.tooltip: Stage 3: bring back thin strands (hair, wire, grass) the segmenter cut off.

enable_joint_bilateral.tooltip: Stage 4: edge-preserving smoothing guided by the image. Needs opencv-contrib-python; skipped without it.

enable_guided_filter.tooltip: Stage 5: guided filter - snaps the soft edge to colour edges in the image (fast, no model).

enable_dense_crf.tooltip: Stage 6: DenseCRF boundary refinement (sharpest edges, slower). Needs pydensecrf; skipped without it.

enable_edge_snap.tooltip: Stage 7: pull the edge band toward image gradients - a cheap alternative to DenseCRF.

cascade_passes.tooltip: Extra refinement passes after stage 7: guided filter (plus joint bilateral / edge snap when on) again, radii halved each pass. 0 = none.

feather_sigma.tooltip: Blur the final soft edge (Gaussian sigma, pixels). 0 = off.

gamma.tooltip: Power curve on the soft alpha: above 1 thins semi-transparent edges, below 1 thickens them.

threshold.tooltip: Above 0: cut the result to a hard 0 / 1 mask at this value. 0 = keep it soft.

enable_domain_transform.tooltip: Gastal & Oliveira (2011) Domain Transform RGB-edge filter. Often sharper than guided filter on hair / fine detail; much faster than DenseCRF. Requires opencv-contrib-python (ximgproc).

enable_color_decontaminate.tooltip: Push alpha in the boundary band toward 0/1 using local LAB-distance to fg/bg means. Fixes 'halo' alpha bleed when bg has similar luminance.

enable_unsharp_alpha.tooltip: Sharpen the soft alpha (α + amount·(α − gauss(α))).

enable_anti_alias.tooltip: Sub-pixel boundary smoothing (bilinear up 2× → soft contrast → down).

enable_chroma_lock.tooltip: When fg/bg luminance is similar but chroma differs, weight the boundary by LAB chroma gradient instead of luma. Helps red-on-red, green-on-green, etc.

enable_speck_removal.tooltip: Drop foreground components below `speck_min_area` and fill background holes inside the subject.

enable_temporal_smooth.tooltip: Bidirectional alpha EMA across the batch dim (for VIDEO masks only). Removes flicker without lag.

advanced_overrides_json.tooltip: Optional JSON overriding any preset numeric. Example: {"gf_radius":12, "jb_sigma_color":40, "crf_iterations":8}. Recognised keys: hole_fill_threshold, morph_radius, thin_threshold, thin_min_branch_len, thin_branch_dilate, jb_diameter, jb_sigma_color, jb_sigma_space, gf_radius, gf_epsilon, crf_iterations, crf_gauss_sxy, crf_bilateral_sxy, crf_bilateral_srgb, edge_snap_strength, edge_snap_band, dt_sigma_s, dt_sigma_r, decontam_band, decontam_strength, unsharp_sigma, unsharp_amount, anti_alias_strength, chroma_lock_strength, chroma_lock_band, speck_min_area, speck_fill_holes_below, temporal_alpha, temporal_bidi.

enable_integrity_check.tooltip: Compute per-frame integrity stats on the refined mask (coverage, abrupt drops, frame-to-frame jumps) and append them to the `info` JSON. Adds negligible cost for single frames; cheap for short clips.

integrity_drop_threshold.tooltip: Relative coverage drop that flags a frame.

integrity_jump_threshold.tooltip: Relative frame-to-frame coverage jump that flags a frame.

refine_region.tooltip: everywhere: every stage works on the whole frame (as before). uncertain band only: the per-frame stages (hole fill ... anti-alias) run on a crop around the band where the INPUT mask is neither surely subject nor surely background, and only that band may change; frames with no uncertain pixel are skipped (faster on clean mattes). The finish stages (temporal smooth, feather, gamma, threshold) still apply to the whole matte. info reports the band's share and the skipped frames.

uncertainty_band_px.tooltip: uncertain band only: half-width of the band around the mask edge, in pixels (the edge is shrunk / grown by this much); a soft (feathered) edge widens it.

temporal_qc.tooltip: Add a temporal matte QC to info (clips): per frame the alpha change, how far the boundary moved (px) and the share of semi-transparent pixels that changed by more than 0.1, plus the 3 worst frames. Measured on the final soft alpha.

MaskRefineMEC.name: MaskRefineMEC
MaskRefineMEC.description: Unified, training-free mask refinement. Toggle each stage on or off and chain them in fixed order: hole-fill → morphology → thin-structure recover → joint bilateral → guided filter → DenseCRF → edge-snap → optional CascadePSP-style multi-pass → feather → gamma → threshold. No model weights. Optional deps: opencv-contrib-python (ximgproc joint bilateral), scikit-image (thin recovery), scipy (hole fill / morphology helpers), pydensecrf (DenseCRF). Each missing dep silently disables only its stage; the rest still run.
output_tooltips: Refined mask, same (B,H,W) as input.
Soft alpha (same as mask before threshold).
RGB×alpha preview for quick visual diff.
JSON describing which stages ran / were skipped.

mode.tooltip: What the node does. Each mode shows only its own controls.

colour_key_color.tooltip: key: colour: Target colour as #RRGGBB — the hue you want to keep or remove.

colour_key_colorspace.tooltip: key: colour: Distance metric. LAB separates dark navy from dark brown; RGB treats them as similar luminance.

colour_key_tolerance.tooltip: key: colour: How far a pixel's colour can drift from the pick and still count as a match.

colour_key_soft_falloff.tooltip: key: colour: Graded band outside tolerance — stops a colour key from cutting like a pair of scissors.

colour_key_invert.tooltip: key: colour: Swap matched and unmatched regions.

luma_key_mode.tooltip:
key: luma: Preset luminance range or custom thresholds.
auto: Analyzes image brightness to pick best range.
highlights: Keys bright regions (0.7–1.0).
midtones: Keys mid-range luminance (0.3–0.7).
shadows: Keys dark regions (0.0–0.3).
custom: Uses the low/high sliders directly.

luma_key_low.tooltip: key: luma: Low threshold – pixels with luminance below this become 0 in the mask. Only used directly in custom mode; presets override this.

luma_key_high.tooltip: key: luma: High threshold – pixels with luminance above this become 1 in the mask. Only used directly in custom mode; presets override this.

luma_key_gamma.tooltip: key: luma: Gamma correction applied after keying. >1 compresses mask toward black (reduces coverage). <1 expands mask toward white (increases coverage).

luma_key_falloff.tooltip: key: luma: Smoothness of the transition between low and high thresholds. 0 = hard binary edge. 1 = standard smooth. >1 = very gradual transition.

luma_key_invert.tooltip: key: luma: Invert the output mask (swap keyed and unkeyed regions).

luma_key_channel.tooltip: key: luma: Channel to key on. Luma is BT.709; hue/sat/value and LAB a/b isolate coloured spill without three separate nodes.

luma_key_low_soft.tooltip: key: luma: Blend-If split below low — ramp into the key instead of a hard cut that looks like a sticker.

luma_key_high_soft.tooltip: key: luma: Blend-If split above high — feather the highlight side of the range.

luma_key_invert_key.tooltip: key: luma: Invert the sampled channel before thresholding (ImageToMask behaviour). Distinct from invert, which flips the finished matte.

difference_key_tolerance.tooltip: key: difference: How far a pixel may differ from the clean plate and still count as background (0..1 of the RGB distance).

difference_key_softness.tooltip: key: difference: Width of the soft edge above the tolerance.

difference_key_invert.tooltip: key: difference: Key the unchanged part instead of what changed.

grade_gain.tooltip: grade: Multiply the matte (above 1 pushes greys toward white).

grade_gamma.tooltip: grade: Bend the greys: above 1 lifts them, below 1 sinks them; black and white stay put.

grade_invert.tooltip: grade: Flip the matte at the end.

grow_left.tooltip: grow / shrink: Pixels to grow the matte toward the left (negative shrinks its left edge).

grow_right.tooltip: grow / shrink: Pixels to grow toward the right (negative shrinks its right edge).

grow_up.tooltip: grow / shrink: Pixels to grow upward (negative shrinks its top edge).

grow_down.tooltip: grow / shrink: Pixels to grow downward (negative shrinks its bottom edge).

grow_feather.tooltip: grow / shrink: Soften the result by this blur radius in pixels.

gradient_width.tooltip: gradient: Output width when size_as is not connected.

gradient_height.tooltip: gradient: Output height when size_as is not connected.

gradient_type.tooltip: gradient: Ramp shape — linear edge fade, radial vignette, or angular wipe.

gradient_angle.tooltip: gradient: Direction for linear, or rotation offset for angular ramps.

gradient_center_x.tooltip: gradient: Radial/angular origin, normalised 0–1 across the frame.

gradient_center_y.tooltip: gradient: Radial/angular origin, normalised 0–1 down the frame.

gradient_start.tooltip: gradient: Mask value at the ramp start (black end).

gradient_end.tooltip: gradient: Mask value at the ramp end (white end).

grain_amount.tooltip: grain: Noise strength — enough to hide banding, not enough to read as texture.

grain_seed.tooltip: grain: Fixed seed holds the grain still through a sequence; upstream reseeded every frame and the matte crawled.

grain_size.tooltip: grain: Noise frequency — larger values give coarser, less speckly grain.

grain_invert.tooltip: grain: Flip mask polarity before adding grain.

motion_blur_angle.tooltip: motion blur: Blur direction in degrees, 0 = horizontal right.

motion_blur_distance.tooltip: motion blur: Blur length in pixels along the angle.

motion_blur_invert.tooltip: motion blur: Flip mask polarity before blurring.

edge_spread.tooltip: edge spread: How many pixels to push inward colour outward — kills the dark fringe on a lighter background.

edge_spread_invert_mask.tooltip: edge spread: Flip mask polarity when your matte is white-on-black.

image.tooltip: keys, edge spread and shuffle: the picture to work on (chroma key: the green / blue screen plate). Temporal cleanup: the clip, for protect_motion.

mask.tooltip: grade, grow / shrink, combine (first matte), grain, motion blur, transform, temporal cleanup; edge spread's matte; gradient's size when nothing else gives one.

plate.tooltip: key: difference - the clean plate (same shot, without the subject).

size_as.tooltip: gradient: take the size from this image.

transform_expand_x.tooltip: transform: Positive = dilate horizontally, Negative = erode horizontally

transform_expand_y.tooltip: transform: Positive = dilate vertically, Negative = erode vertically

transform_blur_x.tooltip: transform: Gaussian blur sigma along X axis

transform_blur_y.tooltip: transform: Gaussian blur sigma along Y axis

transform_feather.tooltip: transform: Feather (smooth edge) radius after transform

transform_threshold.tooltip: transform: Binarize mask after morph ops (0 = keep soft)

grow_angle.tooltip: grow / shrink: turn the up / down / left / right axes by this many degrees (counter-clockwise); 0 = the picture's axes.

grow_units.tooltip: grow / shrink: left / right / up / down in pixels, or in % of the matte's own width (left / right) and height (up / down).

grow_falloff.tooltip: grow / shrink: soft fall-off of the grown band, same units (0 = hard edge).

grow_follow_face.tooltip: grow / shrink: with face_pose connected, turn the axes with each frame's head tilt (added to grow_angle).

face_pose.tooltip: grow / shrink: Face Landmarks' pose_keypoint - the axes follow the head's tilt per frame (first face).

grade_blackpoint.tooltip: grade: this matte value becomes black (0) - raise it to crush faint spill.

grade_whitepoint.tooltip: grade: this matte value becomes white (1) - lower it to make a weak core solid.

grade_lift.tooltip: grade: raise (or lower) the blacks while white stays put.

grade_offset.tooltip: grade: add this to every value (before gamma).

chroma_key_screen.tooltip: key: chroma: The backdrop: green (#00B140) or blue (#0047BB) screen, or custom (the colour below; its strongest channel is the screen channel).

chroma_key_color.tooltip: key: chroma: custom screen: the backdrop colour as #RRGGBB (pick it from the plate).

chroma_key_balance.tooltip: key: chroma: How the screen channel is compared with the other two: 1 = against their max (removes less backdrop), 0 = against their min (removes more), 0.5 between.

chroma_key_gain.tooltip: key: chroma: Screen strength: above 1 removes the backdrop harder (cleaner background, thinner edges), below 1 softer.

chroma_key_clip_black.tooltip: key: chroma: Matte values at or below this become 0 (crush backdrop noise).

chroma_key_clip_white.tooltip: key: chroma: Matte values at or above this become 1 (make a see-through core solid). Must be above clip_black.

chroma_key_despill.tooltip: key: chroma: Spill suppression on the image output: the screen channel is limited to the average, the max (removes least) or the min (removes most) of the other two channels; off = image unchanged.

chroma_key_despill_strength.tooltip: key: chroma: How much of the spill above the limit is removed (1 = all).

chroma_key_invert.tooltip: key: chroma: Output the backdrop's matte instead of the subject's.

temporal_cleanup_window.tooltip: temporal cleanup: Frames on each side that vote (fewer at the clip's ends).

temporal_cleanup_method.tooltip: temporal cleanup: median: removes one-frame drop-outs and pops and keeps edges hard (an even count takes the lower middle value); mean: softer, averages flicker away but blurs fast motion.

temporal_cleanup_hysteresis.tooltip: temporal cleanup: Above 0: a pixel switches on only above 0.5 + this and off only below 0.5 - this, so boundary chatter stops; the output becomes binary. 0 = off.

temporal_cleanup_protect_motion.tooltip: temporal cleanup: With `image` wired (same frames and size): where the picture changes by more than this between frames, the original matte is kept so fast motion does not lag. 0 = off.

MaskToolsMEC.name: MaskToolsMEC
MaskToolsMEC.description: Keyers and matte operations in one node: colour, luma and difference keys; grade (gain, gamma, clamp, invert, black / white point, lift, offset - as Nuke Grade); grow or shrink each side (left / right / up / down) with a feather; combine two mattes; gradient; grain; motion blur; edge spread; channel shuffle; transform (grow, blur and offset per axis, feather, threshold, invert); chroma key with despill (green / blue / custom screen); temporal cleanup of a matte over a clip (median / mean window, hysteresis, motion protection).
output_tooltips: The matte (shuffle: the new alpha; edge spread: the matte it used).
edge spread / shuffle: the processed picture. Other modes: the matte as a grey image, to look at.
What the node did, and anything worth knowing (clamped values, resized inputs).

mode.tooltip:
motion: per-frame motion mask (pixel/flow/bg/hist).
propagate: seed mask on one frame, push to all frames.
anchor: SDF interpolation between anchor masks.
consistency_check: score flicker between consecutive frames.
stabilize: smooth a mask batch over time and flag frames that drop or jump.
spline_track: follow spline keyframes through the video (Lucas-Kanade).
bbox_smooth: smooth a list of boxes over time.

anchor_frames.tooltip: [anchor] CSV frame indices for each anchor mask

mask.tooltip: Required by propagate (seed), anchor (anchor stack), consistency_check (mask_iou). Optional for motion.

video.tooltip: Video frame batch (B,H,W,C). Required by motion, propagate, anchor flow_refinement, and pixel/flow consistency.

stabilize_temporal_mode.tooltip: [stabilize] none = integrity report only; gaussian = smooth across frames; raft_flow = blend each frame with the flow-warped previous one.

stabilize_blend.tooltip: [stabilize] mix factor: 1.0 = pure warped-previous, 0.0 = current only.

stabilize_drop_threshold.tooltip: [stabilize] area ratio / IoU below this flags the frame.

stabilize_jump_threshold.tooltip: [stabilize] centroid jump (normalized) above this flags the frame.

spline_data.tooltip: [spline_track] keyframes from the spline tracker canvas: [{frame:int, points:[[x,y],…]}, …].

spline_closed.tooltip: [spline_track] closed loop (a filled shape) vs open path (a stroke).

spline_tracking_weight.tooltip: [spline_track] blend between the tracker and the keyframe interpolation (1 = pure Lucas-Kanade, 0 = pure interpolation).

spline_stroke_width.tooltip: [spline_track] stroke width of an open spline.

bbox_json.tooltip: [bbox_smooth] JSON array of [x,y,w,h], one per frame.

allow_download.tooltip: [stabilize, raft_flow] let the node download torchvision's RAFT-small weights (about 4 MB) if they are not on this machine yet. Off: an existing copy is used; none = a plain message.

match_mode.tooltip:
Selects how the generated VFX is processed before output (only the selected branch runs):
- Disabled (pass-through): outputs the generated video unchanged.
- Color Match: only works from the second iteration on; matches the video based on the first generation.
- Compose + Match: composites the VFX based on the mask and matches its grading to the plate (heavier).

passthrough.tooltip: Disabled branch: wire the generated video here to output it unchanged.

color_match.tooltip: Color Match branch: the color-matched video (matched to the first generation; from the 2nd iteration on).

compose_match.tooltip: Compose + Match branch: output of the Compose + Match node (composites the VFX and grades it to the plate).

detector_variant.tooltip: Face detector range. 'short' is tuned for close-up faces (within ~2 m of the camera); 'full' covers farther / smaller faces (up to ~5 m) but is slower. 'both' runs both detectors and keeps whichever found more faces per frame (~2× detection cost).

missing_frame_fallback.tooltip: Per-frame behaviour when detection fails in a batch. 'empty' leaves the frame faceless. 'previous' copies the most recent successful detection. 'interpolate' lerps landmarks/bbox/blendshapes between bracketing successful frames. Multi-face: pairs faces across frames by greedy bbox-centre NN.
