MiniMaxH3_EnhancePrompt.description: Turns a one-line idea plus reference images into a MiniMax-H3 prompt, using a local vision model (Ollama / LM Studio / OpenAI-compatible). Wire `prompt` into the Director's global_prompt and `ref_images` into its ref_images, so the model describes exactly the images H3 conditions on.

crops.tooltip:
Wire the INPUT crops here - the 'crops' output of H3 Face Track + Crop - NOT the refined/decoded result.

This matches FaceDetailer: make_sam_mask() runs on the SOURCE image and the resulting mask is what the enhanced patch is later pasted through. Generation never feeds back into the mask.

Masking the generated result instead is actively wrong: if the model nudges the face inward, the mask traces the NEW, smaller silhouette and the ORIGINAL face pokes out past it - most visibly the nose on profile shots. Masking the input covers where the face actually is in the footage being replaced.

It is also cheaper: no dependency on the sampler, so SAM need not be resident alongside the video model.

sam_model.tooltip: SAM model (Impact Pack SAMLoader). Prompted per frame with the face box and its centre point; moved to the device for the run and released afterwards.

transform.tooltip: The transform from H3 Face Track + Crop; its per-frame face rectangles (canvas space) are the SAM box prompts and the fallback masks.

threshold.tooltip: Passed to the SAM model's predict() as its score threshold (0-1). Higher rejects more masks; frames with no accepted mask use sam_fallback.

dilation.tooltip: Mirrors FaceDetailer's sam_dilation default of 0. SAM masks are accurate, so they rarely need growing.

temporal_smooth.tooltip: Frames of averaging across the mask stack. 1 disables it and you will likely see the mask edge shimmer.

sam_fallback.tooltip: A frame SAM cannot segment: the face rectangle (a box edge can pop in a feathered paste; the report names those frames), or the nearest segmented frame's mask moved with the face.

output_tooltips: MASK batch in crop-canvas space, one per frame (1 = face), dilated and temporally averaged. Wire to H3 Face Stitch Back masks.
Text summary: frames segmented by SAM, frames that fell back (rectangle or held mask), dilation, smoothing and mean mask coverage.
MiniMaxH3_FaceMaskSAM.name: MiniMaxH3_FaceMaskSAM
MiniMaxH3_FaceMaskSAM.description: Per-frame SAM face masks on the stabilised crops, temporally smoothed.

base_images.tooltip: The full frames the crops were taken from (same size as the transform's source, else an error). The refined faces are pasted into a copy of these.

refined_crops.tooltip: H3-refined face crops, one per frame, on the crop canvas. If the frame count differs from base_images, only the shorter count is pasted.

transform.tooltip: The transform output of H3 Face Track + Crop for this clip: maps each crop back to its box in the frame and supplies detection fade weights.

paste_region.tooltip: WHAT gets composited back. face_only / face_ellipse paste just the detected face box (FaceDetailer's behaviour - the wider crop exists to give the sampler context, not to be pasted). full_crop pastes the whole crop including hair, shoulders and background, which risks a visible rectangle if H3 alters them.

mask_dilation.tooltip: Grow the face box before blurring, in canvas px. Impact Pack dilates the same way so the blur has room and the blend does not eat into the face itself.

feather.tooltip:
Gaussian blur radius on the paste mask, in SOURCE pixels. Measured against the final frame, not the canvas, so the blend is the same physical width whatever this frame's magnification happens to be.

Canvas-relative feather is a trap: a 75px crop blown up to 512 makes a 40px canvas feather only ~6 source px, while a 720px crop makes it ~56. The blend ends up TIGHTEST exactly where the face is smallest and the composite needs the most help - which reads as a hard edge appearing as a shot zooms out.

colour_match.tooltip: Match the refined crop's per-channel mean/std to the region it replaces. The crop and the full frame went through independent passes, so without this the face can come back subtly brighter or differently tinted and read as pasted on.

blend.tooltip: Global opacity of the refined face. Below 1.0 mixes back toward the original - useful to dial back over-sharpening.

undetected_frames.tooltip:
What to do on frames where no FACE was found (turned away / occluded). ALL frames are still sent through H3 either way - that is what keeps it temporally consistent - this only controls whether the result is pasted back.
fade_out: ramp the composite to zero across the gap (smooth, no pop, recommended).
skip: hard cut - those frames keep original pixels exactly.
composite_anyway: paste regardless. Risks H3 hallucinating a face onto the back of a head.

feather_scales_with_crop.tooltip: Old behaviour: treat feather as CANVAS pixels, so the blend narrows as the crop shrinks. Leave off.

masks.tooltip: Optional per-frame paste masks in CANVAS space, e.g. from H3 Face Mask (SAM). Overrides paste_region. This is the FaceDetailer bbox+SAM path: the mask follows the actual face so the blend falls on the jaw and hairline instead of an arbitrary rectangle. With a SAM mask use a SMALL feather (4-8); a rectangle needs much more.

output_tooltips: IMAGE batch: base_images with the refined faces composited in (same size and frame count as base_images).
MiniMaxH3_FaceStitch.name: MiniMaxH3_FaceStitch
MiniMaxH3_FaceStitch.description: Composite H3-refined face crops back into the source frames.

images.tooltip: Source video frames (IMAGE batch) to track the face in and crop from.

detector.tooltip: Ultralytics YOLO face detector from models/ultralytics (bbox) that finds the face box in every frame. Loaded once and cached.

confidence.tooltip: Minimum detector score (0-1) for a box to count, for the face detector and the fallback detector. Lower finds more faces but more false boxes; frames with no face are interpolated.

crop_factor.tooltip: Crop side as a multiple of detected face HEIGHT. 2.5 puts the face at ~40% of the crop, comfortably inside H3's good regime. Bigger = more context so the seam lands in hair/background, but less magnification. 2.0-3.0 is the useful range.

canvas_width.tooltip: Resolution H3 generates at. 512 is cheap; 768 is H3's native short edge and gives the best faces. Ignored when canvas_mode is not 'manual'. Cost scales with area: 768 is 2.25x the latent tokens of 512.

canvas_height.tooltip: Height in pixels of every crop (the H3 canvas). With canvas_width it sets the crop aspect. Ignored when canvas_mode is not 'manual' (the auto modes use a square canvas).

canvas_mode.tooltip:
manual: use canvas_width/height as given.
auto_no_downscale: size the canvas from the LARGEST crop in the clip so no frame is ever downscaled (magnification never drops below 1.0x). Can get expensive on clips that include close-ups.
auto_capped_768: same, but clamped to 768 - H3's native short edge and a sane VRAM ceiling.

smooth_window.tooltip: Frames of smoothing on the crop CENTRE. 21 at 24fps is ~0.9s. Raise if the box still shivers; lower if it lags behind fast head movement.

size_smooth_window.tooltip: Frames of smoothing on the crop SIZE. Wants MORE than the centre: size jitter makes the crop breathe, which changes the resample factor every frame and reads as shimmer. Real zoom moves are slow, so heavy smoothing here costs nothing.

smooth_method.tooltip: gaussian: best jitter rejection. savgol: preserves the shape of a push-in better at large windows. moving_average: the old boxcar, leaves residual jitter.

size_mode.tooltip: per_frame: constant face-fraction in every crop (correct for push-ins). max_of_clip: one size for the whole clip, only useful when the shot is genuinely static.

identity_track.tooltip: Hold one subject through a crowd. Continuity (nearest box to the previous position) decides most frames; the face-identity embedding is consulted only when two candidates are similarly plausible or their boxes overlap - which is both the accurate and the cheap arrangement, since the embedding model then runs on a handful of frames instead of all of them. The anchor is taken FROM THE CLIP by default (frames where one face clearly dominates), because an external stylised reference sits in a different domain - measured similarity between an illustration and a render of the same character was only 0.305, where same-domain faces score 0.5-0.7.

identity_threshold.tooltip: Minimum cosine similarity to accept a face as the reference person. Below this the frame falls back to continuity (nearest to the previous position at a similar size), which is what carries tracking through profiles and partial occlusion where embeddings become unreliable.

select.tooltip: Used only when no identity_reference is connected, and as the first-frame tie-break.

fallback_detector.tooltip: Used only on frames where the FACE detector finds nothing (subject turned away). A person/body model such as segm\person_yolov8m-seg.pt gives a real head position from the top of the body box, which beats interpolating blindly between the last and next face. Set 'none' to interpolate instead.

fallback_head_frac.tooltip: Head centre as a multiple of face height below the top of the person box. 0.5 puts it half a face-height down, which is about right for a head seen from behind.

identity_reference.tooltip:
A clear face image of the person to track. When supplied, the subject is chosen by FACE IDENTITY rather than by size, so a crowd scene locks onto the right person even when someone else is briefly larger or nearer.

Without it, 'largest' has no notion of WHO it is following - it just takes the biggest box each frame, which switches subject whenever the framing changes.

FOR MULTIPLE PEOPLE: run the pipeline once per subject, each with that person's reference here and their own refs on the H3 node, and chain them - feed run 1's stitched output in as run 2's base_images. The composites accumulate.

output_tooltips: IMAGE batch, one canvas_w×canvas_h face crop per input frame (smoothed track). Feed to the H3 refine pass and to H3 Face Mask (SAM).
Per-frame crop boxes, canvas and source size, detection flags and fade weights. Needed by H3 Face Stitch Back, Face Mask (SAM) and Face Transform Info.
Source frames with the crop box drawn: green = face detected, yellow = body fallback, red = interpolated across a gap.
Text summary: tracking/identity counts, detection rate, face and crop sizes, magnification, jitter before/after smoothing, dropouts and warnings.
Final crop width in pixels (after canvas_mode). Wire to the H3 node's width.
Final crop height in pixels (after canvas_mode). Wire to the H3 node's height.
MiniMaxH3_FaceTrackCrop.name: MiniMaxH3_FaceTrackCrop
MiniMaxH3_FaceTrackCrop.description: Per-frame face track -> smoothed, normalised crop -> constant-size batch for H3, plus the transform needed to paste the result back.

transform.tooltip: The transform from H3 Face Track + Crop to print.

max_rows.tooltip: Roughly how many frame rows to list: every (frames / max_rows)-th frame is shown.

output_tooltips: Text table: frame count, canvas and source size, then per sampled frame the crop box x/y/w/h in source pixels and its magnification. Also printed to the console.
MiniMaxH3_FaceTransformInfo.name: MiniMaxH3_FaceTransformInfo
MiniMaxH3_FaceTransformInfo.description: Print the per-frame transform - sanity-check tracking before spending GPU time.

family.tooltip: Edit task whose six-section prompt template is used (lipsync, face_swap, restyle, ... and the replace_* character families). environment_weather, element_swap and the replacement families set mask_required.

subject_name.tooltip: Words that describe <Subject 1> in the prompt (empty = 'primary subject').

task_notes.tooltip: Free text appended to the family's task sentence in the prompt (stripped; empty adds nothing).

references_manifest.tooltip: Free-text list of the reference assets; not used in the prompt, only copied (stripped) into pipeline_notes JSON as 'references_manifest'.

frame_count.tooltip: Clip length in frames, written to pipeline_notes only (not used in the prompt); Edit Validator flags it when it is off H3's 17k+5 grid.

head_size_mode.tooltip: Character replacement families: how big the new head is - match character proportions (the reference's own head-to-body ratio) or keep original composition (the original head's size and position). Set the same mode on H3 Subject Crop.

face_closeup_reference.tooltip: Character replacement families: you also wire a tight face crop of the character as ref_image_1 (e.g. H3 Face Track + Crop on the character image). The prompt then names it <Picture 2>, the authority for facial identity. Ignored by expression_transfer. Experimental: not A/B-tested on H3 weights.

output_tooltips: The six-section H3 prompt text (section headers + bodies) for the text encoder.

JSON: family, task-type prefix, mask_required, guidance_scale (pinned 1.0), frame_count, references_manifest, subject labels (+ head size / face close-up for replacement families); read by Edit Validator.
One line: family, mask_required, guidance_scale and frame_count.
MiniMaxH3_FamilyPresets.name: MiniMaxH3_FamilyPresets
MiniMaxH3_FamilyPresets.description: Emit catalog #14 six-section prompt shape and #16 style DNA fields. environment_weather and element_swap set mask_required in pipeline_notes.

model.tooltip: Native MiniMax H3 MODEL. Cloned and every DiT block patched; errors if another cache (Block Cache T8, EasyCache, LazyCache, CacheDiT, a second FBC) or any dit block replace is already on it - connect it right after the model loader.

mode.tooltip: A calibrated preset, or Custom to use the values below. In preset mode the manual values are IGNORED - the preset name is what ran.

threshold.tooltip: How much block 0's residual may move before the step must run in full. Relative, not absolute: 0.08 means 8%. Higher is faster and freezes motion sooner. Custom mode only.

start_percent.tooltip: Skip nothing before this point in the denoise. Early steps decide composition, so caching there changes what the shot is of. Custom mode only.

end_percent.tooltip: Skip nothing after this point. The last steps are fine detail and cheap to get wrong. Custom mode only.

max_consecutive_hits.tooltip: How many steps may be skipped back to back. Error compounds: two is recoverable, ten is a still frame. Custom mode only.

warmup_steps.tooltip: Run this many steps in full before caching is allowed at all, regardless of the window. Custom mode only.

temporal_guard.tooltip: Decide on the WORST single frame instead of the whole-clip average. Without it, one frame can change completely while the average stays under threshold - that frame then freezes while the rest of the shot moves. Leave it on for video. Custom mode only.

metric_stride.tooltip: Compare every Nth row instead of all of them. The comparison allocates too; on a long clip a stride of 4 decides the same and costs less. Custom mode only.

output_tooltips: Clone of the H3 model with the first-block cache on all blocks plus sample/diffusion wrappers. Wire it to the sampler; the input model is unchanged.
What was installed. The RUN statistics - how many steps were actually reused - are logged when sampling finishes, because they do not exist yet when this node runs.
MiniMaxH3_FirstBlockCache.name: MiniMaxH3_FirstBlockCache
MiniMaxH3_FirstBlockCache.description: Skip the transformer stack on steps where block 0 says almost nothing changed, reusing the previous step's result for blocks 1..N. Typically 1.3-1.8x with no visible difference. Pushed too far it does not add artefacts - it FREEZES motion, which is harder to notice, so the temporal guard and the warmup are on by default and the report says what actually happened.

images.tooltip: Frames to pad or trim (IMAGE batch). Padding repeats the first (head) or last (tail) frame; trimming drops frames from that side.

handle_frames.tooltip: Frames to add (positive) or trim (negative). 0 + grid mode = auto-pad.

padding_mode.tooltip: Frame grid to land on. H3: 17n+5, WAN: 4n+1, LTX2: 8n+1 - the count is rounded UP to the grid after handle_frames (handle_frames 0 = pad only to the next legal count). disabled: exactly handle_frames, no grid.

handle_side.tooltip: Side where frames (and matching audio) are added or removed: head = before the first frame, tail = after the last.

fps.tooltip: Frame rate used to convert padded/trimmed frames to audio samples (frames / fps x sample_rate). Only matters with audio wired; stored in the handles record.

audio.tooltip: Optional soundtrack kept in sync: silence is inserted where frames are padded and samples are cut where frames are trimmed, on the same side.

undo_handles.tooltip: Wire the 'handles' output of the Frame Handles node that padded these frames (before the model). This node then REMOVES exactly those frames and that sound instead of padding; the widgets above are ignored.

output_tooltips: The padded / trimmed IMAGE batch (or, with undo_handles, the clip with the earlier padding removed).
The audio shifted to match the frame change (silence padding or cut samples); None when no audio is wired.
Number of frames in the images output.
Plain-text summary: original and final frame counts, frames added/trimmed per side, grid mode, fps.
What was padded (JSON). Wire it to undo_handles of a second Frame Handles after the model to trim the clip back.
MiniMaxH3_FrameHandles.name: MiniMaxH3_FrameHandles
MiniMaxH3_FrameHandles.description:
Add or trim editorial handles and land frame count on a model grid.
padding_mode: disabled | H3 (17n+5) | WAN (4n+1) | LTX2 (8n+1).
Audio is re-synced when frame count changes (silence padded at head).
Trim back after the model: a second H3 Frame Handles with its undo_handles wired to the first one's handles output removes exactly the frames and sound that were added, so the delivered clip starts on the plate's first frame.

frames.tooltip:
Comma- or newline-separated frames and ranges:
  12         a single frame
  0:24       frames 0-23 (stop EXCLUDED, as in Python)
  0:24:2     every second frame
  100:end    from 100 to the last frame
  -5         the fifth frame from the end
Overlaps collapse. A RANGE that overruns the clip clamps; a single FRAME outside it is an error, because that is a typo rather than an intent.

frame_count.tooltip: Frames in the clip this mask must match.

width.tooltip: Mask width in px (match the clip's frames).

height.tooltip: Mask height in px (match the clip's frames).

invert.tooltip: Mask the frames you did NOT list instead.

output_tooltips: MASK [frame_count, height, width]: 1 on every pixel of a selected frame, 0 elsewhere (swapped when invert is on).
Text: frames masked out of frame_count, size, inverted, and each parsed segment with its frame count.
MiniMaxH3_FrameRangeMask.name: MiniMaxH3_FrameRangeMask
MiniMaxH3_FrameRangeMask.description:
Build a video MASK straight from a frame list - selected frames are fully masked, the rest empty.

Saves building the batch elsewhere and hoping the frame count lines up. Python slice semantics, so it behaves the way list indexing already does: the stop frame is EXCLUDED, negatives count back from the end, and a range that overruns the clip clamps instead of failing.

media.tooltip: From H3 Media Probe (or CustomNodePacks' Load Video (C2C)).

start.tooltip: First frame of the window (0 = first frame of the media).

count.tooltip: Frames in the window. 0 = to the end (still checked against memory). H3 generates 17k+5 frames (22, 39, 56, 73, 90, 107, 124 ...); the default 81 is not on that grid - the window's JSON says the nearest ones.

lookbehind.tooltip: Extra frames before the window, e.g. for a tracker. Reported separately, never counted as window frames.

step.tooltip: Take every Nth frame (inside the window and the handles).

output_tooltips: Lookbehind + window + lookahead, in order.
Contract h3.frame_window v1: source frames, exact times, which rows are the window.
Row of the first window frame inside images.
Number of window frames inside images.
The sound of exactly these frames (handles included; held frames at the head = silence first). With step > 1: silence.
MiniMaxH3_FrameWindow.name: MiniMaxH3_FrameWindow
MiniMaxH3_FrameWindow.description: Decodes only a window of a long video - start, count, plus tracking handles before and after - checked against free memory first. Every frame keeps its source index and exact time (window_json, contract h3.frame_window v1). Variable frame rate safe.

positive.tooltip: The conditioning the guider / sampler gets.

latent.tooltip: The latent the sampler starts from (with its noise mask).

bboxes.tooltip: Optional crop boxes from Subject Crop: offsets are also given in original-plate pixels.

output_tooltips: Plain-English findings.
The same, as JSON, for tools and tests.
MiniMaxH3_GeometryReport.name: MiniMaxH3_GeometryReport
MiniMaxH3_GeometryReport.description: Before sampling: where each reference, guide and mask lands on H3's token grid. Wire the positive conditioning and the latent the sampler gets. It says, in pixels, how far a reference video that shows the same shot is from the output's own tokens, whether guides share the output's grid, whether picture and sound have the same length, and what the noise mask keeps once ComfyUI has pooled it. Reads shapes only - no model, instant.

mode.tooltip: The H3 task. It decides the prompt structure and which references it needs.
options: V2V edit - edit the source video
Replacement - replace a subject in the plate

brief.tooltip: What should happen, in plain words. Name references as <Picture 1>, <Video 1>, <Audio 1> to give each a role.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Aspect ratio stated to the model in the request (LLM providers; the template does not use it). Text only: nothing is resized.

provider.tooltip: template (no LLM) is offline and deterministic. The others write the prompt with a model: local (transformers, GGUF) or over HTTP.

model_preset.tooltip: A tested model list. model_id, when filled, wins.

model_id.tooltip: Any model: a Hugging Face repo id (Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, google/gemma-4-E4B-it, Jackrong/Qwopus3.5-4B-v3 ...), a local folder or .gguf file, org/repo::file.gguf, an Ollama tag or an API model name.

api_key_env.tooltip: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key (blank = the provider's usual one). The key is never stored in the workflow.

device.tooltip: Local transformers model only: where it runs. auto = CUDA when available, else CPU; cuda stops with an error when there is no GPU.

dtype.tooltip: Local transformers model only: weight precision. auto = float32 on CPU, the checkpoint's own dtype on CUDA.

quantization.tooltip: 8-bit / 4-bit need bitsandbytes and a CUDA GPU.

trust_remote_code.tooltip: Run the model repo's own Python code. Only for repos you trust.

gguf_gpu_layers.tooltip: Layers on the GPU (-1 = all, 0 = CPU only).

unload_after.tooltip: Free the local model after the run.

downloads.tooltip: Download a missing local model (and the two official H3 guides, 40 KB) into models/LLM when the node runs. The C2C setting 'Never download models' always wins.

media_to_model.tooltip: What the model receives besides the reference labels.
media_to_model.default: send connected media (error if the model cannot take it)
options: send connected media (error if the model cannot take it)
images and video only (audio as a label)

video_samples.tooltip: Frames on each video's contact sheet.

temperature.tooltip: Sampling temperature of the model's reply (top_p 0.95); the one repair request always uses 0.3.

max_tokens.tooltip: Most tokens the model may reply with. A reply cut off at this limit is an error: raise it.

seed.tooltip: Change it for a different reply from the same inputs.

repair.tooltip: When an objective format check fails, ask the model for one correction.

timeout_s.tooltip: Longest wait for one reply (HTTP request or llama.cpp child process).

retries.tooltip: Extra attempts after a timeout, 429 or 5xx.

keep_plate_audio.tooltip: V2V edit / Replacement / Continuation: the source video's own sound is kept (audio reuse) when it has one.

mode: V2V edit - edit the source video
Replacement - replace a subject in the plate

images.tooltip: Pictures: each batch item is the next <Picture N>.

images_2.tooltip: More pictures (another size), numbered after images.

video.tooltip: <Video 1>: the source or reference video.

video_frames.tooltip: A video as an IMAGE sequence: the next <Video N>.

video_frames_fps.tooltip: Frame rate of video_frames, for the timestamps.

audio.tooltip: <Audio 1>. Mixed to mono, the first 30 s sent as 16 kHz WAV when media_to_model sends media and the model takes audio; otherwise only the label (its role comes from the brief).

output_tooltips: The H3 prompt in the mode's official format: the template's text, or the model's reply (corrected once when repair is on and the format audit fails).
The negative input, or a short built-in default negative when it is blank.
Text report: mode and provider, each reference and whether it was sent, guide source, format audit, repair, tokens and timing (API keys removed).
MiniMaxH3_H3PromptWriter.name: MiniMaxH3_H3PromptWriter
MiniMaxH3_H3PromptWriter.description: Writes a MiniMax H3 prompt in the official format for the chosen mode, looking at the connected pictures, video and audio. Any model: the offline template, local Hugging Face or GGUF models, Ollama, an OpenAI-compatible server, or the OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini APIs.

image.tooltip: Scene-linear HDR after Log Decode.

table.tooltip: One 'luma: stops' line per point (luma linear, 1.0 = diffuse white; stops the VAE ADDS, negative = it darkens). '#' starts a comment. Flat outside the table.

strength.tooltip: 1 = apply the table as written, 0 = off.

output_tooltips: Scene-linear HDR, each pixel scaled by 2^(-bias(luma) x strength); colour ratios unchanged, not clamped.
Text: parsed table points, strength, mean correction in stops and min/max/% above 1 of the output.
MiniMaxH3_HDRBiasCorrect.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRBiasCorrect
MiniMaxH3_HDRBiasCorrect.description: Undoes the H3 VAE's known exposure bias: every pixel is multiplied by 2^(-bias(luma) x strength), the bias looked up in an editable 'luma: stops' table (log-luma interpolation). Luminance only: colour ratios are unchanged. Default table = the owner's sheet, diffhdr_log_16384 column.

image.tooltip: The SDR picture (0..1 sRGB code values).

over.tooltip: Over-exposed when any channel is at or above this code value.

under.tooltip: Under-exposed when the luma of the code values is at or below this.

grow.tooltip: Dilate both masks by this many pixels.

feather.tooltip: Soften the edges over this many pixels.

output_tooltips: MASK, 1 = over-exposed (any channel >= 'over'), after grow and feather; one mask per frame.
MASK, 1 = under-exposed (Rec.709 luma of the code values <= 'under'), after grow and feather; one mask per frame.
MiniMaxH3_HDRClipMask.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRClipMask
MiniMaxH3_HDRClipMask.description: Where the SDR source is clipped: over = any channel at or above 'over'; under = luma at or below 'under'. Optional grow (dilate) and feather (soft edge) in pixels.

decoded.tooltip: Linear HDR from the pipeline (after Log Decode / Bias Correct).

ground_truth.tooltip: The true linear HDR frames (e.g. Load EXR Sequence).

encoding.tooltip: Curve for the code-domain PSNR and the 8-bit baseline.

output_tooltips: Text table: frames compared, luminance error in stops per brightness band (mean, p99, bias), worst channel, 8-bit rounding baseline and code-domain PSNR.
MiniMaxH3_HDREvalReport.name: MiniMaxH3_HDREvalReport
MiniMaxH3_HDREvalReport.description: Decoded HDR vs ground truth: luminance error in stops per brightness band (mean, p99, bias), worst channel, 8-bit rounding baseline and code-domain PSNR (the H3HDR-Test report).

repo_type.tooltip: Hugging Face repo kind used for the file listing and the snapshot download: dataset = huggingface.co/datasets/<repo_id>, model = a model repo.

cap_gb.tooltip: Refuse the fetch when the matching files total more than this.

wait.tooltip: On: the node waits for the job (progress bar; ComfyUI's Cancel stops it). Off: it returns at once and the job keeps running in the background - follow it in the HDR jobs panel on this node.

output_tooltips: Absolute path of the download folder (output_folder resolved).
JSON summary of the finished download job: repo, patterns, files and size (or a 'started in the background' note when wait is off).
MiniMaxH3_HDRFetchHuggingFace.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRFetchHuggingFace
MiniMaxH3_HDRFetchHuggingFace.display_name: H3 HDR Dataset · Fetch Hugging Face
MiniMaxH3_HDRFetchHuggingFace.description: Downloads the files of a Hugging Face repo that match the allow patterns (snapshot download). The total size is checked BEFORE anything downloads and the fetch is refused above the GB cap. Private / gated repos use the HF_TOKEN environment variable (never an input, never logged).

output_folder.tooltip: Where the HDRIs go. Relative = inside ComfyUI's output folder.

category.tooltip: Poly Haven HDRI category ('all' = no filter).

resolution.tooltip: 2k is plenty for 1344x768 renders at a 60 deg field of view; 8k files are large (100-300 MB each).

limit.tooltip: How many HDRIs (0 = the whole category).

wait.tooltip: On: the node waits for the job (progress bar; ComfyUI's Cancel stops it). Off: it returns at once and the job keeps running in the background - follow it in the HDR jobs panel on this node.

output_tooltips: Absolute path of the HDRI download folder; wire to HDRI -> Clips 'hdri_folder'.
JSON summary of the finished download job (or a 'started in the background' note when wait is off).
MiniMaxH3_HDRFetchPolyHaven.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRFetchPolyHaven
MiniMaxH3_HDRFetchPolyHaven.display_name: H3 HDR Dataset · Fetch Poly Haven
MiniMaxH3_HDRFetchPolyHaven.description: Downloads CC0 HDRIs from Poly Haven (public API api.polyhaven.com) into a folder: most downloaded first, resumable (.part files continue), size + md5 checked, files already there are skipped. Writes a small .json per HDRI (name, categories, tags) used for captions.

draft_hdr.tooltip: Linear HDR at draft size (Log Decode / Bias Correct output).

regen.tooltip: Regenerate STD 4K output of the SAME SDR clip (sRGB 0..1), same frames.

eps.tooltip: Floor of the linear Regenerate picture in the gain division (protects black).

radius.tooltip: Guided-filter window radius at draft resolution: larger = smoother gain.

output_tooltips: Linear HDR at the 'regen' resolution (sRGB-decoded regen x upsampled gain), one frame per input frame; not clamped. Save with Save EXR Sequence or Save HDR10.
Text: draft and regen sizes, gain range, frame count and output min/max/% above 1.
MiniMaxH3_HDRGainMapJoin.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRGainMapJoin
MiniMaxH3_HDRGainMapJoin.description: Draft-resolution linear HDR + the Regenerate 4K SDR output -> 4K linear HDR: gain = hdr / max(downscale(regen_linear), eps), upsampled to 4K with a guided filter on the 4K luma, times the 4K linear picture. Detail from Regenerate, light from the HDR draft. Not clamped.

image.tooltip: Scene-linear frames (not log codes).

output_tooltips: Linear RGB in the target primaries (3x3 matrix applied); not clamped, so out-of-gamut negatives and values above 1 stay.
MiniMaxH3_HDRGamutConvert.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRGamutConvert
MiniMaxH3_HDRGamutConvert.description: Linear RGB 3x3 matrix between Rec.709, Rec.2020 and ACEScg (AP1). No clamp: out-of-gamut values stay.

hdri_folder.tooltip: Folder of .hdr / .exr panoramas (Fetch Poly Haven's output).

output_folder.tooltip: One sub-folder per clip. Relative = inside ComfyUI's output folder.

clips_per_hdri.tooltip: Camera moves rendered per HDRI; each becomes its own clip folder <hdri>_cNN with 'frames' EXR frames.

width.tooltip: Render width in pixels; must be a multiple of 32 (H3: 16x VAE x 2x2 patch). Default 1344 = H3 draft size.

height.tooltip: Render height in pixels; must be a multiple of 32 (H3: 16x VAE x 2x2 patch). Default 768 = H3 draft size.

fov_deg.tooltip: Horizontal field of view at the start of the move.

motion.tooltip: mix = a seeded choice of pan / tilt / push per clip.

exposure.tooltip: grey_0.18 = scale each clip so the median Rec.709 luma of 5 probe views is 0.18 (1.0 = diffuse white); none = keep the HDRI's own values.

seed.tooltip: Seeds the camera move per HDRI and clip index (same seed = same moves).

limit.tooltip: Use only the first N HDRIs (0 = all).

wait.tooltip: On: the node waits for the job (progress bar; ComfyUI's Cancel stops it). Off: it returns at once and the job keeps running in the background - follow it in the HDR jobs panel on this node.

output_tooltips: Absolute path of the clips folder (one sub-folder of half EXR frames + clip.json per clip); wire to Make Pairs 'clips_folder'.
JSON summary of the job: HDRIs, clips rendered / skipped, frames, size, clip ids (or a 'started in the background' note when wait is off).
MiniMaxH3_HDRHDRIToClips.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRHDRIToClips
MiniMaxH3_HDRHDRIToClips.description: Renders camera moves (pan / tilt / push-in, seeded) through each equirect HDRI (.hdr / .exr) into EXR (half) frame folders at the H3 draft size, scene-linear Rec.709 with 1.0 = diffuse white (exposure: the clip's median becomes 18 % grey). Frame counts on H3's 17k+5 grid. Finished clips are skipped.

folder.tooltip: Folder of .exr frames: absolute, or relative to ComfyUI's input folder (then output folder).

output_tooltips: Float IMAGE [frames, H, W, 3] RGB as stored in the EXRs (alpha dropped, grey -> 3 channels), not clamped.
Number of EXR frames loaded after start / step / count.
Text: folder, first and last file, size and min / max / % above 1.
MiniMaxH3_HDRLoadEXRSequence.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRLoadEXRSequence
MiniMaxH3_HDRLoadEXRSequence.description: Loads a folder of EXR frames (natural sort) as float IMAGE frames - no clamp, values above 1 kept.

image.tooltip: Log code values 0..1 (VAE Decode output of the HDR LoRA path).

encoding.tooltip: The curve the LoRA was trained with (A29: diffhdr_log_16384).

output_tooltips: Scene-linear Rec.709 HDR (IMAGE, 1.0 = diffuse white), NOT clamped: values above 1 are highlights. Next: Bias Correct, Gain Map Join or a Save node.
MiniMaxH3_HDRLogDecode.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRLogDecode
MiniMaxH3_HDRLogDecode.description: Log code values (the H3 VAE decode of a log-HDR generation) -> scene-linear HDR, 1.0 = diffuse white. The output is NOT clamped: values above 1 are the HDR highlights.

image.tooltip: Scene-linear Rec.709 frames; values above 1 are kept up to the curve's maximum.

encoding.tooltip: Log curve. diffhdr_log_16384 is the A29 standard (training and inference must match).

output_tooltips: Log code values 0..1 (IMAGE, one frame per input frame); linear values above the curve maximum are held at 1. Feed to VAE Encode or Save Log 16-bit.
MiniMaxH3_HDRLogEncode.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRLogEncode
MiniMaxH3_HDRLogEncode.description: Scene-linear HDR (1.0 = diffuse white) -> log code values 0..1 that H3's VAE can carry. Default diffhdr_log_16384 (DiffHDR log-gamma 2.2, holds up to 16384x white).

clips_folder.tooltip: HDRI -> Clips output (one folder per clip).

output_folder.tooltip: Gets targets/, control/ and meta.jsonl. Relative = inside ComfyUI's output.

seed.tooltip: Seeds per clip the exposure shift, the control CRF and which clips are hard-clip / soft roll-off / unclipped.

ev_range.tooltip: Control exposure shift drawn from -ev_range..+ev_range stops per clip.

unclipped_share.tooltip: Share of clips whose SDR control keeps every highlight (order: 15 %).

crf_min.tooltip: Lowest h264 CRF for the SDR control .mp4 (lower = less compression); each clip draws a seeded CRF in crf_min..crf_max. Must not exceed crf_max.

crf_max.tooltip: Highest h264 CRF for the SDR control .mp4 (higher = more compression artefacts). The log-HDR targets are always lossless.

caption_template.tooltip: HDR Prompt template; {scene}, {lighting} and {camera} are filled per clip from the HDRI name / Poly Haven categories and the camera move.
caption_template.default: HDR scene-linear footage encoded in a log curve, high dynamic range. Scene: {scene}. Lighting: {lighting}. Camera: {camera}.

fps.tooltip: H3 trains at 24 fps.

wait.tooltip: On: the node waits for the job (progress bar; ComfyUI's Cancel stops it). Off: it returns at once and the job keeps running in the background - follow it in the HDR jobs panel on this node.

output_tooltips: Absolute path of the pairs folder (targets/, control/, meta.jsonl); wire to Train IC-LoRA 'dataset_folder'.
JSON summary of the job: pair count, frames, targets / control / meta paths (or a 'started in the background' note when wait is off).
MiniMaxH3_HDRMakePairs.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRMakePairs
MiniMaxH3_HDRMakePairs.description: EXR clips -> the HDR IC-LoRA training set ai-toolkit reads: control/<clip>.mp4 = SDR reference (random exposure shift, half hard clip / half soft roll-off, a share left unclipped, sRGB 8-bit h264 crf 16-28) and targets/<clip>.mp4 = the same frames in diffhdr_log_16384 as lossless RGB (8-bit codes), + targets/<clip>.txt caption and meta.jsonl with every parameter. Same file names in both folders (that is how the trainer pairs them). Finished pairs are skipped.

template.tooltip: Placeholders {scene} {lighting} {camera}. The owner's order (A29) named a template that was missing from the message, so this default is a stand-in: edit it to your wording.
template.default: {scene}. Lighting: {lighting}. Camera: {camera}. High dynamic range footage, scene-linear light, detail kept in bright highlights and deep shadows.

output_tooltips: The filled template text (sentences whose field is empty are removed); wire to the text encoder or use as a training caption.
MiniMaxH3_HDRPrompt.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRPrompt
MiniMaxH3_HDRPrompt.description: Builds the HDR caption / inference prompt from three fields and a template ({scene}, {lighting}, {camera}). Empty fields drop their sentence. Use the same template for the training captions and for inference.

image.tooltip: to_view: scene-linear frames in 'colorspace' (values above 1 allowed). to_scene: display / view-encoded frames (or log codes with code_space on). Alpha is passed through.

direction.tooltip: to_view = scene-linear -> OCIO display/view (or -> log code). to_scene = the inverse back to scene-linear, with an HDR peak audit (not clamped).

colorspace.tooltip: Scene-linear OCIO colorspace of the scene side (input of to_view, output of to_scene). code_space modes require ACEScg.

display.tooltip: OCIO display of the view transform (code_space off only); must hold the chosen view.

view.tooltip: OCIO view applied with the display (code_space off only); checked against the display before running.

tag.tooltip: Label of the incoming frames (code_space off only). HDR / ACEScg turn on the to_scene peak audit; it also feeds tag_out.

code_space.tooltip: HDR for H3 (experimental): to_view encodes ACEScg scene-linear into this log code (what an H3 HDR LoRA sees and generates; values the VAE cannot hold - below 0 / above 1 - are counted in the report); to_scene decodes generated log frames back to ACEScg scene-linear and checks them for fake HDR (pixels below the curve's black code = negative light = an SDR picture pushed through a log curve). off: the OCIO view round trip as before. Save Video (C2C) writes the result as 16-bit LogC3 / EXR.

output_tooltips: Transformed frames, same size and frame count, not clamped: display/view values (to_view), scene-linear (to_scene), or log codes / ACEScg linear in code_space mode.
Label of the output: 'Rec709' after to_view, 'ACEScg' or 'HDR' after to_scene; '<curve> code' / 'ACEScg' in code_space mode.
Text: direction, tags, colorspace / display / view, OCIO config source and the HDR peak audit (code_space: % outside 0..1 or the footroom fake-HDR check).
MiniMaxH3_HDRRoundtrip.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRRoundtrip
MiniMaxH3_HDRRoundtrip.description: Scene-linear ↔ view via OCIO with HDR tag propagation. Uses live display/view names (e.g. 'ACES 2.0 - SDR 100 nits (Rec.709)'). No torch.clamp on HDR paths — values above 1.0 must survive to_scene.

images.tooltip: Scene-linear HDR frames (Rec.709 unless you converted the gamut).

filename_prefix.tooltip: sub/folder/name under output/; each run writes a new folder name_NNNNN/.

precision.tooltip: half = 16-bit float (to 65504, the usual VFX choice); float32 = full precision.

start_frame.tooltip: Number of the first frame.

padding.tooltip: Digits of the frame number (4 -> 1001).

output_tooltips: Text: EXR frames written, precision, backend, output file range, max value, NaN / inf and half-float saturation counts, read-back result.
MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveEXRSequence.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveEXRSequence
MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveEXRSequence.description: Saves linear HDR frames as an OpenEXR sequence (half or float32, ZIP) in a new folder under ComfyUI's output folder. Never clamps light; reads the first and last frame back to check.

images.tooltip: Scene-linear Rec.709 HDR frames.

filename_prefix.tooltip: sub/folder/name under output/; each run writes name_NNNNN.mp4.

fps.tooltip: Frames per second of the written .mp4: passed to ffmpeg as the frame rate (-r) of the piped frames, so it sets playback speed and duration.

paper_white_nits.tooltip: Brightness of diffuse white (1.0); 203 = BT.2408 reference white.

master_display_nits.tooltip: Peak of the mastering display written in the HDR10 metadata.

output_tooltips: Text: written .mp4 path, frames, size, fps, CRF, paper white, MaxCLL / MaxFALL, % clipped above 10000 nits, % out-of-gamut zeroed and the verified colour tags.
MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveHDR10.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveHDR10
MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveHDR10.description: Linear Rec.709 HDR -> Rec.2020 -> nits (1.0 = paper white) -> PQ -> 10-bit HEVC .mp4 with HDR10 metadata (ffmpeg / libx265). PQ holds up to 10000 nits; brighter is clipped and reported. The file's colour tags are read back and checked.

images.tooltip: Log code values (or linear, with 'encode' set).

filename_prefix.tooltip: sub/folder/name under output/; each run writes a new folder name_NNNNN/.

encode.tooltip: Input is already log -> 'none'; linear input -> pick the curve to encode with.

start_frame.tooltip: Number of the first frame.

padding.tooltip: Digits of the frame number.

output_tooltips: Text: number of 16-bit PNG / TIFF frames written, the curve used (if encoded), output folder and % of pixels held at 0 or 1.
MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveLog16.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveLog16
MiniMaxH3_HDRSaveLog16.description: Saves the LOG image (code values 0..1) as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF sequence - compact, lossless at 16 bits, decodes back to linear with Log Decode.

image.tooltip: Scene-linear HDR.

exposure_ev.tooltip: Exposure in stops before the shoulder (-3 shows 3 stops more highlight).

shoulder.tooltip: Highlight roll-off: 0 = hard clip at white, larger = softer, starts lower.

output_tooltips: Display-referred sRGB 0..1 (exposure, shoulder, sRGB transfer) for all frames; the node's own preview shows at most 16. For viewing only - do not save it as HDR.
MiniMaxH3_HDRTonemapPreview.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRTonemapPreview
MiniMaxH3_HDRTonemapPreview.description: Display-only sRGB view of linear HDR: exposure, then a soft shoulder that rolls highlights off instead of clipping them. For looking only - save the linear image, not this.

dataset_folder.tooltip: Make Pairs output (targets/ + control/). Relative = inside ComfyUI's output.

aitoolkit_dir.tooltip: Your ai-toolkit folder (git clone of ostris/ai-toolkit, with MiniMax H3).

python.tooltip: Python of the ai-toolkit environment; empty = its venv / .venv, else ComfyUI's Python.

job_name.tooltip: Names the run and its checkpoints. Same name = resume.

output_folder.tooltip: ai-toolkit training_folder. Relative = inside ComfyUI's output.

steps.tooltip: Total optimiser steps written to the YAML (train.steps; batch size 1, no gradient accumulation).

learning_rate.tooltip: AdamW8bit learning rate written to the YAML (train.lr).

save_every.tooltip: Write a LoRA checkpoint (bf16) every N steps; ai-toolkit keeps the newest 4. Resume continues from the newest one.

resolution.tooltip: ai-toolkit caps each clip's area at resolution x resolution (aspect kept): 768 trains 1344x768 clips at about 1024x576; 1024 trains them full size.

partition.tooltip: Which ref2va checkpoint of Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 to train on.

resume.tooltip: On: continue from the newest checkpoint of this job name. Off: refuse when one exists (pick a new name to start fresh).

dry_run.tooltip: Check everything and write the YAML, but do not start training.

wait.tooltip: Off (default): training runs in the background and the queue moves on. On: the node waits until training ends (ComfyUI's Cancel stops it).

output_tooltips: Text: ai-toolkit commit and H3 capability checks, dataset pairs / frames / size, resume point, YAML path, then the background job id and log (and final steps / loss when wait is on).
Path of the ai-toolkit job YAML written under <output_folder>/a29_runs/<job_name>/ (also in a dry run).
MiniMaxH3_HDRTrainICLoRA.name: MiniMaxH3_HDRTrainICLoRA
MiniMaxH3_HDRTrainICLoRA.description: Trains the HDR in-context LoRA with ai-toolkit (ostris, MIT; run as a separate program): SDR clip = <Video 1> reference, log-HDR clip = target, loss on the target only, LoRA on qkv_proj / out_proj / fc1 / fc2. Checks first that your ai-toolkit has MiniMax H3 support (else: run `git pull` in that folder). Runs in the background with a live log + loss curve; Cancel stops it; the same job name continues from its last checkpoint.

latent.tooltip: The target H3 AV latent (sets the size and frame count).

vae.tooltip: The H3 video VAE (encodes each still).

images.tooltip: One still per position, as a batch (Batch Images).

positions.tooltip: Frame of each still, in the batch's order, e.g. 1, 18, 35.

indexing.tooltip: How positions count frames: 1-based (the first frame is 1; single-frame steps at 1, 18, 35 ...) or 0-based (the first frame is 0; 0, 17, 34 ...).

crop.tooltip: disabled stretches each still to the canvas; center crops it.

output_tooltips: The latent with each still encoded into its latent step and that step's video mask set to 0 (kept); audio and other mask values unchanged. Wire to the sampler's latent input.
Text: which latent steps got keyframes, and a note for each position inside a multi-frame step (with the nearest single-frame positions).
MiniMaxH3_HardKeyframes.name: MiniMaxH3_HardKeyframes
MiniMaxH3_HardKeyframes.description: Write still images into the target latent at chosen frames and protect those latent steps from denoising, for frames that must appear as given (core's Add Guide only suggests them). Single-frame positions are 1, 18, 35, 52 ... (1-based); anywhere else protects the whole 4-frame step it falls in, which can hold the picture for those frames. The decoded pixels can still differ slightly: the VAE decodes with its neighbours. Existing masks are kept; audio is not touched. Feed the output to the sampler's latent input.

ref_name.tooltip: R: the Ref2VA checkpoint (diffusion_models / unet), the base every delta is taken from (S-R, F-R). Ignored when ref_path is set.

ref_path.tooltip: Optional full path override (use for GGUF in unet/).

fl_name.tooltip: F: the FL2VA checkpoint; its delta F-R is projected out of S-R when fl_projection is on. Ignored when fl_path is set.

fl_path.tooltip: Optional full file path of the FL2VA checkpoint; overrides fl_name (use for GGUF in unet/).

sing_name.tooltip: S: the Singularity checkpoint; the extracted residual starts from S-R. Ignored when sing_path is set.

sing_path.tooltip: Optional full file path of the Singularity checkpoint; overrides sing_name (use for GGUF in unet/).

rank.tooltip: Maximum LoRA rank per layer (SVD of the residual); layers may keep fewer singular values when the noise edge cuts them. Higher = larger file and more RAM while extracting.

fl_projection.tooltip: ON: H = (S-R) - a(F-R). OFF: H = S-R plain delta.

block_start.tooltip: First DiT block (inclusive) whose weights are extracted; must be <= block_end.

block_end.tooltip: Last DiT block (inclusive) whose weights are extracted; blocks outside the range are skipped.

edge_margin.tooltip: Marchenko-Pastur edge multiplier when quantisation noise floor is known (int8/bf16/fp16). Singular values above edge are kept.

device.tooltip: Where the checkpoint tensors are read and the SVD runs. auto = ComfyUI's torch device (else CUDA if available, else CPU).

output_name.tooltip: Filename written into the first loras folder.

include_global_parameters.tooltip: Also extract weights that belong to no DiT block (embeddings, refiner, output heads). On = the previous behaviour: the block range never filtered them.

full_hash.tooltip: Hash the whole source checkpoints for the provenance report (slow on 30+ GB files). Off: the first MiB is hashed.

output_tooltips: File name of the written .safetensors LoRA in the first loras folder (a .report.json sits beside it).
Markdown report: sources, variant, coverage, memory, rank, projection, block range, emitted / noise-only tensors and a per-block SVD table.
MiniMaxH3_HybridExtract.name: MiniMaxH3_HybridExtract
MiniMaxH3_HybridExtract.description: Extract the Hybrid HDR LoRA from matched Ref2VA / FL2VA / Singularity checkpoints (a checkpoint-delta experiment: the residual is not proven to be HDR-only). The source weights are read one at a time, but the extracted factors stay in memory until the file is written: up to about 2.4 GB at rank 256 on full H3, plus about 5.5 GB while the largest layer is processed (measured at reduced scale, extrapolated). All three checkpoints must be the same H3 variant. Saves into the loras folder with a .report.json beside it.

model.tooltip: Ref2VA MODEL of the same H3 variant the LoRA was extracted from; it is cloned, the input stays unpatched.

lora_name.tooltip: Hybrid HDR LoRA file in models/loras (Hybrid HDR Extract output).

strength.tooltip: LoRA merge strength. Try 0.5 for a gentle HDR lift.

block_start.tooltip: First DiT block to patch (inclusive). Singularity merge used b25-49.

mode.tooltip: constant merge = fixed strength (unchanged behaviour). scheduled = strength follows the sampling sigma in one run (experimental).

start_sigma.tooltip: scheduled: the adapter starts acting at this sigma (sampling runs from 1 down to 0). 1 = from the first step.

end_sigma.tooltip: scheduled: the adapter stops below this sigma. 0 = to the last step.

ramp_in.tooltip: scheduled: sigma span after start_sigma over which strength rises from 0.

ramp_out.tooltip: scheduled: sigma span before end_sigma over which strength falls to 0.

apply_to.tooltip: scheduled: 'all rows' = as the adapter was made. 'text + visual rows' = the adapter adds nothing to audio rows (audio can still change slightly through attention to the adapted video).

include_global_parameters.tooltip: Also apply LoRA layers that belong to no DiT block (embeddings, refiner, output heads). On = the previous behaviour; the block range never filtered them.

output_tooltips: Clone of the input MODEL with the LoRA added as patches (constant merge) or as sigma-scheduled hooks (scheduled mode); wire to the sampler.
Text: LoRA file, strength or schedule, block range, patched / total layers with coverage counts and the variant check note.
MiniMaxH3_HybridHDR.name: MiniMaxH3_HybridHDR
MiniMaxH3_HybridHDR.description:
Apply the extracted Hybrid HDR LoRA (a checkpoint-delta experiment, not proven HDR-specific) to a Ref2VA MODEL.

mode 'constant merge' (default): fixed strength, as before. For late-step HDR with this mode, sample the first steps with plain Ref2VA, then continue with this patched MODEL (KSamplerAdvanced / SamplerCustomAdvanced start/end steps - not SplitSigmas on H3).
mode 'scheduled (experimental)': one sampler run; the strength follows the sampling sigma (start_sigma .. end_sigma with ramps). Not yet validated on a real H3 run.

model.tooltip: The H3 model, after Mask-Aware ControlNet if you use one.

positive.tooltip: The positive from Reference to Video: it tells which references are the identity pictures and which is the plate video.

replacement_mask.tooltip: Latent-space mask of the region to replace - H3 Mask To Latent Space of head_room_masks, the same one Masked Replace uses.

enabled.tooltip: Off: the model passes through unchanged (no attention override, nothing checked). On: installs the identity-attention weighting on a model clone.

expression_mask.tooltip: Latent-space mouth + eyes mask of the PLATE (e.g. H3 Swap Control render -> mask -> Mask To Latent Space). There identity is eased so the performance comes through.

occluder_mask.tooltip: Latent-space mask of things in front of the face (hands, hair, props): no identity there.

identity_inside.tooltip: Multiplier on the attention to the identity pictures inside the region.

identity_outside.tooltip: Outside the region. 0 keeps identity off the background and other people.

identity_on_expression.tooltip: Multiplier on the attention to the identity pictures on expression_mask rows inside the region, from expression_from on. 0 = no identity there; needs expression_mask.

plate_on_expression.tooltip: Multiplier on the attention to the plate video (<Video 1>) on mouth / eye rows.

identity_on_occluder.tooltip: Multiplier on the attention to the identity pictures on occluder_mask rows; overrides the region and expression values. 0 = no identity on occluders; needs occluder_mask.

expression_from.tooltip: Expression easing starts at this fraction of the steps (fine detail is late).

start_percent.tooltip: Fraction of the sampling schedule (0 = first, noisiest step) where the weighting starts; converted to a sigma by the model. Outside the start..end window attention is unchanged.

end_percent.tooltip: Fraction of the sampling schedule where the weighting stops (1 = through the last step); converted to a sigma by the model.

block_start.tooltip: First DiT block index (0-based) whose attention is weighted; earlier blocks run unchanged. Works with block_end.

asymmetric_flow.tooltip: References do not read the noisy target video (ContextAnyone's idea; untested on H3).

output_tooltips: Clone of the MODEL with the identity-attention override installed (the input model unchanged when disabled). Wire to the sampler.
Text summary: identity/plate reference counts, masked latent-pixel counts, the weights, schedule and blocks used, and whether another attention override runs inside this one.
MiniMaxH3_IdentityFusion.name: MiniMaxH3_IdentityFusion
MiniMaxH3_IdentityFusion.description: Where, when and how the character's identity enters H3: identity attention only inside the replacement region, eased on mouth / eye rows (the plate's performance strengthened there), off on occluders, in chosen blocks and steps. Use with RefMod or plain references - it weights attention, not the reference latents. Experimental: not A/B-tested on H3 weights.

clip.tooltip: The H3 text encoder: tokenizes the prompt together with the reference items and keyframe images (vision context).

vae.tooltip: The H3 video VAE: encodes the keyframes, reference images and reference videos.

audio_vae.tooltip: The H3 audio VAE: encodes ref_video_audio and ref_audio inputs (resampled to its rate). Not used when no audio reference is wired.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt. References are numbered in wiring order: <Picture n> for ref_images, <Video n> for ref_videos, <Audio n> for audio references.

width.tooltip: Output width in px (steps of 32); the empty latent is width / 16 wide. Keyframes, 'match' reference sizes and target-grid reference videos follow it.

height.tooltip: Output height in px (steps of 32); the empty latent is height / 16 high. Keyframes, 'match' reference sizes and target-grid reference videos follow it.

length.tooltip: Frames at 24 fps, snapped up to H3's 17k+5 grid. 124 is about 5 seconds; the model was trained around 124-362 and longer is untested, not forbidden.

first_frame.tooltip: Frame 0 of the output. Stretched to the canvas, because it is the geometry anchor - cropping it would move the shot.

last_frame.tooltip: The final frame. Cover-cropped to preserve its aspect, because it follows the anchor rather than setting the geometry.

ref_image_size.tooltip: 'match' scales each reference to the generation's pixel area. 'max' uses a 2048px short edge for the best identity fidelity and is SEVERAL TIMES SLOWER - reference tokens ride through every sampling step, not just the first.

ref_images.tooltip: Up to 10 reference images, each a <Picture n> in slot order (see image_batches for batches); sized by ref_image_size.

ref_image.tooltip: Identity/style reference. Downscaled if large, never upscaled.

ref_videos.tooltip: Up to 4 reference videos, each a <Video n>; cut to the output length and to the VAE's frame grid, sized by ref_video_fit.

ref_video_audios.tooltip: Up to 4 soundtracks, each paired with the ref_video of the same number and encoded with audio_vae.

ref_video_audio.tooltip: Soundtrack of the reference video with the SAME NUMBER. Paired by number, not by position - leaving video 2 empty does not shift video 3's audio onto video 1.

ref_audios.tooltip: Up to 4 standalone audio references (<Audio n>), encoded with audio_vae, added after all reference videos and their soundtracks.

ref_video_fit.tooltip: How reference videos are sized. 'core canvas' = what ComfyUI's own Reference to Video does (768 short edge, stretched): a reference video showing the same shot as the output (its source, pose or depth) then reaches the model offset by half a token - the report says by how many pixels. 'target grid (zero offset)' sizes it to width x height, so every token of it lands exactly on the output's token: use it when the reference video is a spatial anchor. Costs more reference tokens. The third choice puts only <Video 1> (the plate) on the target grid and leaves a driving clip on core's canvas.
options: target grid for <Video 1>, core canvas for the rest

image_batches.tooltip: A ref_image slot given a BATCH (H3 Reference Bank identity, H3 Subject Memory anchors): 'first image only' uses image 0, as ComfyUI's own Reference to Video does - the report then says how many were left out. 'every image' makes each image of the batch its own <Picture N>, in order (numbering shifts for the slots after it).

output_tooltips: The encoded prompt carrying the keyframes (minimax_keyframes: frame 0 and / or the last frame) and the references (minimax_refs). Wire to the guider.
Empty H3 audio + video latent: width x height, length snapped up to 17k+5 frames (5k+2 latent frames), silent audio of the same duration. Wire to the sampler.
What was built: how many of each reference, what the length snapped to, and where keyframes and reference videos will fight.
MiniMaxH3_ImageAndReferenceToVideo.name: MiniMaxH3_ImageAndReferenceToVideo
MiniMaxH3_ImageAndReferenceToVideo.description: Keyframes AND references in one conditioning. Keyframes (first/last frame) occupy real frame positions and say where the shot starts and ends; references (<Picture n>, <Video n>, <Audio n>) have no position and say who and what sort. The stock nodes make you pick one; most shots want both.

samples.tooltip: Sampled H3 LATENT from an H3 Image Prepare packet. Only the video part is decoded (audio ignored); the packet's frame-profile and output-strategy hints are read from it.

vae.tooltip: H3 video VAE used to decode the video latent (the one-frame profile expects the H3 image VAE).

decode_mode.tooltip: temporal: decode the whole video latent and keep the requested profile frames. single_latent_slice: decode one latent frame on its own, giving one image per batch item.

latent_index.tooltip: single_latent_slice only: 0-based latent frame to decode. Must exist in the latent, otherwise the node stops with an error.

spatial_decode.tooltip: single_latent_slice only. native: the VAE's normal (possibly tiled) decode. full_image (experimental): turns VAE tiling off for this decode and reserves more VRAM.

output_tooltips: IMAGE batch: the requested profile frames for each latent batch item (temporal), or one image per batch item (single slice). Wire to H3 Image Single Output.
Number of images in the frames output.
Text summary: natural vs kept frame counts, batch items, and the preferred still per batch item with its score.

Index of the preferred still for the first batch item, chosen by the packet's output strategy (stable_quality or first_stable_edit); 0 in single_latent_slice. Wire to H3 Image Single Output recommended_index.
MiniMaxH3_ImageDecode.name: MiniMaxH3_ImageDecode
MiniMaxH3_ImageDecode.description: Decode the requested temporal frame profile from a sampled H3 latent.

frames.tooltip: Decoded IMAGE batch to choose from, usually H3 Image Exact Frame Decode's frames output.

strategy.tooltip: sharpest picks edge energy — motion blur mid-transition scores high and looks wrong. stable_quality penalises neighbour disagreement.

manual_index.tooltip: manual_index strategy only: 0-based frame to output; values past the last frame are clamped to the last frame.

skip_first_frames.tooltip: Scored strategies only: frames before this index are never candidates. The window starts at the later of this and candidate_start. 0 = no skip.

candidate_start.tooltip: Scored strategies only: start of the candidate window as a 0-1 fraction of the batch length (0 = first frame).

candidate_end.tooltip: Scored strategies only: end of the candidate window as a 0-1 fraction of the batch length (1 = through the last frame). At least one frame always remains.

similarity_weight.tooltip: balanced_edit only: score = weight × similarity to source_image + (1 - weight) × stable-quality score. 1 = pure similarity, 0 = pure stable quality.

top_k.tooltip: With emit_candidate_batch on: how many highest-scoring candidates go to candidate_batch_debug (best first, limited to the window size).

source_image.tooltip: Reference for most_similar_to_source and balanced_edit (colour and edge difference to its first image). Without it those strategies fall back to best_quality / stable_quality.

emit_candidate_batch.tooltip: Off: selected_image is the one chosen frame and candidate_batch_debug is empty. On: selected_image passes the whole batch and candidate_batch_debug holds the top_k candidates (or the chosen frame for fixed strategies).

recommended_index.tooltip: Frame index used by the decode_recommended strategy; wire from H3 Image Exact Frame Decode recommended_index. Unconnected: frame 0.

output_tooltips: IMAGE: the chosen frame (1 image), or the complete input batch when emit_candidate_batch is on.
IMAGE batch for inspection: the top_k scored candidates (or the chosen frame for fixed strategies) when emit_candidate_batch is on; an empty batch otherwise.
0-based index of the chosen frame within the input batch.
Score of the chosen frame under the effective strategy (relative to the other candidates, roughly 0-1); always 1.0 for fixed strategies.
Text summary: chosen frame, requested and effective strategy, the score components, candidate window and any fallback warning.
MiniMaxH3_ImageFrameSelector.name: MiniMaxH3_ImageFrameSelector
MiniMaxH3_ImageFrameSelector.description: Select one decoded still by index or quality metric.

clip.tooltip: H3 text encoder. Encodes the (optionally wrapped) prompt; in image_to_image it also sees the fitted source, in reference_edit the reference images, as vision input.

mode.tooltip: FL2VA paths anchor or encode sources differently. REF2VA needs explicit <Picture N> tags in the prompt or references drift.

prompt.tooltip: Describe ONE final still. Video phrasing ('pan left', 'over 3 seconds') makes the temporal packet wander between frames.

width.tooltip: Canvas width in pixels, rounded to the nearest multiple of 32. The empty latent is width/16 wide; sources are fitted to this width.

height.tooltip: Canvas height in pixels, rounded to the nearest multiple of 32. The empty latent is height/16 tall; sources are fitted to this height.

frame_preset.tooltip: H3 denoises the whole packet jointly. More frames add temporal context but raise cost; one frame needs the experimental image VAE.

optimize_prompt.tooltip: Wraps the prompt for a locked-camera still. Does not change steps or CFG.

preserve_strength.tooltip: Prompt-language preservation for edits — NOT diffusion denoise strength.

source_fit.tooltip: How sources map to the generation canvas before VAE encode.

reference_size.tooltip: REF2VA encode resolution. max_identity_2048 keeps more identity detail.

vae.tooltip: H3 video VAE that encodes the source / reference images to latents. Required in image_to_image and reference_edit modes; unused in text_to_image.

source_image.tooltip: Image to edit (first image of the batch). image_to_image: fitted to the canvas and pinned as frame 0 (one-frame profile: used as <Picture 1>). reference_edit: <Picture 1>. Ignored in text_to_image.

reference_image_2.tooltip: Extra REF2VA reference, reference_edit mode only (ignored otherwise). Connected references are numbered <Picture 2>..<Picture 9> in socket order, skipping empty sockets; first image of the batch is used.

reference_image_3.tooltip: Extra REF2VA reference, reference_edit mode only. Numbered as the next <Picture N> after the connected sockets above it; first image of the batch is used.

reference_image_4.tooltip: Extra REF2VA reference, reference_edit mode only. Numbered as the next <Picture N> after the connected sockets above it; first image of the batch is used.

reference_image_5.tooltip: Extra REF2VA reference, reference_edit mode only. Numbered as the next <Picture N> after the connected sockets above it; first image of the batch is used.

reference_image_6.tooltip: Extra REF2VA reference, reference_edit mode only. Numbered as the next <Picture N> after the connected sockets above it; first image of the batch is used.

reference_image_7.tooltip: Extra REF2VA reference, reference_edit mode only. Numbered as the next <Picture N> after the connected sockets above it; first image of the batch is used.

reference_image_8.tooltip: Extra REF2VA reference, reference_edit mode only. Numbered as the next <Picture N> after the connected sockets above it; first image of the batch is used.

reference_image_9.tooltip: Extra REF2VA reference, reference_edit mode only (up to 9 pictures in total). Numbered as the next <Picture N> after the connected sockets above it; first image of the batch is used.

output_tooltips: CONDITIONING for the sampler's positive input: the encoded prompt, plus the source as a frame-0 keyframe latent (image_to_image) or the reference latents (reference_edit, native transport).
Empty (all-zero) H3 audio-video LATENT: video width/16 × height/16 × the profile's latent frames, plus decode hints. Wire to the sampler, then to H3 Image Exact Frame Decode.
The source image resized to width×height with source_fit (IMAGE, 1 frame). A black frame in text_to_image mode. Useful as source_image for frame selection or tone lock.
Frame count of the chosen frame_preset (1, 5, 9, 13 or 20 frames); the decoder keeps this many frames.
The exact text given to the text encoder: the prompt wrapped in still-image and preservation instructions when optimize_prompt is on, else the trimmed prompt.
Text summary: mode, canvas, frame profile and packet size, checkpoint advice, inputs that were ignored, and prompt warnings.
MiniMaxH3_ImagePrepare.name: MiniMaxH3_ImagePrepare
MiniMaxH3_ImagePrepare.description: Prepare T2I, I2I, or REF2VA conditioning plus an empty H3 AV latent for still-image sampling.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Wrong aspect for your subject leaves letterboxing or a cropped head. 'source image' copies a connected reference ratio.

megapixels.tooltip: Target area in ComfyUI megapixels (1 MP = 1024²). Above ~1 MP you are outside H3-Base's native training envelope.

multiple.tooltip: Both axes snap to this grid. H3 requires multiples of 32.

native_area_cap.tooltip: Cap total pixels near 768×1344. Turn off only if you accept VRAM spikes and soft detail from out-of-distribution resolution.

custom_width.tooltip: Only when aspect_ratio is "custom dimensions".

custom_height.tooltip: Only when aspect_ratio is "custom dimensions".

output_tooltips: Canvas width in pixels, snapped to the chosen multiple and capped to 768×1344 total pixels when native_area_cap is on. Wire to an H3 Image Prepare node's width.
Canvas height in pixels, snapped to the chosen multiple and capped to 768×1344 total pixels when native_area_cap is on. Wire to an H3 Image Prepare node's height.
Text summary: width×height, megapixels (1024² units), ratio source, multiple, cap state, and a warning when the canvas exceeds the native area.
MiniMaxH3_ImageResolution.name: MiniMaxH3_ImageResolution
MiniMaxH3_ImageResolution.description: Calculate a custom H3 canvas on the 32-pixel grid with an optional native-area cap. Oversize canvases cost VRAM without guaranteed detail gain — H3-Base was trained near 768p.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Portrait vs landscape changes where H3 puts detail — pick the ratio your subject actually fills.

resolution_profile.tooltip: Higher MP costs decode and attention; H3 detail does not scale linearly. Start at native detail unless you have VRAM headroom.

source_image.tooltip: Only read when aspect_ratio is "source image": its width/height ratio is used (pixels are not used). Error if that option is chosen and nothing is connected.

limit_to_native_area.tooltip: Hard-cap near 768×1344 even when the profile name suggests oversize.

output_tooltips: Canvas width in pixels on H3's 32-pixel grid, fitted to the profile's megapixels and the aspect ratio. Wire to an H3 Image Prepare node's width.
Canvas height in pixels on H3's 32-pixel grid, fitted to the profile's megapixels and the aspect ratio. Wire to an H3 Image Prepare node's height.
Text summary: width×height, megapixels (1024² units), ratio source, profile, and whether the canvas is within, limited to, or above the native 768×1344 area.
MiniMaxH3_ImageResolutionPreset.name: MiniMaxH3_ImageResolutionPreset
MiniMaxH3_ImageResolutionPreset.description: Preset megapixel targets for still generation on H3's 32-pixel grid.

model.tooltip: H3 MODEL (with any LoRA already applied). A clone gets the profile's video and audio sigma shift; the input model is not changed.

sampling_profile.tooltip: Preset of sampler, scheduler, steps and video/audio shift (denoise 1.0). Turbo / LightX profiles assume the matching speed LoRA is loaded. 'custom' uses the controls below; the older names are kept for saved workflows.

custom_sampler.tooltip: custom profile only: ComfyUI sampler returned on the sampler output.

custom_scheduler.tooltip: custom profile only: scheduler that builds the sigmas. beta_custom uses the beta scheduler with custom_beta_alpha / custom_beta_beta.

custom_steps.tooltip: custom profile only: number of sampling steps (the sigmas output has steps + 1 values).

custom_denoise.tooltip: custom profile only: 1 = full schedule; below 1 a longer schedule is built and only its last steps are kept (partial denoise); 0 = empty sigmas, no sampling.

custom_shift_video.tooltip: custom profile only: flow sigma shift for the video stream. Higher spends more steps at high noise. Presets use 12 (6 for 768p Turbo).

custom_shift_audio.tooltip: custom profile only: flow sigma shift for H3's audio stream (presets use 3). Image output does not decode audio.

custom_beta_alpha.tooltip: custom profile with scheduler beta_custom only: alpha of the beta-distribution step spacing. Ignored by other schedulers.

custom_beta_beta.tooltip: custom profile with scheduler beta_custom only: beta of the beta-distribution step spacing. Ignored by other schedulers.

output_tooltips: Clone of the input MODEL with the video/audio sigma shift patched in. Use this model (not the original) in the sampler.
SAMPLER object for SamplerCustom / SamplerCustomAdvanced.
SIGMAS schedule (steps + 1 values) computed on the shifted model; empty when denoise is 0.
Text summary: profile, sampler, scheduler, steps, denoise, shifts and the sampling backend used.
MiniMaxH3_ImageSamplingPreset.name: MiniMaxH3_ImageSamplingPreset
MiniMaxH3_ImageSamplingPreset.description: Documented still-image sampling recipes. Turbo profiles must match their LoRA; wrong sampler/step pairs look washed or crunchy.

clip.tooltip: H3 text encoder. Encodes the (optionally wrapped) edit instruction with the fitted source image as vision input.

vae.tooltip: H3 video VAE that encodes the fitted source: as the frame-0 keyframe latent (multi-frame profiles) or as the <Picture 1> reference latent (one-frame profile).

source_image.tooltip: Image to edit; only the first image of the batch is used. It is fitted to width×height with source_fit before encoding.

edit_instruction.tooltip: What to change in the source, as one final still. Refer to the source as <Picture 1>. Motion, camera or timeline words add a warning to the report.

width.tooltip: Canvas width in pixels, rounded to the nearest multiple of 32. The source is fitted to this width; the latent is width/16 wide.

height.tooltip: Canvas height in pixels, rounded to the nearest multiple of 32. The source is fitted to this height; the latent is height/16 tall.

quality_profile.tooltip: One frame switches to REF2VA-style conditioning and needs the image VAE.

source_fidelity.tooltip: Prompt preservation strength — not sampler denoise.

source_fit.tooltip: How the source maps to the canvas: crop_center scales to fill and crops the overflow; contain_pad fits inside and pads with repeated edge pixels; stretch resizes without keeping the aspect ratio.

optimize_for_still.tooltip: On: wraps the instruction in fixed text (<Picture 1> is the source, one finished still, a preservation sentence chosen by source_fidelity). Off: the instruction is used as typed.

output_tooltips: CONDITIONING for the sampler's positive input: encoded instruction plus the source latent (frame-0 keyframe, or <Picture 1> reference for the one-frame profile).
Empty (all-zero) H3 audio-video LATENT: video width/16 × height/16 × the profile's latent frames, plus decode hints. Wire to the sampler, then to H3 Image Exact Frame Decode.
The source resized to width×height with source_fit (IMAGE, 1 frame), as it was encoded. Useful as source_image for frame selection or tone lock.
Frame count of the chosen quality_profile (1, 5, 9, 13 or 20 frames); the decoder keeps this many frames.
The exact text given to the text encoder (wrapped when optimize_for_still is on).
Text summary: canvas, frame profile and packet size, checkpoint advice, and prompt warnings.
MiniMaxH3_ImageToImagePrepare.name: MiniMaxH3_ImageToImagePrepare
MiniMaxH3_ImageToImagePrepare.description: Multi-frame FL2VA anchor or one-frame REF2VA-conditioned image editing.

av_latent.tooltip: H3 joint audio-video LATENT (video + audio streams) whose video stream is replaced. Sets the target latent size; its audio stream is kept as is.

images.tooltip: Frames to encode into the video stream. Width/height must encode to the latent's size (pixels/16), else an error; a frame count that encodes to a different latent length is trimmed or padded, with a warning.

vae.tooltip: H3 video VAE used to encode the frames.

output_tooltips: Copy of the input LATENT with the encoded frames as its video stream. Sample it with denoise below 1 (BasicScheduler) for img2img.
Text summary: encoded latent shape, stream count, input frame count and size, and any temporal trim/pad warning.
MiniMaxH3_InjectVideoLatent.name: MiniMaxH3_InjectVideoLatent
MiniMaxH3_InjectVideoLatent.description: Encode real frames into the video stream of an H3 joint AV latent. Pair with MiniMaxH3_NativeAudioLock for the audio stream, and set strength with BasicScheduler's denoise - NOT with SplitSigmas.

segment.tooltip: H3 Job Controller's segment JSON: the job, segment and attempt to record.

images.tooltip: The whole model window. The accepted frames (and the blend tail) are saved as 16-bit PNGs frame_<global>.png in output/h3_jobs/<job>/segments/seg_NNNN_aNN/; too few frames is an error.

decision.tooltip: auto: the QC verdict and the spec's approval policy decide (pass = accept; fail = retry or hold). accept / reject (retry) / hold for review force that outcome for this segment.

qc_report.tooltip: H3 QC Gate's qc_report. Empty = a pass. Used only by decision auto.

latent.tooltip: The sampler's latent: kept with the accepted frames and handed to the next segment as context_latent.

output_tooltips: One line: what was recorded (accepted, retry, waiting for review), job completion and the auto-continue result. Also shown on the node.
JSON summary: job, state, segment count, count per status, next segment, auto runs, path of job.json.
Path of the assembled movie (output/h3_jobs/<job>/<job>.mov / .mp4 / .mkv, with the plate's sound when it has any) once every segment is accepted; empty until then.
MiniMaxH3_JobCommit.name: MiniMaxH3_JobCommit
MiniMaxH3_JobCommit.description: Records the segment: accepted (its frames kept, numbered by global frame), retried with a new seed, or held for review - by the QC verdict and the approval policy, or your decision. When every segment is accepted it assembles the movie. With auto-continue it queues the next run itself.

task_spec.tooltip: h3.task_spec JSON. Stored in the job's job.json; a changed spec updates the job.

segment_plan.tooltip: h3.segment_plan JSON from H3 Segment Planner. A plan that differs from the job's replaces it; an accepted segment whose entry (and context source) is unchanged stays accepted.

job.tooltip: Job name = its folder output/h3_jobs/<name> (job.json, segment frames, final movie). Created on the first run; the same name resumes the job. Characters other than letters, digits, . _ - become _.

action.tooltip: run: take the next segment. pause / cancel / resume: set the job's state. approve / reject held segment: the first segment waiting for review. retry: redo action_segment and later ones. rollback: keep up to action_segment. choose take / alternate take: see action_take. Auto-queued runs use run.

action_segment.tooltip: Segment id (as in H3 Segment Planner's table) for retry, rollback, choose take and generate alternate take.

action_take.tooltip: Take name. choose take: an existing take of action_segment to use (later segments are redone). generate alternate take: the name of the new take of an accepted segment; empty = take<N>.

matte.tooltip: A matte clip frame-aligned with the plate: matte_window is cut exactly like window (same frames, same held frames).

driving.tooltip: A driving performance frame-aligned with the plate (any size): driving_window is cut exactly like window - performance transfer.

output_tooltips: The plate frames this segment generates over (edit tasks).
The same, with the tracking handles.
The accepted frames this segment continues from.
This attempt's seed: the spec's seed + segment id + 1000 per earlier attempt. Wire it to the sampler.
Model frames of this segment (17k + 5).
Feed H3 QC Gate and H3 Job Commit.
One line of text: job, segment k of N, attempt, seed, shot and any action note - or why nothing runs (paused, waiting for review, completed ...).
This segment's prompt: the task spec's prompt, then its shot's prompt when the job has a shot plan.
The accepted latent of the segment this one continues from (its chosen take), for H3 Motion Context's context_latent. Empty when there is none.
The matte, cut exactly like window.
The driving performance, cut exactly like window.
