MiniMaxH3_JobController.name: MiniMaxH3_JobController
MiniMaxH3_JobController.description: Opens (or creates) the job, applies an action, and hands THIS run the next segment: its source window, seed and ranges. With auto-continue the Commit queues the next run itself - one click runs the whole job. Nothing left to do: the generation is skipped.

frame_count.tooltip: Number of mask frames (pixel frames). Ignored when size_reference is connected.

width.tooltip: Mask width in px. Ignored when size_reference is connected.

height.tooltip: Mask height in px. Ignored when size_reference is connected.

interpolation.tooltip: Between keyframes: linear ramp, smooth (cosine ease in / out), or hold (keep the earlier keyframe's value until the next keyframe).

size_reference.tooltip: Frames whose size and count to use instead of the numbers above.

output_tooltips: MASK [frame_count, height, width]: every pixel of a frame holds that frame's keyframe value, clamped to 0-1.
MiniMaxH3_KeyframeMask.name: MiniMaxH3_KeyframeMask
MiniMaxH3_KeyframeMask.description: A mask whose value changes over time, from frame:value keyframes (e.g. 15:1, 22:0, 30:1); every pixel of a frame has the frame's value. Use it as a time-varying denoise mask (H3 Set AV Noise Mask) or to fade a blend.

model.tooltip: MODEL to patch. Cloned with a post-CFG colour-anchor hook; returned unchanged when neither the latent's noise_mask nor the mask input defines a preserved region.

latent.tooltip: The LATENT wired into the sampler (with Set Latent Noise Mask). Its noise_mask defines preserved vs regenerated regions.

strength.tooltip: How much of the measured drift to remove each active step. 1 = full correction.

mode.tooltip:
mean — subtract the per-channel offset measured on preserved cells.
mean_std — also match spread (contrast) on preserved cells, clamped.

per_frame.tooltip: Correct each latent frame independently. Off = one correction vector for all T.

start_percent.tooltip: Earliest sampling step (high sigma) where anchoring is active.

end_percent.tooltip: Last active step (low sigma). Steps below this are untouched so fine detail and grain are not smeared.

min_preserved.tooltip: Skip frames where fewer than this fraction of cells are preserved.

mask.tooltip: Optional pixel-space mask override (white = regenerate). Converted to the video latent grid with the same geometry as H3 Mask To Latent Space. When connected, replaces the latent noise_mask.

output_tooltips: MODEL with post-CFG colour anchor installed. Input model is never mutated.
MiniMaxH3_LatentColorAnchor.name: MiniMaxH3_LatentColorAnchor
MiniMaxH3_LatentColorAnchor.display_name: H3 Latent Colour Anchor (stop red drift)
MiniMaxH3_LatentColorAnchor.description:
Patches the sampler to remove temporal colour drift every step, before it compounds into the red/blush segments seen on ref2va (Comfy-Org #55).

The model is told which latent cells to KEEP via the noise mask; this node measures how far the denoised prediction has drifted from the source latent on those preserved cells, then removes that offset from the whole frame. Late steps are left alone — they are texture, not colour.

mask.tooltip: Latent-resolution masks, one per latent frame.

compression.tooltip: auto: read the compression geometry from the connected VAE, including the exact frame cycle and 2x2 token grid of chunked models like MiniMax H3. manual: enter it directly.

spatial.tooltip: Pixels per latent pixel on each axis.

token_spatial.tooltip: Latent pixels per model token on each axis; the strongest value in each token block paints the whole block, matching how the model reads the mask. 2 for MiniMax H3, 1 for models that read the mask per latent pixel.

head_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in the model's leading frame group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX. 0 when the model has no leading group.

head_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by the leading group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

chunk_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in each repeating group after the leading group. 4 for Wan and Hunyuan, 8 for LTX. 1 disables temporal expansion (image models).

chunk_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by each repeating group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

frames_per_latent.tooltip: Exact pixel frames covered by each latent frame, comma-separated, repeating from the first frame. Overrides the grid above when set. 1,4,4,4,4 with spatial 16 for MiniMax H3. For frame counts off the model's grid, use auto.

frames.tooltip: Pixel frame count to paint. 0 uses the count the compression grid implies for the incoming latent frames. Set it explicitly to match a source video that is off the model's frame grid.

vae.tooltip: The VAE whose latents this mask matches. Required when compression is auto.

output_tooltips: Pixel-space masks, one per frame.
MiniMaxH3_LatentMaskToMask.name: MiniMaxH3_LatentMaskToMask
MiniMaxH3_LatentMaskToMask.description: Expands a latent-resolution mask back to pixel resolution for visualization or testing. Each latent frame paints every pixel frame in its group and each token block paints as one value, so detail collapsed by the latent reduction stays collapsed.

latent.tooltip: An H3 video + audio latent.

method.tooltip: model: the trained 3D upscaler (sharper, needs the checkpoint). The others interpolate the latent without a model (as core's Upscale Latent).

model_name.tooltip: Checkpoint in models/latent_upscale_models. Download minimax_h3_latent_upscaler_3d_conv_v1_fp16.safetensors from https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler. Pickle files (.pth) are refused.

width.tooltip: Target width in pixels (32 px grid).

height.tooltip: Target height in pixels (32 px grid).

device.tooltip: auto: ComfyUI's device (GPU if there is one).

precision.tooltip: Compute precision on the GPU. On the CPU it always runs fp32.

chunk_latent_steps.tooltip: 0: the whole clip in one pass (exact). > 0: chunks of this many latent steps (4 pixel frames each), cross-faded; less memory, approximate.

chunk_overlap_steps.tooltip: Latent steps shared by neighbouring chunks, cross-faded.

offload_model.tooltip: Move the upscaler back to the CPU afterwards, so the H3 model and the upscaler are never both on the GPU.

size_by.tooltip: width / height: the two size widgets. scale: the latent's own size times 'scale'. megapixels: the latent's aspect at about this many megapixels. All snap to H3's 32 px grid.

scale.tooltip: size_by = scale: multiply the current size by this.

megapixels.tooltip: size_by = megapixels: the target pixel count in millions, aspect kept.

aspect.tooltip: Output ratio for size_by = scale / megapixels: the source's own, a preset (portrait, square, landscape, ultrawide) or custom. With width / height the box sets the ratio and this is ignored.

custom_ratio.tooltip: aspect = custom: W:H (e.g. 4:5, 2.39:1) or a decimal; up to 8:1.

fit.tooltip: How the picture fills the new shape. auto: exact when the ratios match, otherwise stretch as before 2026-11-14 with a WARNING in the report. contain: whole picture, smaller output. crop: fill, cut at 'anchor'. pad: whole picture, border padded (regenerate it). stretch: distort on purpose (the behaviour before 2026-11-14).

anchor.tooltip: crop: which part is kept. pad: where the picture sits.

pad_fill.tooltip: fit = pad: repeat the border cells, or zero latent. Either way the padded area is marked in the noise mask for the next sampler pass to generate.

output_tooltips: H3 AV latent with the video half resized to the target cells (audio unchanged). An H3 AV noise mask is resized with it; padded areas are marked for regeneration. Re-sample it next (Split Upscale, Tiled Diffusion or a low-denoise sampler).
Text: size plan, input/output cells and pixels, scale, method and device, chunking, and warnings (dropped plain mask or geometry record, scale above 4x, unequal axis scales). Also shown on the node.
MiniMaxH3_LatentUpscaleModel.name: MiniMaxH3_LatentUpscaleModel
MiniMaxH3_LatentUpscaleModel.description: Resize the video half of an H3 AV latent to a new pixel size, with the trained H3 3D latent upscaler (LBH-123-AI, models/latent_upscale_models, .safetensors only) or plain interpolation. The audio half passes through untouched. Then re-sample it (H3 Split Upscale, H3 Tiled Diffusion or a sampler at low denoise) to add detail. The conditioning must be made for the new size.

sigmas.tooltip: Sigma schedule to check (e.g. from BasicScheduler). Must be 1-D, finite, in [0, 1], strictly decreasing and end at 0; a split schedule (non-zero last sigma) is refused.

scheduler.tooltip: Scheduler that made the sigmas, for the report only: anything but simple adds an OFF-CONTRACT note. When model is connected, the scheduler measured from the sigmas is used instead.

denoise.tooltip: Denoise that made the sigmas, for the report only: below 1 adds a partial denoise note. When model is connected, the denoise measured from the sigmas is used instead.

model.tooltip: Wire from TurboLoRA to enforce minimax_h3_turbo_step_contract.

output_tooltips: The input sigmas, unchanged, when they are legal (the node raises an error otherwise). Wire to SamplerCustomAdvanced.
Text: how scheduler/denoise were determined, 'H3 sigma schedule OK' plus any warnings, and turbo step-contract notes when a Turbo LoRA model is connected.
MiniMaxH3_LegalScheduler.name: MiniMaxH3_LegalScheduler
MiniMaxH3_LegalScheduler.description: Validate a sigma schedule for H3 sampling. Rejects SplitSigmas / bong_tangent. Warns on non-simple schedulers and partial denoise. When optional model is wired from MiniMaxH3_TurboLoRA, enforces the turbo step contract (4/8/16). Passes sigmas through unchanged when legal. Wire BasicScheduler sigmas → this → SamplerCustomAdvanced.

model.tooltip: The H3 model to patch.

control_net.tooltip: A MiniMax H3 Fun ControlNet, loaded with ComfyUI's ModelPatchLoader.

vae.tooltip: The H3 VAE, used to encode the hint.

strength.tooltip: Overall control strength, as in the core node.

preserved_strength.tooltip: How much control still reaches rows the latent mask asked to preserve. 0 keeps the control out of them entirely, which is the point of this node. 1 restores ComfyUI's behaviour of ignoring the mask.

boundary_softness.tooltip: Blur the gate at the mask edge, in latent patches. A hard gate leaves a visible seam where the control stops; 1-2 patches is usually enough to hide it.

affect_text_rows.tooltip: ComfyUI's control stream also adds a residual to the TEXT rows, because it starts as a copy of the whole sequence. Off here: a depth map should not be editing the prompt. Turn it on to match core exactly.

control_video.tooltip: The hint - depth, pose, edges. Optional if you are only inpainting with mask + source_video.

inpaint.tooltip: Off: structural control only - the visibility channels are filled with ones, meaning nothing is a hole. On: also drive the Union model's inpainting branch from mask + source_video. The upstream model card treats these as two separate modes and ships a different script for each, so this is a switch, not something to infer.

mask.tooltip: PIXEL-space inpaint mask, only used when inpaint is on. This is NOT the latent mask that feeds Set Latent Noise Mask - wire the same pixel mask you send into Mask To Latent Space. A latent mask here is refused by name rather than stretched across the clip. The sampler's own denoise mask is read automatically and needs no wire.

source_video.tooltip: The plate the mask is cut from. REQUIRED when inpaint is on: these become the masked-latent channels, which are the plate with the hole cut out of it, and ComfyUI's own node substitutes a BLACK frame when it is missing. In a cropped workflow this is the CROPPED video - the same one that is VAE-encoded for the sampler.

sigma_start.tooltip: The control is active only while the step's sigma is <= this value (a raw sigma, not core's start_percent). 1.0 = from the first step. Also where the schedule's fade starts.

sigma_end.tooltip: The control is active only while the step's sigma is >= this value (raw sigma). 0.0 = to the last step. Also where the schedule's fade ends.

control_region.tooltip: Where THIS control may steer (1) and where it is ignored (0), e.g. pose only on the person. Combined with the sampler's denoise mask: a row is steered only where both allow it. Pixel space, the target's size (or the plate's with crop_bboxes).

schedule.tooltip: Strength over the steps inside the sigma window. constant: as before. fade out: full at the start, nothing at the end - the control sets the layout and leaves the detail to the model. fade in: the reverse. smooth fade out: eased.

crop_bboxes.tooltip: Subject Crop's boxes. With them, a PLATE-sized control video / source video / mask / region is cropped with the same boxes and stretched like the source, so it lands exactly on the cropped target. Without them, ComfyUI's centre cover-crop is used - a plate-sized control on a cropped target is then misaligned.

output_tooltips: A clone of the H3 model with the ControlNet patch registered; its residual is gated per latent row by the sampler's denoise mask. Wire to the sampler's model.
What was configured, and what to look for if the control still fights the mask.
MiniMaxH3_MaskAwareControlNet.name: MiniMaxH3_MaskAwareControlNet
MiniMaxH3_MaskAwareControlNet.description: H3 Fun ControlNet-Union that works alongside a latent noise mask. Two fixes over ComfyUI's own node. (1) It builds all 49 control channels. ComfyUI only builds the visibility and masked-latent channels when a mask is connected and zero-pads otherwise - but visibility 0 means 'this is a hole', so a control-video-only graph is silently asking the Union model to inpaint the entire frame. Here the neutral value is ONES. (2) Its residual is scaled per latent row by the sampler's own denoise mask, so the control steers only what is actually being generated instead of pushing rows the sampler is holding still. mask/source_video here are PIXEL space, not the latent mask that feeds Set Latent Noise Mask.

masks.tooltip: Mask batch to clean, one mask per frame.

threshold.tooltip: Mask values above this count as subject when finding blobs.

method.tooltip: shrink_grow: shrinks the mask so thin specks vanish, then restores the surviving blobs' exact shapes. components: drops blobs that are both small and short-lived.

shrink.tooltip: Shrink distance in pixels. Blobs thinner than about twice this are removed.

min_frames.tooltip: Surviving blobs must also persist at least this many frames. 1 disables the temporal check.

min_pixels.tooltip: Blobs whose largest single-frame area is below this many pixels are removed.

min_frames.tooltip: Small blobs must persist at least this many frames to survive.

edge_grow.tooltip: Grow kept regions by this many pixels so the subject's soft edges are preserved.

output_tooltips: Cleaned masks, same size and soft values as the input.
How many blobs were removed and which method ran.
MiniMaxH3_MaskCleanup.name: MiniMaxH3_MaskCleanup
MiniMaxH3_MaskCleanup.description: Removes specks and brief flickering blobs from a video mask batch while keeping the real subject, including its soft edges.

mask.tooltip: Any MASK; clamped to 0-1 before the levels are applied.

black_level.tooltip: Output value where the mask is 0 (the least any area gets).

white_level.tooltip: Output value where the mask is 1 (the most any area gets). May be below black_level, which inverts the mask.

gamma.tooltip: Applied as mask^(1/gamma) before the levels: 1 = linear, above 1 lifts mid values, below 1 lowers them.

output_tooltips: MASK of the same shape: black_level + (white_level - black_level) x mask^(1/gamma), clamped to 0-1.
MiniMaxH3_MaskLevels.name: MiniMaxH3_MaskLevels
MiniMaxH3_MaskLevels.description: Output levels for a mask: black becomes black_level, white becomes white_level, gamma bends the middle. For a denoise mask, black_level is the least any area is regenerated and white_level the most (e.g. 0.3 / 0.6 for a refine pass).

mask.tooltip: Pixel mask per frame, 1 = region H3 regenerates, 0 = keep. Should be the size of the clip being encoded; shorter batches are padded with the last frame, longer ones truncated.

width.tooltip: Pixel width of the video the latent belongs to. Sets the latent mask width (width // 16); the mask is centre-cropped to a multiple of 16 like the VAE.

height.tooltip: Pixel height of the video the latent belongs to. Sets the latent mask height (height // 16).

frame_count.tooltip: Pixel frames of the clip. Rounded UP to the next legal H3 length (17k+5), then grouped to latent frames with the (1,4,4,4,4) cycle.

denoise_strength.tooltip: Multiplies the final latent mask (0-1). 1 = masked tokens fully regenerated; lower values give partial noise in the masked region; 0 = mask all zero (nothing regenerated).

temporal_clean.tooltip: Frames: each pixel takes the max of the mask over +-N neighbouring frames before reduction, so the region grows in time and flicker gaps close. 0 = off.

spatial_dilate.tooltip: Pixels: grows the mask by N steps of a 3x3 cross dilation (about N px) before reduction to the 16 px latent grid. 0 = off.

quantize_soft.tooltip: Round values up to 1/256 steps (ceil(m*256)/256), the same quantisation the sampler applies, so re-pooling at sample time changes nothing.

output_tooltips: Video-side latent mask [latent frames, height/16, width/16], 1 = regenerate; max-pooled per 16 px cell and 2x2 token patch. For the noise_mask assembly (N4), not pixel use.
The latent mask upsampled back to pixel size, one frame per pixel frame of the snapped length, to see which 32 px token blocks will change.
Plain-text summary: snapped frame count, latent frame count, mask shape, latent grid size, quantize/strength settings.
MiniMaxH3_MaskPrep.name: MiniMaxH3_MaskPrep
MiniMaxH3_MaskPrep.description:
Clean a pixel mask and reduce it to H3 video-latent resolution with max-reduction on the 16x VAE grid, 2x2 DiT token patches, and the (1,4,4,4,4) temporal cycle. Output is the VIDEO side only at latent resolution — coarse regional denoise (32 source px per token). Fine edge feathering belongs in H3 Stitch Back (pixel space).

Downstream N4 assembles latent['noise_mask'] as comfy.nested_tensor.NestedTensor((video_mask, audio_mask)). N2 does not build that NestedTensor.

The sampler re-pools via model_base._pool_masks_to_token_grid and _token_grid_masks (ceil(m*256)/256). Pre-applying those steps here is idempotent — no double-shrink.

P5 pattern (no separate node): N2 mask → N4 sets latent['noise_mask'] NestedTensor((video_mask, audio_mask)). The DiT applies per-token noise_mask during sampling — regional strength without SplitSigmas.

masks.tooltip: Pixel-space masks, one per frame.

compression.tooltip: auto: read the compression geometry from the connected VAE, including the exact frame cycle and 2x2 token grid of chunked models like MiniMax H3. manual: enter it directly.

spatial.tooltip: Pixels per latent pixel on each axis.

token_spatial.tooltip: Latent pixels per model token on each axis; the mask is unified over each token block. 2 for MiniMax H3, 1 for models that read the mask per latent pixel.

head_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in the model's leading frame group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX. 0 when the model has no leading group.

head_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by the leading group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

chunk_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in each repeating group after the leading group. 4 for Wan and Hunyuan, 8 for LTX. 1 disables temporal reduction (image models).

chunk_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by each repeating group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

frames_per_latent.tooltip: Exact pixel frames covered by each latent frame, comma-separated, repeating from the first frame. Overrides the grid above when set. 1,4,4,4,4 with spatial 16 for MiniMax H3. For frame counts off the model's grid, use auto.

spatial_method.tooltip: How a block of pixels reduces to one latent pixel. max marks the cell if ANY pixel is masked - one stray pixel or one antialiased edge therefore claims a whole 32x32 token, so the mask creeps outward a full token all the way round the subject. min only marks it if every pixel is. mean leaves a fraction, which H3 reads as a partial denoise strength rather than a decision. coverage is the one to reach for on a character or face swap: it measures how much of the token the mask actually covers and decides with coverage_threshold below, so thin edges are rejected and the plate survives.

temporal_method.tooltip: How a group of frames reduces to one latent frame. max marks the frame if any grouped frame is masked.

grow_spatial.tooltip: Grow (+) or shrink (-) the mask this many pixels before reduction.

grow_temporal.tooltip: Grow (+) or shrink (-) the mask this many frames before reduction.

vae.tooltip: The VAE used to encode the latents this mask will be applied to. Required when compression is auto.

grow_tokens.tooltip: Grow the mask by whole TOKENS, after reduction instead of before it. This is the one that does not move the mask: measured drift is 0.000 latent cells at +1, +2 and +3 tokens, against 0.5-1.0 cells for the same growth done in pixels with grow_spatial. Pixel growth is re-quantised onto the 32px token grid, so changing it re-snaps the centre somewhere new - grow_spatial 8 drifts FURTHER than 16. Use this for a face or character swap, where the preserve/regenerate boundary has to stay put relative to the face. One token is 32 pixels. It still moves once the grown mask reaches a frame edge, because the shape is then genuinely lopsided.

coverage_threshold.tooltip: Only for spatial_method=coverage. The fraction of a token block that must be masked before the whole block counts as masked. 0.05 rejects stray pixels and antialiased boundaries while keeping anything genuinely inside; raise it to pull the mask tighter, lower it towards max behaviour. 0 marks a block if any pixel at all is masked, which is what max does.

output_tooltips: Latent-resolution mask for Set Latent Noise Mask.
Input and output dimensions plus compression geometry.
MiniMaxH3_MaskToLatentSpace.name: MiniMaxH3_MaskToLatentSpace
MiniMaxH3_MaskToLatentSpace.description: Reduces a pixel-space mask batch to latent resolution using the VAE's spatial and temporal compression, aligned to causal video VAE frame grouping and to the model's token grid (2x2 latent pixels for MiniMax H3). Feed the result to Set Latent Noise Mask.

av_latent.tooltip: H3 joint AV latent (samples = NestedTensor(video, audio)), e.g. from EmptyMiniMaxH3LatentAV / MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo. Its video stream is the template the encoded crops must match.

crops.tooltip: Canvas-space crops from H3 Track + Crop.

vae.tooltip: The MiniMax H3 video VAE. Encodes the crops (RGB) that replace the latent's video stream; retried on CPU after a GPU failure.

video_latent_mask.tooltip: Video-side mask from H3 Mask Prep (N2).

audio_vae.tooltip: Required when audio is connected.

output_tooltips: The AV latent with the encoded crops as its video stream (audio replaced only when audio is wired) and noise_mask = NestedTensor(video mask 1 = regenerate, audio mask 0 = locked / 1 = generated). Wire to the sampler.
Plain-text summary: encoded latent shape, audio locked or generative, mask shapes, temporal fit note.
MiniMaxH3_MaskedReplace.name: MiniMaxH3_MaskedReplace
MiniMaxH3_MaskedReplace.description:
Two sequential steps on an H3 AV latent:
1) Inject encoded plate crops into the VIDEO stream (audio intact).
2) Set noise_mask = NestedTensor((video_mask, audio_mask)).

video_mask = N2 soft latent mask (1=regenerate, 0=preserve).
audio_mask = zeros when audio is LOCKED (lipsync), ones when generative.

Supply audio + audio_vae to lock the audio stream (vocal stem for lipsync).
No mel spectrogram — H3 audio is a VAE over raw waveform.

Strength is NOT a widget here — control denoise with BasicScheduler. SplitSigmas is illegal on H3; at shift 12 even the last split point is ~sigma 0.80. guidance_scale is distilled (always 1.0).

P5 regional denoise: video_mask from N2 is written into noise_mask; the model soft-scales denoise per token (see comfy/ldm/minimax/model.py). Chain P10 → P11 guards before SigmaShiftLocked → LegalScheduler → sampler.

count.tooltip: Frames to keep. 0 = to the end.

model.tooltip: A MiniMax H3 model. The patch is a pure attention override - it reserves no DiT block, so it stacks with Block Cache and the Spectrum sampler.

clip.tooltip: The same H3 text encoder that built the conditioning. Each term is encoded through it once, here, not per sampling step.

conditioning.tooltip: Your POSITIVE conditioning, from any H3 encode node - the terms are appended to it. Feed the result to the sampler in its place.

terms.tooltip: One phrase per line, each a thing to push AWAY from. Add a weight with a trailing colon - 'blurry : 1.5'. Blank lines and # comments are ignored. These are already negative, so the weight is how hard to push, never a sign: a negative number here is refused rather than quietly turned back into positive guidance.

strength.tooltip: The alpha of eq. 6 - a global multiplier on every term. 1.0 is the paper's setting. Past about 2 the flipped values start to dominate the attention output and the frame degrades, which looks like burn-in rather than like a bad prompt.

context_mode.tooltip: standalone: encode each term on its own. Cheap, and what the original method does. prompt_prefix: encode it after your prompt and keep only the term's rows, so the text encoder (a causal LLM) sees the term in context and produces states on the same scale as the prompt's. Better aimed, but one extra encode per term, and it needs the prompt text below.

prompt_prefix.tooltip: Only for context_mode=prompt_prefix: the exact prompt text used to build the conditioning above. The node verifies that the prefix rows came back unchanged and falls back to standalone, saying so in the report, if they did not.

start_percent.tooltip: Begin flipping at this point through the schedule. Leaving it at 0 applies the terms throughout, which is the usual choice - the early steps are where layout is decided, so that is where a 'no extra limbs' term earns its keep.

end_percent.tooltip: Stop flipping here. Ending around 0.8 lets the last steps refine texture without the negative terms still pulling at it.

output_tooltips: A clone of the model with the NegPiP attention patch: the term rows' values are flipped between start_percent and end_percent. Unchanged when terms is empty.
The conditioning with the encoded term rows appended after the prompt's tokens. Use it in place of the input, with the model above.
Text: the plan (terms, token spans, strength, schedule), encoding notes and fallbacks, and what is not flipped.
MiniMaxH3_NegPiP.name: MiniMaxH3_NegPiP
MiniMaxH3_NegPiP.display_name: MiniMax H3 NegPiP (negative prompt in prompt)
MiniMaxH3_NegPiP.description: Negative prompting for H3 that rides in the SAME forward pass as the prompt, so it costs no extra step time the way CFG does. The terms you list are encoded and appended to the text conditioning; inside the DiT their attention VALUES are negated while their keys are left alone (Value Sign Flip, arXiv:2508.10931, the same trick as hako-mikan's NegPiP). A patch that matches 'blurry' therefore gets the direction of 'blurry' subtracted from it, weighted by how strongly it matched - so the push is adaptive per layer, per step and per token instead of a single global CFG scale. H3 suits this unusually well: it has no cross-attention, just one joint self-attention over a packed sequence, so the concatenation the method needs is already there.
