h3.publish_manifest v1.
JSON list of every published file.
The publish checklist.
MiniMaxH3_ShotPublisher.name: MiniMaxH3_ShotPublisher
MiniMaxH3_ShotPublisher.description: Publishes rendered media into <output>/<publish_root>/<show>/<seq>/<shot>/<task>/v###/ with a reserved version, a stage, optional required QC, verified checksums and a manifest. Never overwrites another version; never writes outside the output folder.

steps.tooltip: Used only when sigmas is not connected: builds a linear video schedule from 1 to 0 with this many steps (steps+1 sigma values).

shift_video.tooltip: Video sigma shift used to map each video sigma to the audio sigma and the derivatives in the table. Set it to the shift your model uses (H3 trained: 12).

shift_audio.tooltip: Audio sigma shift used to compute sigma_a from each sigma_v. Set it to the shift your model uses (H3 trained: 3).

sigmas.tooltip: When connected, inspect this schedule. Otherwise synthesised from steps.

output_tooltips: Text table, one row per sigma: step, sigma_v, sigma_a, analytic and finite-difference dsigma_a/dsigma_v, carry sigma_v/sigma_a, effective video denoise.
Compact JSON with the shifts, the video sigmas and the same per-step fields as the table; the node's live plot widget reads it.
MiniMaxH3_SigmaInspector.name: MiniMaxH3_SigmaInspector
MiniMaxH3_SigmaInspector.description: Read-only debug table: per-step sigma_v, sigma_a, analytic dσa/dσv (shift-invariant), finite-difference dσa/dσv (what the sampler steps), and carry factor σv/σa. Wire BasicScheduler sigmas or leave sigmas unconnected and set steps to synthesise a linear schedule. sigma_json feeds the live plot widget.

preset.tooltip: Model and variant. '(template)' = the settings of ComfyUI's official template for that model; the how-to names the template.
preset.default: MiniMax H3 Ref2VA (template, ref2v turbo LoRA)

steps.tooltip: 0 = the preset's steps. Distilled fixed schedules (LTX stages) ignore it.

denoise.tooltip: Below 1: the last part of a longer schedule, as BasicScheduler does.

width.tooltip: Image width: only Flux.2's scheduler depends on it.

height.tooltip: Image height: only Flux.2's scheduler depends on it.

model.tooltip: Optional: use this model's own sampling (its shift patches included) instead of the preset's.

output_tooltips: The preset's sigma schedule (steps+1 values, after denoise), from ComfyUI's scheduler code. Wire to SamplerCustom(Advanced) sigmas.
The preset's sampler as a SAMPLER object. Wire to SamplerCustom sampler.
The preset's CFG value from its source template. Use it on the guider (e.g. CFGGuider cfg).
Number of sampling steps actually in the sigmas output (its length minus 1).
IMAGE [1, 400, 720, 3]: sigma per step (plus H3's audio clock for H3 presets). Also shown as the node preview.
Plain text: sampler, steps, guidance/cfg, where the sigmas came from, first/last sigma (and H3 audio clock), any LoRA needed, source template, notes and wiring.
MiniMaxH3_SigmaPresets.name: MiniMaxH3_SigmaPresets
MiniMaxH3_SigmaPresets.description: The sigma schedule, sampler and cfg for a model - MiniMax H3 (+ turbo and FastH3), Wan 2.1 / 2.2 / Animate, Flux.1 / Flux.2, SDXL, SD 1.5, SD 3.5, LTX-2 / 2.3 / 2.5, HunyuanVideo, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Chroma, HiDream - as ComfyUI's official workflow templates ship them, with a graph and a how-to. The curves come from ComfyUI's own scheduler code. A preset that needs a speed LoRA or a distilled model says so. Connect your model to use its own shift.

model.tooltip: MiniMax H3 MODEL. Cloned; its model_sampling is replaced by an AV sampling object with the shifts below (the noise scale of the original is kept).

shift_video.tooltip: Sigma shift of the video schedule, sigma(t) = shift*t / (1 + (shift-1)*t). Higher keeps sigma high for longer. H3 was trained with 12. Also stored in transformer_options for other H3 nodes.

shift_audio.tooltip: Sigma shift of the audio schedule. Used as typed only when ratio_lock is off; with ratio_lock on it is replaced by shift_video / ratio. H3 was trained with 3.

ratio_lock.tooltip: On: shift_audio = shift_video / ratio (the report notes when the typed shift_audio was overridden). Off: shift_audio is used as typed.

ratio.tooltip: Video/audio shift ratio used when ratio_lock is on. Default 4 = the trained 12/3 pair.

output_tooltips: Clone of the model with the patched video/audio sigma shifts. Wire it to the scheduler/sampler.
Text: the video and audio shifts applied, any ratio_lock override of shift_audio, and the ratio when the lock is on.
MiniMaxH3_SigmaShiftLocked.name: MiniMaxH3_SigmaShiftLocked
MiniMaxH3_SigmaShiftLocked.description: Patch ModelSamplingAV with a coherent video/audio shift pair. Unlike core MiniMaxH3SigmaShift, ratio_lock keeps shift_audio = shift_video / ratio (default ratio 4 → trained 12/3). Moving shift_video moves shift_audio unless you disable ratio_lock to dial audio independently.

images.tooltip: Source frames (17k+5 of them, e.g. 121 or 124), at the size the model will generate - a multiple of 32 is best.

audio_mode.tooltip: keep: the soundtrack survives untouched. regenerate: all of it is new. follow mask: only the 1/40 s ticks whose frames are masked are new.

size_policy.tooltip: A frame that is not a multiple of 16: refuse (say how to fix it), or pad the right/bottom edge (recorded in the latent; the composite removes it).

audio_vae.tooltip: The MiniMax H3 audio VAE (needed with audio).

audio.tooltip: The source soundtrack. Without it, a silent track of the right length is used.

mask.tooltip: What to regenerate, one per frame at the frame size (1 = regenerate, 0 = keep). Without it everything is regenerated.

output_tooltips: Joint AV latent with its noise masks.
What was encoded and what the mask keeps.
MiniMaxH3_SourceAVLatent.name: MiniMaxH3_SourceAVLatent
MiniMaxH3_SourceAVLatent.description: Encode the source frames and their sound into the joint picture + sound latent H3 edits, with the edit mask on H3's own grid. Feed it to the sampler as latent_image. Unlike a plain VAE Encode it never crops the frame (the H3 VAE silently cuts off-grid edges, which moves the result against the plate), refuses a frame count H3 cannot encode, reduces the mask on H3's own frame grouping, and keeps or regenerates the sound per 1/40 s.

tile_width.tooltip: Tile width in PIXELS. Too small and each tile has no context — edges look like postage stamps. Too large and VRAM blows up before you see a seam.

tile_height.tooltip: Tile height in pixels — same trade-off as width.

overlap_ratio.tooltip: Fraction of each tile that overlaps its neighbour. Zero overlap is fastest but shows a hard grid; 25% is a typical compositor default. Above ~50% you pay for tiles you mostly throw away.

fade_ratio.tooltip: How much of the overlap is a gradual freeze-to-free ramp vs a hard frozen band. Too little fade leaves a visible step in denoise strength — a brightness ridge along the seam.

min_tile_size.tooltip: Smallest edge tile allowed in pixels. Stops the planner from leaving a skinny sliver at the frame edge that has almost no context and blooms differently.

seam_denoise.tooltip: Cap on denoise in the seam neighbourhood. Below 1.0 lets the sampler 'continue' frozen neighbour content at moderate strength — stops fast motion being cut in half at the tile edge under high denoise. 1.0 = classic behaviour (off). Try 0.5–0.8 for sports or hair.

brightness_match.tooltip: Per-frame, per-channel median match of each sampled tile to the source at the same place and frame. Stops tile-to-tile and frame-to-frame brightness drift. Experimental.

dynamic_fade.tooltip: Fade width over a tile's sampling steps. off: fixed. narrowing: starts at the fade width and shrinks to dynamic_fade_min. widening: grows from dynamic_fade_min. Helps seams when a tile is sampled in many steps.

dynamic_fade_min.tooltip: Narrowest fade (pixels) the dynamic fade reaches.

overlap_blend.tooltip: Shape of the cross-fade over an overlap when a tile is stitched: linear, smoothstep (eased) or midpoint (hard switch in the middle of the overlap).

masked_area_noise.tooltip: Noise let into the frozen overlap while sampling. 0: frozen (original behaviour). 1: no freeze at all. Small values (0.01-0.05) let the seam move a little with the scene.

grid_rows.tooltip: Equal tiles: split the height into this many tiles of one size (overlap from overlap_ratio). 0: use tile_height.

grid_cols.tooltip: Equal tiles: split the width into this many tiles of one size. 0: use tile_width.

output_tooltips: Tile size / overlap / fade / seam settings converted to latent cells (H3_SPATIAL_SPLIT_PARAM); wire to H3 Split Upscale 'spatial_split_param'.
Text: the tile grid on an EXAMPLE 64 x 64 latent; Split Upscale recomputes the grid from the real latent size.
MiniMaxH3_SpatialSplitParams.name: MiniMaxH3_SpatialSplitParams
MiniMaxH3_SpatialSplitParams.description: Spatial tiling for Split Upscale: tile size, overlap, fade and seam-denoise cap. Converts pixel sizes to latent cells (÷16, aligned to 2).

model.tooltip: Native MiniMax-H3 MODEL. When enabled, it is cloned and the clone gets the Spectrum sampler and transformer wrappers; the input model is not modified. A model that is not native H3 raises an error.

enabled.tooltip: Off returns the input model unchanged (no clone, no patch). On: on some sampler steps the H3 transformer is skipped and its final hidden feature is forecast from earlier actual steps.

blend_weight.tooltip: Direct video spectral share. Audio uses audio_blend_weight. Video forecasts can still affect later audio through joint transformer calls.

degree.tooltip: Degree of the Chebyshev ridge polynomial fitted over past actual steps to forecast the transformer feature. Needs at least degree+1 stored steps (max_history >= degree+1). Values other than 1 disable bootstrap_first_forecast.

ridge_lambda.tooltip: Ridge (L2) regularisation added to the polynomial fit. 0 = plain least squares; larger values pull the fitted coefficients toward zero. model_aware_mode schedule_confidence and full may adapt it per step.

window_size.tooltip: Starting forecast interval in steps: once history is ready, every floor(window)-th step is an actual transformer call and the steps between are forecast. 1 = every step actual (nothing skipped).

flex_window.tooltip: Added to the current window after each scheduled actual step past warmup, capped at max(window_size, max_history). 0 keeps the interval fixed at window_size; larger values skip more steps later in sampling.

warmup_steps.tooltip: Number of first sampler steps that always run the real transformer before forecasting may start. Values above 1 disable bootstrap_first_forecast.

tail_actual_steps.tooltip: Number of final sampler steps forced to run the real transformer. Some samplers enforce their own minimum tail (RES uses three steps); ER-SDE offline replay may promote one extra penultimate step.

max_history.tooltip: How many past actual transformer features are kept for the fit (oldest dropped first). Must be >= degree+1. Also caps how far flex_window can grow the window. Memory use grows with it (see history_storage).

debug.tooltip: Logs per-run Spectrum summaries, replay transitions and skipped-probe reasons to the console. Does not change the result.

history_storage.tooltip: Where the bounded feature history (max_history entries) is kept: system_ram = CPU memory (copied on each actual step), vram = the model's GPU device. The offline replay archive uses offline_archive_storage instead.

bootstrap_first_forecast.tooltip: Lets sampler step 1 be forecast from the single actual step-0 feature. Applies only with degree 1 and warmup_steps <= 1; otherwise it is turned off with a console warning.

anchor_residual_feedback.tooltip: Experimental: on actual steps, measures the forecast error and may request extra actual refreshes (budgeted); never adds a hidden residual. Only one of this, selective_rollback_correction and offline_smoothing_replay may be on, else an error.

selective_rollback_correction.tooltip: Experimental: thresholded, budgeted rollback that re-runs steps whose forecast error was too large; reviewed for the deterministic Euler sampler only. Turn offline_smoothing_replay off first (the trajectory modes are mutually exclusive).

offline_smoothing_replay.tooltip: Two-pass mode: the first sampler pass records every actual transformer feature, then a replay pass forecasts using past and future anchors, without video-to-audio feedback. Costs a second sampler pass plus the archive memory.

audio_blend_weight.tooltip: Audio rows' forecast mix (0-1): share of the polynomial (spectral) forecast, the rest is linear extrapolation from the last two actual steps. 0 = no spectral mixing of audio. Video uses blend_weight.

offline_archive_storage.tooltip: Where offline_smoothing_replay keeps every actual feature until replay ends. Not capped by max_history. system_ram = CPU memory; vram = GPU memory (faster, can run out on small GPUs).

model_aware_mode.tooltip: Experimental. off = fixed window schedule. schedule = risky forecasts become real transformer calls. schedule_confidence = also adapts ridge, usable degree and blend share. full = also applies the bounded generic correction (generic_correction_*), which adds no transformer call.

model_aware_risk_threshold.tooltip: Risk score (0-1) at or above which a planned forecast is replaced by a real transformer call. Lower = more real calls (slower, fewer forecasts). Ignored when model_aware_mode is off.

model_aware_trust_shrinkage.tooltip: Experimental research switch: shrinks forecasts by a measured forecast-trust probe. Requires model_aware_mode='full' (other modes raise an error); in offline replay it only records shadow diagnostics. Adds no transformer call.

model_aware_replay_generic_correction.tooltip: Offline replay with model_aware_mode='full' only. Off = the replay pass does not reuse the causal latest-delta correction. On = restores the older behaviour that applied it during replay (kept for reproduction).

generic_correction_mode.tooltip: Applied only with model_aware_mode='full': how the gain on the latest-delta correction is estimated. legacy = previous EWMA path; coordinate_rls = recursive least squares scaled by step spacing; coordinate_rls_reliability = adds a reliability factor; regional = experimental per-region gains.

generic_correction_limiter.tooltip: How the correction gain is bounded to +/- generic_correction_limit (model_aware_mode='full'). hard_clip = clamp; tanh = smooth saturation; rational = g/(1+|g|/limit). rational with limit 0.25 and mode legacy reproduces the older exact path.

generic_correction_limit.tooltip: Symmetric bound on the correction gain used by generic_correction_limiter (model_aware_mode='full'). Smaller = smaller possible correction. Default 0.40; 0.25 with legacy/rational/mode_default gives the older exact baseline.

generic_correction_attenuation.tooltip: Scales the correction gain down by confidence (model_aware_mode='full'). no_attenuation = none; general_confidence = forecast confidence; correction_reliability = measured correction reliability; combined_conservative = both; mode_default = per-mode choice (legacy keeps its own path).

output_tooltips: Patched clone of the H3 model with Spectrum forecasting installed (or the input model unchanged when enabled is off). Wire it to the sampler.
MiniMaxH3_SpectrumApply.name: MiniMaxH3_SpectrumApply
MiniMaxH3_SpectrumApply.description: Install Spectrum H3 spectral forecasting on a native MiniMax-H3 model. Clones the model and patches sampler wrappers without mutating the input.

av_latent.tooltip: A joint H3 AV latent (NestedTensor video + audio, with or without a noise-mask pair).

output_tooltips: The video stream [B, 24, T, h, w] with its own noise mask (if any) and the AV latent's other keys.
The audio stream [B, 32, 2, T] with its own noise mask (if any) and the AV latent's other keys.
MiniMaxH3_SplitAV.name: MiniMaxH3_SplitAV
MiniMaxH3_SplitAV.description:
Take a joint AV latent apart into its video and audio streams.

Neither stream inherits the other's noise mask, so you can work on one without silently constraining the other.

model.tooltip: The H3 MODEL that samples every tile / chunk (a Fun ControlNet patch on it is cropped per tile); unloaded at the end of the run.

conditioning.tooltip: Positive conditioning; its minimax_keyframes are trimmed to each chunk and cropped to each tile.

latent.tooltip: H3 AV latent (video + audio NestedTensor), batch 1, already at the target size; it is re-sampled in tiles, not resized. Audio is kept (frozen by the noise mask).

noise.tooltip: Noise source (e.g. RandomNoise); generated once for the whole latent and sliced per tile, so tiles share one seed.

sampler.tooltip: Sampler used for every tile, chunk and seam-polish pass.

sigmas.tooltip: Sigma schedule for each tile pass (steps = len - 1); its start sigma sets how much each tile is re-noised.

cfg.tooltip: CFG scale; used only when 'negative' is wired. 1.0 = no extra guidance (H3 is guidance-distilled).

seam_polish.tooltip: Second-pass resample on seams that fail a colour/correlation probe. 'auto' only polishes bad seams; 'all' is slow but catches subtle colour steps. 'off' if you will fix seams in comp.

color_match.tooltip: Median DC match on overlaps and per-chunk grade pin to the source. Off saves a little time but seams often show a visible colour step between tiles.

negative.tooltip: Optional negative conditioning. Not wired = positive only and cfg is ignored.

temporal_split_param.tooltip: From H3 Temporal Split Params. Not wired = the whole clip in one temporal pass, no anchors.

spatial_split_param.tooltip: From H3 Spatial Split Params. Not wired = the full frame as one tile.

output_tooltips: H3 AV latent at the input size with the re-sampled video and the original audio; wire to VAE Decode.
Text: temporal segments, tile grid and overlaps, seam-polish count, colour match on/off (+ Fun ControlNet windowing note).
MiniMaxH3_SplitUpscale.name: MiniMaxH3_SplitUpscale
MiniMaxH3_SplitUpscale.description:
Re-sample a MiniMax H3 AV latent tile by tile, in time and/or space, with frozen overlap bands, colour matching and optional seam repolish. It does NOT change the resolution: feed it a latent that is already at the target size (an upscaled video VAE-encoded, or a latent upscale) and it refines it in tiles that fit in memory. A Fun ControlNet on the model (Apply MiniMax H3 Fun ControlNet) follows the tiles: each tile and chunk gets only its own part of the control video, mask and source.

Prevention: pre-fill overlap from neighbours + triple temporal anchors. Correction: spatial/temporal DC match + per-chunk grade pin. Anti-fork: seam_denoise cap on the freeze mask.

plate.tooltip: Full-size source frames the crops are pasted onto (same clip Track + Crop received). Pixels outside the paste mask are returned unchanged (RGB only).

crops.tooltip: Generated crops at the transform's canvas size, one per frame. A batch the VAE cut to a multiple of 16 is re-centred onto the canvas with plate margins instead of stretched.

transform.tooltip: The H3_TRANSFORM from H3 Track + Crop, unchanged: per-frame crop boxes used for the inverse warp, plus subject rectangles and detection weights.

paste_region.tooltip: Area of each crop pasted back when no paste_mask is wired. subject: the tracked subject rectangle; subject_ellipse: the ellipse inside it; full_crop: the whole crop. Edges are feathered by feather_px.

mask_dilation.tooltip: Canvas pixels the paste area is grown by before feathering (subject rectangle/ellipse, or a max-filter on paste_mask). Not used by full_crop. 0 = no growth.

feather_px.tooltip: Gaussian feather of the paste edge, in SOURCE pixels (converted to canvas pixels per 8-frame chunk; kernel 2N+1). 32 = one H3 latent token. 0 = hard edge.

colour_match.tooltip: 0-1: per frame and channel, shift the crop's mean and standard deviation inside the paste mask toward the plate's. 0 = crop colours as generated; 1 = full match.

blend.tooltip: 0-1 opacity of the pasted crop over the plate (multiplies the paste mask). 0 = output is the plate.

undetected_frames.tooltip: Frames where Track + Crop found no subject. fade_out: paste opacity follows the detection rate over a 9-frame window (ramps to 0); skip: those frames keep the plate; composite_anyway: paste every frame.

paste_mask.tooltip: Optional per-frame mask in CANVAS space.

output_tooltips: Plate frames (RGB) with the crops warped back and composited; pixels outside the composite mask are the plate unchanged.
Per-frame MASK at source size, 1 = fully the pasted crop, fractional on the feather, 0 = plate; includes blend and detection weights.
Plain-text summary: frames stitched, planner mode, feather in source and canvas pixels, any VAE 16 px cut recovery.
MiniMaxH3_StitchBack.name: MiniMaxH3_StitchBack
MiniMaxH3_StitchBack.description: Paste crops back using the exact H3_TRANSFORM from Track + Crop. Inverse affine warp, feather in SOURCE pixels (default 32px = one latent token), mask-confined composite. Pixels outside the paste mask are the literal plate tensor (invariant 5).

overlap_frames.tooltip: Use actual_overlap_frames from Prepare Continuation. A continuation latent made by Prepare Continuation is checked against it and a mismatch stops the run; one made elsewhere cannot be checked, and a wrong value there joins at the wrong place (a stutter or a jump cut).

blend_video_overlap.tooltip: Smoothstep the video across the seam. Off by default because the pinned context should already match; turn it on when a residual difference still shows.

offload_to_cpu.tooltip: Keep the growing result in system RAM. Worth enabling for long multi-pass runs: this accumulator is only read by the next stitch and the final decode, so holding it in VRAM across many passes just starves the sampler.

output_tooltips: H3 AV latent: the previous segment followed by the continuation minus its overlap (optionally blended across it); length and A/V sync are verified. Feed it back as previous_av or decode it.
Pixel frames of stitched_av (previous + continuation - overlap).
Text: frames joined, overlap used, audio / video latent rows, blend / offload, and whether the overlap was checked.
MiniMaxH3_StitchContinuation.name: MiniMaxH3_StitchContinuation
MiniMaxH3_StitchContinuation.description:
Join a sampled continuation onto the previous segment along their shared overlap, without shifting time.

The overlap must be the value Prepare Continuation actually used after grid snapping, not the one you typed. A continuation made by Prepare Continuation carries that value, and a different overlap_frames stops the run. The result is verified too: if the stitched length or the audio/video sync does not come out exactly as predicted it raises, rather than handing on a latent that is quietly the wrong length.

images.tooltip: Full-size PLATE frames (the clip given to H3 Track + Crop). Pose is detected here, never on the crops. Frames used = min(images, transform frames).

transform.tooltip: H3_TRANSFORM from H3 Track + Crop. Its per-frame boxes map plate keypoints / hints into crop canvas pixels.

mode.tooltip: inhouse_vitpose: YOLO + ViTPose-H wholebody (ONNX, CPU) on the plate; needs models/detection/vitpose_h_wholebody_model.onnx (+ yolov10m.onnx). passthrough: crop the wired passthrough_hints with the transform instead (no keypoints).

confidence.tooltip: inhouse_vitpose: keypoints below this ViTPose score get confidence 0, are not drawn, and do not count toward coverage. Higher = fewer, surer joints.

temporal_smooth.tooltip: inhouse_vitpose: One Euro filter (24 fps, min_cutoff 1.0, beta 0.05) on each keypoint's x/y over time, in plate space, before warping to the crop.

gap_fill.tooltip: inhouse_vitpose: longest low-confidence gap (frames, between two confident detections) whose x/y is interpolated; a longer gap keeps the detector's own x/y. 0 = interpolate every gap. Filled points keep their low score, so they are not drawn; this changes keypoints_json, not the hints image.

output_tooltips: IMAGE batch at the crop canvas size, one per frame: white 1 px skeleton lines (arms, torso, legs, ankles/feet) on black; passthrough = the wired hints cropped.
JSON {"format":"minimax_h3_keypoints_v1","frames":[{"keypoints":[{"x","y","c"}...]}]}: 133 COCO-WholeBody points per frame in crop canvas pixels; all c=0 in passthrough.
0-1 share of frames with a usable pose: ViTPose = at least 17 keypoints above confidence; passthrough = a hint pixel left inside the crop.
Plain-text summary: detector/model note, mode, coverage, settings, crop size, frame count, planner mode.
MiniMaxH3_StrongestPose.name: MiniMaxH3_StrongestPose
MiniMaxH3_StrongestPose.description: Detect pose in PLATE space (ViTPose-H wholebody when available), then warp hints to crop space via the N1 H3_TRANSFORM — never detect in crop space (INVARIANT 10). Includes feet/ankles for ground-contact shots.

masks.tooltip: Subject masks, one per frame. Clean them first (Mask Cleanup) if the segmentation is noisy.

mode.tooltip: In order of increasing complexity. combined: one static crop with padding around the subject's whole travel. tracked: a constant-size crop that stays still until the subject would leave it, then moves as little as possible. zoomed: the crop also follows the subject's size, planned over the whole clip, every crop resampled to a fixed output resolution.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's combined extent across all frames: 1.5 leaves a third of the crop as margin around the whole travel. 1.0 hugs the travel exactly. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Crop shape as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78), reached by growing the smaller dimension. 0 sizes width and height from the mask's whole travel.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's size: 1.5 keeps the subject at two thirds of the crop with the rest as padding, at any resolution. 1.0 crops tight, leaving no padding for the padding setting to keep; 4.0 surrounds the subject with three times its own size. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

padding.tooltip: How firmly the crop_scale padding is kept. guaranteed: never less than promised on any frame, whatever it costs in size or movement; only the image edge can break it, and mask noise counts as subject, so clean the masks first. firm: at least 70% is always kept, the rest yields briefly during fast motion. flexible: padding yields first whenever keeping it would cost stillness or tightness.

prefer.tooltip: What pays for keeping the padding when the subject moves. stillness: the crop runs larger so it can move less. tightness: the crop stays as small as the padding allows and moves as much as needed instead.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Crop shape as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78). 0 lets the planner choose the shape that best balances padding, stillness, and size for this clip.

seamless_loop.tooltip: Plan the crop path so the last frame wraps seamlessly into the first. Only for clips that genuinely repeat.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's size: 1.5 keeps the subject at two thirds of the crop with the rest as padding, so the subject holds a constant share of the output at any resolution. 1.0 crops tight, leaving no padding for the padding setting to keep; 4.0 surrounds the subject with three times its own size. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

padding.tooltip: How firmly the crop_scale padding is kept. guaranteed: never less than promised on any frame, whatever it costs in size, movement, or rescaling; only the image edge can break it, and mask noise counts as subject, so clean the masks first. firm: at least 70% is always kept, the rest yields briefly during fast motion. flexible: padding yields first whenever keeping it would cost stillness or tightness.

prefer.tooltip: What pays for keeping the padding when the subject moves. stillness: the crop moves and rescales as little as possible, running larger instead. tightness: the crop and the output resolution stay as small as the padding allows, moving and rescaling as much as needed instead.

pad_surplus_tol.tooltip: Extra padding (a crop bigger than needed) lasting shorter than this many frames is kept rather than trimmed, riding out occlusions and dips at a steady size. At 1 the crop follows every size change tightly; very high holds one constant size for the whole clip.

zoom_step.tooltip: Whether crop size changes smoothly or snaps to discrete zoom levels this ratio apart. At 1.0 size changes continuously; at 2.0 every zoom level doubles the previous one.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Shape of every crop and of the output resolution, as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78). 0 lets the planner choose the shape that best balances padding, stillness, and rescaling for this clip. Output size is automatic: the largest crop stays at 1:1 pixel scale.

head_size_mode.tooltip: match character proportions: room for the new character's own head-to-body ratio (from the poses, or head_scale), anchored at the chin. keep original composition: the original performer's head size and position. Decides the crop room, the mask padding and head_room_masks; the head is never stretched.

head_scale.tooltip: New head size / original head size. 0 = measure it from original_pose and reference_pose (face width against shoulder width); without poses it is 1. Ignored in keep original composition.

original_pose.tooltip: Pose of the original performer, per frame (DWPose / SDPose / OpenPose JSON). Gives the face size, the chin and the shoulders.

reference_pose.tooltip: Pose of the new character's reference image: its face width against its shoulder width sets the head scale. Needs the shoulders in the picture.

bboxes.tooltip: Optional: crop exactly at these boxes instead of planning - wire the bboxes of a Subject Crop run on the WHOLE clip (or one box). A job that runs Subject Crop per window otherwise plans each window on its own and the crop moves between segments.

MiniMaxH3_SubjectCropAdvanced.name: MiniMaxH3_SubjectCropAdvanced
MiniMaxH3_SubjectCropAdvanced.description: Subject Crop with every planner cost exposed. The standard node's padding and prefer settings are presets over these dials; the defaults here reproduce its firm/stillness cell.

max_anchors.tooltip: Approved frames to add after the identity images (nearest segments first).

segment.tooltip: H3 Job Controller's segment (this run's scene).

MiniMaxH3_SubjectMemory.name: MiniMaxH3_SubjectMemory
MiniMaxH3_SubjectMemory.description: What the subject looks like so far, rebuilt from the job on every run: the bank's identity images plus approved frames from ACCEPTED segments of the current scene (never a rejected one; a cut starts over). anchors feed the model's reference inputs; memory feeds H3 QC Gate's colour continuity check.

images.tooltip: The frame(s) with the new detections.

bboxes.tooltip: core SAM 3 Detect's bboxes.

subject.tooltip: The subject's memory: H3 Multi-Subject Selector's or H3 Temporal Subject Tracker's subject.

frame.tooltip: Which image of the batch (and which frame of the bboxes) to search; clamped to the last image.

confirmation.tooltip: always ask: stop and show the candidates; pick index: take '#index'.

index.tooltip: With confirmation = pick index: the '#' number of the candidate in the gallery to accept.

min_confidence.tooltip: auto when confident: when the best score (appearance x colour similarity - motion penalty) is under this, it stops for review.

margin.tooltip: Review when the second candidate scores within this of the best.

appearance_weight.tooltip: Multiplier on the colour-histogram similarity (body and clothing colours) to the subject's memory; 0 ranks by distance only.

motion_weight.tooltip: Penalty per frame width of distance from where the subject was.

search_distance.tooltip: Ignore candidates farther than this (a fraction of the width).

MiniMaxH3_SubjectReIdentification.name: MiniMaxH3_SubjectReIdentification
MiniMaxH3_SubjectReIdentification.description: Finds the tracked person again among new detections (after a cut, an occlusion, a lost track). Score = appearance x colour similarity to the subject's memory - motion x how far they moved (a fraction of the width). Below min_confidence, or with a second candidate within margin, it stops for review and shows the candidates: the subject id is never changed silently. Appearance is the body and clothing colours; no face model is used.

bboxes.tooltip: Boxes from Subject Crop, one per frame. A single box or single frame is applied to every frame; extra boxes within a frame are ignored. When inputs disagree on frame count, extra frames are dropped.

feather.tooltip: Blend width in pixels, feathered inward from the crop border. Sides touching the image edge are not feathered.

cropped_masks.tooltip: Confines the paste to the mask, one per crop at any resolution. A single mask is applied to every frame. Used exactly as given; pre-blur the mask for a soft edge.

protect.tooltip: feathered box: the whole crop goes back, feathered at the box border (as before; the background inside the box is the model's). exact outside mask: every pixel outside cropped_masks stays bit-exact the original; the feather runs INSIDE the mask edge. soft mask edge: the mask's own soft values are the blend. whole crop: the crop replaces the box, no feather.

output_tooltips: Original frames with the crops blended back in.
What was kept exactly, blended and replaced, measured.
Per frame: box, crop size, scale, pixel counts, largest change where the original was kept.
MiniMaxH3_SubjectUncrop.name: MiniMaxH3_SubjectUncrop
MiniMaxH3_SubjectUncrop.description: Pastes processed crops back into the original frames with a feathered border, optionally confined by a mask. The paste is pixel-exact when the crop size was not changed.

pose_keypoint.tooltip: Whole-body pose from the DUPE - the performance you want recreated. Must be a whole-body detector (SDPose, DWPose, ViTPose-wholebody): a 17-point body model carries no face landmarks, so there is nothing to drive the lips with.

swap_scope.tooltip: Which VFX operation this is. face: the whole face drives it and the face region is masked. lips: mouth and jaw drive it - the chin has to drop for the mouth to open - but only the mouth is regenerated, so a lip-sync never reshapes the chin. head: as face, with hair and skull in the mask too. body: body, feet and hands, face left alone. person: all of it.

width.tooltip: Control frame width. Match the generation, or the control lands at the wrong scale.

height.tooltip: Control frame height. Match the generation.

confidence_gate.tooltip: Landmarks below this are not drawn. Raise it if a flickery detection is making lines twitch between frames; lower it if features drop out during fast motion.

face_line_width.tooltip: Face line thickness. 0 means half the body width, which is the useful default: a thick line closes the gap between the lips, and the model then cannot tell an open mouth from a shut one.

drive_jaw.tooltip: Draw the dupe's jaw contour into the control. ON is usually right: those 17 points carry head POSE (which way the head is turned) and the CHIN DROP that lets the mouth open, not just skull shape. They also carry the dupe's face WIDTH, so if the swapped head starts looking like the dupe, lower the ControlNet strength before reaching for this. OFF removes the contour entirely - the reference actor's skull is then unopposed, but a profile will read as a front-on face and the mouth cannot open as far.

drive_mouth.tooltip: Draw the dupe's lips into the control. Leave it ON when the audio is that dupe's own take, or when there is no audio at all - then the lips follow the performance. Turn it OFF for a DUB: the mouth is still masked, so it is free to change, but nothing is telling it the old lip shape and a locked audio track decides instead. With it off and no audio locked, the lips have nothing driving them at all.

mask_pad.tooltip: How far the region mask reaches past the landmark hull, as a fraction of the hull's own size. -1 uses the per-scope default (head pads furthest, because hair has no landmarks to find). Padding scales about the hull's centroid, so growing it does not move the boundary relative to the face.

mask_feather.tooltip: Soften the mask edge, in pixels. Feather in PIXEL space here; the latent reduction downstream is where the 32px token grid takes over.

person_index.tooltip: Which detected person is the dupe, when the frame holds more than one.

output_tooltips: Feed to H3 Mask-Aware ControlNet's control_video.

The region allowed to change, built from the SAME landmarks as the control so the two cannot drift apart. Send it to H3 Mask To Latent Space (with spatial_method=coverage, and grow it with grow_tokens) and to the ControlNet's pixel-space mask. Masked and driven are NOT the same set: the jaw is both, so head pose comes through while the skull can still move toward your reference, and 'lips' drives the jaw for the chin drop but masks only the mouth, so a lip-sync never reshapes the chin.
Plain-text summary: what the scope drives and masks, the keypoint source, edges drawn out of possible, warnings (no pupils, no face landmarks past the gate), mask coverage and pad.
MiniMaxH3_SwapControl.name: MiniMaxH3_SwapControl
MiniMaxH3_SwapControl.display_name: H3 Swap Control (face / head / body / lips)
MiniMaxH3_SwapControl.description:
Turn a dupe's detected pose into the control video that drives a swap on H3. H3 has NO face conditioning path - no face_images, no expression coefficients - so expression and lip movement can only arrive through the control video.

The whole face drives it: jaw for head pose and chin drop, brows and eyes for expression, PUPILS for gaze direction, mouth for lip movement. The same region is masked, so the skull shape can still move toward your reference actor while the dupe's performance comes through.

That is a real tension, not a solved problem: a strong jaw control pulls face width toward the dupe. Lower the ControlNet strength if the head starts taking the dupe's shape, or turn drive_jaw off to remove the contour from the control entirely - at the cost of head pose and chin drop.

Feed the output to the control_video input of H3 Mask-Aware ControlNet. Any whole-body detector works - SDPose is the strongest (72.8 AP on COCO-WholeBody against DWPose's ~66, and better out of domain) - but a BODY-ONLY detector has no face landmarks at all and cannot drive expression.

model.tooltip: The MiniMax H3 model.

tau.tooltip: Strength. 0 = no patch (the A/B baseline). Usual 0.1-0.3; up to 0.3 when small faces break up. Applied strongest in deep layers and early steps.

output_tooltips: Clone of the model with the TST query correction mounted (attention override plus wrappers); the unchanged input model when tau = 0.

MiniMaxH3_TSTAttention.name: MiniMaxH3_TSTAttention
MiniMaxH3_TSTAttention.description: Experimental, unmeasured on H3 here. Training-free correction against temporal flicker and small faces that break up (Spectral Transport Homeostasis, arXiv 2609.08505). For every video attention call it measures, per head, whether the frames over-mix or fragment, and scales the video queries to pull them back. Put it after other attention patches (closer to the sampler). It changes the result, so compare against tau = 0. The console prints one summary per sampling run.

samples.tooltip: The sampler's AV latent.

task.tooltip: edit (source-driven): the job works over a source plate - connect 'media' (the validator errors without it). generate (source-free): no plate; the length comes from 'count' or the shot plan.

first.tooltip: First GLOBAL frame number of the job. -1 = the media's first frame number.

segment_frames.tooltip: Frames per segment, on the H3 grid (17k + 5: 22, 39, 56 ... 124, 141).

context.tooltip: Accepted frames each next segment continues from (H3 Continuation: 5, 22, 39 or 56).

seed.tooltip: The job's base seed: segment k's first attempt uses seed + k, retries add 1000.

max_retries.tooltip: Extra attempts a segment gets after it is rejected (each with a new seed: +1000 per attempt). When they are used up the segment waits for review. 0 = no retry.

approval.tooltip: QC decides: a failed segment is retried with a new seed (up to max_retries, then it waits for review). review when QC fails: a failed segment waits for you at once. review every segment: every segment waits for you.

auto_continue.tooltip: After each committed segment, queue the next run automatically.

max_auto_runs.tooltip: Most runs one auto-continue chain queues by itself; then it stops and says so in the status (queue again to go on). A run you queue by hand starts a new chain.

fps.tooltip: The job's frame rate, kept as an exact rate (23.976 = 24000/1001) and used for the final movie. Ignored when 'media' is connected (the plate's rate wins). The validator warns when it is not 24 (H3's rate).

deliver_codec.tooltip: Codec of the final movie H3 Job Commit assembles in the job folder: h264 (.mp4, 8-bit, even size), prores (.mov, 10-bit, even size), ffv1 (.mkv, 10-bit).

prompt.tooltip: The job's prompt, shared by every segment: H3 Job Controller's prompt is this, then the segment's shot prompt when a shot plan is connected. Its hash is part of the spec's fingerprints.

references.tooltip: Reference identity (any text / JSON that changes when they change) - e.g. H3 Reference Bank's fingerprint.

hold_head.tooltip: Frames of the first picture a segment without continuation context generates before its window and then drops (the PRB workflow's AV handles: 8). The model's first frames settle on a held picture, not on the cut.

shot_plan.tooltip: From H3 Shot Planner: the job becomes its shots (their length sets 'count'; each segment gets its shot's prompt, with 'prompt' above as a shared prefix). Cuts never carry context; dissolves cross-fade.

output_tooltips: h3.task_spec v1
MiniMaxH3_TaskSpec.name: MiniMaxH3_TaskSpec
MiniMaxH3_TaskSpec.description: What a job does: the task, the frame range, segment length / context / blend / tracking handles, seed, retries, the QC and approval policy, auto-continue. Fingerprints the source and references, so a changed source makes only the segments that used it stale.

images.tooltip: Frame sequence (IMAGE batch) to deflicker. Needs 3 or more frames (fewer pass through unchanged); first and last frames are not changed; an alpha channel is passed through.

amount.tooltip: How much of the boil is removed.

radius.tooltip: Box radius in pixels that separates boil (fine) from motion (coarse). 0 = 8 px at 704 rows, scaled with the height.

motion_low.tooltip: Coarse change (0-255 scale) below which the filter works fully.

motion_high.tooltip: Coarse change (0-255 scale) above which the filter is off.

mask.tooltip: Deflicker only here (1 = deflicker). Outside, the frames are unchanged.

output_tooltips: IMAGE batch, same size and frame count as the input, with the static boil removed (only inside mask when one is connected).
JSON: frames, mean_change and max_change (mean absolute 0-1 pixel change per frame), and the radius actually used.
MiniMaxH3_TemporalDeflicker.name: MiniMaxH3_TemporalDeflicker
MiniMaxH3_TemporalDeflicker.description: Removes the fine frame-to-frame boil of a generated sequence where nothing moves (fine detail the three-frame median does not share), and leaves real motion alone: where the difference is coherent - an arm, an ear moving faster than its own width - the filter fades out. Optionally only inside a mask (e.g. the regenerated subject). The first and last frames pass through.

images.tooltip: Full-size PLATE frames. Depth is computed on these (or, in passthrough with nothing wired, their luminance is used); frames used = min(images, transform frames).

transform.tooltip: H3_TRANSFORM from H3 Track + Crop. Its per-frame boxes crop the plate depth to the H3 canvas.

backend.tooltip: passthrough: the depth wired into passthrough_hints, else a luminance proxy (not depth). Model backends run through ComfyUI-CustomNodePacks' depth runners and stop with an error when that pack or the weights are missing.

window.tooltip: Frames the temporal alignment looks back over (1 = no alignment).

emit_normals.tooltip: Also compute normals from the plate depth (Sobel gradients, no model), cropped like the hints. Off = the normals output is all zeros.

passthrough_hints.tooltip: Plate-space depth hints for passthrough backend.

temporal.tooltip: align: fit each frame's depth scale / offset to the previous `window` frames (removes per-frame normalisation flicker). Experimental: measured to help per-frame scale jitter, not a clean pan.

allow_download.tooltip: Let a model backend download its weights (some are many GB; Depth Anything V2 Large and DVD are non-commercial). Off: only installed copies are used and the error says what is missing.

output_tooltips: IMAGE batch at the crop canvas size, one per frame: the plate depth (3 equal channels, 0-1) cropped through the transform.
IMAGE batch at the crop canvas size: normals as RGB = (-dx, -dy, 1) normalised and mapped to 0-1; all zeros when emit_normals is off.
Plain-text summary: backend and its note (e.g. luminance proxy warning), temporal-align flicker numbers, crop size, frames.
MiniMaxH3_TemporalDepth.name: MiniMaxH3_TemporalDepth
MiniMaxH3_TemporalDepth.description: Depth hints in crop space: plate depth from a backend, warped through the N1 transform. passthrough = the depth map you wire into passthrough_hints (e.g. core 'Run Depth Anything 3'); with nothing wired it is a LUMINANCE proxy, not depth, and the report says so. The model backends (Depth Anything V2 / 3, Depth Pro, DepthCrafter, DVD) run through ComfyUI-CustomNodePacks' depth runners when that pack is installed; otherwise they stop with what is missing. temporal = align (experimental, off by default): fits every frame's depth scale / offset to the median of the previous `window` frames and normalises the clip once - it removes per-frame scale / offset flicker (measured on synthetic jitter) but did not help a clean pan, so it is opt-in. normals carries zeros when emit_normals is off.

masks.tooltip: Mask sequence (MASK batch, 1 = subject) whose short dropouts are closed. Crop-space masks need bboxes to be judged in plate space.

window.tooltip: Frames a dropout may last and still be closed.

plate_width.tooltip: With bboxes: the plate's width (0 = the right edge of the boxes).

plate_height.tooltip: With bboxes: the plate's height (0 = the bottom edge of the boxes).

bridge_take_ends.tooltip: Also close a dropout at the very start or end of the take. Only for a subject that holds still: a moving subject's next 'window' frames of path would be painted into the first frames.

bboxes.tooltip: Crop boxes (Subject Crop) when the masks are crop-space.

output_tooltips: MASK batch, same size and frame count as the input, values 0-1: the input with dropouts of up to window frames filled in (coverage only added, never removed).
JSON: frames, window, frames_bridged (indices that gained coverage, first 200), mean_added coverage fraction, and the space (mask or plate).
MiniMaxH3_TemporalMatteChatterCorrector.name: MiniMaxH3_TemporalMatteChatterCorrector
MiniMaxH3_TemporalMatteChatterCorrector.description: Closes short dropouts in a mask sequence: a pixel stays covered while the mask covered it within 'window' frames before AND after, so a segmenter losing the hair, a sleeve or the whole subject for a few frames no longer pastes the plate back over the new cast (it reads as flicker). A pixel the subject really leaves stays uncovered. With bboxes (crop boxes) the masks are judged in plate space, where the set holds still while a follow-cam crop moves.

chunk_frames.tooltip: Frames per temporal pass. Off-grid values snap to 17n+5 — a wrong length produces a temporal POP at the chunk boundary because the latent rows no longer align with the model's token clock.

temporal_overlap_frames.tooltip: Shared frames between chunks — what gets cross-faded and colour-matched. Too little looks like a hard cut; too much doubles render time. Snapped to the H3 grid.

anchor_strength.tooltip: How tightly the new chunk is pinned to the previous segment's last latent row. Low values let the seam drift and look like two different takes spliced together.

motion_anchor_frames.tooltip: Motion keyframes borrowed from the accumulated result to carry fast movement across the seam. 0 disables; 22 is one H3 cycle — use when limbs cross the boundary.

identity_anchor_frames.tooltip: Spacing of identity anchors sampled from the ORIGINAL latent inside each chunk. Stops faces or wardrobe from slowly morphing across a long upscale. 0 disables.

output_tooltips: Chunk length, overlap and anchor settings (H3_TEMPORAL_SPLIT_PARAM); wire to H3 Split Upscale 'temporal_split_param'.
Text: the segment plan for an EXAMPLE 124-frame clip (37 latent rows); Split Upscale recomputes it from the real latent.
MiniMaxH3_TemporalSplitParams.name: MiniMaxH3_TemporalSplitParams
MiniMaxH3_TemporalSplitParams.description: Temporal chunking on H3's native grid (5-frame head + 17-frame cycles). Feeds Split Upscale with legal segment sizes, overlap and triple-anchor settings.

initial_mask.tooltip: The subject on the clip's first frame: H3 Multi-Subject Selector's mask.

job.tooltip: Job name: the folder in output/h3_jobs/<job>/track/.

backend.tooltip: SAM 3 (core): track with core SAM3_VideoTrack (needs 'model'). masks input (precomputed): take the per-frame masks from 'masks' and only run the loss and re-identification checks (validate_backward is off).

review.tooltip: When the job waits for review: go on with candidate '#review_pick', end the track there (the subject has left), or track again (after you connected model + conditioning or changed nothing but want a retry).

review_pick.tooltip: With review = continue with candidate: the '#' number in the preview of the candidate the track is reseeded from.

action.tooltip: restart: start this track again on this run (the old files are kept aside); set it back to run afterwards.

proxy_width.tooltip: Track at this width (the reference uses 960); 0 = the source width.

area_ratio.tooltip: Loss: the mask shrinks under this share of the median of its last 5.

jump.tooltip: Loss: the centre moves more than this share of the width in one frame.

validate_backward.tooltip: Also track each window backwards; frames where the two disagree (IoU under confidence_threshold) count as a loss. Twice the time.

confidence_threshold.tooltip: With validate_backward on: a frame whose forward/backward mask IoU (0-1) is under this counts as a loss.

reid_interval.tooltip: Every N frames compare the tracked person's colours with the memory (0 = off): catches a tracker that moved to someone else. 12 for a new node (2026-11-23, T6); a saved workflow keeps its own value.

drift_similarity.tooltip: On every reid_interval-th frame: a colour similarity (0-1) of the tracked mask to the subject's memory under this counts as a loss.

max_gap.tooltip: Frames the subject may be gone (occluded, off frame: no candidate matches well enough) before the job asks. Those frames get an empty mask.

min_confidence.tooltip: Re-identification below this score stops for review.

margin.tooltip: Re-identification after a loss: stops for review when the second candidate scores within this of the best.

motion_weight.tooltip: Re-identification after a loss: score penalty per proxy-frame width of distance from the last box (score = similarity - this x distance).

search_distance.tooltip: Re-identification after a loss: candidates farther than this fraction of the proxy width from the last box are ignored.

detection_threshold.tooltip: Threshold for core SAM3_Detect when it searches for the subject again after a loss (needs model + conditioning); lower returns more candidates.

max_auto_runs.tooltip: With auto_continue: stop queuing the next window automatically after this many chained runs; queue again by hand to go on.

model.tooltip: The SAM 3 / 3.1 checkpoint's MODEL (core).

media.tooltip: The clip as H3 Media Probe's lazy handle (any length: read a window at a time).

images.tooltip: Or the clip as images (short clips).

conditioning.tooltip: The text 'person:20' (CLIP Text Encode with the SAM 3 checkpoint's CLIP; ':20' lets SAM 3 return up to 20 people - plain 'person' returns only one): needed to find the subject again after a loss.

masks.tooltip: backend = masks input: a finished track of the whole clip (any tracker); losses are still checked.

jump_2d.tooltip: Loss rule: measure the centre jump in 2-D, so two people swapping at a similar x (one above the other, crossing in depth) is caught too. Off: horizontal only (the reference rule).

output_tooltips: This run's window, at the proxy size.
Every tracked frame so far, in source pixels (an empty list where the subject is absent).
The lowest per-frame confidence so far.
JSON list of the last 50 track events (start, lost, absent, reacquired, review, complete), each with its frame.
The subject's memory, updated.
One line: tracking / waiting review / done, frames tracked of the total, the review reason and what to set, and what this run did (e.g. next window queued).
IMAGE batch: this window's frames at the proxy size, the accepted mask tinted, its box and the subject's path; while waiting for review, the candidate gallery instead.
Contract h3.subject_track: the folder, frames, boxes.
When the track is done: the subject's matte at the plate's size, as a lazy handle (H3 Job Controller's matte).
MiniMaxH3_TemporalSubjectTracker.name: MiniMaxH3_TemporalSubjectTracker
MiniMaxH3_TemporalSubjectTracker.description: Tracks one person through a clip of any length with core SAM 3, a window per run, and queues the next run itself. A frame where the mask vanishes, shrinks under area_ratio of its recent size or jumps sideways is a loss: the person is found again by appearance (H3 Subject Re-Identification's rule) and tracking goes on - or, when the match is not clear, the job STOPS for review and shows the candidates (the subject is never changed silently). State and masks are kept in ComfyUI's output folder (h3_jobs/<job>/track/), so a crash or a restart resumes where it stopped. Changing a setting starts a new track; the old one is kept.

positive.tooltip: Positive conditioning, passed through unchanged. This node sits ON the conditioning wire because that is the only way to say 'after the encode, before the sampler' in a dataflow graph.

clip.tooltip: The exact encoder to free. Connect the SAME CLIP output the text-encode nodes used - a different one frees a model nothing was waiting on.

negative.tooltip: Negative conditioning, if you have one. Connect an encoded negative or a Conditioning Zero Out. Whatever is connected must finish before the encoder is freed, which is what wiring it here guarantees. NOTE: H3's own reference pipeline uses BasicGuider and has no negative at all.

output_tooltips: The positive conditioning, unchanged, emitted after the encoder has been freed.
The negative conditioning, unchanged. Leave this output unconnected if you did not connect a negative input.
Text: the device the text encoder (and its clones) was released from, and that the diffusion model, VAEs and ControlNets were not touched.
MiniMaxH3_TextEncoderUnload.name: MiniMaxH3_TextEncoderUnload
MiniMaxH3_TextEncoderUnload.description: Free the text encoder from VRAM after conditioning and before sampling. H3's encoder is Qwen3-VL-32B and is used once, at the start - then it sits in memory for the whole sample. On a card that is tight this is the difference between a clip rendering and an out-of-memory. Only the encoder wired in here is freed: the diffusion model, VAEs and ControlNets are untouched, which a general 'free memory' cannot promise.

clip.tooltip: H3 text encoder that encodes the (optionally wrapped) prompt. No image input is used in text-to-image.

prompt.tooltip: One finished still — not a shot list or storyboard.

width.tooltip: Canvas width in pixels, rounded to the nearest multiple of 32. The empty latent is width/16 wide.

height.tooltip: Canvas height in pixels, rounded to the nearest multiple of 32. The empty latent is height/16 tall.

quality_profile.tooltip: How many frames (1, 5, 9, 13 or 20) H3 denoises jointly for the still. More frames cost more compute; the one-frame profile needs the separate H3 image VAE to decode sharply.

optimize_for_still.tooltip: On: prefixes the prompt with fixed instructions for one finished still (no collage, motion, cuts or audio). Off: the prompt is used as typed. Does not change sampling.

output_tooltips: CONDITIONING with the encoded prompt, for the sampler's positive input.
Empty (all-zero) H3 audio-video LATENT: video width/16 × height/16 × the profile's latent frames, plus decode hints. Wire to the sampler, then to H3 Image Exact Frame Decode.
Frame count of the chosen quality_profile (1, 5, 9, 13 or 20 frames); the decoder keeps this many frames.
The exact text given to the text encoder (wrapped when optimize_for_still is on).
Text summary: canvas, frame profile and packet size, checkpoint advice, and prompt warnings (e.g. motion or camera words).
MiniMaxH3_TextToImagePrepare.name: MiniMaxH3_TextToImagePrepare
MiniMaxH3_TextToImagePrepare.description: FL2VA text-to-image conditioning and empty H3 latent for still generation.

model.tooltip: The MiniMax H3 diffusion model to patch.

method.tooltip: Blend weight per tile. trapezoid: full weight inside, linear ramps over the overlaps (neighbours sum to 1). gaussian: Mixture of Diffusers, each tile dominates its centre. uniform: MultiDiffusion, plain averaging.

tile_width.tooltip: Tile width in pixels, snapped to the 32 px H3 patch grid.

tile_height.tooltip: Tile height in pixels, snapped to the 32 px H3 patch grid.

tile_overlap.tooltip: Smallest overlap between neighbouring tiles in pixels (32 px grid). Keep it at about a quarter of the tile or more, or the tiles drift apart in content.

output_tooltips: The patched model: feed it to an H3 sampler or to H3 Split Upscale.
Text: snapped tile size and minimum overlap (pixels and latent cells), blend method, the kill-switch variable, and whether an existing model function wrapper is wrapped. Also shown on the node.
MiniMaxH3_TiledDiffusion.name: MiniMaxH3_TiledDiffusion
MiniMaxH3_TiledDiffusion.description: Experimental. Patches an H3 model so every denoising step splits the frame into tiles, runs the model once per tile and blends the predictions. All tiles share the same sigmas and noise, so no overlap has to be frozen and no seam repaired. Each tile keeps its global frame positions, so it predicts what the full frame would. Feed the patched model to any H3 sampler, or to H3 Split Upscale with spatial_split_param unconnected. Masks and core's H3 Fun ControlNet are split per tile; the audio is whole in every tile. Costs more time than one full-frame call; it bounds memory to one tile.

trim_end.tooltip: Frame to stop before. 0 = to the end.

reverse.tooltip: Play backwards. The audio flag flips with it.

output_fps.tooltip: Convert to this constant frame rate by nearest frame. 0 = keep the source rate.

offset.tooltip: Global number of the first output frame.

info_json.tooltip: From H3 Media Probe: the ledger covers the whole (trimmed) media.

window_json.tooltip: From H3 Frame Window Reader: the ledger covers the window's rows, handles included.

segments_json.tooltip: A planner's segments (a JSON list), attached and checked.

output_tooltips: Contract h3.frame_ledger v1.
The first and last rows of the map, the operations, and any problem.
Output frames in the ledger after trim, retime and reverse.
MiniMaxH3_TimelineMapper.name: MiniMaxH3_TimelineMapper
MiniMaxH3_TimelineMapper.description: Builds the frame ledger: which source frame every output frame shows, after trim, reverse and frame-rate conversion, numbered from 'offset'. Reverse and retime are described here once and every later stage (images, masks, audio) follows the same map. No pixels are touched.

source.tooltip: The PREVIOUS segment. Its last frames are the anchor the new segment was told to continue from. You can pass the whole segment; only the tail overlap is used.

target.tooltip: The NEW segment, straight out of the sampler. Its first frames are the model's regeneration of the source tail.

mode.tooltip:
frame_shift - per-frame additive shift. The overlap is a REGENERATION, not a pixel-wise transform of the source, so matching the mean is honest and a per-pixel curve is not. Start here.
gain_bias - one affine per channel; extrapolates cleanly when the whole segment is uniformly lifted or crushed.
lut - per-pixel tone curve. Catches nonlinear drift but OVERFITS on regenerated content, because those pixels genuinely differ from the source.

overlap.tooltip: How many frames the two segments share - the KEYFRAME count used when generating, not the segment length. 48 is 2s at 24 fps. Getting this wrong fits the correction over frames that were never meant to match, which is the usual reason this node 'does nothing'.

lut_bins.tooltip: Aggregation bins for lut mode only. More bins follow the curve more closely and overfit sooner.

output_tooltips: The corrected target segment.
Measured drift per channel, and anything that had to be adjusted.
MiniMaxH3_ToneCompensate.name: MiniMaxH3_ToneCompensate
MiniMaxH3_ToneCompensate.description:
Remove the brightness step where two chained H3 segments meet.

H3's denoiser carries a tone bias: a generated segment tends to run darker than the keyframes it was anchored to. Chain segments into a long shot and that bias becomes a visible STEP at every seam - the classic 'my infinite video pulses' complaint.

This measures the bias on the overlap, which is the stretch the new segment regenerated from the previous one, and takes it back out of the whole segment. It reports the drift it measured, so you can tell whether the seam was a tone problem at all before chasing it.

images.tooltip: Source clip (IMAGE batch, one frame per entry). Only RGB is cropped; its size is the src_size stored in the transform for H3 Stitch Back.

crop_factor.tooltip: tv_lp / one_euro_preview: square crop side = larger side of the subject box x this factor (clamped to the frame's short side). follow_camera: margin around the subject. Higher = subject smaller in the crop.

canvas_mode.tooltip: Pixel size the crops are resampled to. manual: canvas_width x canvas_height. auto_no_downscale: a square canvas the size of the largest crop in the clip (rounded up to 32, 128-1344), so no frame is downscaled. auto_capped_768: the same, at most 768x768.

canvas_width.tooltip: manual canvas_mode: crop output width in pixels (step 32, the H3 canvas multiple). follow_camera also uses width/height as the crop aspect.

canvas_height.tooltip: manual canvas_mode: crop output height in pixels (step 32). tv_lp / one_euro_preview plan a square box, so a non-square canvas stretches it.

planner_mode.tooltip: tv_lp: one crop size, a pan-safe centre path. one_euro_preview: causal preview. follow_camera: a virtual camera that keeps the subject large - the crop has the canvas's aspect, its zoom follows the subject smoothly but never cuts it (limbs opening up), crop_factor is the margin around the subject (1.45 = tight).

movement_cost.tooltip: tv_lp: L1 cost per pixel of crop movement between frames, weighed against a 0.001 pull toward the subject centre. Higher = the crop holds still longer and moves in fewer, straighter pans.

lock_size.tooltip: tv_lp / one_euro_preview: on = crop side is the median subject size x crop_factor x safety_margin; off = the median without safety_margin. Either way one size is used for the whole clip.

safety_margin.tooltip: Multiplier on the median crop size when lock_size is on (and on the one_euro_preview anchor size), so frames larger than the median still fit. 1.0 = no extra room. Clamped to the frame's short side.

smooth_detection.tooltip: one_euro_preview: pre-smooth the detected subject centres with a zero-phase One Euro filter (forward + backward pass averaged) before building the boxes. Off = raw detection centres.

one_euro_min_cutoff.tooltip: one_euro_preview: One Euro minimum cutoff frequency (Hz, 24 fps assumed) for the crop centre. Lower = smoother but laggier path.

one_euro_beta.tooltip: one_euro_preview: One Euro speed coefficient. Higher = the cutoff rises with subject speed, so fast moves lag less; 0 = fixed cutoff.

subject_mask.tooltip: Per-frame subject mask. Extents are derived per frame.

bboxes_json.tooltip: Per-frame boxes as JSON: [[x1,y1,x2,y2], null, ...]. Works alone for tests.

min_crop.tooltip: follow_camera: the smallest crop height, as a share of the frame height (0 = no floor). Stops the camera zooming into a far-away subject.

follow_radius.tooltip: follow_camera: frames the camera's path and zoom are smoothed over.

output_tooltips: IMAGE batch, one bilinear sub-pixel RGB crop per input frame, at the canvas size. This is what H3 generates on.
H3_TRANSFORM: per-frame float crop boxes (x, y, w, h in source pixels), canvas and source size, detection flags. Wire unchanged to H3 Stitch Back.
Source frames (RGB, full batch) with each frame's crop box drawn as a 2-pixel green/red outline.
Plain-text summary: planner mode and solver status, detected frames, canvas size, crop size in pixels.
JSON {"src_size":[w,h],"canvas":[w,h],"frames":n,"boxes":[[x,y,w,h],...]}: the crop box per frame in source pixels (also drives the node preview widget).
MiniMaxH3_TrackCrop.name: MiniMaxH3_TrackCrop
MiniMaxH3_TrackCrop.description: Plan a stable per-frame crop path and emit sub-pixel warped crops plus an H3_TRANSFORM spine for stitch-back. This node is a *planner*, not a detector: wire subject_mask and/or bboxes_json from an upstream detection node. Default centre path uses clip-global TV/L1 (piecewise-constant on pans); one_euro_preview is causal preview only.

model.tooltip: MiniMax H3 MODEL. A pruned H3 base (adaln curves) also needs mmx_utils/h3_silu_temb_grid.safetensors, otherwise an error is raised.

lora_name.tooltip: Turbo LoRA file from models/loras. A missing file (or the '<no loras folder>' placeholder) raises an error.

strength.tooltip: LoRA multiplier applied to every patched layer. 1 = as trained; 0 = no effect; negative values subtract the LoRA.

low_vram.tooltip: OFF (default): bypass path — sharpest, more peak VRAM. ON: merge into weights — lowest VRAM, softer on int8/fp8 bases.

output_tooltips: Clone of the model with the Turbo LoRA applied and the step contract (target 4, warn above 8, refuse above 16 steps) stored in transformer_options. Wire through H3 Legal Scheduler's model input.
Text: LoRA file, strength, merge/bypass mode and the stored step contract.
MiniMaxH3_TurboLoRA.name: MiniMaxH3_TurboLoRA
MiniMaxH3_TurboLoRA.description: Apply the MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA. Stashes step contract (4, 8, 16) (target/warn/refuse) on transformer_options for MiniMaxH3_LegalScheduler to enforce — wire model → LegalScheduler (optional model input) → sampler. low_vram=ON merges weights (softer on quantized bases); OFF=bypass (sharper, more VRAM).

output_tooltips: KSAMPLER object running the H3 turbo Euler step (single schedule on ModelSamplingAV builds, separate video/audio clocks on older ones). Wire to SamplerCustomAdvanced sampler.
MiniMaxH3_TurboSampler.name: MiniMaxH3_TurboSampler
MiniMaxH3_TurboSampler.description: 4-step sampler for the MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA. Feed into SamplerCustomAdvanced with BasicScheduler set to 4 steps. Auto-adapts to ComfyUI version: recent builds with ModelSamplingAV use a single-schedule Euler step; older builds step video and audio on separate clocks.

global_image_mode.tooltip: Analysis preset (vision_prompts.json) the LLM gets for every reference image, e.g. Subject / Identity, Lighting & Camera. custom_prompt_override can replace it per image.

global_video_mode.tooltip: Analysis preset for every reference video (up to 4 frames of each are sent), e.g. Motion Focus, Camera Tracking.

provider.tooltip: LLM provider from the Promptor config.json. The images / video frames are sent to it (a cloud provider = network upload). With ollama, ComfyUI first unloads all its models and frees VRAM.

temperature.tooltip: Sampling temperature of the vision LLM calls (0 = most repeatable).

max_tokens.tooltip: Upper limit on the tokens each vision LLM call may return.

seed.tooltip: Not used by the analysis (discarded in execute); changing it only makes ComfyUI run the node again.

ref_images.tooltip: Up to 9 reference images, analysed in order as <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>... (sent to the LLM in batches of the provider's batch_size, default 4).

ref_videos.tooltip: Up to 3 reference videos, each analysed as <Video N> from up to 4 of its frames.

ref_audios.tooltip: Up to 3 reference audios. Not analysed (no audio LLM path): each only adds an <Audio N> entry so the Promptor knows audio is present.

custom_prompt_override.tooltip: Per-item instructions replacing the preset, one 'key: text' per line, e.g. '<Picture 2>: describe the jacket' or 'video 0: ...' (image/video N without '<' counts from 0). Lines without a number are ignored.

output_tooltips: JSON: the analysis per tag (<Picture N>, <Video N>, <Audio N>) plus _media_keys; wire to MiniMax H3 Promptor's vision_context. '{}' when nothing was analysed; '[Analyzer Exception]: ...' on an error.

The connected reference images passed through in input order, as a list (one IMAGE per reference, sizes may differ; a node downstream runs once per image unless it takes lists). A 64x64 black image after an error.
MiniMaxH3_Vision.name: MiniMaxH3_Vision
MiniMaxH3_Vision.description: Multimodal vision analysis for H3 prompt pipelines. Ported from Comfyui-Minimax-H3-Promptor (1038lab, GPL-3.0). No custom JS.

head_chunks.tooltip: Number of head groups to split the attention call into. Kernel-internal transients scale down with this; heads are independent so the result is unchanged.

MiniMaxLowVRAMAttention.name: MiniMaxLowVRAMAttention
MiniMaxLowVRAMAttention.description: Reduces peak VRAM of the MiniMax H3 attention without changing the math. Splits the attention call into head groups so the kernel's internal transients (int8 q/k copies, fp32 accumulator) shrink by the chunk count while the fused qkv buffer is alive, and frees the qkv buffer / normed block input as soon as they're consumed. Output is identical to the unpatched model.

max_duration.tooltip: Maximum duration in seconds; the model can end the song earlier.

MiniMaxMusic3TextEncode.name: MiniMaxMusic3TextEncode
MiniMaxMusic3TextEncode.description: Uses a MiniMax Music3 CLIP model to generate the acoustic conditioning sequence.

prompt.tooltip: With reference images connected, the prompt can be at most 8,000 characters.

size.tooltip: 2K and 4K derive the size from the aspect ratio; custom sets an exact width and height.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: With 'auto', MiniMax picks the ratio from the prompt, or follows the reference image when one is connected. Text-to-image with enhance_prompt off needs a fixed ratio.
With 'auto', MiniMax picks the ratio from the prompt, or follows the reference image when one is connected. Text-to-image with enhance_prompt off needs a fixed ratio.

width.tooltip: Width x height must be 655,360 to 20,000,000 pixels with an aspect ratio of at most 3:1.

height.tooltip: Width x height must be 655,360 to 20,000,000 pixels with an aspect ratio of at most 3:1.

enhance_prompt.tooltip: MiniMax rewrites the prompt into a detailed scene description before generating. Image edits are always enhanced. When off, pick an aspect ratio or a custom size.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

images.tooltip: Optional reference images to edit or combine, referred to in the prompt as @Image1..@Image16 in connection order. Up to 16.

MinimaxH3ImageNode.name: MinimaxH3ImageNode
MinimaxH3ImageNode.description: Generate images from text, or edit and combine up to 16 reference images, with MiniMax H3-Image. Refer to the references in the prompt by their order: @Image1, @Image2, and so on.

latent.tooltip: Input latent (image or video).

model_name.tooltip: Minimax H3 upscale model.

mode.tooltip: How the target size is computed.

Total parameter count summed across all tensors.
SHA256 fingerprint over (size, first 1 MB, last 1 MB) when enabled.
License + lineage information as JSON when present in metadata.
compare_path set: tensors only in A / only in B, shape and dtype mismatches, parameter delta, as JSON. Empty when off.
integrity_report or full_hash on: format check, full SHA-256, structure warnings, suspicious pickle callables and a verdict (ok / warnings / suspicious), as JSON. Empty when off.

torch_compile.tooltip: Most likely required for reasonable memory usage
