images.tooltip: The video, as frames.

audio.tooltip: Its soundtrack.

audio_vae.tooltip: Resampled to this VAE's own rate first, so the audio doesn't have to arrive at it.

audio_mode.tooltip: This is what decides, always. Keep: the original soundtrack survives untouched. Regenerate: all of it is resampled, which is what you get with no audio mask at all. Follow mask: resampled only over the stretch of time a mask is on — audio mask if you connected one, the picture mask otherwise — to the nearest 1/40 s, the rate the sound is masked at.

fps.tooltip: Frame rate of the video going in — MiniMax H3 is 24. It is the only thing needed to know how long the soundtrack should be: the sound is cut or padded to exactly the number of audio frames the model expects for this many pictures. Get it wrong and picture and sound drift apart from each other.

ramp_ticks.tooltip: Follow mask only. Run-up INTO each regenerated stretch, in audio ticks (1/40 s): the last ticks of the ORIGINAL sound before it rise toward the cut, so the model may rework the very end of the real audio to land on the generated one; the first regenerated tick is already fully new. 0 keeps the seam hard. 8 ticks = 200 ms.

ramp_out_ticks.tooltip: Follow mask only. Descent OUT of each regenerated stretch, back into the original sound. Separate from Ramp In because the exit usually wants a hard cut: a descent there lets the model keep 'transitioning' over audio that should simply resume. Leave at 0 unless the return sounds abrupt.

ramp_shape.tooltip: Both ramps. cosine eases in and out; linear is the control; high band spends the whole ramp between 0.85 and 0.995, the narrow range of mask values the model actually distinguishes.

latent_mask.tooltip: What to repaint in the picture. Leave it unconnected and the whole video is generated. Feed the latent_mask output of 😺NKD Mask Ops (with its VAE and model connected) and it lands on the model's own grid instead of being stretched onto it here.

audio_mask.tooltip: Which moments Follow mask follows, instead of the picture mask above: white regenerates the sound of that moment, black keeps it. Only its timing is read, so feed one at frame rate — the picture mask is already coarser than a frame. Does nothing on the other two settings.

NKDAVLatent.name: NKDAVLatent
NKDAVLatent.description: Picture and sound in, one masked AV latent out, for a model that samples both at once (MiniMax H3, LTXV). Replaces the whole chain — VAE Encode, VAE Encode Audio, a Set Latent Noise Mask on each and Concat AV Latent — and says what happens to the soundtrack, which is the part that has no node of its own.

previous.tooltip: The AV latent of the segment to continue — the previous stage's KSampler output, before decoding.

new_latent.tooltip: The empty AV latent of the new segment, from MiniMax H3 Reference To Video. Its length is the length rendered; the overlap eats its first chunks.

overlap_chunks.tooltip: How much of the previous clip the model sees to continue from, in latent chunks. 1 chunk = 5 frames, each extra adds 17 (2 = 22 frames, ~0.9 s — the workflow default). More = smoother continuity, less new footage per stage.

output_tooltips: Masked AV latent, ready for the KSampler.
Pixel frames of overlap. Feed Image Batch Extend With Overlap (side=source, mode=cut) to drop the regenerated head after decoding.
The same overlap in seconds, on the AUDIO latent grid (1/40 s) — feed Trim Audio Duration's start_index. Cutting at the video-frame time instead drifts a few ms per stage.
NKDAVLatentExtend.name: NKDAVLatentExtend
NKDAVLatentExtend.description: Extend a MiniMax H3 clip: the tail of the previous AV latent is planted at the start of the new empty one and masked as 'keep', so the sampler generates a continuation of its motion and sound. Feed the result to the KSampler; after decoding, drop the regenerated overlap with Image Batch Extend With Overlap (overlap_frames) and Trim Audio Duration (trim_seconds).

image.tooltip: Image or video frames.

mask.tooltip: Roto mask, one per frame or one for all. Resized to the image if it differs.

mask_is_subject.tooltip: On: white in the mask is what you keep (SAM, rembg, painted masks). Off: white is what becomes transparent, as Load Image's alpha mask.

black_point.tooltip: Alpha at or below this becomes fully transparent. Raise it to clear the faint haze a roto model leaves around the subject.

white_point.tooltip: Alpha at or above this becomes fully opaque. Lower it to make a subject that came out slightly see-through solid again. Set both to the same value for a hard matte.

expand.tooltip: Grow the matte by this many pixels, or choke it with a negative value to lose a rim of old background.

feather.tooltip: Soften the edge by this many pixels.

smooth_in_time.tooltip: Video only. Average each frame's matte with this many frames either side, to stop the edge from boiling.

decontaminate.tooltip: Rebuild the subject's own colour where the edge is semi-transparent, so the old background doesn't show through as a halo. Opaque pixels are left exactly as they were.

output_tooltips: RGBA cut-out, straight (not premultiplied) alpha. Save Image keeps the transparency.
The matte that was applied, 1 = opaque.
NKDAlphaMatte.name: NKDAlphaMatte
NKDAlphaMatte.description: Turns an image and a roto mask into a transparent cut-out (RGBA), frame by frame for video. Shapes the edge on the GPU and cleans the old background's colour out of the soft parts (hair, motion blur), so it doesn't halo over a new background.

audio_latent.tooltip: The soundtrack, straight off VAE Encode Audio. Comes back with the mask on it, ready for Concat AV Latent.

mask.tooltip: The same mask you give the picture, one per video frame. Only its timing survives: a frame counts as masked if any pixel of it is, and the mask is read as covering the whole clip.

ramp_ticks.tooltip: Run-up INTO each regenerated stretch, in audio ticks (1/40 s). The last ticks of the ORIGINAL sound before it rise toward the cut, so the model may rework the very end of the real audio to land on the generated one; the first regenerated tick is already fully new. 0 keeps the seam hard. 8 ticks = 200 ms.

ramp_out_ticks.tooltip: Descent OUT of each regenerated stretch, back into the original sound. Separate from Ramp In because the exit usually wants a hard cut: a descent there lets the model keep 'transitioning' over audio that should simply resume. Leave at 0 unless the return sounds abrupt.

ramp_shape.tooltip: Both ramps. cosine eases in and out; linear is the control; high band spends the whole ramp between 0.85 and 0.995, the narrow range of mask values the model actually distinguishes.

NKDAudioMask.name: NKDAudioMask
NKDAudioMask.description: Mask the soundtrack in time, so an AV model (MiniMax H3, LTXV) regenerates the sound only while the picture mask is on. Goes straight between VAE Encode Audio and Concat AV Latent, replacing the Solid Mask and Set Latent Noise Mask that usually sit there — or skip the whole chain with 😺NKD AV Latent.

media.tooltip: Connect audio, or a video to work on its sound - the picture is ignored and only the audio track is read, without decoding a single frame. More slots appear as you connect.

fps.tooltip: Frames the timeline is measured in. Sound has no frames of its own, so this is what makes a cut land on the same frame as the picture it will be married to.

start_frame.tooltip: First frame to render. The in point.

frame_count.tooltip: 0 = to the end of the material.

import_mode.tooltip: Where a newly connected source lands. 'append' puts it after the previous one on the same lane, to assemble a sequence - the usual thing for sound. 'stack' gives each source its own lane so they can overlap, which is what a crossfade or a music bed under dialogue needs.

output_tooltips: The SILENT stretches — muted clips and gaps no clip covers — as in,out second pairs (e.g. 0.292,0.833), relative to the rendered range: the exact syntax MVEx Audio Mask To Latent's time_ranges input parses. Mute a clip to mark its sound for regeneration.
NKDAudioTimeline.name: NKDAudioTimeline
NKDAudioTimeline.description: Cut and arrange sound on a multi-track timeline: scrub it, blade it, set a level and drag fades in and out of the joins. Same editor as 😺NKD Timeline with the picture taken away, so a reference cut does not cost a whole video timeline.

mesh.tooltip: The mesh being painted: a MESH from Trellis2, Pixal3D or any mesh builder, a TRIMESH, or a GLB/GLTF. Bake with it at Reset in the viewport's Object panel, since a transform made there stays in the browser.

texture_size.tooltip: Resolution of the repainted texture. Ignored on a mesh with no UVs, which gets vertex colours.

angle_threshold.tooltip: Surface turned further than this from the camera is not painted by that pass. Grazing angles smear.

falloff.tooltip: How sharply the most head-on view wins. Low values average the views into mud; high ones can show the switch between them.

occlusion.tooltip: Skip surface hidden behind the model from that camera. Off is faster and fine on a convex shape.

occlusion_bias.tooltip: Slack in the hidden-surface test, as a fraction of distance. Raise it if surface that should be painted comes out blank.

passes.tooltip: One 😺NKD Projection Pass per view. A slot fed by a muted group is skipped, so Ctrl+M is the per-view switch.

model_3d_info.tooltip: The placement the viewport rendered the model at, straight from the same Load3D. Without it the bake projects onto where the mesh sits untransformed, which is not where the camera saw it.

NKDBakeProjection.name: NKDBakeProjection
NKDBakeProjection.description: Merges every projection pass onto the mesh, all at once, so the result does not depend on the order you painted in. Repaints the UV texture when the mesh has one, and falls back to vertex colours when it does not.

image.tooltip: Image, mask or video.

blur_type.tooltip: Gaussian: smooth falloff. Box: flat average, harder edges. Tent sits between the two. All three blur by the same amount at the same radius, only the shape changes.

radius.tooltip: Blur radius in pixels. Fractions work.

NKDBasicBlur.name: NKDBasicBlur
NKDBasicBlur.description: Plain blur: Gaussian, Tent or Box, by a radius in pixels. Takes an image, a mask or a video and gives back the same type.

camera_from.tooltip: The camera of image 1 — where the shot started. Typically the solved plate camera (😺NKD fSpy Camera), or the camera_info you fed into Preview 3D.

camera_to.tooltip: The camera of image 2 — where you moved to. Typically Preview 3D's camera_info output, after unlocking the camera and orbiting.

template.tooltip: Your prompt. '{camera}' is replaced by the JSON. Leave it out and you get the prompt unchanged; set the template to just {camera} to get the JSON alone.
template.default: Referring to the scene in image 1, restore the perspective of the scene in image 2. Repair the perspective and missing areas. The camera has moved by: {camera}

space.tooltip: Frame for x/y/z. 'camera': the FROM camera's own axes (+X right, +Y up, -Z forward), so the numbers read as 'moved right / up / back'. 'world': raw scene axes. UNVERIFIED against the LoRA — nobody published which one it was trained on. Try both.

scale.tooltip: Multiplies x/y/z. Your scene units are almost certainly not the LoRA's: it was trained on COLMAP poses, which have arbitrary scale. This is the dial for that.

decimals.tooltip: Decimal places. Trailing zeros are dropped, so an unmoved camera always prints the template's exact {"x":0,...} whatever this is set to.

flip_z.tooltip: Negate z. The first thing to try when the repair pushes the scene the wrong way: three.js has -Z forward, OpenCV has +Z forward, and the two disagree on exactly this axis.

flip_rotation.tooltip: Negate pitch/yaw/roll, for when the camera turns the opposite way to what you asked. To reverse the move entirely, swap the two camera cables instead.

output_tooltips: The template with {camera} filled in.
NKDCameraDeltaPrompt.name: NKDCameraDeltaPrompt
NKDCameraDeltaPrompt.description: Writes the move between two cameras as the JSON a 'the camera has moved by: {...}' LoRA expects, substituted into your prompt.

region.tooltip: Managed by the crop editor on the node — no need to edit by hand.

fill.tooltip: How the outpainted area is filled before generation: edge replicates the border pixel, reflect mirrors it, pick a flat colour, or leave it transparent (the image gains an alpha channel).

max_megapixels.tooltip: Resize the result to this many megapixels — up as well as down, so a small crop reaches the target too, not just a big one getting capped. 0 disables.

divisible_by.tooltip: Align the crop rectangle itself to a multiple of 8/16/32/64 (grown, not resized) — the pixel grid models like MiniMax need. Also snaps the final size after a megapixel resize.

mode.tooltip: Crop: the rectangle stays inside the source. Outpaint: it can extend past the edge to grow the canvas.

resize_method.tooltip: Filter used when max_megapixels or divisible_by actually resizes the result. Masks always use bilinear regardless.

output_tooltips: The cropped/outpainted image (or video frames). None if the input was a mask.
Input was image/video: white = outpainted area (generate here). Input was a mask: the cropped/outpainted mask itself.
Connect to 😺NKD Crop / Outpaint Stitch to composite the processed image back. None if the input was a mask.
NKDCrop.name: NKDCrop
NKDCrop.description: Interactive crop on the node itself — drag a rectangle over the connected image, mask or video, or rotate it with the handle above it. Crop mode keeps the rectangle inside the source; Outpaint mode lets it extend past the edge, filling the new area per `fill` and reporting it white in the output mask (generate here), same polarity as NKD Timeline's coverage mask. `divisible_by` aligns the crop itself to a pixel grid (no resample needed) instead of just resizing the result to fit. Connect `crop_data` to 😺NKD Crop / Outpaint Stitch to composite the processed result back.

image.tooltip: The processed crop.

feather.tooltip: Softens the edge of the pasted area, in pixels.

edge_hardness.tooltip: Firms up the blend edge to stop the original background from ghosting through as a halo. 0 = off, 1 = hard edge.

match_colors.tooltip: Pulls the colors of the regenerated area back toward the original image, correcting the slight color and brightness drift models introduce. 0 = off, 1 = full match.

seamless_edges.tooltip: Extra pass that erases any remaining color or lighting seam at the edge. Heavier, and can smear fine texture — use only if a seam is still visible after Match Colors. Requires OpenCV.

output_tooltips: Original image with the crop composited back.
NKDCropStitch.name: NKDCropStitch
NKDCropStitch.description: Composite a processed crop back onto the original image, at 😺NKD Crop / Outpaint's original position and rotation — the manual counterpart to 😺NKD Inpaint Stitch / 😺NKD Face Stitch.

mask.tooltip: Optional — confine the grade to the mask, feathered by its values (soft edges blend in).

output_tooltips: The graded image.
NKDCurves.name: NKDCurves
NKDCurves.description: Brightness, contrast and color balance with tone curves, like Photoshop: an RGB master curve plus one per channel, previewed live as you drag.

guide.tooltip:
The kind of action.
P (punch): sharp single events on an on/off curve - bounces, steps, hits.
F (flow): gradual intensity on a smooth curve - lights, wind, water.
M (motor): something revving, higher as the curve rises - engines, acceleration.
B (blast): a bang on each rise that rings while the curve stays on - explosions, gunshots, thunder.
U (uncanny): a warbling high tone, faster and higher as the curve rises - UFOs, magic, sci-fi effects.
W (words): someone talking where the curve is up, the higher the faster the words come - give it a low until (around 0.2) so it only sets the timing.

shape.tooltip: Custom is the curve you draw in the node. The others repeat a shape over the clip; P and B guides read them as on/off. Ignored when source is connected.

cycles.tooltip: How many times a periodic shape repeats over the clip, so how many events. A full-body action needs about a second per cycle; short events fit twice as many.

phase.tooltip: Slides a periodic shape along the clip, in cycles (0.5 = half a cycle later).

length.tooltip: Clip length in frames. Use the same value as the video latent.

strength.tooltip: How hard the guide pushes. Lower it if the result feels forced.

curve.tooltip: The hand-drawn curve, edited in the node.

preview_width.tooltip: Width of the preview frames. Match the video to stack it underneath.

source.tooltip: Optional: take the curve from here instead. An audio gives its loudness (sync to music or to a recorded sound); video frames give how much the picture moves (copy the timing of another clip).

output_tooltips: Anchor it at frame 0: Add Guide for MiniMax H3, or a slot of NKD MiniMax Guides.
The curve as frames, one per video frame, with a line on the current instant. Stack it under the generated clip to show both in sync.
NKDEventCurveAudio.name: NKDEventCurveAudio
NKDEventCurveAudio.description: Draw when things happen in the video. Pick the kind of action, draw the curve, and anchor the guide at frame 0 of a joint audio+video model (MiniMax H3): whatever the prompt describes happens where the curve is high. The curve can also be a periodic shape, or follow an audio or a video wired to source.

size.tooltip: Side of the square crop, in pixels.

padding.tooltip: How much wider than the face the crop is. 1.0 is the face alone; 1.7 leaves room for hair and chin.

upright.tooltip: Rotate the crop so the head is level. Turn off to keep the original angle and crop axis-aligned.

offset.tooltip: Slides the crop along the face's own axis, as a fraction of its size. Negative moves it up, taking in more forehead.

face_index.tooltip: Which face to use when the picture has more than one, in order of how sure the detector is. 0 is the surest.

mask_region.tooltip: What the mask covers. 'face' is the whole head area, 'face without features' leaves the eyes and mouth out of it, 'skin' also leaves the eyebrows, 'features' is only the eyes, brows and mouth, and 'none' returns an empty mask.

forehead.tooltip: How far above the eyebrows the mask reaches. The landmarks stop at the brow, so this is an estimate: 1.0 lands near the hairline on most faces, lower keeps the mask below it, higher takes in more scalp.

refine_edges.tooltip: Let the picture decide the last few pixels of the outline instead of the polygon, so the edge follows hair and jaw rather than cutting across them. Slower, and it cannot see through anything held in front of the face.

output_tooltips: The square, upright crop.
The face mask, in the crop's coordinates.
Degrees of tilt taken out of the first frame, positive clockwise.
NKDFaceCrop.name: NKDFaceCrop
NKDFaceCrop.description: Find the face, rotate it upright and crop it square at the size your model wants, with a mask drawn from the facial landmarks. Feed the result to 😺NKD Face Stitch to put it back at its original angle.

padding.tooltip: How wide the face search frames the head while it looks. Only affects finding the face, not the mask.

face_index.tooltip: Which face to use when the picture has more than one, in order of how sure the detector is. 0 is the surest.

mask_region.tooltip: What the mask covers. 'face' is the whole head area, 'face without features' leaves the eyes and mouth out of it, 'skin' also leaves the eyebrows, 'features' is only the eyes, brows and mouth, and 'none' returns an empty mask.

forehead.tooltip: How far above the eyebrows the mask reaches. The landmarks stop at the brow, so this is an estimate: 1.0 lands near the hairline on most faces, lower keeps the mask below it, higher takes in more scalp.

refine_edges.tooltip: Let the picture decide the last few pixels of the outline instead of the polygon, so the edge follows hair and jaw rather than cutting across them. Slower, and it cannot see through anything held in front of the face.

feather.tooltip: Softens the mask edge, in pixels.

expand.tooltip: Grows (or shrinks, when negative) the mask before feathering, in pixels.

NKDFaceMask.name: NKDFaceMask
NKDFaceMask.description: A mask of the face, drawn from its landmarks, in the image's own coordinates. No segmentation model and no extra download — the same landmarks 😺NKD Face Rig uses, filled in.

image.tooltip: The portrait to pose. Only the first frame is used.

rig.tooltip: The rig pose, written by the editor. Editing it by hand is allowed but the editor is easier.

crop_factor.tooltip: How much around the face to take in. Larger keeps more hair and shoulders but gives the model less face to work with.

src_ratio.tooltip: How much of the expression already in the photo to keep. Lower it to neutralise a face that is already smiling before posing it.

stitching.tooltip: Blend the posed face back into the original shoulders. Turn it off only to see the raw crop.

face_index.tooltip: Which face to pose when the picture has more than one. Faces are numbered by detector confidence, so Face 1 here can be a different person than Face 1 in 😺NKD Face Crop.

expression.tooltip: An expression from another rig, added on top of this one.

output_tooltips: The feathered paste region, aligned with the output image — feed it to a face detailer to refine exactly what the 512 renderer touched.
NKDFaceRig.name: NKDFaceRig
NKDFaceRig.description: Edit a portrait's expression with draggable controls sitting on the face itself, previewed live. Open the rig from the node's button; the handles hang off the detected landmarks, left and right eyes and brows move independently, and the expression presets are the standard FACS combinations rather than invented ones.

image.tooltip: The processed face crop.

feather.tooltip: Softens the edge of the pasted area, in pixels of the original image.

edge_hardness.tooltip: Firms up the blend edge to stop the original face from ghosting through as a halo. 0 = off, 1 = hard edge.

match_colors.tooltip: Pulls the colors of the new face back toward the original photo. 0 = off, 1 = full match.

seamless_edges.tooltip: Extra pass that erases any remaining color or lighting seam at the edge. Heavier, and can smear fine texture.

NKDFaceStitch.name: NKDFaceStitch
NKDFaceStitch.description: Put the processed face back where it came from, at its original angle and size, blended with the mask from 😺NKD Face Crop.

max_blur.tooltip: How many pixels of blur a pin turned all the way up means. Every pin's strength is a fraction of this.

falloff.tooltip: How tightly each pin holds its own area. Low values blend every pin across the whole frame for a soft gradient; high values keep the change close to the pins, which is what stops a sharp pin on a subject from being dragged blurry by the ones around it.

mask.tooltip: Optional. Where the mask is white the original image is kept, so you can protect a subject from the blur without a second composite node.

NKDFieldBlur.name: NKDFieldBlur
NKDFieldBlur.description: Drop pins on the image and set how much blur each one wants; everywhere in between is interpolated smoothly. One pin blurs the whole frame evenly, two pins give you a gradient — the usual way to fake a shallow depth of field or push a background back without a depth map. Ctrl-drag a pin to widen its reach, so a single sharp pin can hold a whole subject in focus instead of being dragged blurry by the ones around it. Pin strengths are relative; Max Blur sets what a fully-turned-up pin means in pixels.

amount.tooltip: How much grain shows through (Lightroom Amount).

size.tooltip: Grain size — bigger = coarser, chunkier grain.

roughness.tooltip: Irregularity of the grain: blends a fine and a coarse field, like Lightroom.

color.tooltip: 0 = clean monochrome grain. Raise for colored dye-cloud grain.

animate.tooltip: Fresh grain on every frame of the batch — real film shimmer. Off = the same static grain on all frames.

seed.tooltip: Same seed, same grain.

mask.tooltip: Optional — confine the grain to the mask, feathered by its values (soft edges blend in).

output_tooltips: The grained image.
NKDFilmGrain.name: NKDFilmGrain
NKDFilmGrain.description: Lightroom / Camera Raw-style film grain: Amount, Size and Roughness. Monochrome by default; raise Color for dye-cloud color grain. On a video batch each frame gets fresh grain so it shimmers like real emulsion.

images.tooltip: The batch to pick from - normally the 'images' output of NKD Timeline.

frames.tooltip: Indices into the batch, any separator. Negatives count from the end. Repeats are kept.

NKDFreezeFrames.name: NKDFreezeFrames
NKDFreezeFrames.description:
Hold individual frames of a batch as still images, one per socket.

Wire the 'markers' output of NKD Timeline into 'frames' and every frame you marked with M comes out of its own 'frame_N' output, previewed on the node so you can see which is which. The field can also just be typed: '0, 12, 47'. 'images' carries the same frames as one batch.

low_frequency.tooltip: Base image the detail lands on (e.g. the relit result).

mode.tooltip: Must match the Separate that made the HF.

linear.tooltip: Must match the Separate that made the HF.

detail_strength.tooltip: Attenuate (<1) or boost (>1) the transferred detail. 1.0 restores it faithfully.

mask_feather.tooltip: Soften the mask edge before applying.

mask.tooltip: Optional — apply the detail only inside the mask (feathered by its values).

output_tooltips: Base with the detail recombined.
NKDFrequencyCombine.name: NKDFrequencyCombine
NKDFrequencyCombine.description: Merge a high-frequency detail layer onto a low-frequency base. Feed the HF from one image and the LF (or any target) from another to transfer detail. mode / linear must match the Separate that produced the HF.

method.tooltip: How the base is smoothed. Guided keeps edges clean without the halo Gaussian leaves; Rolling Guidance erases texture by size while keeping shapes; Median is for spot blemishes.

radius.tooltip: Detail scale. Larger = coarser base, more goes into the detail layer.

edge_threshold.tooltip: How strongly edges are protected (Guided / Rolling Guidance). Lower = sharper edges kept.

mode.tooltip: How detail is encoded. Divide (ratio) is lighting-invariant — best for transferring detail between differently-lit images.

detail.tooltip: Luminance keeps detail achromatic so a Divide recombine never touches color. RGB carries the chromatic detail too.

linear.tooltip: Process in linear light (correct). Turn off to work in gamma like classic Photoshop.

mask.tooltip: Optional — attenuate the detail layer outside the mask.

output_tooltips: Full detail layer, whole image (intermediate).
Soft base (intermediate — feed Combine).
Detail neutralised outside the mask (feathered by its values). Same as high_frequency when no mask is connected.
NKDFrequencySeparate.name: NKDFrequencySeparate
NKDFrequencySeparate.description: Split an image into a soft base (low frequency) and a fine detail layer (high frequency). Pair with Frequency Combine to transfer texture between images — e.g. restore skin detail onto a relit result.

handles.tooltip: Gradient handles, dragged on the preview above.

blend_mode.tooltip: How the gradient composites over the optional image. 'none' outputs the bare gradient (the image only sets the size).

opacity.tooltip: How much of the composited gradient shows through. Ignored when blend_mode is 'none'.

image.tooltip: Optional — the gradient takes this image's size (width/height are ignored). Composite over it with blend_mode, or leave blend_mode on 'none' to use it as a size reference only.

output_tooltips: The generated gradient.
Luminance of the gradient — use it as a mask.
NKDGradientGenerate.name: NKDGradientGenerate
NKDGradientGenerate.description: Generate a gradient image from a color ramp — linear, radial, angular (conic) or diamond. Drag the handles on the preview to set direction and extent; edit the ramp below.

invert.tooltip: Swap which end of the ramp lands on darks vs. lights.

strength.tooltip: How much of the effect shows through. 0 = original image, 1 = full effect.

mask.tooltip: Optional — confine the recolor to the mask, feathered by its values (soft edges blend in).

output_tooltips: The recolored image.
Luminance of the result — use the grade as a mask.
NKDGradientMap.name: NKDGradientMap
NKDGradientMap.description: Recolor the image by brightness: darks become one end of the ramp, lights the other. Classic duotone / color-grading look, drawn live as you edit the ramp.

curve_data.tooltip: Serialised curve JSON (managed by the curve widget)

mult_min.tooltip: Curve bottom (y=0) multiplies the incoming shift_audio by this

mult_max.tooltip: Curve top (y=1) multiplies the incoming shift_audio by this

debug.tooltip: Log the shift applied at each step to the console

NKDH3AudioShiftCurve.name: NKDH3AudioShiftCurve
NKDH3AudioShiftCurve.description: MiniMax H3 only: rewrite the audio stream's sigma shift on every sampling step from a drawn curve. Low shift = audio resolves early and the video locks onto it; high shift = both streams move together. Left-click to add points · Shift+click to remove · Drag to move.

fill_holes.tooltip: Fill enclosed gaps in the mask so each area becomes a solid shape.

mask_expand.tooltip: Grow the mask outward by this many pixels.

mask_blur.tooltip: Soften the mask edge by this many pixels. The same softness is used when compositing back.

inpaint_blend.tooltip: How sharp the transition is between the regenerated area and the original image. Lower values fade the two together more gently. Only used when model is connected.

padding.tooltip: How much surrounding image to include around the mask, in pixels. More context helps the edit blend with the scene.

resize_mode.tooltip: How the crop's working resolution is chosen. Automatic: keeps the original resolution and only rescales when the crop is too small or too big. Megapixels: fixed budget. Longest Side: exact size.

megapixels.tooltip: Working resolution for the crop, in megapixels (1.0 ≈ 1024×1024). 0 = keep the original resolution untouched.

longest_side.tooltip: Exact size of the crop's longest side, in pixels.

min_resolution.tooltip: If the crop is smaller than this, it is scaled up to reach it.

max_resolution.tooltip: If the crop is larger than this, it is scaled down to fit. Crops in between keep their original resolution.

separate_regions.tooltip: Detail several areas in one go: each separate area of the mask gets its own crop, your sampler runs once per area automatically, and Stitch puts them all back. A batch of masks always gets one crop per mask, with or without this.

region_min_area.tooltip: Ignore areas smaller than this percentage of the image.

max_regions.tooltip: Process at most this many areas.

region_order.tooltip: Order in which the areas are processed.

model.tooltip: Optional. Connect your model and use the model output: the regenerated area will follow the mask softness for a cleaner inpaint, with no extra nodes.

vae.tooltip: Optional. Connect your VAE and the latent output comes out ready to plug straight into the sampler.

output_tooltips: Model prepared for masked inpainting. Requires model.
The cropped region(s), at working resolution.
Mask for each crop.
Ready-to-sample crop(s). Requires vae.
Connect to 😺NKD Inpaint Stitch.
NKDInpaintCrop.name: NKDInpaintCrop
NKDInpaintCrop.description: Crop the image around the mask (plus context padding) and resample the crop to a megapixel budget for sampling. Connect crop_data to 😺NKD Inpaint Stitch to composite back.

image.tooltip: The processed (inpainted) crop(s).

feather.tooltip: Softens the edge of the pasted area, in pixels.

edge_hardness.tooltip: Firms up the blend edge to stop the original background from ghosting through as a halo. 0 = off, 1 = hard edge.

match_colors.tooltip: Pulls the colors of the regenerated area back toward the original image, correcting the slight color and brightness drift models introduce. 0 = off, 1 = full match.

seamless_edges.tooltip: Extra pass that erases any remaining color or lighting seam at the edge. Heavier, and can smear fine texture — use only if a seam is still visible after Match Colors. Requires OpenCV.

output_tooltips: Original image with the detailed region(s) composited back.
NKDInpaintStitch.name: NKDInpaintStitch
NKDInpaintStitch.description: Composite one or more processed crops back onto the original image at its native resolution, feathered by the masks from 😺NKD Inpaint Crop. With separate_regions, all detailed regions are stitched sequentially in one pass.

detections.tooltip: What was found: a MASK (SAM3, a segmenter, or one you painted), BOUNDING_BOX from SAM3 / RT-DETR, or SEGS from an Impact Pack detector (Ultralytics / YOLO). Each object becomes one element. BOUNDING_BOX doesn't say how big the image was, so it must come from the same image Presampling gets; if that one is resized, use the detector's mask instead.

action.tooltip: remove: erase it. keep: hold it in place while the rest changes (also how you name something the prompt talks about). new: desc says what goes there or how to change it ("Change the jacket to blue").

tag.tooltip: The name to use in your prompt: dog gives <dog_1>, <dog_2>… numbered left to right, and carries on across chained nodes. Empty: the detector's label, or obj.

desc.tooltip: What it is, or for new what to do. Empty: the detector's label when it gives one. Run the node to see the tags it made.

boxes.tooltip: Elements from a previous Box Detections node, to chain several.

reference.tooltip: Which reference the detections were made on (ref_0 = 0).

NKDKleinBoxDetections.name: NKDKleinBoxDetections
NKDKleinBoxDetections.description: FLUX.3 Klein only. Connect what a detector found (a mask, SAM3 / RT-DETR boxes, or Ultralytics SEGS) and pick what to do with it: remove it, keep it in place, or change it. Chain one node per detection and wire the last one into Presampling's boxes input.

caption.tooltip: A full scene caption. Tag each element with <id> in the text. For edits, refer to references as <ref_image_0>, <ref_image_1>… counting from 0, the same number as 'from N' below. Any element you don't tag gets a sentence added for it, but your own words work better.

elements.tooltip:
One element per line:
id: desc | [t,l,b,r]   — new element at a box
id from 1: desc | [src] -> [tgt]   — move (from = reference number)
id from 0: desc | [src] -> remove   — remove
id from 0: desc | [src] -> keep   — keep in place
id: desc | -> [tgt]   — no source: add something there, or change what is there (desc: 'Change the jacket to blue')
To only name something the caption talks about, keep it.
Lines starting with # are ignored.

NKDKleinBoxPrompt.name: NKDKleinBoxPrompt
NKDKleinBoxPrompt.description: FLUX.3 Klein only — places, moves or removes things by bounding box. Write your caption, then one line per element; the node appends the layout list FLUX.3 reads. Wire the output into Presampling's positive input. Boxes are [top, left, bottom, right] on a 0–1000 grid and guide placement and scale — they are not a hard mask.

image.tooltip: The image coming out of your sampler chain.

bundle.tooltip: Comes from NKD Klein Presampling. Carries everything this node needs to assemble the final image.

uncrop_feather.tooltip: How softly the regenerated zone blends back into the original image. Higher values give a more gradual transition; lower values keep the edge crisp. Without detailing the fade runs inward from the mask edge, so nothing outside the mask changes.

match_original_colors.tooltip: Pulls the colors and lighting of what the model regenerated back toward the original image, to correct the slight white balance or saturation drift it often adds. With a mask (or Auto-Detect Edit Region) it works on the edited area; without either, on the whole image against ref_0. 0 leaves the colors as the model made them, 1 matches them fully. High values also pull back color changes you asked for (a relight, a new color): keep it low then.

seamless_edges.tooltip: Uses Poisson blending to mathematically erase any remaining color or lighting seam at the edge of the regenerated zone. Turn this on when the boundary is still visible after color matching — usually on dramatic relighting or strong style changes. Heavier than a normal blend and can introduce smearing on textured edges, so leave it off by default.

auto_detect_edit_region.tooltip: When you run an edit without giving a mask, this turns on automatic detection of what actually changed between your input and the generated image, and composites only that region back. Keeps the unchanged parts of the original pixel-perfect across multiple iterative edits, instead of letting the model rewrite the whole canvas every time. Only used when there is an input image but no mask — ignored otherwise.

edge_softness.tooltip: How softly the auto-detected region fades into the original. Expressed as a percentage of the image diagonal, so the same value looks the same at any resolution. Higher values give a wider, gentler transition (good for skin, fabric, hair); lower values keep the edge tight (good for geometric edits). Only used when Auto-Detect Edit Region is on.

region_padding.tooltip: Grows or shrinks the auto-detected region before blending. Positive values expand outward — handy when the detection falls just short of the true edges. Negative values pull the region inward — handy when it bleeds into background that should stay untouched. Expressed as a percentage of the image diagonal. Only used when Auto-Detect Edit Region is on.

fill_inner_gaps.tooltip: Fills small holes inside the auto-detected region. When the edit changed an object's color or texture but not its interior contrast, detection can leave little voids in the middle. Turn this on to seal them so the whole object gets composited cleanly. Only used when Auto-Detect Edit Region is on.

remove_specks.tooltip: Cleans up the little floating scraps the detection leaves scattered around the image — grain and noise that changed just enough to be flagged. Any detected patch smaller than this percentage of the image area gets dropped. Raise it if specks still get through, lower it if a genuinely small edit (an earring, a button) is being erased. 0 turns it off. Only used when Auto-Detect Edit Region is on.

extend_to_borders.tooltip: Extrapolates the auto-detected region into any border void the alignment step leaves behind. Without this, a thin frame of the original can peek through around the edge of the regenerated zone. Leave on unless you see mirrored artifacts at the image border. Only used when Auto-Detect Edit Region is on.

transparent_background.tooltip: Outputs the image with an alpha channel: only the regenerated area stays opaque and everything else becomes transparent — ready to save as a PNG cutout or composite elsewhere. Needs a mask (or Auto-Detect Edit Region) to know what the edited area is; without one the image comes out normal.

output_tooltips: A debug view that exaggerates the difference between the result and the original. Connect it to a Preview Image to spot where things changed and check the edges look clean. Not needed for normal use.
NKDKleinPostsampling.name: NKDKleinPostsampling
NKDKleinPostsampling.description: The other half of the Klein workflow. Pair it with NKD Klein Presampling — connect your sampler's image output here, plus the bundle from the start of the chain, and this node delivers the final image ready to use.

model.tooltip: Your Flux Klein model.

clip.tooltip: The text encoder that goes with the model.

vae.tooltip: The VAE that goes with the model.

model_family.tooltip: Which Klein you connected. This only decides which settings are shown: Klein 2 shows Reference Strength, Klein 3 shows the Draw boxes editor. The node always detects the real model itself when it runs.

positive.tooltip: Describe what you want in the image. To use a reference, say what you want from it and which image it is: "the red apple from the second image" (the first image is ref_0). With Klein 3 boxes, this is the caption: tag elements as <id> and images as <ref_image_0>…; untagged elements get a sentence added.

boxes_json.tooltip: Boxes drawn in the editor (managed by the widget). Klein 3 only.

pin_model.tooltip: Keeps the model in your graphics card so it doesn't reload between runs. Faster, but only turn it on if you have plenty of VRAM.

resize.tooltip: On (default): the node sizes the image for you from Aspect Ratio and Megapixels. Off: the node leaves every image at its own size and works at your input image's native size — use this when you want to handle sizing yourself elsewhere. Turning it off hides Aspect Ratio and Megapixels.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: The shape of the final image. 'As Reference' copies the shape of your input image. 'Custom' lets you type any size you want.

megapixels.tooltip: How big the final image should be, in megapixels. Bigger values mean more detail and sharper results, but also slower generation and more VRAM needed.

custom_width.tooltip: Width in pixels. Only used when Aspect Ratio is set to Custom.

custom_height.tooltip: Height in pixels. Only used when Aspect Ratio is set to Custom.

image_fit.tooltip: How to handle your input image when the chosen canvas has a different shape. Only matters when the canvas shape doesn't match the image. Native: the model rebuilds the canvas around your subject without distorting it (best for changing aspect ratio or upscaling). Center Crop: cuts the image to fit the canvas (no distortion, loses the edges). Outpaint: fits the whole image inside the canvas and lets the model fill in the surrounding space.

outpaint_fill.tooltip: What to put in the empty space around your image when using Outpaint. Gray is neutral and lets the model decide freely. Black or White nudge it toward dark or bright surroundings. Smart fills the space with a soft continuation of the image so the model has a natural starting point. Only used with Outpaint.

slide.tooltip: Shifts the image off-centre. With Outpaint it moves the image within the empty space; with Center Crop it chooses which part of the image is kept. 0.5 stays centred. The direction follows the canvas shape: a taller canvas moves it up (toward 1) or down (toward 0); a wider canvas moves it right (toward 1) or left (toward 0). Used with Outpaint and Center Crop.

bypass_reference.tooltip: Turn off the model's ability to look at your reference image while it works. Leave it off in most cases — turn it on only if you want the model to ignore the reference completely.

reference_strength.tooltip: How tightly the result follows the layout of your reference image. 0 is the default (balanced — good for most edits). Higher values lock the result more strictly to the original layout (useful when things need to line up perfectly with the input). Negative values give the model more creative freedom to reinterpret what it sees.

mask_expand.tooltip: Makes the masked area a bit bigger so the regenerated region blends naturally with its surroundings.

mask_blur.tooltip: Softens the edges of the mask so the transition between the new and old parts of the image looks smoother.

inpaint_blend.tooltip: Controls how sharp the transition is between the regenerated area and the original image. 0.0 gives a clean cut along the mask edge; higher values fade the two together more gently.

use_detailing.tooltip: Zooms into the masked area before regenerating it, so you get more detail in small zones (faces, hands, eyes…) without having to upscale the whole image. Needs both an input image and a mask.

detail_padding.tooltip: How much extra space around the mask the zoom should include. More padding gives the model more context, less padding focuses tighter on the masked area.

upsample_prompt.tooltip: Klein 3. With an upsampler connected, rewrite your prompt into the detailed one Klein works best with. Turn it off to send your prompt as typed without disconnecting anything.

upsample_style.tooltip: Klein 3. Faithful keeps to what you wrote and only adds what the image needs to be drawn. Full is BFL's original upsampler: it plans every detail you left open, adding props, people's looks and scenery.

ref_images.tooltip: Connect your input image to ref_0. More slots will appear automatically if you want to add extra reference images.

img.tooltip: ref_0 is your main image — the one you want to edit or use as a starting point. Extra slots (ref_1, ref_2…) let you give the model more images to draw inspiration from.

mask.tooltip: Paint a mask to tell the model which part of the image to regenerate. White areas get redone, black areas stay the same. Connecting a mask switches the node into inpainting mode.

boxes.tooltip: Klein 3 only. Box elements from Box Detections nodes. They are added to the boxes drawn in the editor and follow the same rules (detailing crop included).

upsampler.tooltip: Optional. Load FLUX.3 Klein's prompt upsampler (or another instruct LLM) with Load CLIP and connect it here: your short prompt is rewritten into the detailed one Klein works best with. It sees every reference and keeps your boxes exactly where you drew them. See the prompt output for the result.

output_tooltips: The mask after expanding and softening — useful if a downstream node needs to know which area was regenerated.
Your input image after the Image Fit / Outpaint preprocessing, at the final canvas size. Handy to feed into other parts of the workflow that need the same prepared image.
The positive prompt exactly as the model reads it: after the upsampler, and with the box list appended.
NKDKleinPresampling.name: NKDKleinPresampling
NKDKleinPresampling.description: All-in-one starting point for a Flux Klein workflow. Connect your model, prompt and reference image, and this node prepares everything the sampler needs. Pair it with NKD Klein Postsampling at the end of the chain — between the two goes your sampler.

user_prompt.tooltip: Your main description — the subject of the image. It is always placed first, because word order matters most to Klein.

format.tooltip: natural: a flowing sentence (recommended for Klein). json: a structured template, handy for automation or other FLUX.2 models — usually flattened to prose before use.

medium.tooltip: The kind of image: photo, painting, render, illustration…

style.tooltip: The overall artistic style or treatment.

lighting.tooltip: How the scene is lit. Lighting has the biggest impact on the look, so it's worth setting.

lens_shot.tooltip: Focal length and how close the shot is framed.

color_grade.tooltip: Overall color treatment or film stock.

extra.tooltip: Any extra detail to append at the end, exactly as typed. Use this for anything the dropdowns don't cover.

output_tooltips: The assembled prompt. Connect to Presampling's positive.
NKDKleinPromptBuilder.name: NKDKleinPromptBuilder
NKDKleinPromptBuilder.description: Builds a prompt for Klein by combining your own text with curated presets that Klein understands. Type your subject, pick from the dropdowns (leave any on '—' to skip it), and the node assembles the final prompt — shown live in the preview box. Wire the output into Presampling's positive input. 'format' switches between flowing prose (best for Klein) and a structured JSON template (for automation). Presets are read from klein_presets.json — edit it and restart ComfyUI to customise them.

reference_index.tooltip: Which reference this node controls. 0 = the main reference (ref_0), 1 = ref_1, … in the order added.

weight.tooltip: Overall strength of this reference. 1.0 = no change, below 1 dilutes (0 = removed), above 1 reinforces (up to 2). A connected curve multiplies this per step.

region_weight.tooltip: (Regional) how strongly the reference shows up INSIDE the zone. 1.0 = normal, up to 4 reinforces. Only used with a mask.

outside_suppression.tooltip: (Regional) how much the reference is held back OUTSIDE the zone. 1.0 = only inside the zone; 0.0 = no restriction. Only used with a mask.

region_hardness.tooltip: (Regional) crispness of the zone edge. 0.0 = soft falloff; 1.0 = hard binary edge (tightest containment). Raise it if the reference bleeds outside the mask. Only used with a mask.

schedule.tooltip: Optional per-step curve in [0,1] (e.g. the FLOAT output of NKD Sigmas Curve) that MULTIPLIES the strength across denoise steps. Leave unconnected for a flat strength.

mask.tooltip: Optional zone to confine the reference to. Connect it to turn on regional control; leave it unconnected for a pure strength node.

latent.tooltip: The canvas latent from Presampling — needed only when a mask is connected, to map it onto the token grid. Chain it from another Reference Control's latent output.

output_tooltips: The latent passed through — chain into the next Reference Control to drive several references.
NKDKleinReferenceControl.name: NKDKleinReferenceControl
NKDKleinReferenceControl.description: EXPERIMENTAL — full control of ONE reference image in a single node. Sets how STRONG it is (with an optional per-step curve) and, if you connect a mask, confines WHERE it applies on the canvas. Leave the mask unconnected to use it purely as a strength control. Chain one per reference; put it on the model line between Presampling and your sampler.

image.tooltip: The reference image to place inside the masked region.

mask.tooltip: The zone to place the reference in. Its bounding box sets the position and size; its resolution sets the canvas size. Use the same mask as the Reference Region node.

fit.tooltip: contain: scale the whole reference to fit inside the zone (keeps its proportions, may leave a neutral border). stretch: fill the zone exactly (may distort).

padding.tooltip: Grow the bounding box by this many pixels before placing.

background.tooltip: What fills the area around the placed reference. Gray is neutral. Mostly irrelevant outside the zone (the Region node suppresses it there), but it shows in any border inside the zone when using 'contain'.

output_tooltips: Canvas-sized image with the reference placed in the zone. Feed into Presampling's reference slot.
NKDKleinReferenceFit.name: NKDKleinReferenceFit
NKDKleinReferenceFit.description: EXPERIMENTAL — scales a reference image to fit a mask's region and places it there on a canvas-sized image. Use it so the WHOLE reference lands inside the zone you mask, instead of only the slice that happens to overlap it. Wire: reference image → this node (with your mask) → the reference slot of Presampling. Use the SAME mask in the Reference Region node.

latent.tooltip: The canvas latent from Presampling — used to map your mask onto the model's token grid. Connect Presampling's latent output here.

mask.tooltip: The zone this reference should fill. White = the reference applies here; black = it's kept out.

reference_index.tooltip: Which reference to confine to the zone. 0 = the main reference (ref_0), 1 = ref_1, … in the order added. Usually a secondary reference (1+).

region_weight.tooltip: How strongly the reference shows up INSIDE the zone. 1.0 = normal, above 1 reinforces (up to 4), below 1 dilutes it even inside the zone. Note: pushing this high can make the reference bleed into neighbouring areas — use region_hardness to tighten the zone instead.

outside_suppression.tooltip: How much the reference is held back OUTSIDE the zone. 1.0 = it appears only inside the zone; 0.0 = no regional restriction (acts everywhere, like a normal reference). In between fades the restriction.

region_hardness.tooltip: Crispness of the zone edge. 0.0 = soft falloff (follows your mask's blur — natural blend, but the reference can halo just outside the zone). 1.0 = hard binary edge (tightest containment; the boundary snaps to the token grid so it may look slightly stepped). Raise this if the reference bleeds into areas you didn't mask.

output_tooltips: The same latent, passed through — chain it into the next Reference Region to drive several regions.
NKDKleinReferenceRegion.name: NKDKleinReferenceRegion
NKDKleinReferenceRegion.description: EXPERIMENTAL — directs ONE reference image to a specific ZONE of the canvas. Paint a mask for the zone, pick which reference it applies to, and that reference's influence is confined to the zone (and optionally strengthened inside it). Works by biasing the attention between the canvas and that reference, so it's independent of resolution. Chain one node per region/reference. Put it on the model line between Presampling and your sampler.

reference_index.tooltip: Which reference this node controls. 0 = the main reference (ref_0), 1 = ref_1, … in the order added.

weight.tooltip: Attention weight for this reference. 1.0 = no change, below 1 dilutes (0 = removed), above 1 reinforces (up to 2). A connected curve multiplies this per step; with no curve it applies flat across all steps.

schedule.tooltip: Optional per-step curve in [0,1] for THIS reference that MULTIPLIES its weight (e.g. the FLOAT output of NKD Sigmas Curve). With weight 2.0, a 1→0.5 curve runs the effective weight from 2.0 to 1.0, a 1→0 curve from 2.0 to 0 (removed). Leave unconnected for flat weight.

NKDKleinReferenceWeight.name: NKDKleinReferenceWeight
NKDKleinReferenceWeight.description: Controls the attention WEIGHT of one reference image, independently of the others — so a secondary reference can assert itself, or an over-dominant one can be diluted. (Distinct from Presampling's Reference Strength, which sets positional anchoring.) Pick the reference by index (0 = ref_0, 1 = ref_1, …), set its weight (1.0 = no change, <1 dilutes, >1 reinforces, up to 2), and optionally a per-step curve that multiplies it. Chain one node per reference you want to control; untouched references keep their default influence. Works by scaling that reference's attention tokens, so it's independent of resolution and reference count.

mode.tooltip: Distort: bend a clean image as a lens would. Undistort: straighten a real plate.

k2.tooltip: Edge correction. Opposite sign to k1 gives moustache distortion.

k3.tooltip: Extreme-corner term. Only matters near fisheye.

p1.tooltip: Tangential: vertical decentring of the lens elements. Keep tiny.

center_x.tooltip: Optical centre offset, fraction of half-width.

center_y.tooltip: Optical centre offset, fraction of half-height.

squeeze.tooltip: Anamorphic factor. 1.0 for spherical lenses, 2.0 for a classic anamorphic.

zoom.tooltip: Covers the empty corners the warp leaves. WHICH WAY depends on Mode: in Undistort raise it above 1, in Distort LOWER it below 1. That is not a quirk — zoom is measured in the rectified image, which is what makes it cancel exactly when lens_data feeds the return trip. Open the editor and switch Frame on to see the gaps you are covering.

ca_red.tooltip: Radial scale of the red channel. 1.0 is off; 1.002 is already a visible edge fringe.

ca_blue.tooltip: Radial scale of the blue channel.

ca_falloff.tooltip: How the fringe ramps out from the centre. 1 is linear; higher keeps the middle of the frame clean and concentrates the colour split in the corners, the way real glass behaves. The corner amount is always CA Red/Blue, whatever the exponent.

vignette_falloff.tooltip: Higher keeps the centre clean and darkens only the corners.

edge_mode.tooltip: What to sample where the warp reaches outside the frame.

composite.tooltip: Distort mode only, and only once lens_data carries a plate. Instead of rebuilding the photo from the straightened image — which cannot return the outer ring straightening threw away — paste just the masked region back onto the untouched original.

feather.tooltip: Soften the edge of the pasted region, in pixels.

edge_hardness.tooltip: Push the feathered edge back towards hard.

diff_threshold.tooltip: Only used when no mask is connected: how much a channel must move to count as edited.

mask.tooltip: Undistort: the mask is straightened with the image, ready for the sampler. Distort with composite on: the region to paste back onto the plate — normally the same inpaint mask, in the straightened frame. Leave unconnected to derive it from what actually changed.

lens_data.tooltip: Connect the lens_data of the node that did the outbound warp. When connected it OVERRIDES every coefficient widget above (CA, vignette and edges stay local).

output_tooltips: Wire into the node that reverses this warp. Carries the plate, so the return trip can composite instead of rebuild.
The mask carried through the same warp — straightened alongside the image, or (after a composite) the region that was pasted back.
NKDLensDistort.name: NKDLensDistort
NKDLensDistort.description: Brown-Conrady lens distortion with chromatic aberration and vignette. Set mode to Undistort to straighten a plate before solving or generating, then feed lens_data into a second copy in Distort mode to put the exact same lens back on the result. Open the editor to trace features that should be straight and solve k1/k2 from them.

NKDLoader.name: NKDLoader
NKDLoader.description: Loads a saved combination of models (diffusion model, text encoders, VAE, upscalers, adapters…). Save presets by selecting loader nodes and choosing "Save as NKD Loader preset" in the canvas menu.

lora_name.tooltip: LoRA file to load and analyse

strength.tooltip: Overall LoRA strength. Multiplies the curve when one is connected.

blocks.tooltip: Per-block rules, written by the panel

curve.tooltip: Strength over sampling steps, as a float list (e.g. the 'floats' output of 😺NKD Sigmas Curve).

NKDLoraControl.name: NKDLoraControl
NKDLoraControl.description: Loads a LoRA with per-block control. Blocks are read from the file, so any architecture works without a preset. Connect a float curve to shape the LoRA strength over sampling steps.

mask.tooltip: Mask or mask batch (one per video frame).

invert.tooltip: Swap masked and unmasked before anything else runs.

black_point.tooltip: Mask values at or below this become empty. Raise it to cut the faint halo a segmentation model leaves around the subject.

white_point.tooltip: Mask values at or above this become fully masked. Set it to the same value as Black Point for a hard threshold with no soft edge left.

despeckle.tooltip: Remove blobs thinner than about twice this many pixels. What survives keeps its exact shape — thin details like fingers or hair are not shaved off.

fill_holes.tooltip: Fill gaps fully enclosed by the mask, so each area becomes a solid shape.

close_gaps.tooltip: Bridge cracks and notches narrower than about twice this many pixels without growing the mask overall.

temporal_expand.tooltip: Video only. Each frame also covers what the mask covered this many frames before and after, so a mask that lags the motion still covers it.

temporal_smooth.tooltip: Video only. Average each frame's mask with this many frames either side to stop the edge from flickering.

expand.tooltip: Grow the mask outward by this many pixels, or shrink it with a negative value.

blockify.tooltip: Snap the mask to a grid of squares this many pixels wide, so it survives the trip into latent space with no bleeding into neighbouring blocks. Connect a VAE and the size comes from it; otherwise set it yourself (8 or 16 for most models). Any value above 0 turns it on.

blockify_threshold.tooltip: How much of a block must be covered for it to turn on fully. 0 keeps each block's average as a gray value instead, for a pixelated look.

feather.tooltip: Soften the edge by this many pixels. Runs last, so nothing hardens it again.

edge_low.tooltip: Where the soft part of a feathered edge starts. Leave 0 and 1 and nothing happens. Some video models only react to a narrow band of mask values, so a feather drawn across the full range behaves like a hard edge; set that band here and the whole feather becomes the transition. Fully black and fully white are left alone, so what the mask protects stays protected.

edge_high.tooltip: The other end of that band.

vae.tooltip: Optional. Connect the VAE you are sampling with and Blockify turns on with that VAE's own grid — including, on a video VAE, the frames it collapses into a single latent. The mask then lands on latent boundaries exactly, with nothing bleeding into the neighbouring blocks.

model.tooltip: Optional, alongside the VAE. A few models (MiniMax H3) read the mask themselves and regenerate a whole token the moment any part of it is covered, so the block that has to stay clean is bigger than one latent. Connect the model and Blockify uses whichever of the two applies — it asks the model rather than assuming, and changes nothing for the models where the latent is the unit.

output_tooltips: With a VAE connected, the same mask already reduced to latent resolution — feed this one to Set Latent Noise Mask. It arrives exactly as built: a mask still in pixels gets resampled on the way in, evenly across the frames, which is not how a video VAE groups them. Same as the mask output when no VAE is connected.
NKDMaskOps.name: NKDMaskOps
NKDMaskOps.description: All the mask preprocessing in one node, on the GPU, over the whole batch at once: levels, speck removal, hole filling, gap closing, expand/contract, blockify and feather, plus temporal expand and smoothing for video. Steps run in a fixed order — clean, stabilize, shape, soften — so a feathered edge is never re-hardened by a later step. Anything left at 0 is skipped.

mask.tooltip: Mask or mask batch (one per video frame).

fill_holes.tooltip: Fill gaps fully enclosed by the mask, so each area becomes a solid shape.

expand.tooltip: Grow the mask outward by this many pixels, or shrink it with a negative value.

feather.tooltip: Soften the edge by this many pixels. Runs last, so nothing hardens it again.

NKDMaskOpsLean.name: NKDMaskOpsLean
NKDMaskOpsLean.description: The three mask tweaks a composite usually needs — fill holes, expand/contract, feather — in one GPU pass over the whole batch. Same engine as 😺NKD Mask Ops, without the rest of the panel; reach for the full node when you need levels, speck removal, gap closing, blockify or the temporal steps.

on_image_change.tooltip:
clear_mask: wipe the painted mask when the input image changes.
keep_mask: keep the painted mask even when the input image changes.

mask_input_mode.tooltip:
How to combine the optional `mask` input with what you have painted:
Use as start: copy the upstream mask into the canvas when nothing is painted yet. After that your edits stick.
Replace: copy the upstream mask into the canvas every time it changes.
Add: painted plus upstream.
Subtract: painted minus upstream.
Intersect: only where both are set.
Add, Subtract and Intersect never touch what you painted: the editor shows the result, Reseed copies the upstream mask into the canvas.
Disconnected: the input is connected but ignored.

mask.tooltip: Optional upstream mask to start from or combine with what you paint.

NKDMaskPainter.name: NKDMaskPainter
NKDMaskPainter.description: Paint a mask straight on the node, over any image the graph made. Brush, eraser and lasso fill. Outputs the image, the mask and its inverse. Instantiate the node multiple times for independent masks.

image.tooltip: Only the first image of a batch is used.

model.tooltip: SAM3 or SAM3.1, from Load Checkpoint.

edges.tooltip: vitmatte: an alpha matte of each object's edge, so hair, fur and soft borders come out soft. sam: SAM's hard edge.

edge_margin.tooltip: How far past SAM's edge the matte may look, as a fraction of the object's size. Raise it for hair and fur, lower it for low-contrast parts.

refine_iterations.tooltip: SAM passes that re-segment each picked object in a crop around it, like SAM3 Detect's option. 0: the mask as previewed.

points_only.tooltip: Place SAM's points yourself instead of picking found objects: click for a positive point, right click for a negative one, + Object starts another object.

detail.tooltip: How many objects Analyze lists. Higher finds smaller parts and odder zones, doubtful ones too, and gives the wheel more sizes to step through; max takes about 1 s. Press Analyze again after changing it.

selection.tooltip: Written by the preview when you click.

output_tooltips: Every pick in one mask, with the cuts applied.
One mask per object or drag, as a batch; Inpaint Crop gives each its own crop.
NKDMaskPicker.name: NKDMaskPicker
NKDMaskPicker.description: Press Analyze, then hover the preview to see what can be masked and click to pick it. Drag across objects to pick them as one entry of separated masks and bboxes. Shift adds, Alt+click or Alt+drag cuts holes in what is marked, the mouse wheel steps to a bigger or smaller object. Click or drag where nothing is listed to make SAM look there. points_only: no automatic objects, place positive and negative points yourself.

width.tooltip: Width of the generated mask (used when no 'mask' is plugged in).

height.tooltip: Height of the generated mask (used when no 'mask' is plugged in).

value.tooltip: Base value of the generated solid mask before scheduling.

mask.tooltip: Optional. If plugged in, this mask is scheduled instead of a generated solid one.

normalize.tooltip: Divide the schedule by its max so the peak maps to 100% (handles sigma magnitudes ≠ 1).

NKDMaskScheduler.name: NKDMaskScheduler
NKDMaskScheduler.description: Generate a mask that follows a schedule of floats (e.g. the 'floats' output of NKD Sigmas Curve). Emits one mask per schedule value, scaled by that value — 1.0 → full mask, 0.0 → empty. Leave 'mask' unplugged to generate a solid width×height mask; plug one in to schedule it instead.

background.tooltip: Image or frames. Sets the output size.

foreground.tooltip: RGBA cut-out, as Alpha Matte makes. An RGB image is treated as fully opaque.

fit.tooltip: What scale 1 means. fit: the whole foreground fits inside the background. fill: it covers the background, overflow cropped. pixels: its own size in pixels.

blend_mode.tooltip: Same modes as core's Create Layered Image.

transform.tooltip: Position, scale and rotation, set by dragging in the node.

invert_alpha.tooltip: Flip the foreground's matte, whether it comes from the alpha input or the foreground itself: what was see-through becomes solid and the other way round.

alpha.tooltip: Optional matte for the foreground, 1 = opaque. Replaces the foreground's own alpha.

output_tooltips: As many frames as the longer input; the shorter one loops. RGBA only if the background was RGBA.
The foreground's matte where it landed on the background, 1 = foreground. For working on the subject alone afterwards.
NKDMerge.name: NKDMerge
NKDMerge.description: Places a transparent cut-out over a background, frame by frame. A still background works under a video cut-out and the other way round. Run once, then drag the cut-out in the node to move, scale and rotate it.

vae.tooltip: Video VAE, for the slots that carry picture.

audio_vae.tooltip: Audio VAE, for the slots that carry sound.

snap_positions.tooltip: Move every guide onto the nearest frame H3 starts a video token on, a multiple of 17. Off-grid guides sit between the video's tokens and that frame flashes like a cut in the wrong place, so leave this on unless you are placing a guide by hand for a reason. The last frame is never moved: off-grid is where fl2va's own closing keyframe lives.

guide.tooltip: Image, frame sequence, video or audio to anchor.

position_1.tooltip: Frame this guide is anchored at. Negative counts from the end, so -1 is the last frame — the anchor that closes a loop on the opening image. H3 only starts a video token every 17 frames (0, 17, 34, 51...), which is where snap positions puts this. Two slots sharing a position (a clip and its sound) become one guide.

until_1.tooltip: How far into sampling this guide is obeyed, as a fraction of the steps. 1 = the whole way. Lower it to let the model follow the guide for the composition and then finish the fine detail on its own. With H3's usual shift of 12, 0.5 lets go around sigma 0.92 and 0.9 around 0.57.
