NKDMiniMaxGuides.name: NKDMiniMaxGuides
NKDMiniMaxGuides.description: Anchor several guides on a MiniMax H3 video from one node: each connected slot takes an image, a frame sequence, a video (picture + its soundtrack) or an audio, and gets its own frame position. latent, vae and audio_vae come back out so the chain carries them downstream instead of being re-cabled from upstream.

frames.tooltip: Batch length. >1 makes an animated sequence.

scale.tooltip: Feature count across the frame — higher = smaller, busier features.

roughness.tooltip: How much each finer octave contributes.

distortion.tooltip: Domain warp — swirls the pattern for an organic look.

evolution.tooltip: Animation speed — evolves the field across frames (the 4D time dimension).

loop.tooltip: Seamless loop: the last frame flows back into the first over `frames`.

mask.tooltip: Optional — confine the noise to the mask, feathered by its values.

output_tooltips: The noise as a grayscale image.
The noise as a mask.
NKDNoise.name: NKDNoise
NKDNoise.description: Procedural fractal noise (fBm) — clouds, fog, smoke, organic textures. Animate it over a frame batch and loop it seamlessly. Outputs an image and a mask; feed it into Gradient Map to tint it.

normals.tooltip: The base normal map (Marigold, DSINE, any tangent-space map).

image.tooltip: The photo the micro-detail is read from.

resolution.tooltip: image: output at the photo's size — the base is upscaled and the detail is read at full resolution, where the pores live. normals: output at the base's size, photo downscaled. Radii are in pixels of this working size.

amount.tooltip: How much detail lands on the base. 0 = base untouched.

blend.tooltip: Reoriented rotates the detail onto the base's surface (correct on slopes). UDN is the cheap sum. Overlay is the per-channel Photoshop blend, for comparison.

fine_radius.tooltip: Size of the finest detail in pixels (pores, stubble). 0 turns the band off.

fine_strength.tooltip: Slope strength of the fine band.

medium_radius.tooltip: Size of the medium detail in pixels (wrinkles, hair locks, fabric). 0 turns the band off.

medium_strength.tooltip: Slope strength of the medium band.

noise_reduction.tooltip: Blur the photo before reading detail, so grain and compression do not become bumps.

flip_detail_y.tooltip: Invert the detail's green channel for a DirectX-style base (+Y down).

mask.tooltip: Optional — confine the detail to the mask, feathered by its values.

output_tooltips: The base with the detail blended in.
The micro-detail normal on its own — preview it to tune the radii.
NKDNormalDetail.name: NKDNormalDetail
NKDNormalDetail.description: Adds micro-detail (pores, stubble, hair) from the photo to any normal map. Model normals get the shape, the photo gets the texture, blended the way normals should be.

width.tooltip: Canvas width when no image is connected.

height.tooltip: Canvas height when no image is connected.

bg_color.tooltip: What the strokes output shows where nothing is painted (and the canvas colour when no image is connected).

controlnet.tooltip: Scribble mode: the brush is always white and strokes is white on black.

image.tooltip: Optional base image. Sets the canvas size and shows behind the strokes.

output_tooltips: The base image untouched, so the graph can continue from it.
Strokes blended over the base.
Strokes alone, straight colour with bg_color where there is nothing (white on black in controlnet mode).
Alpha of the strokes.
1 - mask. This is what Join Image with Alpha wants to make strokes transparent.
NKDPaint.name: NKDPaint
NKDPaint.description: Paint or scribble straight on the node, over an image or a blank canvas. Outputs the untouched image, the painted one, the strokes alone, their exact mask and its inverse.

strength.tooltip: How far a pixel travels, in pixels, where a full-speed stroke passes. Very high values break the smear into visible steps — the sampling is capped, so past a point it ghosts rather than blurs.

spread.tooltip: How far each stroke's influence reaches, as a fraction of the image. Small keeps the blur tight around the strokes; large blends them into one smooth field across the whole frame.

mask.tooltip: Optional. Where the mask is white the original image is kept — the usual way to stop a blurred background from smearing over the subject.

NKDPathBlur.name: NKDPathBlur
NKDPathBlur.description: Draw strokes showing which way things move and the image smears along them — directional motion blur that curves, instead of the one straight angle a normal motion blur gives you. Each stroke has its own speed — and Ctrl-dragging a point gives that point its own on top, so one stroke can accelerate along its length — and the direction between strokes is blended, so a few strokes describe a whole frame. Areas far from every stroke stay sharp. Note there is no occlusion information here: at the ends of a stroke the background will smear over whatever is in front of it, which is what the mask input is for.

image.tooltip: The edited flattened image.

feather.tooltip: Soften the quad edge, in pixels.

edge_hardness.tooltip: Firm the blend edge to stop the original from ghosting through as a halo.

match_colors.tooltip: Pull the edit's colors back toward the original.

transparent_bg.tooltip: Output the warped element on transparency (RGBA) instead of compositing it onto the original — for external compositing. Skips Match Colors / Seamless Edges (they blend against the background).

output_tooltips: Original photo with the edited region warped back, or the element on transparency (RGBA) if Transparent Background is on.
The quad's alpha (feathered), for compositing.
NKDPerspectiveRewarp.name: NKDPerspectiveRewarp
NKDPerspectiveRewarp.description: Composite an edited flattened image back into the original photo at its quad, feathered at the edge. Pair with 😺NKD Perspective Unwarp via warp_data.

aspect_source.tooltip: Auto: estimate from the quad edges. Metric: true aspect from a connected focal length (fSpy). Manual: use the ratio below.

focal_length_mm.tooltip: 35mm-equivalent focal length for Metric mode (defaults to a 35mm lens). Wire this from 😺NKD fSpy Camera's focal output for a real solve. 0 falls back to Auto.

output_tooltips: The flattened, fronto-parallel region.
Connect to 😺NKD Perspective Rewarp.
NKDPerspectiveUnwarp.name: NKDPerspectiveUnwarp
NKDPerspectiveUnwarp.description: Flatten a four-corner perspective region to a fronto-parallel 2D image you can paint or inpaint. Drag the corners on the node, then connect warp_data to 😺NKD Perspective Rewarp to put the edit back.

reference.tooltip: Optional reference image — hold in the viewer to flash it over this preview (A/B). Wins over the global NKD Reference slot.

mask.tooltip: Optional mask — shown as a tinted overlay in the viewer. Wins over the global NKD Reference mask.

filename_prefix.tooltip: Folder for the saved still (tokens: %project% %category% %node% %date:yyyy-MM-dd%). Empty uses the active project's prefix.

filename.tooltip: File name for the saved still. Empty keeps the prefix's own name.

output_tooltips: The input image, untouched.
NKDPopupPreviewNode.name: NKDPopupPreviewNode
NKDPopupPreviewNode.description: Preview an image in a floating window on top of the browser. The window can be moved to a secondary monitor and maximised. Saves the still into the active project's folder, with an optional per-node folder/name override and off/auto versioning. Wire the optional reference/mask inputs to compare against them right here instead of a far-away NKD Reference node.

model_file.tooltip: A 3D model (GLB/GLTF), a MESH straight from a mesh-building node (MoGe, DA3...), a TRIMESH (Hunyuan3D wrapper), a gaussian splat (.ply/.spz/.splat/.ksplat) from an upstream node, or a path under the input or output folder.

scene_depth_invert.tooltip: On if your depth map reads far as white. This node's own depth output, and most disparity maps, read near as white.

scene_depth_near.tooltip: Scene distance the map's nearest value stands for. A depth map has no scale of its own, so these two numbers are what tie it to the 3D scene — tune them until the model sits at the right depth.

scene_depth_far.tooltip: Scene distance the map's farthest value stands for.

scene_depth_space.tooltip: How the map's greys relate to distance. Monocular estimators (Depth Anything, MiDaS...) emit INVERSE depth: grey falls off fast near the camera, slowly far away. The object's exported grey follows the same curve, so its tone matches the scene's at the same distance. Pick linear only for metric z maps.

camera_info.tooltip: Solved camera, e.g. from 😺NKD fSpy Camera.

bg_image.tooltip: Backdrop photo, shown behind the model and composited into the exported image.

mask3d.tooltip: A 3D mask painted in another 😺NKD Preview 3D on the same mesh. This viewport shows it, renders it from its own camera as paint_mask, and lets you keep painting on top of it.

scene_depth.tooltip: Depth of the backdrop photo (Depth Anything, Marigold...). Composited into the depth output as its base layer, so the model reads as sitting in the scene. Never clips the render. Must line up with bg_image.

output_tooltips: The full composite: model over the backdrop.
The model alone, RGBA with straight alpha, for compositing.
The model's silhouette, white — ready to drive an inpaint.
Depth, near white to far black. The model's depth composited over the scene's depth map (when one is connected).
The 3D mask you painted on the model, seen from this camera: white where an inpaint may touch. Pixel-aligned with `image`. Black when nothing is painted.
The same painted mask, whole, for 😺NKD Bake Projection: it then paints only inside it, whichever view the paint came from.
The model this viewport shows, as a 3D file. Chain it into another 😺NKD Preview 3D for a second view, or into 😺NKD Bake Projection.
The placement passed in, unchanged, so a chained viewer or bake sits the model in the same place.

The model's contours, white on black, for a canny or lineart ControlNet: outline, parts covering parts and sharp turns of the surface. Same lines as the camera pins' ghost view; its Detail slider sets how many.
The silhouette of the object slice: the object cut to a band of its OWN depth, not the scene's (Occlude tab). `image` shows it cut too; object and mask stay whole.
NKDPreview3D.name: NKDPreview3D
NKDPreview3D.description: 3D viewport that exports its render. Place a model against a background photo and a solved camera, then feed the resulting image/mask/normal into the rest of the graph.

image.tooltip: The edited view. Same framing as the render that produced camera_info. Resolution may differ, the projection is normalised.

camera_info.tooltip: camera_info from the 😺NKD Preview 3D that rendered this view.

weight.tooltip: Multiplies this pass's say in the merge. 0 mutes it without unwiring.

feather.tooltip: Softens the mask inwards, so the blend never reaches surface you did not paint.

silhouette.tooltip: Where the render has model at all: the `mask` output of the same 😺NKD Preview 3D. Wire it. Without it a surface that projects just off the model, or onto a gap in it, is painted with the backdrop.

silhouette_erode.tooltip: Pulls the silhouette in by this many pixels. Its edge pixels are a blend of model and backdrop, and they sit where the surface is most edge on, which is where a projection is least trustworthy.

mask.tooltip: Where this pass is allowed to paint, normally the same mask you inpainted with. Without one the whole view projects, which overwrites good texels with re-rendered ones.

mask3d.tooltip: The geometry this view may paint: a mask painted on the model in 😺NKD Preview 3D. The 2D mask says where in the picture; this says what receives it, wherever the pixels land. Same mesh as the bake.

mirror.tooltip: Also paint across the model's symmetry plane, in its own space: X mirrors left and right. For a SIDE view, so one pass does both headlights or carries the near side of a head to the far side. Leave a frontal view at none: it already covers both sides.

NKDProjectionPass.name: NKDProjectionPass
NKDProjectionPass.description: Packages one inpainted viewport render and the camera it came from into a single cable, ready to fan into 😺NKD Bake Projection. One of these per view.

text.tooltip: The prompt. {variable_N} marks where each variable lands.

randomize_all.tooltip: When a variable receives a list, pick one random item instead of generating one prompt per item. Shift-click a chip in the text to randomize just that variable.

seed.tooltip: Drives the random picks — same seed, same choices.

saved.tooltip: Managed by the editor: this node's copy of the saved variables it uses.

output_tooltips: The resolved prompt(s). Lists on plain variables produce one prompt per item.
NKDPromptVariables.name: NKDPromptVariables
NKDPromptVariables.description: Prompt box with variables: write your prompt, drop variable chips into it, and each chip is filled by whatever text arrives on its input. Wire a list into a variable and the prompt resolves once per item.

image.tooltip: The image coming out of your sampler chain (after VAE Decode).

uncrop_feather.tooltip: Width in pixels of the soft ring, just outside the masked area, where the result fades into your original image. It hides the seam without touching the regenerated area itself.

match_original_colors.tooltip: Pulls the regenerated area's colors and lighting back toward the original image. 0 leaves them as the model produced them; 1 fully matches them to the original.

seamless_edges.tooltip: Uses Poisson blending to erase any remaining color or lighting seam at the edge of the regenerated zone. Heavier than a normal blend and can smear textured edges. Needs OpenCV.

auto_detect_edit_region.tooltip: When you edit without a mask, detects what actually changed and composites only that region back, keeping the rest of the original pixel-perfect. Only used with an input image and no mask. Needs OpenCV.

edge_softness.tooltip: How softly the detected region fades into the original (% of the image diagonal).

region_padding.tooltip: Grows (positive) or shrinks (negative) the detected region (% of the image diagonal).

fill_inner_gaps.tooltip: Fills small holes inside the detected region.

remove_specks.tooltip: Drops detected patches smaller than this % of the image area. Raise it if specks get through, lower it if a small edit is erased. 0 turns it off.

extend_to_borders.tooltip: Extends the detected region into the border the alignment leaves empty, so no thin frame of the original peeks through.

transparent_background.tooltip: Outputs the image with an alpha channel: only the regenerated area stays opaque. Needs a mask (or Auto-Detect Edit Region).

realign_to_source.tooltip: Qwen edits often come back slightly zoomed or shifted. This measures that drift against your input image and undoes it, so the result lines up with the original again. Best for edits that keep the framing (retouch, relight, style); skip it for edits that are meant to recompose the shot.

alpha.tooltip: Qwen Image 2.1 can generate transparency. Discard (default) outputs a plain RGB image. Keep outputs RGBA with the transparency the model generated, and keeps your input image's own transparency outside the regenerated area.

output_tooltips: Exaggerates where the result differs from the original. Not needed for normal use.
NKDQwenPostsampling.name: NKDQwenPostsampling
NKDQwenPostsampling.description: The other half of the Qwen workflow. Connect your decoded image here plus the bundle from NKD Qwen Presampling, and this node delivers the final image ready to use.

model.tooltip: Your Qwen Image 2.1 model.

clip.tooltip: The text encoder that goes with the model.

vae.tooltip: The VAE that goes with the model.

ref_images.tooltip: Connect your input image to ref_0. More slots appear automatically when you add extra reference images.

img.tooltip: ref_0 is your main image — the one you want to edit or use as a starting point. Extra slots (ref_1, ref_2…) give the model more images to draw from.

positive.tooltip: Describe what you want in the image. Qwen likes long, detailed prompts.

negative.tooltip: Describe what you don't want. Only has an effect with CFG above 1.

resize.tooltip: On (default): the node sizes the image for you from Aspect Ratio and Megapixels. Off: every image stays at its own size and the canvas takes your input image's native size — use this when you handle sizing yourself elsewhere.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: The shape of the final image. 'As Reference' copies the shape of your input image. 'Custom' lets you type any size you want.

megapixels.tooltip: How big the final image should be, in megapixels. Qwen Image 2.1 works best around 2. Bigger means more detail but slower and more VRAM; extra reference images are sized to the same budget.

custom_width.tooltip: Width in pixels. Only used when Aspect Ratio is set to Custom.

custom_height.tooltip: Height in pixels. Only used when Aspect Ratio is set to Custom.

image_fit.tooltip: How to handle your input image when the chosen canvas has a different shape. Native: the model rebuilds the canvas around your subject without distorting it. Center Crop: cuts the image to fit (no distortion, loses the edges). Outpaint: fits the whole image inside the canvas and lets the model fill the surrounding space.

outpaint_fill.tooltip: What to put in the empty space around your image when using Outpaint. Gray is neutral; Black or White nudge toward dark or bright surroundings; Smart fills it with a soft continuation of the image.

slide.tooltip: Shifts the image off-centre. With Outpaint it moves the image within the empty space; with Center Crop it chooses which part is kept. 0.5 stays centred.

bypass_reference.tooltip: Stop the model from looking at your reference images. Leave it off in most cases — turn it on only to run a plain img2img or inpaint.

reference_strength.tooltip: How much the model listens to your reference images overall. 1.0 is the model's own balance. Higher values stick closer to the references (pose, identity, layout); lower values give the prompt more freedom to change things. 0 ignores the images' pixels. For one reference only, use NKD Qwen Reference Control.

pack_references.tooltip: Joins all the extra references (ref_1, ref_2…) side by side into a single image before encoding. Much faster with many references, at the cost of less detail per image. While on, Reference Control index 1 controls the whole pack.

mask_expand.tooltip: Makes the masked area a bit bigger so the new region blends naturally.

mask_blur.tooltip: Softens the edges of the mask for a smoother transition.

inpaint_blend.tooltip: How the soft edge of the mask (Mask Blur) is regenerated. 1.0 rebuilds the edge gradually, from the centre of the mask outwards, for the smoothest transition. 0 treats the edge as a plain partial repaint. Only noticeable with some Mask Blur.

use_detailing.tooltip: Zooms into the masked area before regenerating it, for more detail in small zones (faces, hands, eyes…). Needs an input image and a mask.

detail_padding.tooltip: How much extra space around the mask the zoom includes.

mask.tooltip: Paint a mask to tell the model which part of the image to regenerate. White areas get redone, black areas stay the same.

output_tooltips: The mask after expanding and softening.
Your input image after the Image Fit preprocessing, at the final canvas size.
NKDQwenPresampling.name: NKDQwenPresampling
NKDQwenPresampling.description: All-in-one starting point for a Qwen Image 2.1 workflow. Connect your model, prompt and reference images, and this node prepares everything the sampler needs. Pair it with NKD Qwen Postsampling at the end of the chain — between the two goes your sampler.

reference_index.tooltip: Which reference this node controls. 0 = the main reference (ref_0), 1 = ref_1, … in the order connected.

weight.tooltip: How much the model listens to this reference. 1.0 = no change, below 1 dilutes it (0 = its pixels are ignored), above 1 makes it dominate. A connected curve multiplies this per step.

region_weight.tooltip: (Regional) how strongly the reference shows up INSIDE the zone. 1.0 = normal, up to 4 reinforces.

outside_suppression.tooltip: (Regional) how much the reference is held back OUTSIDE the zone. 1.0 = only inside the zone; 0.0 = no restriction.

region_hardness.tooltip: (Regional) crispness of the zone edge. 0.0 = soft falloff; 1.0 = hard edge. Raise it if the reference bleeds outside the mask.

schedule.tooltip: Optional per-step curve in [0,1] (e.g. the FLOAT output of NKD Sigmas Curve) that MULTIPLIES the strength across denoise steps. Leave unconnected for a flat strength.

mask.tooltip: Optional zone (in canvas coordinates) to confine the reference to. Connect it to turn on regional control; leave it unconnected for a pure strength node.

NKDQwenReferenceControl.name: NKDQwenReferenceControl
NKDQwenReferenceControl.description: Full control of ONE reference image. Sets how STRONG it is (with an optional per-step curve) and, if you connect a mask, confines WHERE it applies on the canvas. Leave the mask unconnected to use it purely as a strength control. Chain one per reference; put it on the model line between Presampling and your sampler.

NKDReferenceImage.name: NKDReferenceImage
NKDReferenceImage.description: Captures the connected IMAGE, MASK or VIDEO as the workflow's active reference. Any NKD Popup Preview node can then press-and-hold to flash a reference image over the current preview, or overlay a reference mask (tinted, adjustable) on top of it; NKD Video Viewer wipes between its own render and a reference video. Image, mask and video are separate slots — wire several Reference nodes to have more than one. Within each slot the last executed node wins.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: The shape of the output. 'As Reference' copies the shape of the connected image. 'Custom' uses Custom Width and Custom Height.

megapixels.tooltip: Target size in megapixels. 1.0 MP ≈ 1024×1024 for a square. Ignored by 'Custom'.

custom_width.tooltip: Width in pixels. Only used when Aspect Ratio is Custom.

custom_height.tooltip: Height in pixels. Only used when Aspect Ratio is Custom.

multiple.tooltip: Round the result to a multiple of this. 16 is safe for every current model, 8 for SD-era ones.

preview.tooltip: Live preview of the output resolution.

image.tooltip: Shape source for 'As Reference'.

NKDResolutionSelector.name: NKDResolutionSelector
NKDResolutionSelector.description: Width and height from an aspect ratio and a megapixel budget. Same ratio list as NKD Klein Presampling, plus 'As Reference' to copy the shape of an image and 'Custom' for your own size.

latent_image.tooltip: Same size you will sample at. A batch > 1 averages several seeds.

scheduler.tooltip: Reference schedule for the calibration pass; also the result at equalize 0

calib_steps.tooltip: Steps of the reference pass. More = finer profile, slower

boundary.tooltip: Sigma where model_low takes over (Wan 2.2: 0.875 T2V, 0.9 I2V). Ignored without model_low

vae.tooltip: Connect to get the reference pass decoded on the image output

model_low.tooltip: Two-expert video models (Wan 2.2): the low-noise model, used below boundary

output_tooltips: Result of the reference pass
Reference pass decoded (needs vae; black without it)
NKDSigmasCalibrate.name: NKDSigmasCalibrate
NKDSigmasCalibrate.description: Runs one long reference pass and measures how much the predicted image changes at every noise level. Feed the profile to Sigmas Equalize; this node stays cached while you tune that one.

curve_data.tooltip: Serialised curve JSON (managed by the curve widget)

steps.tooltip: Number of sigma steps to generate

max_sigma.tooltip: Maximum sigma value — curve top (y=1) maps to this

reference_sigmas.tooltip: Optional reference sigmas to display as a ghost overlay in the curve editor

NKDSigmasCurve.name: NKDSigmasCurve
NKDSigmasCurve.description: Control sigma values interactively with a spline curve. Left-click to add points · Shift+click to remove · Drag to move.

steps.tooltip: Steps of the output schedule

equalize.tooltip: 0 = reference schedule as is · 1 = every step changes the image equally

output_tooltips: Two-expert profiles: first step for model_low (feed SplitSigmas). 0 otherwise
NKDSigmasEqualize.name: NKDSigmasEqualize
NKDSigmasEqualize.description: Spreads the steps over a Sigmas Calibrate profile so each one does a comparable share of the work. Wire its SIGMAS into a custom sampler, or into Sigmas Curve's reference_sigmas to see it and redraw it.

text.tooltip: The text to split.

custom_delimiter.tooltip: Your own separator, used when Delimiter is Custom. \n and \t are understood.

trim_whitespace.tooltip: Remove spaces and line breaks around each piece.

skip_empty.tooltip: Drop pieces that end up empty.

remove_numbering.tooltip: Strip leading markers like '1.', '2)' or '-' from each piece — for numbered lists written by an LLM.

output_tooltips: One item per piece. Downstream nodes run once per item.
How many pieces came out.
NKDStringSplit.name: NKDStringSplit
NKDStringSplit.description: Split one block of text into a list of strings. Downstream nodes run once per item — one prompt per piece, no extra wiring. Handy for lists written by an LLM.

images.tooltip: The video to fix, as frames.

vae.tooltip: The video VAE of the model that will redraw it.

spans.tooltip: Frames to redraw, e.g. '30-52, 90-110'. With nothing marked the video passes through and the sampler does not run.

every.tooltip: A new drawing every how many frames. 1 redraws every frame; 2 is animation on twos, each drawing held two frames, and costs less.

context.tooltip: Frames kept around each stretch, untouched, so the model sees how the motion comes in and goes out and the splice has room to blend.

audio.tooltip: The video's soundtrack, slowed down with it so mouths keep following the voice. Needs the audio vae.

audio_vae.tooltip: For models that generate sound with the picture (MiniMax H3, LTX 2). The soundtrack is kept, not redrawn; with no audio connected it is silence.

prompt.tooltip: The video's prompt. Shot times written as 'At 00:01.200' are moved onto the slowed clock.

output_tooltips: The slowed clip, ready for the sampler: only the marked drawings are redrawn.
The slowed clip as frames, for conditioning nodes that want pictures.
Frames in the slowed clip.
NKDTemporalCrop.name: NKDTemporalCrop
NKDTemporalCrop.description: A detailer in time. Mark the fast moments that come out smeared and they are slowed down so the model can draw every pose crisp. Sample the latent with your usual sampler and bring it back with 😺NKD Temporal Stitch.

images.tooltip: The original video, the same frames the Crop got.

redrawn.tooltip: The decoded output of the sampler. Only computed when something was marked.

NKDTemporalStitch.name: NKDTemporalStitch
NKDTemporalStitch.description: Brings the redrawn moments from 😺NKD Temporal Crop back to real time and puts them over the original video.

media.tooltip: Connect a video, an image sequence, a mask or audio - the same socket takes any of them and the timeline puts it on the right lane. More slots appear as you connect.

import_mode.tooltip: Where a newly connected source is placed. 'stack' gives each one its own track from frame 0, so they layer like any other timeline - the higher track is the one you see. 'append' puts it after the previous one on the same track, to assemble a sequence.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: 'Custom' uses width/height below, which is what this node always did. Any other ratio computes them from the megapixel budget, and the monitor follows immediately - no run needed.

width.tooltip: 0 = take the width of the first clip.

height.tooltip: 0 = take the height of the first clip.

megapixels.tooltip: Pixel budget for the chosen ratio. Ignored when aspect_ratio is 'Custom'.

size_multiple.tooltip: Round the computed size to a multiple of this. Match the model's canvas grid (MiniMax H3 uses 32) or it resizes every frame again on its way in.

fit.tooltip: How a clip is fitted when its aspect ratio does not match the output. The preview shows this live.

fps.tooltip: Timeline frame rate. Sources at a different rate are resampled.

model.tooltip: The model this timeline feeds. Its frame count is snapped to the grid that model requires: Wan, Hunyuan Video, Kandinsky, Cosmos Predict and SCAIL use 4n+1; LTX and Cosmos 1 use 8n+1; Mochi uses 6n+1; MiniMax H3 uses 17n+5.

frame_count.tooltip: 0 = up to the end of the last clip.

clip_audio.tooltip: Include the videos' own audio in the mix.

clip_markers.tooltip: Also emit the first and last frame of every picture clip on the 'markers' output, AHEAD of the hand-placed markers: clip 1 in, clip 1 out, clip 2 in… NKD Freeze Frames then freezes each cut's boundary frames without marking them by hand.

raw_fill.tooltip: What 'raw_images' puts where there is no material. black: as 'images'. hold last frame: repeat the last real frame (the first one, at the head) - use this for guides, a black tail asks the model for black. trim tail: end the batch at the last real frame, gaps in the middle stay black; careful, MiniMax H3's Add Guide trims a guide DOWN to 17n+5, so 20 frames become 5. 'images' and the masks are unaffected.

output_tooltips: The mask lane, and nothing else.
White where there is NO material, i.e. the stretches the editor labels 'generate'. Feed it straight to a temporal inpainting mask. For the gaps PLUS the mask lane, use 'generate'.

Everything the model should generate: the mask lane UNION the gaps. A gap is a region to generate, so it belongs in the conditioning mask - 'mask' alone leaves it black and nothing is generated there. This is the socket for temporal inpainting.

WHITE where the rendered soundtrack is silent: frames covered by a MUTED clip, and frames no clip gives sound to at all — silence is a region to generate, like a picture gap in coverage. One value per frame: feeds the audio mask of 😺NKD AV Latent / 😺NKD Audio Mask directly. For MVEx Audio Mask To Latent use audio_ranges instead.
The same silent stretches as in,out second pairs (e.g. 0.292,0.833), relative to the rendered range — the exact syntax MVEx Audio Mask To Latent's time_ranges input parses.
Length of the output range in seconds.
Comma-separated indices of the freeze-frame markers (press M on a clip), counted INTO the 'images' batch. Feed it to NKD Freeze Frames.

The timeline cut as-is: every clip contributes its picture, including audio-only clips. Gaps with no material follow 'raw_images fill' (black by default; 'hold last frame' for guides). Use as reference for models that need the original video.
NKDTimeline.name: NKDTimeline
NKDTimeline.description: Lay several videos and audio tracks on a multi-track timeline and get fps, frame count and resolution back as connectable sockets, so the material can be coordinated before it enters the graph. Gaps in the timeline are regions to generate: the `coverage` output is WHITE there, ready to use as a temporal inpainting mask.

image.tooltip: The image to draw over. Its size sets the mask size.

expand.tooltip: Grow every shape outward by this many pixels, or shrink it with a negative value. Runs after the shapes are combined.

feather.tooltip: Soften the whole mask edge by this many pixels. Shapes can also carry their own feather in the editor — this one is on top of that, and runs last.

NKDVectorMask.name: NKDVectorMask
NKDVectorMask.description: Draw mask shapes by hand over the image with a pen tool and get a MASK out. Points can be smooth Bezier with handles, or B-spline for the fewest possible points on an organic outline — per shape, and mixable. Double-click a point for a hard corner. Shapes marked Subtract cut holes out of the ones before them, each with its own feather, so a soft cut-out is one shape rather than a second node. Ctrl-drag a point to pull out a feather clone and place it where the edge should have faded to nothing, so one part of the outline blends away while the rest stays crisp. The shapes live in the workflow as control points, so they stay editable and survive a resolution change.

pingpong.tooltip: Play forward then backward, for a seamless loop.

crf.tooltip: Lower is better quality and bigger.

profile.tooltip: Editing codec: big files, no generation loss. 4444 is the one that keeps an alpha channel.

colors.tooltip: Palette size. Below 256 also unlocks transparent delta frames, which is where most of the file size goes.

dither.tooltip: Off compresses a lot better: dithering is noise, and noise does not pack.

max_size.tooltip: Scale the longest side down to this many pixels. 0 keeps the original. The biggest lever on GIF size; 512 is a common sticker.

padding.tooltip: Digits in the frame number: shot.0001.png

filename_prefix.tooltip: Relative to output/. Tokens: %project% and %category% (the active ones, picked in the chip on this node — one click moves every NKD node in the graph), %node% (this node's TITLE — rename the node to SH010_comp and it lands there), %v###% (version, one digit per hash), %res%, %fps%, %frames%, %duration%, %format%, %codec%, %time:HH-mm-ss%, plus ComfyUI's own %date:yyyy-MM-dd% and %Node title.widget%. Tokens work in the folder part too.

versioning.tooltip: Adds _v001 to the name — no need to type %v###% yourself; spell the token out only to place it elsewhere (a folder) or pad it differently. `auto` takes the next unused version in the target folder. Turning this on also drops ComfyUI's _0001_ counter, which would number the same thing twice. Note that a cached graph does not re-run, so it makes no new version — the render would be identical; use `manual` to force one (and it overwrites, like re-rendering a version in Nuke). `project (shared)`: one version per RUN for every saver in the graph — a render and its mask land as v014 together. The number lives in the project chip, where it can also be pinned to re-render a version.

numbering.tooltip: `counter` is ComfyUI's _0001_ suffix. `none` gives a clean name - what you want once the version is carrying the uniqueness.

NotifyPixaroma.name: NotifyPixaroma
NotifyPixaroma.description:
Plays a notification sound when this node is reached during a workflow run. Drop one at the end of a workflow to hear when rendering finishes, or branch one off any node mid-graph to be alerted at a checkpoint. Useful when you are in another browser tab or app while ComfyUI is running.

Sound files are auto-enumerated from assets/sounds/ - drop in a .mp3, .wav, or .ogg there to add more (restart ComfyUI to pick up new files).

Each node is also a checkpoint timer: on every Run it measures how long the workflow took to reach it, shows that time on the node, and keeps a per-node history you can open by right-clicking (Notify time history). Timing is independent of the sound (it still records when the sound is off) and can be switched off per node from the right-click menu.

A small arrow on the clock row folds the node down to just the clock when you want it compact, and folds it back out again (also on the right-click menu as Collapse / Expand).

Each node has its own sound toggle, and a master sound switch covers every Notify node at once - it lives in this node's own settings, opened with the gear button on the node toolbar or by right-clicking the node, and on the right-click menu as Mute all Notify sounds. The Preview button bypasses both toggles, since clicking it is a manual request to hear the sound right now.

NukeMax_CameraGamutConvert.name: NukeMax_CameraGamutConvert
NukeMax_CameraGamutConvert.description: Convert scene-linear RGB between gamuts (ARRI Wide Gamut 3/4, Sony S-Gamut3(.Cine), Panasonic V-Gamut, Canon Cinema Gamut, RED Wide Gamut RGB, DaVinci Wide Gamut, Blackmagic Gen5, ACES AP0/AP1, Rec.709, Rec.2020, P3, AdobeRGB). Curve ONLY — the plate keeps its camera primaries, so follow 'Log to Linear' with a Camera Gamut Convert step. No OCIO needed. HDR-safe: nothing is clipped in either direction.

NukeMax_EXRMetadataReaderPro.name: NukeMax_EXRMetadataReaderPro
NukeMax_EXRMetadataReaderPro.description: Reads an EXR's headers WITHOUT decoding pixels: size, display / data window, channels and their types, compression, parts, bit depth, colour information, timecode - JSON, outputs and a summary.

file.tooltip: An EXR in ComfyUI's input folder. Upload new ones with the node's Upload EXR button (sequences: select all their frames).

pass_1.tooltip: A pass name for output pass_1 (pass_names lists them); empty = that output is not read.

pass_2.tooltip: A pass name for output pass_2 (pass_names lists them); empty = that output is not read.

pass_3.tooltip: A pass name for output pass_3 (pass_names lists them); empty = that output is not read.

pass_4.tooltip: A pass name for output pass_4 (pass_names lists them); empty = that output is not read.

NukeMax_EXRPassReader.name: NukeMax_EXRPassReader
NukeMax_EXRPassReader.description: Loads a multipart / multilayer EXR (or its sequence): the beauty, every pass as one bundle (Shuffle Pass takes any of them), the pass names, and up to four named passes as their own outputs.

path.tooltip: Any frame of the sequence, a ####/%04d pattern, or a single .exr

start_frame.tooltip: -1 = first detected frame

use_oiio_reader.tooltip: When off (default), legacy EXR-only loader. When on, OIIO reads TIFF/PNG/DPX/etc.

ocio_input_colorspace.tooltip: ACES/OCIO: file colorspace on load. Empty = no conversion (legacy).

ocio_output_colorspace.tooltip: ACES/OCIO: working colorspace after load. Empty = no conversion.

single_file.tooltip: Read exactly this one file (no sequence detection), OpenImageIO first then OpenEXR then imageio, RGB out; info_json lists every channel, the compression and the metadata.

NukeMax_EXRSequenceLoad.name: NukeMax_EXRSequenceLoad
NukeMax_EXRSequenceLoad.description: Nuke Read: load an EXR sequence (render.####.exr, %04d, or any frame file of the sequence) or a single EXR. Missing frames can error, insert black, or hold the previous frame.

filename.tooltip: %04d is replaced by the frame number

use_oiio_writer.tooltip: When off (default), legacy OpenEXR writer. When on, OIIO writes multi-format.

passes.tooltip: Optional multi-pass bundle; used only with use_oiio_writer. Each frame gets the image's own frame as its R G B A layer plus the passes: per-frame passes ([frames, H, W, C]) by frame, a single-frame bundle on every frame.

ocio_input_colorspace.tooltip: Working colorspace before write. Empty = no conversion (legacy).

ocio_output_colorspace.tooltip: File colorspace to encode. Empty = no conversion.

colorspace_in_filename.tooltip: Append a short colorspace tag to the output filename (OCIO Write style).

file_path.tooltip: One path instead of output_dir + filename: a single frame is written to exactly this file, a batch as _0001, _0002... OpenImageIO first; writes metadata_json and aov_alpha. Codecs: ZIPS, ZIP, PIZ, DWAA, DWAB, RLE, None.

metadata_json.tooltip: With file_path: a JSON object of EXR attributes to embed, e.g. {"comment": "shot_0010", "camera": "ARRI"}.

aov_alpha.tooltip: With file_path: a MASK written as a named A channel next to RGB.

NukeMax_EXRSequenceSave.name: NukeMax_EXRSequenceSave
NukeMax_EXRSequenceSave.description: Nuke Write: save an IMAGE batch as an EXR sequence (filename %04d → frame numbers) — half/float, all standard compressions.

NukeMax_EdgeDetect.name: NukeMax_EdgeDetect
NukeMax_EdgeDetect.description: Edge detection (Sobel / Prewitt / Laplacian / Roberts) on luma → matte.

grey.tooltip: Bias to mid-grey like a classic emboss.

size.tooltip: Pixels: negative = erode, positive = dilate, 0 = passthrough.

NukeMax_ErodeDilate.name: NukeMax_ErodeDilate
NukeMax_ErodeDilate.description: Morphological erode/dilate. Negative size erodes (shrinks bright/matte regions), positive dilates (grows them).

exposure_mode.tooltip: Unit for the stops knob: f-stops, printer lights, or film density.

preserve_highlights.tooltip: On (default since L9.39): linear float, values above 1 stay. Off: clamp to 0-1 (older workflows keep the value they were saved with).

image.tooltip: Image batch to transform into the frequency domain.

NukeMax_FFTAnalyze.name: NukeMax_FFTAnalyze
NukeMax_FFTAnalyze.description: Compute the centered 2D FFT of an image batch and return its magnitude/phase as an FFT_TENSOR.
output_tooltips: FFT tensor bundle (magnitude, phase, original spatial size).

NukeMax_FFTSynthesize.name: NukeMax_FFTSynthesize
NukeMax_FFTSynthesize.description: Inverse-FFT an FFT_TENSOR back into an image batch.
output_tooltips: Reconstructed image clamped to [0,1].

exemplar.tooltip: Reference texture image whose spectrum is cloned.

seed.tooltip: Random seed driving the synthesized phase.

NukeMax_FFTTextureSynthesis.name: NukeMax_FFTTextureSynthesis
NukeMax_FFTTextureSynthesis.description: Synthesize a same-spectrum texture from an exemplar by cloning its magnitude and randomizing phase.
output_tooltips: Synthesized texture image at the requested resolution.

image.tooltip: Source image batch to warp.

flow.tooltip: Flow field bundle from Compute Optical Flow.

direction.tooltip: Which flow vector to use for the backward warp.

NukeMax_FlowBackwardWarp.name: NukeMax_FlowBackwardWarp
NukeMax_FlowBackwardWarp.description: Backward-warp an image batch using a precomputed flow field in either the forward or backward direction.
output_tooltips: Image batch resampled by the chosen flow direction.

image.tooltip: Source image batch to splat-forward.

flow.tooltip: Flow field bundle from Compute Optical Flow.

NukeMax_FlowForwardWarp.name: NukeMax_FlowForwardWarp
NukeMax_FlowForwardWarp.description: Splat-style forward warp of an image batch using the forward flow; also returns the splat weight as a mask.
output_tooltips: Forward-warped image, normalized by accumulated splat weight.
Per-pixel splat coverage (0=no contribution, 1=full).

flow.tooltip: Flow field bundle from Compute Optical Flow.

NukeMax_FlowOcclusionMask.name: NukeMax_FlowOcclusionMask
NukeMax_FlowOcclusionMask.description: Extract the occlusion mask from a flow bundle, computing it from forward-backward consistency if missing.
output_tooltips: Per-pixel forward-flow occlusion mask (1=occluded/inconsistent).

flow.tooltip: Flow field bundle from Compute Optical Flow.

max_magnitude.tooltip: Pixel magnitude that maps to full saturation in the visualization.

NukeMax_FlowVisualize.name: NukeMax_FlowVisualize
NukeMax_FlowVisualize.description: Render a Middlebury-style HSV color visualization of the forward flow vectors.
output_tooltips: RGB image visualizing flow direction (hue) and magnitude (saturation).

frame.tooltip: 0-based index into the batch. Negative counts back from the end, like Python.

length.tooltip: How many frames to output. 0 = match the input batch.

NukeMax_FrameHold.name: NukeMax_FrameHold
NukeMax_FrameHold.description: Nuke FrameHold: freeze one frame of an image batch and repeat it. Use it to hold a clean plate, a matte painting or a reference frame against a moving sequence.

low.tooltip: Inner radius of the pass band as a fraction of Nyquist.

high.tooltip: Outer radius of the pass band as a fraction of Nyquist.

softness.tooltip: Edge softness of the band-pass transition.

NukeMax_FrequencyMask.name: NukeMax_FrequencyMask
NukeMax_FrequencyMask.description: Apply a soft radial band-pass filter to an FFT_TENSOR, keeping frequencies between low and high.
output_tooltips: Band-pass filtered FFT tensor bundle.

NukeMax_Gamma.name: NukeMax_Gamma
NukeMax_Gamma.description: Apply gamma correction (out = in ^ (1/gamma)); >1 brightens mids.

image.tooltip: A model's [0,1] output, believed to be log-encoded.

log_curve.tooltip: The encoding the model was TRAINED to emit - not one picked for the look. LogC3 carries about 55x linear, LogC4 about 470x, ACEScct about 223x.

assume_encoded.tooltip: Decode even when the check says the input is not in this encoding. The result is an expansion, not a reconstruction - useful for looking at, not for shipping as HDR.

clamp_negative.tooltip: Clamp negative linear values to zero. Turn it OFF only to inspect how far below zero a bad decode goes; an EXR with negative light in it will upset anything downstream.

NukeMax_GeneratedHDRDecode.name: NukeMax_GeneratedHDRDecode
NukeMax_GeneratedHDRDecode.description: Decode a model's [0,1] output as a log encoding to get scene-linear HDR - and check that the claim holds. Every log curve maps linear zero to a positive code value, so an image with pixels below that point is not in that encoding: those pixels decode to negative light. The check is arithmetic, not a guess, and it catches the case that otherwise passes silently - an sRGB-trained model whose output looks like HDR after decoding but has no highlight detail to recover.
output_tooltips: Scene-linear HDR. Values run well above 1.0 - send it to an EXR writer, not to a preview.
Reinhard-tonemapped for looking at. Scene-linear cannot be shown directly, and a plain clamp would hide the highlights this is about.
False when the input is not actually in the chosen encoding.
The largest linear value produced.
What was decoded and whether it meant anything.

size.tooltip: Glow radius in pixels.

NukeMax_Glow.name: NukeMax_Glow
NukeMax_Glow.description: Bloom/Glow: isolate pixels above a brightness threshold, blur them, and add the halo back over the image.

mask.tooltip: Where the grade applies; another size is resized to the image.

white_clamp.tooltip: Clamp results above 1 (off: highlights stay, linear float).

reverse.tooltip: Apply the inverse grade - undoes this grade with the same settings.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the input (0 = untouched).

NukeMax_Grade.name: NukeMax_Grade
NukeMax_Grade.description: Nuke Grade: blackpoint/whitepoint remap to lift/gain, multiply, offset and gamma, exactly as Nuke computes it: A = multiply*(gain-lift)/(whitepoint-blackpoint), B = offset+lift-A*blackpoint, out = (A*in+B)^(1/gamma) (gamma leaves values <= 0 alone). black_clamp (on) / white_clamp (off) as in Nuke; reverse undoes the grade; mix blends with the input. Linear float: no other clamp.

NukeMax_Grid.name: NukeMax_Grid
NukeMax_Grid.description: Generate a grid / graph-paper pattern (line spacing, width, colours).

NukeMax_HDR360Generate.name: NukeMax_HDR360Generate
NukeMax_HDR360Generate.description: Project a source image into an equirectangular HDRI panorama (scene-linear, may exceed 1.0).

NukeMax_HDRExpandDynamicRange.name: NukeMax_HDRExpandDynamicRange
NukeMax_HDRExpandDynamicRange.description: Expand SDR to scene-linear HDR by highlight rolloff (output may exceed 1.0).

NukeMax_HDRExposureBlend.name: NukeMax_HDRExposureBlend
NukeMax_HDRExposureBlend.description: Fuse exposure brackets into scene-linear HDR (output may exceed 1.0).

image.tooltip: Scene-linear float32 [B,H,W,C]; may exceed 1.0.

NukeMax_HDRFloat32ColorCorrect.name: NukeMax_HDRFloat32ColorCorrect
NukeMax_HDRFloat32ColorCorrect.description: Scene-linear grade with lift/gain/exposure; clamp_output off preserves HDR super-whites.

NukeMax_HDRHighlightSynthesis.name: NukeMax_HDRHighlightSynthesis
NukeMax_HDRHighlightSynthesis.description: Expand clipped highlights with procedural grain (scene-linear output may exceed 1.0).

stops_range.tooltip: Width of the stops axis (axis = stops), centred on 18% grey.

axis.tooltip: linear: 0 to the brightest value. stops: log2(value / 0.18), from -stops_range/2 to +stops_range/2 - how film and HDR scopes read exposure.

NukeMax_HDRHistogram.name: NukeMax_HDRHistogram
NukeMax_HDRHistogram.description: HDR histogram and stops stats; input may exceed 1.0. luminance or R/G/B (rgb), on a linear axis or in stops around 18% grey (axis = stops, stops_range wide). A scope: it runs and shows on the node with nothing after it.

normalize.tooltip: Normalize each frame independently when max > 1.0.

source_gamma.tooltip: Decode gamma to linear. 1.0 = already linear.

NukeMax_HDRImageToFloat32.name: NukeMax_HDRImageToFloat32
NukeMax_HDRImageToFloat32.description: Promote images to float32 scene-linear; optional per-frame normalize (HDR values may exceed 1.0).

NukeMax_HDRShadowHighlightRecovery.name: NukeMax_HDRShadowHighlightRecovery
NukeMax_HDRShadowHighlightRecovery.description: Lift shadows and compress super-whites in scene-linear HDR without hard clamp.

image.tooltip: Scene-linear HDR input; may exceed 1.0.

preset.tooltip: A preset overrides every setting below. None (Custom) uses them.

NukeMax_HDRToneMap.name: NukeMax_HDRToneMap
NukeMax_HDRToneMap.description: Map scene-linear HDR to display-referred SDR [0,1] via filmic or Reinhard operators.

mask.tooltip: Input matte to choke.

image.tooltip: Companion image used to estimate hair-frequency energy.

choke.tooltip: Choke amount; positive erodes, negative dilates, 0 is no-op.

hair_window.tooltip: Window size in pixels for the local std-dev hair detector.

NukeMax_HairAwareChoke.name: NukeMax_HairAwareChoke
NukeMax_HairAwareChoke.description: Choke a matte adaptively, applying less choke in high-frequency 'hair' regions and more in smooth regions.
output_tooltips: Hair-aware choked mask.

manifest.tooltip: A writer's manifest (Write EXR Pro / Write / OCIO Write).

otio_timeline.tooltip: OpenTimelineIO JSON; DaVinci Resolve imports it (File > Import > Timeline).

manifest_2.tooltip: A writer's manifest (Write EXR Pro / Write / OCIO Write).

manifest_3.tooltip: A writer's manifest (Write EXR Pro / Write / OCIO Write).

manifest_4.tooltip: A writer's manifest (Write EXR Pro / Write / OCIO Write).

ocio_config.tooltip: From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; else the outputs' own config, else $OCIO / built-in.

NukeMax_Handoff.name: NukeMax_Handoff
NukeMax_Handoff.description: Hands rendered outputs to Nuke and Resolve: re-checks every written file against its manifest, then writes a versioned package - handoff.json (frame range, channels, colour interpretation, OCIO), a Nuke script, an OpenTimelineIO timeline, a contact sheet and the OCIO config.

NukeMax_HistEQ.name: NukeMax_HistEQ
NukeMax_HistEQ.description: Histogram equalisation / CLAHE on luma — boost local contrast (cv2 if available).

target.tooltip: saturation = chroma gain about Rec.709 luma; luminance = overall gain on that hue.

NukeMax_HueCorrect.name: NukeMax_HueCorrect
NukeMax_HueCorrect.description: Nuke HueCorrect: six hue buckets (red/yellow/green/cyan/blue/magenta) each drive a gain on either saturation or luminance. Weights are triangular with 60-degree spacing, so leaving every gain at 1.0 is an exact identity. Hue is measured scale-invariantly, so HDR pixels are bucketed correctly instead of all reading as white.

hue_width.tooltip: Half-width of the fully-keyed band, in degrees.

hue_softness.tooltip: Degrees of falloff outside the band.

min_saturation.tooltip: Below this, a pixel is too grey to have a reliable hue and is excluded.

set_alpha.tooltip: Write the matte into the output image's alpha channel.

NukeMax_HueKeyer.name: NukeMax_HueKeyer
NukeMax_HueKeyer.description: Pull a matte from a hue range with a saturation floor — the fast way to isolate 'everything green' or 'that red jacket' without a screen. Hue and saturation are both measured scale-invariantly, so an HDR pixel at 8.0 keys the same as the identical colour at 0.8.

NukeMax_Invert.name: NukeMax_Invert
NukeMax_Invert.description: Invert RGB (1 - value). Alpha is preserved.

NukeMax_Keyer.name: NukeMax_Keyer
NukeMax_Keyer.description: Luminance/channel keyer: build a matte from a value range with soft edges. Outputs the matte as RGB + alpha.

NukeMax_Keymix.name: NukeMax_Keymix
NukeMax_Keymix.description: Keymix: A where mask=1, B where mask=0 (A*mask + B*(1-mask)).

lut_file.tooltip: A .cube file from ComfyUI/models/luts/ or the input folder.

interpolation.tooltip: Tetrahedral matches Nuke/Resolve and is more accurate on the neutral axis. Trilinear is the cheaper classic.

above_domain.tooltip: extrapolate = continue along the LUT's edge gradient (HDR survives). clamp = Nuke Vectorfield behaviour, crushes highlights. passthrough = out-of-domain pixels keep their input value.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

native_lut_path.tooltip: When set, load .3dl/.csp/.spi* from this path instead of lut_file.

NukeMax_LUTApply.name: NukeMax_LUTApply
NukeMax_LUTApply.description: Apply an Iridas/Adobe .cube LUT (1D or 3D) with tetrahedral or trilinear interpolation. A LUT is only defined over its domain (normally 0-1); rather than silently crushing every highlight to the LUT's white corner, this node lets you extrapolate along the LUT's own edge gradient (default), clamp (Nuke Vectorfield behaviour), or pass out-of-domain pixels through. The fraction of samples that fell outside the domain is always reported in `info`.
output_tooltips: Image with the LUT applied.
LUT title, size, domain, interpolation, and the fraction of samples outside the LUT domain.

noise_latent.tooltip: Source noise latent to be spectrum-corrected.

context_image.tooltip: Reference image whose ring-averaged spectrum is the target.

n_bins.tooltip: Number of radial bins used to estimate the ring spectrum.

NukeMax_LatentFrequencyMatch.name: NukeMax_LatentFrequencyMatch
NukeMax_LatentFrequencyMatch.description: Reshape a noise latent's ring-averaged frequency spectrum to match a context image while preserving phase.
output_tooltips: Latent whose spectrum is matched to the context image.

clamp.tooltip: On: the input is clamped to input black..white (classic Levels). Off: values below black and above white keep going - HDR and negatives survive (L9.80 slice 6).

NukeMax_Levels.name: NukeMax_Levels
NukeMax_Levels.description: Remap input black/white through gamma to output black/white with mix, Nuke ColorLookup-style.

image.tooltip: Source image (sRGB) to extract incoming radiance from.

materials.tooltip: Material set providing albedo and normal for the same image.

probe_height.tooltip: Height of the output equirect probe in pixels.

probe_width.tooltip: Width of the output equirect probe in pixels.

NukeMax_LightProbeEstimator.name: NukeMax_LightProbeEstimator
NukeMax_LightProbeEstimator.description: Estimate an HDR equirectangular light probe by dividing the image by albedo and binning radiance by surface normal.
output_tooltips: Equirectangular HDR light probe bundle.

probe.tooltip: Light probe to write to disk.

filename.tooltip: Output file name; .exr if OpenEXR is available.

NukeMax_LightProbeToEXR.name: NukeMax_LightProbeToEXR
NukeMax_LightProbeToEXR.description: Write a LIGHT_PROBE to a 32-bit float EXR file (or .npy fallback) for use in external DCC apps.
output_tooltips: Filesystem path of the written probe file (forward slashes).

rig_state.tooltip: Optional JSON string describing lights and ambient; overrides the simple sliders.

key_intensity.tooltip: Intensity of the key light when no JSON state is provided.

fill_intensity.tooltip: Intensity of the fill light when no JSON state is provided.

rim_intensity.tooltip: Intensity of the rim/back light when no JSON state is provided.

ambient.tooltip: Greyscale ambient term added to all surfaces.

NukeMax_LightRigBuilder.name: NukeMax_LightRigBuilder
NukeMax_LightRigBuilder.description: Build a LIGHT_RIG from a JSON state or key/fill/rim parameters with a global ambient term.
output_tooltips: Light rig bundle (lights tuple plus ambient color).

NukeMax_Log2Lin.name: NukeMax_Log2Lin
NukeMax_Log2Lin.description: Nuke Log2Lin: Kodak Cineon log <-> linear with black / white code values and film gamma (0.002 density per code value). Defaults 95 / 685 / 0.6 are Cineon; code 1023 is about 13.5 linear. Not clamped.

image.tooltip: Input image to decompose into materials.

albedo_blur_sigma.tooltip: Gaussian sigma in pixels used to estimate albedo as a local mean.

depth_strength.tooltip: Strength of luminance-gradient lift used to fake the normal map.

NukeMax_MaterialDecomposerHeuristic.name: NukeMax_MaterialDecomposerHeuristic
NukeMax_MaterialDecomposerHeuristic.description: Heuristic albedo/normal/depth/roughness decomposition from a single image, using local-mean albedo and luminance gradients.
output_tooltips: Material set bundle (albedo, normal, depth, roughness).

image.tooltip: Input image to decompose.

depth_model.tooltip: Identifier of the depth model to use if available.

normal_model.tooltip: Identifier of the normal model to use if available.

NukeMax_MaterialDecomposerModels.name: NukeMax_MaterialDecomposerModels
NukeMax_MaterialDecomposerModels.description: Model-backed material decomposition (Marigold/StableNormal); falls back to heuristic decomposer if weights are unavailable.
output_tooltips: Material set bundle (albedo, normal, depth, roughness).
Status message describing which backend was used.

kernel.tooltip: Row-major numbers, whitespace or comma separated. 9 values for 3x3, 25 for 5x5.

normalize.tooltip: Divide by the kernel sum so overall brightness is preserved. Ignored when the sum is 0 (edge kernels).

include_alpha.tooltip: Filter the alpha channel too. Off keeps the matte crisp.

NukeMax_Matrix.name: NukeMax_Matrix
NukeMax_Matrix.description: Nuke Matrix: convolve every channel with an arbitrary 3x3 or 5x5 kernel you type in. Sharpen, soften, edge-detect, custom relief — all from one node. Linear float, so kernels with negative lobes keep their negative results instead of being crushed to zero.

mask.tooltip: Input matte to adjust.

gamma.tooltip: Gamma applied to the edge band; <1 darkens, >1 brightens.

contrast.tooltip: Contrast multiplier around 0.5 for the edge band.

edge_lo.tooltip: Lower alpha bound that defines the edge band.

edge_hi.tooltip: Upper alpha bound that defines the edge band.

NukeMax_MatteDensityAdjust.name: NukeMax_MatteDensityAdjust
NukeMax_MatteDensityAdjust.description: Adjust gamma and contrast only on the semi-transparent edge band of a matte; opaque and clear regions are preserved exactly.
output_tooltips: Mask with adjusted edge density.

NukeMax_Median.name: NukeMax_Median
NukeMax_Median.description: Median filter (salt-and-pepper / grain denoise). size = window radius.

mix.tooltip: Blend the merge result back toward B (1 = full merge).

mask.tooltip: Optional matte: the mix is applied only where it is white.

invert_mask.tooltip: Use the inverse of the mask.

NukeMax_Merge.name: NukeMax_Merge
NukeMax_Merge.description: Nuke Merge: A merged with B by the chosen operation (over, under, atop, in, out, mask, stencil, plus, minus, from, multiply, screen, overlay, difference, max, min, average, divide, conjoint / disjoint over, ...). As in Nuke the operation runs on alpha too, the output takes B's format (A is resized to it), and nothing is clamped. 'mix' (times the optional mask) dissolves the result back toward B.

NukeMax_MinMax.name: NukeMax_MinMax
NukeMax_MinMax.description: Morphological min / max / range filter (grow or shrink bright regions).

mode.tooltip: undistort: remove lens warp. distort: re-introduce it (e.g. for re-rendering CG into a distorted plate).

NukeMax_MochaApplyLens.name: NukeMax_MochaApplyLens
NukeMax_MochaApplyLens.description: Apply or remove Mocha-estimated lens distortion to an IMAGE batch (Brown-Conrady model).

source.tooltip: Source plate to warp INTO the tracked region.

out_width.tooltip: Output width. 0 = the track's canvas width (the pins are in its pixels).

out_height.tooltip: Output height. 0 = the track's canvas height.

NukeMax_MochaApplyTracking.name: NukeMax_MochaApplyTracking
NukeMax_MochaApplyTracking.description: Warp the source IMAGE batch onto the tracked plane defined by a MOCHA_TRACK. Useful for screen replacements (corner-pin) or per-frame transform follow.

nk_text.tooltip: Paste a Mocha/Nuke CornerPin2D or Transform/Tracker4 .nk export here.

uploaded_file.tooltip: Filename under ComfyUI/input/mocha/ — set by the Upload .nk button.

NukeMax_MochaImportAuto.name: NukeMax_MochaImportAuto
NukeMax_MochaImportAuto.description: One importer for Mocha/Nuke tracking exports: paste the .nk text OR upload a file. Auto-detects CornerPin2D vs Transform/Tracker4 and returns a MOCHA_TRACK.
output_tooltips: Parsed tracking data.
Which format was detected and parsed.

file_path.tooltip: Absolute path to Mocha corner-pin export (.nk or .txt).

NukeMax_MochaImportCornerPin.name: NukeMax_MochaImportCornerPin
NukeMax_MochaImportCornerPin.description: Load a Mocha Pro corner-pin tracking export (.nk Nuke or ASCII .txt) into a MOCHA_TRACK socket.

nk_text.tooltip: Paste tracking data here — in Mocha use Export → After Effects Corner Pin (or CC Power Pin) → COPY TO CLIPBOARD and paste the whole block (starts with 'Adobe After Effects … Keyframe Data'). .nk CornerPin2D exports and plain 'frame x1 y1 … x4 y4' rows also work.

uploaded_file.tooltip: Filename inside ComfyUI/input/mocha/ — set automatically by the Upload .nk button.

NukeMax_MochaImportCornerPinPaste.name: NukeMax_MochaImportCornerPinPaste
NukeMax_MochaImportCornerPinPaste.description: Paste Mocha's tracking data straight from the clipboard: supports Mocha Pro's 'Copy to Clipboard' After Effects Keyframe Data (Corner Pin AND CC Power Pin), the Nuke .nk CornerPin2D export, and plain ASCII 'frame x1 y1 … x4 y4' rows. AE clipboard blocks carry the true plate size — canvas_width/height are then auto-corrected from the data. Files can also be uploaded via the Upload button.

NukeMax_MochaImportLens.name: NukeMax_MochaImportLens
NukeMax_MochaImportLens.description: Load a Mocha Pro lens calibration export (key/value .txt) into a MOCHA_LENS socket.

file_path.tooltip: Absolute path to a .mocha project file.

NukeMax_MochaImportProject.name: NukeMax_MochaImportProject
NukeMax_MochaImportProject.description: Open a Mocha Pro .mocha project (zipped XML) and extract canvas size, fps, and a layer/shape/track summary. Use the dedicated import nodes for tracking/shape/lens data.

NukeMax_MochaImportShapesAsMask.name: NukeMax_MochaImportShapesAsMask
NukeMax_MochaImportShapesAsMask.description: Load a Mocha Pro Shape Data export (.nk) and rasterize all contained shapes to a per-frame MASK batch.

nk_text.tooltip: Paste the Mocha shape .nk export here. Or click Upload .nk.

uploaded_file.tooltip: Filename inside ComfyUI/input/mocha/ — set by Upload .nk button.

NukeMax_MochaImportShapesAsMaskPaste.name: NukeMax_MochaImportShapesAsMaskPaste
NukeMax_MochaImportShapesAsMaskPaste.description: Mocha shape → MASK. Paste the .nk shape export directly into nk_text, OR press Upload .nk to drop in a file (stored under ComfyUI/input/mocha/). No absolute paths needed.

NukeMax_MochaImportTransform.name: NukeMax_MochaImportTransform
NukeMax_MochaImportTransform.description: Load a Mocha Pro transform tracking export (.nk Transform/Tracker4 or ASCII frame/tx/ty/rot/sx/sy) as MOCHA_TRACK.

NukeMax_MochaImportTransformPaste.name: NukeMax_MochaImportTransformPaste
NukeMax_MochaImportTransformPaste.description: Same as Mocha Import Transform, but accepts the .nk export pasted directly into the text box OR uploaded via the Upload .nk button.

NukeMax_MochaInvertTrack.name: NukeMax_MochaInvertTrack
NukeMax_MochaInvertTrack.description: Invert a MOCHA_TRACK so applying it stabilizes the plate (locks the tracked plane).

angle.tooltip: linear: direction of travel in degrees.

samples.tooltip: More samples = smoother trail, linear cost.

NukeMax_MotionBlur.name: NukeMax_MotionBlur
NukeMax_MotionBlur.description: Motion blur by accumulated resampling: linear (angle + distance in pixels), rotational (degrees about a centre) or zoom (scale about a centre). Samples are averaged in linear float, so a blurred specular keeps its energy instead of being clipped to white.

NukeMax_Multiply.name: NukeMax_Multiply
NukeMax_Multiply.description: Multiply RGB by a constant (per-channel optional). Linear gain.

text.tooltip: Nuke-style .nk text block to parse.

NukeMax_NkScriptParse.name: NukeMax_NkScriptParse
NukeMax_NkScriptParse.description: Parse a Nuke-style text block (.nk syntax) and emit a JSON description of the encoded subgraph.

subgraph_json.tooltip: JSON describing nodes + links to serialise.

NukeMax_NkScriptSerialize.name: NukeMax_NkScriptSerialize
NukeMax_NkScriptSerialize.description: Convert a JSON subgraph description (same shape produced by NkScriptParse) into Nuke-style text.

NukeMax_Noise.name: NukeMax_Noise
NukeMax_Noise.description: Generate uniform/fractal noise (greyscale or RGB), seeded.

mask.tooltip: Mask to blur.

normal.tooltip: Normal map (0..1 RGB) used to gate the bilateral kernel.

normal_threshold.tooltip: Minimum cosine similarity between normals for samples to contribute.

NukeMax_NormalAwareEdgeBlur.name: NukeMax_NormalAwareEdgeBlur
NukeMax_NormalAwareEdgeBlur.description: Cross-bilateral mask blur gated by a normal map; smooths within surfaces while preserving normal discontinuities.
output_tooltips: Mask blurred only across surfaces with similar normals.

grade_info.tooltip: grade_info JSON from OCIO Grade or OCIO Grade Match. Wire it in, or paste it.

NukeMax_OCIOApplyGrade.name: NukeMax_OCIOApplyGrade
NukeMax_OCIOApplyGrade.description: Apply a grade_info JSON string from OCIO Grade or Grade Match to a new image, with optional strength lerp toward identity.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

NukeMax_OCIOCDLTransform.name: NukeMax_OCIOCDLTransform
NukeMax_OCIOCDLTransform.description: ASC CDL grade through OpenColorIO: per-channel slope / offset / power plus saturation, forward or inverse. This is the exchange format grading houses send back as a .cdl/.ccc. Scene-linear safe — no clipping.

image.tooltip: Source image.

list_spaces.tooltip: If true, emit the available colorspaces in info_json and pass image through unchanged.

NukeMax_OCIOColorTransform.name: NukeMax_OCIOColorTransform
NukeMax_OCIOColorTransform.description: Industry-standard OpenColorIO v2 color transform. Drop config folders in ComfyUI/models/ocio_configs/ (or set $OCIO env var). Requires PyOpenColorIO. Float32 scene-linear preserved.
output_tooltips: Transformed IMAGE.
JSON with config path and applied transform.

ocio_config.tooltip: From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; overrides config.

NukeMax_OCIOConfigInfo.name: NukeMax_OCIOConfigInfo
NukeMax_OCIOConfigInfo.description: Introspect an OCIO config: colourspaces, roles, displays, views, looks and named transforms. Every other OCIO node in this pack raises with the exact name it could not find — this node tells you what the valid names are. No image input; it reads the config only.
output_tooltips: Newline-separated colourspace names.
Each display and the views valid for it.
Look names and role -> colourspace bindings.
JSON summary: config path, OCIO version, counts, search paths.

config.tooltip: Built-in ACES, $OCIO or a config in models/ocio_configs/.

config_file.tooltip: A .ocio file path on this server (overrides config; held to the C2C media roots on a server reachable from other machines).

NukeMax_OCIOConfigManager.name: NukeMax_OCIOConfigManager
NukeMax_OCIOConfigManager.description: The active OCIO config for the graph: built-in ACES, $OCIO, models/ocio_configs or a file. Reports source, working space, roles, colour spaces, displays, views, looks, readable LUT formats and missing LUTs; connect ocio_config to any NukeMax OCIO node. An edited config reloads by itself.

view.tooltip: Blank = default view for the display.

list_options.tooltip: Pass image through; emit displays/views in info_json.

ocio_config.tooltip: From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; overrides config.

NukeMax_OCIODisplay.name: NukeMax_OCIODisplay
NukeMax_OCIODisplay.description: Apply the config's display/view pipeline (e.g. sRGB / ACES SDR video) to a scene-referred image and bake it in — mirrors Nuke's OCIODisplay. Set list_options to see the available displays and views.

file.tooltip: A LUT/CDL/CLF file from ComfyUI/models/luts/ or the input folder.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

NukeMax_OCIOFileTransform.name: NukeMax_OCIOFileTransform
NukeMax_OCIOFileTransform.description: Apply a LUT or grade file through OpenColorIO: .cube, .3dl, .spi1d, .spi3d, .csp, .ccc, .cdl, .clf, .ctf and more. Forward or inverse (inverse needs an invertible file — OCIO will say so if it is not). Use the LUT Apply node instead when you want explicit control over out-of-domain HDR behaviour.

lift_g.tooltip: Shadow lift: raises the black point without moving white. 0 = no-op.

lift_b.tooltip: Shadow lift: raises the black point without moving white. 0 = no-op.

gamma_r.tooltip: Gamma (sign-preserving power, exponent 1/gamma). 1 = no-op; >1 brightens midtones.

gamma_g.tooltip: Gamma (sign-preserving power, exponent 1/gamma). 1 = no-op; >1 brightens midtones.

gamma_b.tooltip: Gamma (sign-preserving power, exponent 1/gamma). 1 = no-op; >1 brightens midtones.

offset_r.tooltip: Offset: adds a constant to the channel. 0 = no-op.

offset_g.tooltip: Offset: adds a constant to the channel. 0 = no-op.

offset_b.tooltip: Offset: adds a constant to the channel. 0 = no-op.

pivot.tooltip: Contrast pivot point. Default 0.18 = scene-linear mid-gray (18% reflectance).

saturation.tooltip: Saturation, luminance-preserving (Rec.709 luma weights). 1 = no-op, 0 = grayscale.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

clamp_output.tooltip: Clamp the graded RGB to 0..1. Default off: values above 1.0 or below 0.0 (scene-linear HDR, out-of-gamut) pass through unclipped.

NukeMax_OCIOGrade.name: NukeMax_OCIOGrade
NukeMax_OCIOGrade.description: Lift/gamma/gain/offset grade with contrast-about-pivot and luminance-preserving saturation; emits grade_info JSON for stamping the same correction elsewhere.
output_tooltips: Image with the lift/gamma/gain/offset grade applied.
JSON grade_info describing this grade - wire into OCIO Apply Grade to stamp the same grade elsewhere.

match_strength.tooltip: How much of the computed correction to apply: 1.0 = full match, 0.0 = no correction.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

clamp_output.tooltip: Clamp the graded RGB to 0..1. Default off: values above 1.0 or below 0.0 (scene-linear HDR, out-of-gamut) pass through unclipped.

NukeMax_OCIOGradeMatch.name: NukeMax_OCIOGradeMatch
NukeMax_OCIOGradeMatch.description: Shot-to-shot color match via Reinhard-style CIE Lab mean/std transfer, expressed as grade_info gain/offset for stamping across a sequence.
output_tooltips: Image color-matched toward the reference.
JSON grade_info for the computed correction - wire into OCIO Apply Grade to stamp the same match elsewhere.
Human-readable note on the match (Lab mean/std moved, per channel).

ocio_config.tooltip: From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; overrides config.

NukeMax_OCIOLogConvert.name: NukeMax_OCIOLogConvert
NukeMax_OCIOLogConvert.description: Convert between the config's scene_linear and compositing_log roles (ACES: ACEScg ↔ ACEScct) — mirrors Nuke's OCIOLogConvert.

look.tooltip: Look name from the config. Blank = no look (a plain colourspace conversion). Run 'OCIO Config Info' to list the looks this config defines.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

ocio_config.tooltip: From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; overrides config.

NukeMax_OCIOLookTransform.name: NukeMax_OCIOLookTransform
NukeMax_OCIOLookTransform.description: Apply a creative look defined by the OCIO config (e.g. 'ACES 1.3 Reference Gamut Compression'), converting from an input to an output colourspace. Forward or inverse. Raises if the look, or either colourspace, is not in the config.

file.tooltip: A still, a frame of a sequence or a video in the input folder (Upload media adds files; several frames at once = a sequence).

mode.tooltip: auto: a numbered frame reads its whole sequence, a video its frames; single frame: only that file.

frame_range.tooltip: e.g. 1001-1100 or 1001-1100x2 (frame numbers; a video counts from 0, as Load Video (C2C) does). Empty = everything.

missing_frames.tooltip: A gap in the sequence: refuse, black, hold the last frame, the nearest frame, or skip it.

outside_range.tooltip: A range that reaches past the first / last frame.

frame_shift.tooltip: Added to every frame number in frame_numbers and the metadata (a slip, as in Nuke).

layer.tooltip: EXR: the layer for the image (pass_names / passes give the others).

sequence_fps.tooltip: A sequence's rate; 0 = the file's own (EXR / DPX) or 24.

ocio_config.tooltip: From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; empty = $OCIO, else the built-in ACES studio config.

source_space.tooltip: Empty = the file's header, else the config's file rules.

NukeMax_OCIORead.name: NukeMax_OCIORead
NukeMax_OCIORead.description: Reads stills, sequences and video into the OCIO working space: the source space from you, the file's header or the config's file rules (said which), converted to scene_linear or your working space; alpha kept; a native VIDEO of the source clip with its sound.

format.tooltip: Only what this machine can write is listed.

bit_depth.tooltip: auto: EXR half, DPX 10-bit, TIFF 16-bit, PNG / JPEG 8-bit, a movie its codec's own.

quality.tooltip: JPEG and H.264.

fps.tooltip: 0 = the metadata's rate, else 24. 23.976 is written exactly (24000/1001).

video.tooltip: A native VIDEO: its frames, sound, rate and alpha are written.

audio.tooltip: A movie: muxed in (a still / sequence: ignored, said).

frame_numbers.tooltip: Frame mapping (NukeMax Read's frame_numbers, or 1001-1010, 1020). Empty: from frame_start.

ocio_config.tooltip: From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; empty = $OCIO, else the built-in ACES studio config.

output_space.tooltip: Empty = the config's file rule for this format.

NukeMax_OCIOWrite.name: NukeMax_OCIOWrite
NukeMax_OCIOWrite.description: Writes IMAGE or a native VIDEO through OCIO: from the working space (or your input space) to the output space you type or the config's file rule for the format, then NukeMax Write; the OCIO facts go into the manifest sidecar.

NukeMax_PARDesqueeze.name: NukeMax_PARDesqueeze
NukeMax_PARDesqueeze.description: Anamorphic plate → SQUARE pixels for AI processing (Nuke: 4448x3840 @ PAR 1.7266 → 7680x3840 at 2:1). par_info feeds PAR Resqueeze for an exact round trip.

NukeMax_PARResqueeze.name: NukeMax_PARResqueeze
NukeMax_PARResqueeze.description: Square-pixel AI output → the plate's original pixel dimensions (reapply PAR in Nuke's format). Exact W×H restore, even if the AI changed resolution.

NukeMax_Position.name: NukeMax_Position
NukeMax_Position.description: Integer pixel translate (no interpolation), with black / wrap edges (Nuke Position).

NukeMax_Posterize.name: NukeMax_Posterize
NukeMax_Posterize.description: Quantise each channel to N levels (banding / cel-shade).

alpha.tooltip: Matte to premultiply with (1 keeps, 0 zeroes). Not connected: the image's own alpha, as Nuke's Premult does.

output.tooltip: rgba keeps the alpha with the premultiplied colour (what Merge over needs); rgb drops it.

NukeMax_Premult.name: NukeMax_Premult
NukeMax_Premult.description: Premultiply: multiply RGB by an alpha matte (straight → premultiplied), as required before a Merge (over).

fps.tooltip: 23.976 / 29.97 / 59.94 are written as exact NTSC rates (24000/1001 ...).

ocio_input_colorspace.tooltip: Working colorspace before encode. Empty = no conversion (legacy).

NukeMax_ProResSave.name: NukeMax_ProResSave
NukeMax_ProResSave.description: Export an IMAGE batch as Apple ProRes MOV (422 / 422 HQ / 4444 / 4444 XQ via PyAV prores_ks; 4444 keeps alpha on RGBA input) or H.264 MP4.

NukeMax_Radial.name: NukeMax_Radial
NukeMax_Radial.description: Generate a radial gradient (centre -> edge) — soft vignette / falloff source.

extended_pattern.tooltip: When off, only horizontal/vertical (legacy). Otherwise overrides direction.

NukeMax_Ramp.name: NukeMax_Ramp
NukeMax_Ramp.description: Generate a linear gradient ramp (horizontal/vertical) between two values.

image.tooltip: The input image to apply lighting effects to

preset.tooltip: Select a preset or 'None' for custom settings. NOTE: a preset overrides the widgets below - the values shown on the node are ignored for whatever the preset defines. The one exception is 'effect_strength', which scales the preset instead of being replaced by it

num_light_sources.tooltip: Number of light sources (1-3). Lights 2 and 3 have their own position, radius and color, but in color-correction mode they reuse Light 1's correction settings

preserve_positioning.tooltip: Keep your own light positions and radii when a preset is selected, instead of letting the preset set them

show_debug_info.tooltip: Output a debug visualization image (first image of the batch; zone overlays show Light 1, position and radius indicators are drawn for every light)

use_colored_lights.tooltip: Use additive colored light instead of color correction?

use_gradient_mode.tooltip: Use directional gradient masks instead of radial?

apply_3d_lighting.tooltip: Master switch for occlusion. Leave on and use 'light_direction' to choose the behaviour; turning this off forces 'No Occlusion'

light_direction.tooltip: How light interacts with the subject. 'Behind'/'In Front' require a mask

remove_background.tooltip: Composite the lit result back over the untouched original using the mask, so only the subject is relit. Does not remove anything. Ignored for 'Behind Subject' and 'In Front of Subject'

effect_strength.tooltip: Overall intensity multiplier for lighting adjustments/colors, gamma included. 0.0 leaves the image untouched. With a preset active this scales the preset's own strength, so 1.0 is the preset as designed. Does not scale rim_amplification or mask_blur - those have their own controls

mask_blur.tooltip: Blur radius for light mask edges (smoother transitions)

rim_amplification.tooltip: Intensity boost specifically for rim light component (when 'Behind Subject')

light_color_r.tooltip: Light 1: Red color (if 'Use Colored Lights' is True)

light_color_g.tooltip: Light 1: Green color (if 'Use Colored Lights' is True)

light_color_b.tooltip: Light 1: Blue color (if 'Use Colored Lights' is True)

light_intensity.tooltip: Light 1: Intensity (if 'Use Colored Lights' is True)

inner_brightness.tooltip: Light 1: Inner area brightness (Color Correction mode)

inner_contrast.tooltip: Light 1: Inner area contrast (Color Correction mode)

inner_saturation.tooltip: Light 1: Inner area saturation (Color Correction mode)

inner_gamma.tooltip: Light 1: Inner area gamma. Above 1.0 brightens midtones, below 1.0 darkens them

outer_brightness.tooltip: Light 1: Outer area brightness (Color Correction mode)

outer_contrast.tooltip: Light 1: Outer area contrast (Color Correction mode)

outer_saturation.tooltip: Light 1: Outer area saturation (Color Correction mode)

outer_gamma.tooltip: Light 1: Outer area gamma. Above 1.0 brightens midtones, below 1.0 darkens them

mask.tooltip: Foreground mask (white=subject, black=background). Needed for occlusion ('Behind Subject' / 'In Front of Subject') and for 'remove_background' compositing. Resized automatically if it does not match the image

output_tooltips: The relit image
Pass-through of the input mask, normalised to (batch, height, width) and resized to the image (black if none connected)
Visualization of light positions and masks (enable 'show_debug_info')
NukeMax_ReLight2D.name: NukeMax_ReLight2D
NukeMax_ReLight2D.description: Creates realistic lighting effects with multiple light sources, colored lights, and 3D lighting simulation with subject occlusion

file.tooltip: A still, a frame of a sequence or a video in the input folder (Upload media adds files; several frames at once = a sequence).
