NukeMax_Read.name: NukeMax_Read
NukeMax_Read.description: Reads stills, numbered sequences and video (EXR, DPX, TIFF, PNG, JPEG, HDR, TGA, BMP, WebP, MOV, MP4, MKV ...): a sequence from one frame or a pattern, frame range and step, missing-frame policy, frame shift, OCIO on read, the video's sound, a contact sheet of the range.

file.tooltip: An EXR in ComfyUI's input folder. Upload new ones with the node's Upload EXR button (sequences: select all their frames).

mode.tooltip: file: that one EXR. sequence: every frame of its sequence. server path: server_path (held to the C2C media roots when this server is reachable from other machines).

layer.tooltip: auto = RGB(A); else a layer name from metadata (e.g. diffuse, specular, depth).

server_path.tooltip: mode = server path: a file, a frame of a sequence or a pattern (shot.####.exr).

NukeMax_ReadEXRPro.name: NukeMax_ReadEXRPro
NukeMax_ReadEXRPro.description: Reads an EXR - a file you upload or pick from the input folder, a whole sequence from one of its frames, or a server path - as scene-linear float (never clamped), its alpha, every layer for Shuffle Pass, and a header / layer report. The preview is made on the server.

load_as_sequence.tooltip: Expand %04d / #### patterns using the frame input

print_pass_list.tooltip: Print the pass list to the console when executed

NukeMax_ReadMultiPass.name: NukeMax_ReadMultiPass
NukeMax_ReadMultiPass.description: Load all EXR layers into a NUKE_PASSES bundle plus a beauty IMAGE preview and pass list.

NukeMax_Rectangle.name: NukeMax_Rectangle
NukeMax_Rectangle.description: Generate a filled rectangle on black (normalised x,y,w,h) — a quick garbage-matte / mask source.

aspect_preset.tooltip: Overrides target height from width: named cinema ratio, the input's own ratio (from_input), or custom W:H below.

NukeMax_Reformat.name: NukeMax_Reformat
NukeMax_Reformat.description: Nuke-style Reformat: fit (letterbox), fill (crop), width, height, or explicit distort. Never distorts unless 'distort' is selected. Aspect presets (cinema ratios) or the input's own ratio can drive the target box.

NukeMax_RotoShapeFromFile.name: NukeMax_RotoShapeFromFile

NukeMax_RotoShapeRenderer.description: Rasterize a ROTO_SHAPE to a per-frame mask with optional flow-driven directional motion blur.

feather_5.tooltip: Feather override for layer 5; <0 uses the shape's per-vertex mean.

feather_6.tooltip: Feather override for layer 6; <0 uses the shape's per-vertex mean.

NukeMax_RotoShapeStack.description: Composite up to 6 animated ROTO_SHAPE inputs into a single MASK. Per-frame tracking data (coords, velocity, confidence) for the vertices.

roto.tooltip: Roto shape to convert into diffusion guidance.

soft_radius_px.tooltip: Gaussian feather radius in pixels for the soft mask.

latent_downscale.tooltip: Spatial downscale factor for the latent-resolution mask (e.g. 8 for SD VAE).

NukeMax_RotoShapeToDiffusionGuidance.name: NukeMax_RotoShapeToDiffusionGuidance
NukeMax_RotoShapeToDiffusionGuidance.description: Convert a roto shape into hard, soft, and latent-resolution masks plus SAM-style box+point prompts as JSON.

Soft Gaussian-feathered roto mask for inpainting.

canvas_height.tooltip: Canvas height in pixels when the JSON does not specify one.

NukeMax_STMapIdentity.description: Build an identity STMap at the given resolution (R=U, G=V, B=0).

NukeMax_Saturation.description: Adjust saturation around Rec.709 luminance (0 = greyscale, 1 = unchanged, >1 = more saturated).

NukeMax_Sharpen.name: NukeMax_Sharpen
NukeMax_Sharpen.description: Unsharp-mask sharpen: amount * (image - blurred), added back.

output.tooltip: rgb: three channels (alpha on the MASK output), as before. rgba: the shuffled alpha stays in the image too.

NukeMax_ShuffleImage.name: NukeMax_ShuffleImage
NukeMax_ShuffleImage.description: Remap RGBA channels Nuke-style. Each output channel is picked from any source channel or a constant.

mapping.tooltip: Comma-separated source-channel indices (or 'z' for zero, 'o' for one) for each output channel. Works on image (4-D) and video (5-D) latents; the latent's noise mask and other entries are kept.

NukeMax_ShuffleLatent.name: NukeMax_ShuffleLatent
NukeMax_ShuffleLatent.description: Remap latent channels by index. Use this to swap or zero out specific latent dimensions.

passes.tooltip: Read MultiPass's bundle (one frame), or Load Video (C2C)'s exr_passes (every loaded frame of the layer).

pass_name.placeholder: e.g. RGBA, diffuse, N, Z, crypto00

channel_mode.tooltip:
How to convert the pass to a 3/4-channel IMAGE:
  auto: 1ch->gray, 2ch->pad, 3/4ch->as-is, 5+->first 4
  rgb: force 3 channels
  rgba: force 4 channels (add alpha=1)
  single_to_rgb: always treat as grayscale

on_missing.tooltip: If the named pass is not found: return black or raise

NukeMax_ShufflePass.name: NukeMax_ShufflePass
NukeMax_ShufflePass.description: Extract one named pass from a NUKE_PASSES bundle as a standard IMAGE.

knee.tooltip: Values below this are passed through unchanged.

ceiling.tooltip: Asymptote. Output approaches but never reaches it. Must be greater than 'knee'.

floor.tooltip: Lower asymptote. Must be less than 'shadow_knee'.

NukeMax_SoftClip.name: NukeMax_SoftClip
NukeMax_SoftClip.description: Nuke SoftClip: roll highlights off asymptotically toward a ceiling instead of clipping them flat. Below 'knee' the image is untouched and the slope is continuous at the knee, so no visible edge appears. Optionally does the same on the shadow side.

NukeMax_Soften.name: NukeMax_Soften
NukeMax_Soften.description: Gentle gaussian soften (mix of blurred + original).

image.tooltip: Image batch to detect edges on.

top_k.tooltip: Number of strongest edge points kept per frame as tracks.

NukeMax_SubPixelEdgeDetect.name: NukeMax_SubPixelEdgeDetect
NukeMax_SubPixelEdgeDetect.description: Sobel edge detector with sub-pixel localization; emits an edge magnitude mask and the top-K edge points as tracking data.
output_tooltips: Per-pixel edge magnitude normalized to [0,1].
Top-K edge point coordinates with confidence per frame.

NukeMax_Switch.name: NukeMax_Switch
NukeMax_Switch.description: Pass through input A or B selected by 'which' (0 = A, 1 = B).

NukeMax_Text.name: NukeMax_Text
NukeMax_Text.description: Burn text onto the image (slate / annotation). Uses PIL if available.

rig.tooltip: Light rig describing the lights and ambient.

fov_deg.tooltip: Camera vertical field-of-view in degrees used to reconstruct view rays.

tonemap.tooltip: Apply a Reinhard tonemap before returning sRGB.

NukeMax_ThreePointRelight.name: NukeMax_ThreePointRelight
NukeMax_ThreePointRelight.description: Relight a MATERIAL_SET with a LIGHT_RIG using a Lambert+Phong shader and optional Reinhard tonemap.
output_tooltips: Relit sRGB image of the materials under the rig.

NukeMax_Tile.name: NukeMax_Tile
NukeMax_Tile.description: Tile / repeat the image in a grid (columns x rows).

invert.tooltip: Apply the inverse transform (undoes this one with the same settings).

NukeMax_Transform.name: NukeMax_Transform
NukeMax_Transform.description: 2D Transform: translate (px), rotate (deg), scale, around a center, with a chosen filter. Uses an affine grid sample.

alpha.tooltip: Matte to divide by; zero-alpha pixels are left unchanged. Not connected: the image's own alpha.

output.tooltip: rgba keeps the alpha; rgb drops it.

NukeMax_Unpremult.name: NukeMax_Unpremult
NukeMax_Unpremult.description: Unpremultiply: divide RGB by an alpha matte (premultiplied → straight) so colour ops act on un-darkened edges. Division by zero is guarded.

ocio_input_colorspace.tooltip: File colorspace; empty = no OCIO conversion on load.

ocio_output_colorspace.tooltip: Working colorspace after load; empty = no conversion.

NukeMax_VideoSequenceLoad.name: NukeMax_VideoSequenceLoad
NukeMax_VideoSequenceLoad.description: Load frames from a video file (ProRes, H.264, DNxHD, etc.) as an IMAGE batch via PyAV.

NukeMax_Viewer.name: NukeMax_Viewer
NukeMax_Viewer.description: Preview an IMAGE with Nuke-style channel isolation (R G B A L, M = matte overlay), gain, gamma and an optional mask overlay. An output node: it runs and shows the frame with nothing after it. The IMAGE output carries the viewed result in linear float (alpha kept for rgba); only the preview is clipped for display.

alpha.tooltip: Shown as the alpha channel when the image has none.

image_b.tooltip: B, for A/B compare (split / wipe, difference, heatmap, blink).

passes.tooltip: Read EXR Pro's passes: each layer can be viewed (up to 8) and the EXR inspector lists them.

video.tooltip: A native VIDEO: its sound plays with the timeline.

audio.tooltip: Sound to play with the timeline (instead of the video's).

metadata.tooltip: Read / Read EXR Pro metadata: frame numbers, fps and the source shown in the panel.

frame_numbers.tooltip: e.g. 1001-1100 (Read's frame_numbers); empty = from the metadata, else from 0.

fps.tooltip: 0 = the metadata's rate, else 24.

apply_view_adjustment.tooltip: Off: the output is the input, untouched. On: exposure / gamma / gain below are applied.

exposure.tooltip: Stops. Used only when apply_view_adjustment is on.

NukeMax_ViewerPro.name: NukeMax_ViewerPro
NukeMax_ViewerPro.description: A professional viewer on the node: fit / 100% / zoom / pan, R G B A luma, exposure in stops, gamma, gain, checkerboard alpha, exact pixel values, timeline with timecode. VIEW ONLY: the output is the input, untouched, unless you press Apply view to output.

NukeMax_Vignette.name: NukeMax_Vignette
NukeMax_Vignette.description: Radial vignette — darken (or brighten) toward the frame edges.

format.tooltip: Only what this machine can write is listed.

bit_depth.tooltip: auto: EXR half, DPX 10-bit, TIFF 16-bit, PNG / JPEG 8-bit, a movie its codec's own.

quality.tooltip: JPEG and H.264.

fps.tooltip: 0 = the metadata's rate, else 24. 23.976 is written exactly (24000/1001).

audio.tooltip: A movie: muxed in (a still / sequence: ignored, said).

frame_numbers.tooltip: Frame mapping (NukeMax Read's frame_numbers, or 1001-1010, 1020). Empty: from frame_start.

NukeMax_Write.name: NukeMax_Write
NukeMax_Write.description: Writes stills, numbered sequences (EXR, DPX, TIFF, PNG, JPEG) or a movie (ProRes, H.264, FFV1 - what this machine can write) with sound: versioned, never a silent overwrite, atomic, a manifest with SHA-256, the exact files listed.

output_dir.tooltip: A folder inside ComfyUI's output folder, or an absolute path (a server reachable from other machines: only inside the C2C media roots).

versioning.tooltip: A new name_v### folder per write (never touches an earlier one), or plain names in output_dir.

overwrite.tooltip: Replace files that already exist. Off: a write that would replace a file is refused, naming it.

passes.tooltip: The pass bundle of NukeMax Read EXR Pro / EXR Pass Reader.

metadata.tooltip: Read EXR Pro / Metadata Reader Pro metadata: its source header is embedded, its fps used.

frame_numbers.tooltip: Frame mapping, e.g. 1001-1010, 1020 or 1001-1019x2 (one number per image). Empty: count from frame_start.

version.tooltip: 0 = the next free version; a number = exactly that version (refused if it exists, unless overwrite).

passes_to_write.tooltip: Comma-separated pass names; empty = every pass in the bundle.

data_passes_float.tooltip: Depth, position, normal, motion and other data passes stay 32-bit float when the beauty is half.

alpha_mode.tooltip: EXR stores premultiplied (associated) alpha: premultiply a straight image here.

colour_space.tooltip: The colour space of the written pixels, stored in the header (e.g. ACEScg). Empty = none stored.

convert_from.tooltip: OCIO: convert the colour channels from this space to colour_space before writing (data passes never). Empty = no conversion.

ocio_config.tooltip: OCIO config file; empty = $OCIO, else the built-in studio config.

fps.tooltip: Written as FramesPerSecond; 0 = the metadata's rate, else none.

NukeMax_WriteEXRPro.name: NukeMax_WriteEXRPro
NukeMax_WriteEXRPro.description: Writes EXR frames safely: half / float (data passes stay float), any compression, single part or multipart with passes, OCIO colour conversion, a new version folder by default and overwrite only when asked, atomic writes, a manifest with SHA-256 - and it lists exactly the files it wrote.

NukeMax_ZDefocus.name: NukeMax_ZDefocus
NukeMax_ZDefocus.description: Depth-driven defocus — blur scales with distance from the focal plane (a depth map drives it).

in_colorspace.tooltip: Source colourspace. Lists come from the active OCIO config ($OCIO or built-in ACES); changing $OCIO needs a ComfyUI restart.

out_colorspace.tooltip: Destination colourspace. Lists come from the active OCIO config ($OCIO or built-in ACES); changing $OCIO needs a ComfyUI restart.

display.tooltip: Target display. Lists come from the active OCIO config ($OCIO or built-in ACES); changing $OCIO needs a ComfyUI restart.

view.tooltip: View transform (must belong to the chosen display). Lists come from the active OCIO config ($OCIO or built-in ACES); changing $OCIO needs a ComfyUI restart.

input_colorspace.tooltip: Colourspace of the input image. Lists come from the active OCIO config ($OCIO or built-in ACES); changing $OCIO needs a ComfyUI restart.

custom_lut_path.placeholder: Optional: absolute path to a LUT file

load_as_sequence.tooltip: Treat path as image sequence (enable for patterns like ####, %04d)

colorspace.tooltip:
Colorspace the FILE IS IN on disk (matches Nuke's Read node convention). The node converts from this into the OCIO working space (the config's scene_linear role, e.g. ACEScg).

  raw - no conversion (pixels are passed through as stored)
  auto - take the colourspace from the file's metadata (EXR colorInteropID / OpenImageIO tag; untagged PNG and JPEG count as sRGB) and convert from it; files without a usable tag are passed through raw with a warning
  any other entry - OCIO colourspace the file is encoded in (e.g. 'sRGB Encoded Rec.709 (sRGB)' for PNG / JPG, 'ACEScg' for linear EXR)

The list comes from the active OCIO config ($OCIO, or the built-in ACES Studio config) and is built when ComfyUI starts - restart ComfyUI after changing $OCIO.

load_as_sequence.tooltip: Expand %04d / #### patterns using the frame input

print_pass_list.tooltip: Print the pass list to the console when executed

colorspace.tooltip:
Colorspace the FILE IS IN on disk. Light passes (beauty, diffuse, specular, ...) are converted from it into the OCIO working space; data passes (N, P, Z, motion, IDs, mattes, UVs) are never converted.

  raw - no conversion
  auto - take the colourspace from the file's metadata (EXR colorInteropID / OpenImageIO tag); an untagged file is passed through raw with a warning
  any other entry - OCIO colourspace the file is encoded in (e.g. 'ACEScg' for a linear render)

The list comes from the active OCIO config ($OCIO, or the built-in ACES Studio config) and is built when ComfyUI starts - restart ComfyUI after changing $OCIO.

save_format_as.tooltip: When format is 'custom' and this is non-empty, the custom width/height/pixel aspect are saved under this name and appear in the format dropdown after a frontend refresh.

input_pixel_aspect.tooltip: Pixel aspect ratio of the incoming image (1.0 = square pixels). ComfyUI images carry no format metadata, so declare it here when the source is anamorphic (e.g. PAL 1.09).

pass_name.placeholder: e.g. RGBA, diffuse, N, Z, crypto00

channel_mode.tooltip:
How to convert the pass to a 3/4-channel IMAGE:
  auto: 1ch->gray, 2ch->pad, 3/4ch->as-is, 5+->first 4
  rgb: force 3 channels
  rgba: force 4 channels (add alpha=1)
  single_to_rgb: always treat as grayscale

on_missing.tooltip: If the named pass is not found: return black or raise

file_path.placeholder: Output path (e.g., output.%04d.exr or output.#### or output)

image.tooltip: Image input. Used when channels is 'rgb' or 'rgba'. Not needed when channels='all_channels'.

channels.tooltip:
Channel layout for the output file:
  rgba - write 4 channels (RGB + alpha). Uses the IMAGE input.
  rgb - write 3 channels (RGB only). Uses the IMAGE input.
  all_channels - write all passes as multi-channel EXR. Uses the PASSES input. Colorspace conversion is applied only to light passes, not to data passes (normal, depth, position, motion, IDs, mattes, UVs).

passes.tooltip: Multi-pass bundle from Nuke Read MultiPass. Used when channels='all_channels'.

compression.tooltip: EXR compression. zips (Zip, 1 scanline - Nuke's default), zip, piz, rle and none are lossless. pxr24 is lossless for 16f but lossy for 32f; b44, b44a, dwaa and dwab are lossy.

frame_padding.tooltip: Number of digits for frame numbers (e.g., 4 = 0001, 0002...)

overwrite.tooltip:
True: overwrite existing files at the exact target paths (each frame is written atomically via a temp file + rename).
False: never clobber - if any target frame already exists, the WHOLE sequence is written with a versioned base name (name_1.0001.exr, name_1.0002.exr, ...) so one render always shares one consistent name.

colorspace.tooltip:
Colorspace to WRITE the file as on disk (matches Nuke's Write node convention). Input is assumed to be in the OCIO working space (the config's scene_linear role, e.g. ACEScg); the node converts from there into the chosen space.

  raw - write input as-is, no conversion and no colourspace tag in the file
  any other entry - OCIO colourspace to encode to (e.g. 'sRGB Encoded Rec.709 (sRGB)' for PNG / JPG, 'ACEScg' for linear EXR)

The list comes from the active OCIO config ($OCIO, or the built-in ACES Studio config) and is built when ComfyUI starts - restart ComfyUI after changing $OCIO.

t.tooltip: How far from a to b (0..1).

curve.tooltip: linear: straight; smoothstep and cosine ease in and out near a and b; hold: keeps the earlier value until the next key (steps).

keyframes.tooltip: Optional keyframes 'position:value', comma separated, e.g. '0:0, 0.5:1, 1:0' (positions in the time_mode's unit: 0..1, frames or seconds). When set, a and b are ignored and curve shapes each segment; before the first / after the last key the value holds.

time_mode.tooltip: normalised t: evaluate at t (0..1) as before. frame / seconds: evaluate at 'time' instead; without keyframes t = time / duration.

time.tooltip: frame / seconds mode: where to evaluate (a frame number or seconds).

duration.tooltip: frame / seconds mode: length of one cycle in the same unit. Needed without keyframes; with keyframes 0 = up to the last key.

loop.tooltip: frame / seconds mode: clamp holds the end value, loop restarts every cycle, ping-pong runs forward then back.

NumberLerpMEC.name: NumberLerpMEC
NumberLerpMEC.description: Linear / smoothstep / cosine interpolation between two values. t is clamped to [0,1].
output_tooltips: The interpolated value.
The interpolated value, rounded to the nearest whole number.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

OCIOCDLTransform.name: OCIOCDLTransform
output_tooltips: Image with the ASC CDL grade applied.

plate.tooltip: The original frames. Everything outside the mask comes from here unchanged, which is what preserves tone, texture and frame-to-frame stability.

reconstruction.tooltip: Output of an SDR-to-HDR pass over the same frames (LumiPic, LTX HDR IC-LoRA, ...). Used only inside the mask.

repair_highlights.tooltip: Rebuild blown highlights. This is the end that reconstructs well: a clipped sun comes back with a falloff.

highlight_level.tooltip: Repair above this code value. Detail usually dies before 1.0, so values in the 0.90-0.99 band are normal. Lower catches more, at the cost of overwriting pixels that were fine.

repair_shadows.tooltip: OFF by default on purpose. Measured on real material the reconstruction returned SMOOTH shadows, replacing the plate's real (if noisy) texture. Turn on only if your pass demonstrably does better in the blacks.

shadow_level.tooltip: Repair below this code value. A plate typically loses most shadow structure by about 0.04.

grow.tooltip: Expand the mask outward, so the repair starts slightly before the damage does.

feather.tooltip: Soften the mask edge. This is what stops the composite reading as a seam.

match_levels.tooltip: Scale the reconstruction to the plate on mid-tones before compositing, so the patch sits at the plate's exposure instead of its own.

plate_space.tooltip: What the plate is in, which the node cannot reliably detect: a scene-linear plate made from an 8-bit source peaks at exactly 1.0, same as a display one. Say it here. The two levels are ALWAYS quoted in display codes, because that is where clipping happens; on a linear plate the node encodes internally for the mask only and still composites in linear.

OCIOClipRepair.name: OCIOClipRepair
OCIOClipRepair.description: Composite an HDR reconstruction into a plate's clipped highlights and/or crushed shadows only, leaving the rest of the frame untouched. Thresholds are widgets because detail dies before the code reaches 1.0, and where it dies is a property of the plate. Shadow repair is off by default: on measured material the reconstruction smoothed the blacks rather than restoring their texture.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

config_path.tooltip: OCIO config: built-in ACES, or a .ocio file dropped in the ComfyUI input folder. Pick from the list.

OCIOColorSpace.name: OCIOColorSpace
output_tooltips: Image converted from in_colorspace to out_colorspace.
Same conversion as a ComfyUI VIDEO (carries data only when a VIDEO is fed in).

view.tooltip: View transform (from the config). Must be valid for the chosen display.

invert_direction.tooltip: Invert (display-referred back to the input colorspace).

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

config_path.tooltip: OCIO config: built-in ACES, or a .ocio file dropped in the ComfyUI input folder. Pick from the list.

OCIODisplay.name: OCIODisplay
output_tooltips: Image with the display + view transform applied (or inverted).

exposure.tooltip: Stops. out = in * 2**exposure. 0.0 is a pass-through. Nothing is clamped: highlights above 1.0 and negatives both survive.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

OCIOExposure.name: OCIOExposure
output_tooltips: Image scaled by 2**exposure. Nothing is clamped at either end.

file_path.tooltip: No LUT in the input folder; type a path. FEED IT THE DOMAIN IT WAS MADE FOR: a LUT clamps anything outside its range to the edge, so a scene-linear plate peaking at 15 lands on the corner value silently. Put a LogConvert ahead.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

OCIOFileTransform.name: OCIOFileTransform
output_tooltips: Image with the LUT / CCC / CDL file transform applied.

curve.tooltip: The TRANSFER CURVE only, not the gamut. Log to Linear decodes to linear in the camera's OWN primaries, so pair it with a camera-gamut to ACEScg ColorSpace step. Per-curve anchors: docs/NODES_COLOR.md.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

OCIOLogConvert.name: OCIOLogConvert
output_tooltips: Image with the lin<->log curve applied.

look.tooltip: OCIO look from the config. '(none)' = no look.

mix.tooltip: Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass.

config_path.tooltip: OCIO config: built-in ACES, or a .ocio file dropped in the ComfyUI input folder. Pick from the list.

OCIOLookTransform.name: OCIOLookTransform
output_tooltips: Image with the OCIO look applied (or inverted).

input_colorspace.tooltip: The colorspace the incoming batch is in (front-end auto-guesses ACEScg for HDR / >1 data, else sRGB - Display).

output_colorspace.tooltip: The colorspace the viewer converts to for display.

raw_data.tooltip: Show pixels untouched (no colorspace conversion for display).

start_frame.tooltip: First frame to play, in the source numbering shown on the timeline. The viewer holds the whole input.

end_frame.tooltip: Last frame to play, source numbering (0 = through the end).

fps.tooltip: Playback rate for the viewer.

images.tooltip: Any IMAGE batch - still (N=1), sequence or video (N>1). Optional: connect a Load Video node to 'video' instead to stream a movie without materializing it.

video.tooltip: Connect a Load Video node here to STREAM a movie in the viewport (WebCodecs decode-on-demand, no whole-clip materialization). Takes priority over 'images' for what the viewer shows.

alpha.tooltip: Optional alpha to view / carry through.

base.tooltip: Hidden. The source's first-frame number, set from the upstream OCIO Read: start_frame / end_frame are SOURCE numbers and this is subtracted to reach batch indices. 0 = already 0-based.

audio.tooltip: Optional soundtrack for the frames on the left. Plays with them and feeds the L/R meters, cut to the frames the viewer cached so sound cannot drift from picture. Ignored when a movie is streamed through 'video' - that clip brings its own track.

source.tooltip: Path to a still, a sequence folder, one numbered frame or a video - anywhere on disk, or relative to the ComfyUI input folder. Use Open Files, or type it. A folder or one frame gives the whole sequence.

frame_mode.tooltip: auto: a numbered file with siblings becomes the whole sequence. single: just this file. sequence: force-collapse siblings. video: a movie clip. A folder is always a sequence; a video always its full clip. Your own choice is kept.

input_colorspace.tooltip: Colorspace from the active OCIO (ACES) config.

output_colorspace.tooltip: Colorspace from the active OCIO (ACES) config.

raw_data.tooltip: Nuke 'Raw Data': skip the colorspace conversion and pass the file's values through untouched (input/output colorspace are ignored).

start_frame.tooltip: First frame number to load (0 = from the detected start). Auto-filled to the range when you pick a source. Below the original range, edge_mode fills in.

end_frame.tooltip: Last frame number to load (0 = to the detected end). Above the original range, edge_mode fills in.

frame_shift.tooltip: Re-base: the number the FIRST frame becomes downstream (Nuke frame offset). 0 = keep the source number (e.g. 86). Set 1 to start at 1, 10 to start at 10 - the whole range shifts with it. Flows to OCIO Write (first_frame + start_number).

missing_frames.tooltip: Gaps INSIDE the sequence (e.g. 24 missing between 23 and 25): black = a black frame; hold = repeat the previous frame; error = stop. Missing frames are listed in 'info'.

edge_mode.tooltip: Frames OUTSIDE the original range (Nuke before/after): hold the end frame, loop the sequence, bounce (ping-pong), or black.

fps.tooltip: 0 = take from the video metadata (24 for stills). Flows to OCIO Write through the wire.

samples.tooltip: The latent to decode, same input the stock VAE Decode takes.

vae.tooltip: The VAE that belongs to the model. A VAE is trained together with its transformer and cannot be swapped for another one.

precision.tooltip: float32 is the default and costs 5.2x the model's own dtype: 28.8 s against 5.5 s, 25 frames at 1280x704 tiled 384. float16 applies only where the VAE lists it; LTX does not, so it falls back and the report says so. docs/NODES_VAE.md 3.2.

clamp.tooltip: OFF (default) passes values through as the model produced them, including anything below 0 or above 1. ON reproduces the stock VAE Decode exactly - use it only to compare against the standard path.

tiled.tooltip: Decode in tiles. ON by default since v1.3.0: the untiled path is the one that runs out of memory on a real clip, and it is slower even when it fits - 121 frames at float32 took 912 s untiled against 60 s tiled. Tiling does change the picture, by roughly 30x what precision does, so turn it off for a short clip where the whole frame fits. docs/NODES_VAE.md 3.3.

tile_size.tooltip: Spatial tile in PIXELS, divided by the VAE's compression ratio (32x on LTX, so 384 becomes 12). 384 measured clean at 60 s for 121 frames; 768 overflowed. If a decode crawls, lower this first. docs/NODES_VAE.md 3.3.

overlap.tooltip: Spatial overlap between tiles in PIXELS, feathered by the blend. Held to a quarter of the tile, ComfyUI's own convention (comfy/sd.py:1234). Spatial seams are not the problem: measured gradient excess is 1.03-1.05x.

temporal_size.tooltip: TILE SPACE, NEVER TIME. The 4096 default exceeds any clip on purpose, making the whole sequence one temporal tile so no time tiling happens. Lowering it leaves a visibly soft frame at a fixed period. docs/NODES_VAE.md 3.3.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: Temporal overlap in PIXEL frames, used only when temporal_size is small enough to split the clip. Held to half the temporal tile. It cannot repair the soft frame: a wider blend spreads the weak edge over more frames instead of removing it.

OCIOVAEDecode.name: OCIOVAEDecode
OCIOVAEDecode.description: Decode a latent without the 0..1 clamp, optionally with the VAE in float32, with spatial tiling for long clips and a range report on a second output. With clamp ON it reproduces the stock VAE Decode bit for bit, so it is a safe drop-in. Measured honestly: on an SDR generation the clamp costs 0.06% of samples (+0.05 above white), and on real ACEScct HDR material carrying +3.9 stops it costs nothing at all, because 15x white only reaches code 0.80. The clamp removes range only above code 1.0, i.e. linear past ~222. Use this for control over the decode, not as a rescue for dynamic range the model never produced. Tile SPACE and not time: a temporal tile edge leaves a visibly soft frame, a spatial one does not.
output_tooltips: The decoded frames, unclamped unless you asked otherwise. What the values MEAN depends on how the generation encoded them: display RGB for SDR, ACEScct log codes on LTX-2's HDR path.

min, max, mean, percentiles, and the exact share of samples below 0 and above 1 - the range the standard clamp would have destroyed. Also carries a note for anything the node declined to do, which would otherwise reach the server log only.

pixels.tooltip: The image or sequence to encode. Values are expected in 0..1; anything outside that is outside the VAE's training domain and is handled according to 'out_of_range'.

vae.tooltip: The VAE that belongs to the model. A VAE is trained together with its transformer and cannot be swapped for another one.

precision.tooltip: float32 is the default and costs 1.8x the model's own dtype: 5.4 s against 3.0 s, 25 frames at 1280x704. float16 applies only where the VAE lists it; LTX does not, so it falls back and the report says so. docs/NODES_VAE.md 3.2.

out_of_range.tooltip: Values outside 0..1 are outside the VAE's training domain. 'report only' matches the stock node but tells you. 'clamp to 0..1' keeps the VAE in domain. 'raise an error' stops the job. docs/NODES_VAE.md 3.4.

OCIOVAEEncode.name: OCIOVAEEncode
OCIOVAEEncode.description: Encode an image to a latent as the entry point of the OCIO family, so a graph does not have to leave it between Read and Write. Adds three things the stock VAE Encode does not: it reports values outside the VAE's 0..1 training domain instead of passing them through in silence (comfy/sd.py:501 applies image*2-1 with no clamp), it reports the silent crop to the VAE's compression ratio (sd.py:1315), and it can run the encode at float32. It does NOT convert colour - put OCIO LogConvert in front of it for that, where the curve is visible in the graph.
output_tooltips: The encoded latent, ready for a sampler.
What the encoder was handed: the input range, the share outside the VAE's 0..1 training domain and what was done about it, any silent crop, and the precision actually used.

profile.tooltip: Sets from/output colorspace; the HDR presets also force EXR 16f. LTX 2.3 is for 2.3 only: it expects linear, because Lightricks' own node already undid LogC3. There is no 2.5 preset - undo 2.5's ACEScct curve with OCIO LogConvert instead. SDR Rec.709 delivery: read docs/NODES_IO.md first.

input_colorspace.tooltip: Colorspace from the active OCIO (ACES) config.

output_colorspace.tooltip: Colorspace from the active OCIO (ACES) config.

still_format.tooltip: Used for still image / sequence (hidden for video). EXR keeps float, so negatives and values above 1.0 survive. DPX is the film-pipeline interchange format, integer, 10 or 16 bit. TIFF is float only at 32f. PNG and JPEG are integer and clip both tails; JPEG is always 4:2:0.

video_codec.tooltip: Video only. The node's footer states the depth once you pick. FFV1 is the only one that returns this pack's input unchanged (16-bit, .mkv, archival). HEVC 4:4:4 12-bit is the only genuine 12-bit encode - ffmpeg's ProRes and DNxHR encoders top out at 10 whatever the format is nominally worth. 8-bit: DNxHR HQ, h264, hevc, and those two move to 10-bit on an HDR output. Measured table: README.md.

bit_depth.tooltip: Per format: JPEG 8; PNG 8/16; TIFF 8/16/32f; EXR 16f/32f; DPX 10/16. The list narrows to the chosen format.

compression.tooltip: EXR compression. ZIP (default) / ZIPS / RLE are lossless; PIZ is lossless and suits grain. DWAA / DWAB are much smaller and LOSSY: measured on a real frame they cost about half the distinct values and multiply the error by eighty, at 16f as well as 32f, and they quantise float32 to HALF before compressing - so 32f + DWAA is a half-precision file that still says 'float'. Pick DWAA for a review or comp copy, never for a master or a data pass (depth, normals, IDs). EXR only.

auto_range.tooltip: ON: first_frame / last_frame / start_number / fps come from the upstream OCIO Read. CANVAS ONLY - an API prompt gets whatever is in its JSON, with this ticked and doing nothing. Set the four explicitly for farm work.

first_frame.tooltip: still image: WHICH frame to save - a number outside the batch is refused by name, not rounded to the nearest frame. sequence/video: first frame to write (frame numbers, auto-filled from the source, e.g. 86).

last_frame.tooltip: sequence/video: last frame to write (0 = to the end; auto-filled from the source, e.g. 97). Ignored for a still image.

start_number.tooltip: OUTPUT file numbering start (auto-filled to the source's first frame, e.g. 86; set 1 for 0001..). This is the re-base, NOT retime.

source_start.tooltip: (auto) the source's first frame number, used to map first_frame/last_frame to the batch. Set by the wire.

raw_data.tooltip: Nuke 'Raw Data': write the pixels as-is, skipping the from->out colorspace conversion. The file is also left UNTAGGED - no chromaticities on a still, no colour primaries / transfer / matrix on a movie - because unconverted pixels have no delivery space to name.

colorspace_in_name.tooltip: Put the output colorspace in the file name, before the frame number: name_acescg.0001.exr. Uses the sanitized output_colorspace (or 'raw' when Raw Data is on).

output_folder.tooltip: Empty = the ComfyUI output dir. Relative or $OUTPUT/sub sits under it; an absolute path is written there. PREFER relative or $OUTPUT: this value is stored in the workflow, and other nodes embed the workflow into the files they write.

filename.tooltip: Base name. Numbering / extension are added automatically.

auto_colorspace.tooltip: Superseded and inert - it changes nothing, which is why it is hidden. Use profile = 'auto', which traces the upstream source and covers more cases. Kept only so earlier saved graphs keep their other values in place.

view.tooltip: How to cross the scene/display boundary, on the pairs that cross it at all. Left on (none) the conversion is colorimetric: no tone mapping, so scene-linear 4.0 leaves as 1.78 and the container clips it flat. Pick a view and the ACES Output Transform is applied instead, rolling highlights off - 4.0 becomes 0.905, and nothing reaches 1.0 until about 128. Use a view for a review deliverable; leave it off for a technical re-encode or for material already scene-referred. Ignored entirely when both colorspaces sit on the same side, so camera logs and ACEScg to ACEScct are untouched.

images.tooltip: An image / sequence / video frame batch to write. Mutually exclusive with the ComfyUI Video input.

video.tooltip: A ComfyUI native VIDEO (e.g. Load Video) to render out with ALL these Write settings (container, codec, colorspace, bit depth). Mutually exclusive with the image input; the movie's own frame rate is used for a video container.

alpha.tooltip: Optional alpha channel -> RGBA (EXR / TIFF / PNG; ignored for JPEG). Wire OCIO Read's alpha output, or any MASK.

fps.tooltip: Video frame rate. Wire OCIO Read's fps output here to carry the source rate. This sets the TIME BASE, it does not resample: the same frames are written either way, so a 24fps batch written at 48 plays twice as fast and half as long (a conform, not a frame-rate conversion). NTSC rates go out as their exact rational, 23.976 as 24000/1001.

render_nonce.tooltip: Internal, hidden. The Render button bumps it so a repeat render to the same path really re-writes; ComfyUI would otherwise cache an identical Write and skip it.

audio.tooltip: Optional track. A video container muxes it in, trimmed to the frames written so it cannot drift; a sequence gets a sidecar .wav, because EXR / TIFF / PNG hold no audio. Formats per container: docs/NODES_IO.md.

metadata.tooltip: (optional) Wire OCIO Read's 'metadata' output here - or any node that emits the same JSON - to carry the plate's camera, lens, editorial attributes AND its start timecode into the written file. Claims a colour transform invalidates are dropped, not copied: docs/NODES_IO.md. A wire this node cannot read is reported and ignored; it never stops the render.

write_audio.tooltip: OFF: no sound at all, no muxed track and no sidecar .wav, even when one is wired or a native Video input brings its own. ON: the wired input wins, else the Video input's track. Off for a picture-only master.

write_sidecar.tooltip: The <name>.json written beside the render, holding the FULL metadata set. ON is right for a movie, whose container cannot hold all of it - check `sidecar_only` in the file to see exactly what would be lost. OFF is safe for EXR, whose header already carries everything (`sidecar_only` is empty there), and for any delivery that must be the picture files and nothing else. It never affects the pixels, the container tags or the .wav beside a sequence.

steps.tooltip: 3 = release setting (0.909375, 0.857, 0.667). 2 = 0.7, 0.494: ~30% faster, softer fine texture.

start_sigma.tooltip: 0 = the release grid for 2 / 3 steps. Above 0: the refiner's shift-6 grid from this start noise (e.g. 0.8 for the resolution ladder).

latent.tooltip: Draft latent (video or H3 AV latent; audio passes through).

OpenH3RegenUpscale.name: OpenH3RegenUpscale
OpenH3RegenUpscale.description: H3-Latent-Upscaler (LBH 3D conv) straight onto the target grid, no decode / re-encode. 4K runs two passes (to 2K, then 4K) so each stays within the trained range.

samples.tooltip: The sampler's output (video or AV latent).

frame_count.tooltip: Frames to keep when decoding later (Prepare Draft frame_count; 0 = all).

audio.tooltip: Soundtrack for the final MP4 (stored with the latent).

OpenH3SaveRefinedLatent.name: OpenH3SaveRefinedLatent
OpenH3SaveRefinedLatent.description: Saves the refined latent (+ frame count and soundtrack) to output/open_h3_latents/ and passes it on. Put it between the sampler and the decoder: the file is written before decoding starts, so a failed decode never costs the refine — open 'Decode Saved Latent' and run that instead.

images.tooltip: The clip's frames (Get Video Components images).

fps.tooltip: Frame rate of the frames (Get Video Components fps).

server_url.tooltip: OpenAI-compatible base URL (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, LM Studio). HTTPS certificates are always verified.

model.tooltip: Model id; empty = the server's first listed model.

api_key_env.tooltip: Name of the environment variable holding the API key (the key itself never goes into the workflow). Empty = no key.

send_as.tooltip: video: a small H.264 clip at 4 fps (the model sees the motion). frames: 8 JPEG stills, for servers without video input.

extra_instructions.tooltip: Optional notes for the model: names, style words, what to emphasise.

seed.tooltip: 0 = server default. Change it to get a new variant.

manual_prompt.tooltip: Leave empty to generate. Any text here is passed through as the prompt and the server is not called.

ca_file.tooltip: PEM file of the CA that signed the server's certificate, if Windows does not trust it already.

image.tooltip: Frames shot with non-square pixels (anamorphic lens, DV, HDV ...).

par_preset.tooltip: Camera / format the frames come from; sets the pixel aspect ratio. custom = type it in pixel_aspect.

pixel_aspect.tooltip: Used when par_preset = custom. PAR>1 = pixels wider than tall.

method.tooltip: stretch_width keeps every scanline (recommended); squash_height keeps the pixel count low.

filter.tooltip: How pixels are resampled: bicubic (sharp, default), bilinear (soft), nearest (no new values; for masks / IDs), area (best when shrinking).

lens_metadata.tooltip: Camera / lens facts to carry through the round trip, as 'key: value' lines or a JSON object (e.g. camera: ARRI Alexa 35, lens: Cooke 2x, squeeze: 2). Stored in par_info and given back by PAR Resqueeze's metadata. A squeeze / pixel_aspect value that disagrees with the PAR used is reported as a warning. Empty = nothing added (as before).

overscan_percent.tooltip: Add this much border (percent of each side, edge-extended) around the square-pixel frame so an AI step has room at the edges. PAR Resqueeze crops it off again before restoring the plate size. 0 = none (as before).

overscan_multiple.tooltip: Round the padded frame UP to a multiple of this (e.g. 16 or 64 for a model's size rule); the extra goes into the border. 1 = no rounding (as before).

PARDesqueezeMEC.name: PARDesqueezeMEC
PARDesqueezeMEC.description: Convert an anamorphic plate to SQUARE pixels before AI processing (Nuke: 4448x3840 @ PAR 1.7266 → 7680x3840 at 2:1). Wire par_info into PARResqueezeMEC to restore the original geometry losslessly.
output_tooltips: The frames with square pixels (wider with stretch_width, shorter with squash_height).
What was done, as JSON - connect it to PAR Resqueeze to undo it exactly after processing.
1 on the overscan border this node added (edge-extended pixels), 0 on the real picture; all 0 without overscan. Use it to let the AI step repaint only the border.

image.tooltip: The processed square-pixel frames from after PAR Desqueeze.

par_info.tooltip: PAR Desqueeze's par_info output: the original size and aspect.

filter.tooltip: How pixels are resampled: bicubic (sharp, default), bilinear (soft), nearest (no new values; for masks / IDs), area (best when shrinking).

reference.tooltip: Optional: the original plate (what went into PAR Desqueeze). The result is checked against it - size, frame count, largest / mean difference, PSNR - in metadata, and the difference output shows where they differ.

PARResqueezeMEC.name: PARResqueezeMEC
PARResqueezeMEC.description: Return an AI-processed square-pixel frame to the plate's original pixel dimensions (PAR metadata is reapplied in Nuke). Wire par_info from PARDesqueezeMEC — the round trip restores the exact original W×H even if the AI changed resolution.
output_tooltips: The frames back at the plate's original width x height.
What was restored, as JSON.
The plate's original pixel aspect ratio from par_info, to wire into a writer / format.

The plate's metadata restored as JSON: size, pixel aspect, display aspect, a Nuke format line, the lens metadata given to PAR Desqueeze, the overscan removed and, with reference wired, the round-trip check.
With reference wired: |result - reference| per pixel (mean of the channels, clipped to 0..1). All 0 without a reference.

vae.tooltip: The p-h3-image VAE. With it the pictures are also anchored as reference latents, without it they only condition the text encoder.

multiple.tooltip: Pad so width and height are divisible by this number. Padding is split evenly between opposite sides, with the extra pixel going to the right/bottom.

padding_style.tooltip: What to fill the padded area with.

color.tooltip: Fill color for the padded area. Alpha is ignored.

feathering.tooltip: Blend this many pixels of the image edge into the fill color on the padded sides.

all_history: show recent parameter changes across all nodes

run_b.tooltip: Second run number for diff mode (0 = auto-detect last two)

snapshot_action.tooltip: Branch snapshots. save: store the parameters of run_b (0 = the latest run) under snapshot_name; snapshots are kept when old runs are pruned. compare: differences between snapshot_name and compare_to. restore_plan: only the parameters matching restore_filter from snapshot_name (empty = latest run). snapshot_name.tooltip: Name of the snapshot to save, compare or restore from (e.g. 'branch-A').

compare_to.tooltip: compare: the second snapshot's name; empty = the latest run.

restore_filter.tooltip: restore_plan: comma-separated node classes, node titles, node ids, parameter names or Class.param (e.g. 'KSampler, cfg'). Only matching parameters are listed; the output is the exact patch to apply, nothing else is touched.

ParameterHistoryMEC.description: Query the parameter history database. Shows what parameters were changed, when, and what the previous values were. Supports run-to-run diffs.

snapshot_action result as JSON: the saved snapshot, the differences, or the restore patch {node_id: {params}}. Empty when snapshot_action is none.

allow_compile.tooltip: Allow torch.compile to trace into the flash attention function. If disabled (default), the function is wrapped with torch.compiler.disable() for compatibility, matching the sage attention node.

PatchFlashAttentionKJ.name: PatchFlashAttentionKJ
PatchFlashAttentionKJ.description: Experimental node for patching attention to use flash attention, without the silent SDPA fallback the ComfyUI default does. Patches the attention of the model passing through this node; to disable, bypass or disconnect this node. Requires the flash_attn library to be installed.

patch_order.tooltip: Patch the comfy patch_model function to load weight patches (LoRAs) before compiling the model

full_load.tooltip: Disabling may help with memory issues when loading large models, when changing this you should probably force model reload to avoid issues!

PatchModelPatcherOrder.name: PatchModelPatcherOrder
PatchModelPatcherOrder.description: NO LONGER NECESSARY OR FUNCTIONAL, keeping node for backwards compatibility. Use the TorchCompileModelAdvanced to use LoRA with torch.compile.

fuse_norm_silu.tooltip: Replace norm+SiLU chains (RMSNorm for Wan, GroupNorm for KL VAEs) with fused Triton kernels (single pass, fp32 accumulation). Requires triton.

channels_last.tooltip: Convert conv weights to channels_last memory format, removing cuDNN layout transposes around every conv. Required for the fused GroupNorm kernel to engage on KL VAEs.

int8_conv.tooltip: EXPERIMENTAL: run the VAE decoder's 3x3 convolutions on int8 tensor cores (4x the bf16 rate on Ada+). Weights quantized per-out-channel, activations dynamically per-tensor; ~45-48 dB vs the bf16 decode, minor quality loss possible. Wan 2.1/2.2 and KL image VAEs (Flux2/SDXL/SD1.5), ignored for others.

autotune.tooltip: Benchmark several kernel block-size configs on first use of each tensor shape and cache the fastest. Brief stutter per new resolution, usually a few percent faster after warmup.

PatchTritonVAE.name: PatchTritonVAE
PatchTritonVAE.description: Speeds up VAE decode/encode with fused Triton norm+SiLU kernels and channels_last conv layout. Supported VAEs (auto-detected): Wan 2.1/2.2 video VAEs incl. Qwen-Image (RMSNorm, ~1.4x/1.15x), KL image VAEs such as Flux/Flux2, SDXL and SD1.5 (GroupNorm, ~1.6-1.8x at 2048px), and LTXV/LTX2 video VAEs (PixelNorm; timestep-conditioned decoder blocks get norm-only fusion). Other architectures are not supported. Applied as object patches on a cloned patcher, so it only exists while this VAE is loaded.

sage_attention.tooltip: Patch the attention of the model passing through this node to use sageattn. To revert, run this node again with the disabled option. Requires the sageattention library to be installed.

allow_compile.tooltip: Allow the use of torch.compile for the sage attention function, requires latest sageattn 2.2.0 or higher.

PathchSageAttentionKJ.description: Experimental node for patching attention mode. This doesn't use the model patching system and thus can't be disabled without running the node again with 'disabled' option.

PatinaMaterialNode.description: Generate a complete seamlessly tiling PBR material (texture image + PBR maps) from a text prompt, up to 8K. Optionally drive it with an input image (img2img) or an image + mask (inpaint).

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible denoising.

auto_downscale.tooltip: Automatically downscale an input image whose longest side exceeds 2048px (the model's input limit), preserving aspect ratio; smaller images are left as-is. Disable to raise an error on oversized images instead.

style_to_apply.tooltip: The style you want for your image.

text.tooltip: The prompt to encode.

This node takes a prompt, adjusts its visual style according to the chosen option, and then encodes it using the provided text encoder to generate an embedding that will guide image generation.
